FCO.text: Rome is the capital of Italy and a city in layers, from the Colosseum and the Pantheon to the Vatican Library. The main sights run to about seventeen hours, so three or four days is a fair minimum. April and May are the best months.

CIA.text: Rome is the capital of Italy and a city in layers, from the Colosseum and the Pantheon to the Vatican Library. The main sights run to about seventeen hours, so three or four days is a fair minimum. April and May are the best months.

VCE.text: Venice is a city in Italy built across islands in a lagoon, with canals in place of streets. St Mark's Basilica, the Doge's Palace and the Rialto Bridge lead the sights, and ten hours covers them. May to July is the season.

TSF.text: Venice is a city in Italy built across islands in a lagoon, with canals in place of streets. St Mark's Basilica, the Doge's Palace and the Rialto Bridge lead the sights, and ten hours covers them. May to July is the season.

CDG.text: Paris is the capital of France and its main centre for art, food and fashion. The Eiffel Tower, the Louvre Museum and the Musee d'Orsay carry a first visit, and the main sights run to seventeen hours. May to September is the best stretch.

ORY.text: Paris is the capital of France and its main centre for art, food and fashion. The Eiffel Tower, the Louvre Museum and the Musee d'Orsay carry a first visit, and the main sights run to seventeen hours. May to September is the best stretch.

BVA.text: Paris is the capital of France and its main centre for art, food and fashion. The Eiffel Tower, the Louvre Museum and the Musee d'Orsay carry a first visit, and the main sights run to seventeen hours. May to September is the best stretch.

BCN.text: Barcelona is a port city on the Mediterranean coast of Spain and the capital of Catalonia. Sagrada Familia and Park Guell lead the sights, with city beaches close to the centre. April to June and September avoid the worst heat.

DBV.text: Dubrovnik is a walled town on the Adriatic coast of Croatia, compact enough to cross on foot. The Rector's Palace, Dubrovnik Cathedral and Lokrum lead the sights, and six hours covers them. May to August is the season.

gem:amalfi-coast.text: The Amalfi Coast is a run of cliffside villages in Campania, Italy, listed by UNESCO. Pompeii and Mount Vesuvius are the main sights within reach, and public transport along it is limited. May to August is the season.

gem:pompeii.text: Pompeii is a Roman town near Naples, buried by Mount Vesuvius in AD 79 and dug out since. The House of the Faun and the Amphitheatre of Pompeii are the set pieces, with Herculaneum nearby. Six hours is enough.

VIE.text: Vienna, the capital of Austria, grew up around the Habsburg court and is known for its musical life. Schonbrunn Palace, the Hofburg Palace and the Museum of Art History lead the sights. April to September is the best stretch.

SZG.text: Salzburg is a baroque city in Austria near the German border, and the birthplace of Mozart. Hohensalzburg Fortress looks down on the old town, with Salzburg Cathedral and Schloss Mirabell below. Ten hours covers the sights.

AMS.text: Amsterdam, the capital of the Netherlands, is laid out around a ring of canals. The Rijksmuseum and the Van Gogh Museum are the two that fill a day, with Vondelpark for the gap between them. June to August is the warmest stretch.

BGO.text: Bergen is a coastal city in Norway, the usual starting point for the western fjords. Bryggen and Bergenhus Fortress stand by the harbour, with Floyen and Ulriken rising behind. June to August is the season.

gem:bruges.text: Bruges is a medieval city in Flanders, Belgium, with its old centre largely intact. The Basilica of the Holy Blood, the Church of Our Lady and the Groeningemuseum are the sights that matter. June to August is busiest.

gem:tuscany-siena.text: Siena is a city in Tuscany, Italy, at the head of the Val d'Orcia wine country. Siena Cathedral, piazza del Campo and the Palazzo Pubblico lead the sights, and public transport is poor. May, June and September are the best months.

FLR.text: Florence is the capital of Tuscany and the city where the Italian Renaissance began. Santa Maria del Fiore, the Galleria degli Uffizi and the Ponte Vecchio are the fixed points. April to June and September are the best months.

LIS.text: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal, set on hills where the Tagus meets the Atlantic. Belem Tower, the Jeronimos Monastery and the Alfama district carry most of a visit. June to September is the warm season.

OPO.text: Porto is the second city of Portugal, stacked above the Douro estuary and known for its wine. The Dom Luis I Bridge, Porto Cathedral and the Palacio da Bolsa lead the sights, and ten hours covers them. June to August is the warm season.

EDI.text: Edinburgh is the Scottish capital, built on volcanic rock between a castle and a palace. Edinburgh Castle, the Palace of Holyroodhouse and St Giles' Cathedral anchor the old town, with Arthur's Seat rising above it. June to August is the season.

gem:como.text: Lake Como is a long alpine lake in Lombardy, Italy, ringed by villages and old villas. Bellagio and Varenna face each other across the water, and Villa Carlotta is the garden to see. Public transport is poor, so a boat helps.

gem:kotor.text: Kotor is a walled coastal town in Montenegro, set at the head of the Bay of Kotor. The Fortifications of Kotor climb the slope behind the old town, and Lovcen stands above. May and June are the best months.

SPU.text: Split is a coastal city in Dalmatia, Croatia, where the old town grew inside a Roman palace. Diocletian's Palace and the Cathedral of Saint Domnius are the core, with Klis Fortress inland. Ten hours covers the sights.

gem:cinque-terre.text: Cinque Terre is a line of five coastal villages in Liguria, Italy, with terraced slopes behind them. Cinque Terre National Park covers the ground they stand on, and the islands of Palmaria and Tino lie off the point. June to August is the season.

gem:granada.text: Granada is a city in Andalucia, Spain, below the Sierra Nevada. The Alhambra and the Generalife gardens take up most of a visit, with the Albaicin quarter on the hill opposite. May, June and September are the best months.

gem:syracuse.text: Syracuse is a coastal city in Italy with a baroque old town and ancient ruins. Ortigia holds the Cathedral of Syracuse and Castello Maniace, with the Ear of Dionysius inland. April and May are the best months.

NAP.text: Naples is a port city on the Mediterranean coast of Italy, dense and layered, with Mount Vesuvius close by. Castel dell'Ovo, Castel Nuovo and the Teatro di San Carlo lead the sights. May is the best month.

PRG.text: Prague is the largest city in Czechia and the old seat of Bohemia, laid out along the Vltava. Prague Castle, Saint Vitus Cathedral and Charles Bridge form one walk across the river. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:hallstatt.text: Hallstatt is a lakeside village in Austria, wedged between the Hallstatter See and the slopes behind it. The Dachstein Mountains and Krippenstein are the reason to stay past the viewpoint. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:matera.text: Matera is a city in Basilicata, Italy, with a quarter cut into the rock. The Sassi di Matera are the reason to come, and Matera Cathedral stands above them. May and June are the best months.

gem:meteora.text: Meteora is a cluster of rock pillars in Greece with monasteries built on top of them. The Monastery of the Holy Trinity and Varlaam monastery are the two most visited, and three hours covers a circuit. April and May are the best months.

gem:taormina.text: Taormina is a hillside town above the sea in Sicily, Italy. The Ancient theatre of Taormina looks out over the water, and Isola Bella lies on the shore below. May and June are the best months.

gem:agrigento-valle-dei-templi.text: Agrigento is a coastal town in Italy above a line of ancient temples. The Valle dei Templi holds the Temple of Concordia, the best preserved of them, and six hours covers the site. April and May are the best months.

CFU.text: Corfu is a Greek island in the Adriatic, off the northwest coast of the country. Beaches such as Agios Gordios and Myrtiotissa ring the island, and Butrint is within reach. May and June are the best months.

VRN.text: Verona is a city in the Veneto, Italy, with a Roman core and a reputation from Shakespeare. The Verona Arena is the largest thing in the centre, with the Museo di Castelvecchio and Porta Borsari nearby. April to June and September suit best.

JTR.text: Santorini is a volcanic island group in the Cyclades, Greece, arranged around a caldera. Akrotiri preserves a settlement buried by the eruption, and Nea Kameni sits in the middle of the bay. May to September is the season.

STN.text: London is the largest city in the United Kingdom, spread along the Thames in the south of England. The Tower of London, Westminster Abbey and the British Museum lead a long list, and the main sights run to seventeen hours. June to September is best.

LTN.text: London is the largest city in the United Kingdom, spread along the Thames in the south of England. The Tower of London, Westminster Abbey and the British Museum lead a long list, and the main sights run to seventeen hours. June to September is best.

LGW.text: London is the largest city in the United Kingdom, spread along the Thames in the south of England. The Tower of London, Westminster Abbey and the British Museum lead a long list, and the main sights run to seventeen hours. June to September is best.

LHR.text: London is the largest city in the United Kingdom, spread along the Thames in the south of England. The Tower of London, Westminster Abbey and the British Museum lead a long list, and the main sights run to seventeen hours. June to September is best.

KRK.text: Krakow is a city in southern Poland and was its capital in the Middle Ages. Wawel sits above the river, with the Krakow Old Town and Kazimierz below. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:lauterbrunnen.text: Lauterbrunnen is a village in a steep valley in the Bernese Oberland, Switzerland, with waterfalls down both walls. The Jungfrau, the Eiger and the Monch rise at the head of it, and Trummelbach is the waterfall to see. June to August is the season.

gem:dolomites.text: The Dolomites are a mountain range in Italy, walked in summer and skied in winter. Tre Cime di Lavaredo is the best known group, and Cortina d'Ampezzo is the main base. Public transport is poor.

gem:toledo.text: Toledo is a walled city in Castilla La Mancha, Spain, on a bend of the Tagus. Toledo Cathedral, the Alcazar of Toledo and the Synagogue of Santa Maria la Blanca sit within a few streets of each other. April and May are the best months.

gem:bath.text: Bath is a spa city in the United Kingdom, built in pale Georgian stone over Roman baths. Bath Abbey, the Royal Crescent and Pulteney Bridge are the set pieces, and ten hours covers them. June to September is the season.

gem:portovenere.text: Portovenere is a coastal village in Italy, listed by UNESCO along with the islands off it. Isola Palmaria, Tino and Isola del Tinetto lie offshore. May to July is the season, and public transport is poor.

gem:mount-etna.text: Mount Etna is an active volcano in Sicily, Italy, with a national park around it. The Grotta del Gelo and Acireale Cathedral are the sights nearby, and five hours covers a visit. June to August is the season.

SVQ.text: Seville is a large city in Andalusia, southern Spain, and its historic core is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Seville Cathedral and Torre del Oro lead the sights, which run to roughly 17 hours. March to May and October are the best months.

PMO.text: Palermo is a coastal city in Italy, historic and food-minded, with a UNESCO World Heritage Site listing. Palermo Cathedral, Monreale Cathedral and the Palazzo dei Normanni lead, and the sights fill about 17 hours. May and June are the pick of the year.

gem:zermatt.text: Zermatt is a small mountain village in Switzerland, set under the Matterhorn. The Monte Rosa Massif, Breithorn and Klein Matterhorn stand around it, and the sights themselves take about four hours. June to August is the season.

gem:lucerne.text: Lucerne is a small city in Switzerland beside Lake Lucerne. The Lion Monument and Kapellbrucke hold the old town, while Mount Pilatus and Rigi rise close by, and the sights run about ten hours. May to September is the window.

gem:annecy.text: Annecy is a small town in France on Lake Annecy, in the Alps. The Palais de l'Isle and Chateau d'Annecy anchor the old centre, and six hours covers the sights. June to September is the run to aim for.

gem:lake-district.text: The Lake District is a national park of fells and water in the United Kingdom, listed by UNESCO. Windermere draws the crowds while Scafell Pike and Helvellyn pull the walkers, and seven hours barely starts it. June to August is the season.

gem:capri.text: Capri is a small, expensive island off the coast of Italy. The Blue Grotto is the headline, with Villa Jovis and Monte Solaro behind it, and about seven hours covers the main sights. June to August is the season.

MAD.text: Madrid is a big inland city in Spain, strong on art, food and late nights. The Museo del Prado and Reina Sofia lead, the Royal Palace of Madrid is close, and the sights run to about 17 hours. May and September are the comfortable months.

MAH.text: Menorca is the quiet one of the Balearic Islands, in Spain, and a UNESCO biosphere reserve. The Cami de Cavalls coast path and the Talati de Dalt stones are the draws, with Cala Mitjana for a swim. June to August is the season.

TFN.text: Tenerife North is the green, northern side of the island in Spain. San Cristobal de La Laguna carries the UNESCO listing, and the Auditorio de Tenerife and Playa de Las Teresitas round out about ten hours. May to September is the stretch.

ATH.text: Athens spreads out below the Acropolis of Athens in Greece, ancient city and modern one at once. The Parthenon leads, with the Theatre of Dionysus and Daphni Monastery behind it, and the sights add up to about 17 hours. April and May are best.

BOD.text: Bordeaux is a wine city in southwest France, its centre a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Bordeaux Cathedral and the Musee des Beaux-Arts de Bordeaux head the list, and ten hours covers the place on foot. May to September is the long season.

OHD.text: Ohrid is an old town on Lake Ohrid in North Macedonia and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Ancient Theatre of Ohrid and the cliff church at Kaneo lead, and six hours covers the old quarter. May and June are the best months.

gem:cesky-krumlov.text: Cesky Krumlov is a small medieval town in Czechia and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Cesky Krumlov Castle towers over it, the Egon Schiele Art Centrum is worth an hour, and six hours covers the whole place. May to September is the season.

gem:bled.text: Lake Bled is an alpine lake in Slovenia below the Julian Alps. Bled Island in the middle and Bled Castle on the cliff are the two sights, and seven hours takes in both plus a walk round the shore. May to August is the season.

gem:san-sebastian.text: San Sebastian is a Basque city on the coast in Spain, built around food and a beach. La Concha Beach curves through the middle and Urgull rises at its end, and ten hours covers the city. June to September is the season.

gem:papingo.text: Papingo is a stone village high in the Pindus mountains of Greece. Vikos Gorge and Vikos-Aoos National Park begin at the edge of it, and the village itself takes about two hours. June is the month to come.

gem:pont-du-gard.text: Pont du Gard is a Roman aqueduct bridge in southern France and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The site itself takes about three hours, with the Gorges du Gardon reserve under 10 km away. April, May and September are the best months.

gem:augsburg.text: Augsburg is a historic city in Bavaria, Germany, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Augsburg Cathedral, the Fuggerei almshouses and the Perlachturm lead the way, and the sights run to about 17 hours. May to September is the season.

gem:mannheim.text: Mannheim is a large city in Germany and part of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. The Kunsthalle Mannheim and the Technoseum are the two museums to pick, with Luisenpark for an afternoon. May to September is the season.

gem:bochum.text: Bochum is a former mining city in the Ruhr, Germany, inside a UNESCO Global Geopark. The Schauspielhaus Bochum leads, with the Zeiss Planetarium Bochum and Haus Kemnade after it. May to September is the season.

gem:koln.text: Koln is a big city on the Rhine in Germany, built around its cathedral. Cologne Cathedral is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the first stop, with Museum Ludwig and the Hohenzollern Bridge beside it. May to September is the season.

IBZ.text: Ibiza is a Balearic island in Spain with two faces, clubs after dark and quiet coves by day. Ibiza Cathedral sits above the old town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and Cala Salada is the beach to find. May to August is the season.

BER.text: Berlin is a sprawling, unpolished capital in Germany where history sits in the open. The Brandenburg Gate, Reichstag Building and Museum Island are the first round, and the sights run to about 17 hours. May to September is the season.

NCE.text: Nice is a large coastal city in France and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Nice Cathedral and the Musee des Beaux-Arts Jules Cheret lead, with the Opera de Nice for an evening. June to August is the season.

KEF.text: Reykjavik is a small, low-rise capital in Iceland and the base for most trips into the country. Hallgrimskirkja marks the skyline, the National Museum of Iceland fills a morning, and ten hours covers the city. June and July are the best months.

MLA.text: Malta is a small island state in the Mediterranean, dense with fortified towns. Valletta and Mdina lead, with Comino for the water, and about seven hours of sights in all. May to August is the season.

gem:mont-saint-michel.text: Mont-Saint-Michel is an abbey on a rocky island off the coast of France, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Mont-Saint-Michel Abbey is the whole visit, and about four hours covers the rock and the walls. June to September is the season.

gem:bonifacio.text: Bonifacio is a fortress town in Corsica, France, perched above a narrow harbour. The Eglise Saint-Dominique and the boat out to the Lavezzi Islands are the two things to do, and three hours covers the old town. May to August is the season.

gem:cefalu.text: Cefalu is a small beach town in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Cefalu Cathedral is the one big sight, the Museo Mandralisca the small one, and four hours covers both with time on the sand. May is the month to come.

gem:giants-causeway.text: Giant's Causeway is a stretch of basalt columns on the coast of Northern Ireland and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The site takes about two hours, and Dunluce Castle and the Carrick-a-Rede Rope Bridge fill the day. June to August is the season.

CCF.text: Carcassonne is a walled medieval town in southern France and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Cite de Carcassonne holds the ramparts and Carcassonne Cathedral, and six hours covers the whole circuit. May, June and September are the best months.

BUD.text: Budapest is a big riverside city in Hungary, known for thermal baths and a long night. The Hungarian Parliament Building and Buda Castle lead, the Szechenyi Chain Bridge links them, and the sights run to about 17 hours. April to June is best.

INN.text: Innsbruck is an alpine city in Austria, hemmed in by mountains on both sides. The Golden Roof marks the old town, with Schloss Ambras and the Bergisel above it, and ten hours covers the lot. May to September is the season.

LJU.text: Ljubljana is a small, walkable city in Slovenia built along a river and under a castle hill. Ljubljana Castle looks down on the Triple Bridge and the Dragon Bridge, and ten hours covers the centre. May to August is the season.

gem:strasbourg.text: Strasbourg is a river city in Alsace, France, with a UNESCO World Heritage Site at its centre. The Cathedral of Our Lady of Strasbourg leads and the Grande Ile around it holds the old streets, and ten hours covers the walk. May to September is best.

gem:chamonix.text: Chamonix is a mountain town in France directly below Mont Blanc. The cable car to the Aiguille du Midi and the train to the Mer de Glace are the two rides that matter, and six hours covers them. June to September is the season.

gem:sintra.text: Sintra is a hill town in Portugal, stacked with royal palaces. The National Palace of Pena and the Castle of the Moors sit on the ridge above, and six hours covers both plus the Convento dos Capuchos. June to September is the season.

gem:plitvice.text: Plitvice Lakes is a national park of linked lakes and waterfalls in Croatia and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The walkways run past Kozjak and the smaller pools, and six hours covers the main circuit. June to August is the season.

gem:hvar.text: Hvar is a long island in Croatia, known for lavender and late nights. Zlatni Rat and Stiniva are the beaches to aim for, with Grapceva cave inland, and five hours covers the town. May to August is the season.

gem:geiranger.text: Geirangerfjord is a UNESCO listed fjord in western Norway. The Seven Sisters waterfall and the Dalsnibba viewpoint lead the list; allow about 6 hours. July and August are the season, and public transport is poor.

gem:visby.text: Visby is a walled medieval town on the island of Gotland, Sweden, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Sankta Maria domkyrka and the old ruins fill about 7 hours of sightseeing. July and August are the season.

gem:san-gimignano.text: San Gimignano is a small walled town in the Tuscan hills, known for the towers over its UNESCO listed historic centre. Torre Grossa gives the best climb, and about 4 hours covers the place. May, June and September are the pick.

gem:golden-circle.text: The Golden Circle is a short touring loop through the volcanic country of Iceland, built around a national park. Thingvellir and Oxararfoss lead the stops, with Thingvallavatn alongside; about 5 hours. June and July are the best months.

gem:skocjan-caves.text: Skocjan Caves is a UNESCO listed cave system in the karst country of Slovenia. Postojna Cave and Predjama Castle sit within reach, and about 7 hours covers the main round. June, July and August are the best months.

gem:ordesa.text: Ordesa y Monte Perdido National Park protects high limestone country in the Pyrenees of Spain, listed by UNESCO. Monte Perdido and the Cirque de Gavarnie lead, with about 7 hours of walking on offer. July and August are the season.

gem:calanques-de-piana.text: Sea cliffs and coves make up the Calanques de Piana, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Scandola Nature Reserve lies along the same coast and Monte Cinto rises inland; about 5 hours covers it. June to August is the window.

gem:skellig-michael.text: Skellig Michael is a steep rock island off the coast of Ireland, listed by UNESCO. The boat trip also passes Little Skellig, and the visit runs about 4 hours. June to September is the only reliable window, and the sea decides the day.

PMI.text: Palma is the port city of Mallorca, a historic core wrapped in beach resorts. Palma Cathedral and Bellver Castle lead the sights, and the full list runs to about 17 hours. May to July is the best stretch.

FNC.text: Funchal sits on the south coast of Madeira, a harbour city that doubles as the base for the island's mountains. Madeira Botanical Garden and the climb to Pico Ruivo are the draws, about 7 hours of them. May to September is the long season.

CHQ.text: Chania is the port town of western Crete, with a tight old quarter behind the harbour. The Nautical Museum of Crete and Etz Hayyim Synagogue sit inside it; about 9 hours covers the town. April to June and September are best.

TLL.text: Medieval walls and a UNESCO listed old town make Tallinn the set piece of the Baltic coast. Toompea Castle, Alexander Nevsky Cathedral and Kadriorg Palace lead a list worth about 17 hours. July and August are warmest, and public transport is excellent.

BRN.text: Bern holds the Federal Palace of Switzerland inside a UNESCO listed old town. The Zytglogge clock tower and Zentrum Paul Klee are the two to fix on, with about 10 hours of sights in all. June to September is the good stretch.

gem:neuschwanstein.text: Neuschwanstein Castle rises over a valley in the Alps of southern Germany, the fairytale model of a castle. Hohenschwangau Castle sits just below and Wieskirche is nearby; allow about 6 hours. June to August is the season.

gem:grindelwald.text: Grindelwald sits in a valley under the Eiger, in the Alps of Switzerland. The lifts run up toward Jungfrau and Bachalpsee makes the classic walk; about 4 hours of sights. June to August is the window.

gem:provence-luberon.text: The Luberon is a run of hill villages in Provence, best known for lavender and stone. Senanque Abbey is the set piece, with Goult and Joucas for quiet lanes; about 3 hours of formal sights. May, June and September are the months to come.

gem:assisi.text: Assisi climbs a hillside in central Italy, a quiet medieval town shaped by pilgrimage. The Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi leads, with Rocca Maggiore above the roofs; about 4 hours covers it. May and June are the months.

gem:theth.text: Theth is a remote village in the Albanian Alps, set inside a national park. Valbone Valley National Park and Maja Jezerce rise around it, and about 6 hours covers the local sights. June to August is the season.

gem:arles.text: Arles keeps a set of Roman remains inside a UNESCO listed town in Provence. The Arles Amphitheatre is the centrepiece, and Musee Reattu and Museon Arlaten hold the art; about 10 hours in all. May, June and August work best.

gem:les-baux-de-provence.text: A medieval village perched above the Alpilles, Les Baux-de-Provence is one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Chateau des Baux crowns the rock and Glanum lies below; about 4 hours. May to August is the stretch.

gem:mount-olympus.text: Mount Olympus is a national park of high ridges in Greece, with Mytikas the summit that draws walkers. Ancient Dion and Agia Triada Monastery sit at the foot, and the marked sights take about 2 hours. June to August is the season for the climb.

gem:tre-cime-di-lavaredo.text: Tre Cime di Lavaredo is a set of sheer rock towers in the Alps of Italy. Lago di Misurina and Monte Cristallo fill the same valley, and about 7 hours covers the loop and the views. June to August is the season.

gem:la-gomera.text: La Gomera is a small, steep island in the Canary group, with a national park across its high centre. Garajonay National Park holds the UNESCO listing, and Roque de Agando and Torre del Conde round out about 5 hours. June to September suits.

SCQ.text: The pilgrim routes across Spain end at Santiago de Compostela, a compact stone city with a UNESCO listed core. The Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela and Glory's Portico lead, within about 10 hours of sights. June to September is the best stretch.

JMK.text: Mykonos is the party island of the Cyclades, where beaches and nightlife carry the summer. The boat to the ruins on Delos is the one fixed excursion, and about 7 hours covers the sights. May to September is the season.

FAE.text: Vagar is a thinly settled island in the Faroe Islands, open to the ocean on every side. Sorvagsvatn and Mykines are the draws, and about 6 hours covers the island. June to August is the window.

gem:garda.text: Lake Garda sits between the Alps and the plain in northern Italy, a family lake with villages along both shores. Gargnano and Isola del Garda are the quiet end, Gardaland the loud one; about 7 hours. April to June and September are best.

gem:ravenna.text: Ravenna holds Byzantine mosaics inside plain brick churches, a quiet city in Emilia-Romagna. Basilica di San Vitale and the Mausoleum of Galla Placidia lead the UNESCO list, and about 10 hours covers them. May to August is the stretch.

gem:urbino.text: Urbino is a Renaissance hill town in the Marche, small enough to walk in an afternoon. Galleria Nazionale delle Marche holds the paintings and the Cathedral of Urbino stands next to it; about 4 hours covers the town. May and June are the pick.

gem:cordoba.text: Cordoba is a city in Andalusia built around one extraordinary building. The Mosque-Cathedral of Cordoba is that building, and Madinat Al-Zahra lies outside town; about 17 hours of sights. April and May are the months.

gem:douro.text: The Douro Valley is a UNESCO listed wine landscape in northern Portugal, vineyards terraced above the river. Alto Douro Wine Region and Mateus Palace are the fixed stops, and about 5 hours covers them. May and June are the months to come.

gem:lofoten.text: The Lofoten Islands run out into the Arctic off northern Norway, sharp peaks rising straight from the sea. Reinebringen is the climb to make and the Lofotr Viking Museum covers the history; about 4 hours. July and August have the light.

gem:bergen-nearby.text: Sognefjord reaches far inland from the coast of Norway, its side arms narrowing to walls of rock. Hopperstad stavkyrkje and Hove kyrkje stand in the villages along it, and the listed sights take about 2 hours. July and August are the season.

gem:rila.text: Rila Monastery sits deep in the mountains of Bulgaria, a UNESCO listed complex in a wooded valley. Rila National Park climbs behind it toward Musala, and about 6 hours covers a visit. June to September is the window.

gem:curonian-spit.text: The Curonian Spit is a long sand peninsula off the coast of Lithuania, half forest and half dune, protected as a national park. Parnidis dune and the Dancing Forest sit near Nida, and about 3 hours covers them. June to August is the season.

gem:tropea.text: Tropea is a small coast town in Calabria, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, with beaches under its old centre. The set sights run to only about 2 hours, so the time goes on the sand. May to August is the season.

gem:cadiz.text: Cadiz is an old port city on the Andalusia coast, with beaches at the edge of the historic centre. Cadiz Cathedral and Torre Tavira give the views, and the sight list runs to about 10 hours. May to July and September are best.

gem:guimaraes.text: Guimaraes is a medieval town in northern Portugal with a UNESCO listed centre below its castle. The Castle of Guimaraes and the Palace of the Dukes of Braganza stand at the top of town, about 6 hours in all. May and June are the pick.

gem:soller.text: Soller sits in a bowl of the Serra de Tramuntana on Mallorca, with Port de Soller down at the water. Puig Major rises behind the town and the old centre is listed; about 7 hours of sights. May to August is the stretch.

gem:sarlat-la-caneda.text: Sarlat-la-Caneda is a medieval town in the Dordogne, as much about the market and the food as the buildings. Sarlat Cathedral anchors the centre, and Chateau de Beynac and Jardins de Marqueyssac are short drives; about 6 hours. May to September works.

gem:moustiers-sainte-marie.text: Moustiers-Sainte-Marie is a small village in the French Prealps, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Lake of Sainte-Croix and the Plateau de Valensole lie close by, and three hours covers the village. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:lucca.text: Lucca sits in Tuscany, a historic town holding about ten hours of sights. Lucca Cathedral, Piazza Anfiteatro and San Michele in Foro lead, with the Museo Nazionale di Palazzo Mansi for a quieter hour. May, June and September are the best months.

gem:berchtesgaden.text: Berchtesgaden is a small mountain town in Bavaria, hard against the Austrian border. Konigssee is the draw, with Nationalpark Berchtesgaden and the Jenner ridge behind it, and about four hours covers the town. May to September is the season.

gem:mantua.text: Mantua is a UNESCO World Heritage Site town in Lombardy, with the Parco del Mincio close by. Palazzo Te and the Basilica of Sant'Andrea lead, and six hours covers the centre. April, May and September are the pick.

gem:ortisei.text: Ortisei is an alpine village in Val Gardena, Italy, with trails and ski runs on its doorstep. The Seiser Alm, Sassolungo and the Sella Pass all sit within reach, and the village itself takes about four hours. June to August is the window.

gem:ferrara.text: Ferrara sits in Italy and carries UNESCO World Heritage Site status for its old centre. Este Castle leads, with Palazzo Schifanoia and Palazzo dei Diamanti close behind, and ten hours covers the lot. April to June and September suit best.

gem:padua.text: Padua is a university city in the Veneto, an easy hop from Venice. The Scrovegni Chapel leads, with the Basilica of Saint Anthony of Padua and the Orto Botanico di Padova filling out ten hours. April to June and September work well.

gem:picos-de-europa.text: The Picos de Europa are a mountain range in Spain, protected as a national park and a UNESCO Man and the Biosphere reserve. Picu Urriellu and Torre Cerredo pull the climbers, Lake Ercina the walkers. July and August are the reliable months.

gem:el-escorial.text: San Lorenzo de El Escorial is a small town in Spain built around one huge monastery. The Real Monasterio de San Lorenzo de El Escorial takes most of a visit, with the Valley of the Fallen and Mount Abantos nearby. May, June and September are best.

HAM.text: Hamburg is a port city in Germany with a UNESCO World Heritage Site warehouse quarter. The Speicherstadt and the Elbe Philharmonic Hall lead, the Hamburger Kunsthalle covers the art, and seventeen hours of sights means two days. May to August is the season.

GDN.text: Gdansk is a Baltic port in northern Poland with a rebuilt merchant old town. The Museum of the Second World War and Westerplatte carry the history, Green Gate and Artus Court the streetscape. June to August brings the beach weather.

RIX.text: Riga is a medieval old town turned capital city on the Daugava, in Latvia. Riga Cathedral, Riga Castle and the Freedom Monument sit within a short walk, and seventeen hours of sights suggests two days. June to August is the warm stretch.

gem:heidelberg.text: Heidelberg is a castle town on the Neckar in Germany, and the country's oldest university is here. Heidelberg Castle looms above the old streets, and with Schloss Schwetzingen there are about ten hours of sights. May to September is the run.

gem:avignon.text: Avignon sits on the Rhone in Provence, a UNESCO World Heritage Site centre in France. The Palais des Papes and Pont Saint-Benezet lead, with Avignon Cathedral nearby, and ten hours covers the old town. April, May and September are the pick.

gem:segovia.text: Segovia, in Castile and Leon, carries UNESCO World Heritage Site status for its old town. The Aqueduct of Segovia and the Alcazar of Segovia bracket it, with Catedral de Segovia between, and ten hours covers the city. May, June and September suit.

gem:albarracin.text: Albarracin is a medieval village of about a thousand people in Teruel, Aragon. Castillo de Albarracin and Catedral del Salvador fill most of a three hour stop, and the Pinares de Rodeno nearby draw climbers. May, June and September are best.

gem:quedlinburg.text: Quedlinburg sits in Saxony-Anhalt below the Harz Mountains, a medieval town on the UNESCO World Heritage Site list. Quedlinburg Abbey and its Stiftskirche lead the way, and six hours covers the whole town. May to September is the stretch.

gem:durmitor.text: Durmitor is a mountain area in Montenegro built around Durmitor National Park. Black Lake is the easy walk, Bobotov Kuk the hard climb, and the Tara River Canyon cuts in alongside. July and August are the dependable months.

gem:riquewihr.text: Riquewihr is a medieval wine village in Alsace, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The lanes carry half-timbered houses, Chateau de Saint-Ulrich sits in the hills above, and four hours covers it. May to September is the season.

gem:noto.text: Noto is a baroque town in Sicily, Italy, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Noto Cathedral and Palazzo Ducezio line the main street, with Noto Antica and Calamosche beach a short drive out. April and May are the best months.

gem:flam.text: Flam is a fjord village at the head of the Aurlandsfjord in Norway. The Stegastein viewpoint looks down the water, Undredal Stave Church sits along the shore, and five hours covers the area. June to August is the season.

gem:durham.text: Durham is a small cathedral and university city in the United Kingdom. Durham Cathedral and Durham Castle together form a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and six hours covers the pair. June to August is the best window.

gem:canterbury.text: Canterbury is a medieval cathedral city in the United Kingdom. Canterbury Cathedral, St Augustine's Abbey and St Martin's Church make up the UNESCO World Heritage Site, and ten hours covers them and the old streets. July and August are warmest.

gem:formentera.text: Formentera is a low, sandy island in Spain, the southernmost of the Balearic Islands. Platja de Migjorn and Platja de Llevant are the long beaches, Cala Saona Beach the small one, and six hours covers the sights. June to August is the season.

gem:malbork.text: Malbork is a small town in Poland built around one enormous fortress. Malbork Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, takes most of a six hour visit, with the Old Town Hall of Malbork after that. May to September is the stretch.

gem:potsdam.text: Potsdam is a city of palaces and lakes on the edge of Berlin. Sanssouci Palace carries the UNESCO World Heritage Site listing, with Glienicke Bridge and Filmpark Babelsberg after it. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:grossglockner-road.text: The Grossglockner High Alpine Road runs through the Nationalpark Hohe Tauern in Austria. Grossglockner and the Pasterze Glacier are the reason to drive it, with a stop at Fuscher Torl, and seven hours is realistic. June to August is the window.

gem:tivoli.text: Tivoli is a Roman town in Lazio with two extraordinary villas. Hadrian's Villa and Villa d'Este each deserve half a day, so six hours is about the minimum. May, June and September work best.

gem:lipari-aeolian.text: Lipari is an island in the Aeolian Islands, a volcanic group off Italy and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Vulcano, Salina, Panarea and Stromboli all sit within reach, and six hours covers Lipari itself. May to August is the season.

gem:morskie-oko.text: Morskie Oko is a mountain lake in the Tatra Mountains of Poland, reached on foot. The walk in and back takes about four hours, with Rysy rising straight behind the water. July and August are the reliable months.

gem:pico-do-arieiro.text: Pico do Arieiro is a high summit on Madeira Island in Portugal, reached by road. The ridge walk across Pico das Torres to Pico Ruivo is the main event and takes about three hours. July to September is the season.

gem:versailles.text: Versailles is a town just west of Paris, and everything turns on one palace. The Palace of Versailles and its gardens fill a long day, with Chateau de Saint-Cloud and Chateau de Malmaison nearby. June to September is the best run.

gem:rodos.text: Rodos is a historic port city in Greece, with the Medieval City of Rhodes at its core as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Palace of the Grand Master of the Knights of Rhodes leads, and nine hours covers it. May and June are best.

gem:bayreuth.text: Bayreuth is a quiet baroque city in Upper Franconia that wakes for the Richard Wagner Festival. The Margravial Opera House is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and Haus Wahnfried and the Bayreuth Festival Theatre follow. June to September is the stretch.

gem:darmstadt.text: Darmstadt sits south of Frankfurt in Hesse and trades on Jugendstil architecture. The Artists' Colony in Darmstadt is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with the Hessian State Museum Darmstadt after it. May to September is the stretch.

gem:koblenz.text: Koblenz opens the Upper Middle Rhine Valley in Rhineland-Palatinate, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Deutsches Eck sits at the confluence, Ehrenbreitstein Fortress looks down from above, and ten hours covers the city. May to September is the season.

gem:bourges.text: Bourges is a cathedral city in Centre-Val de Loire, France. Bourges Cathedral is the UNESCO World Heritage Site and the reason most people come, with Palais Jacques-Coeur close behind, and nine hours covers the centre. May to September is the season.

gem:pesaro.text: Pesaro is a coastal city in Italy and part of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. Casa Rossini and the Arch of Augustus anchor the old centre, Spiaggia di Pesaro takes everyone else, and eight hours covers it. June to August is the season.

gem:dessau.text: Dessau is a city in Saxony-Anhalt where modern design meets landscape gardens. Bauhaus Dessau is the UNESCO World Heritage Site draw, with the Dessau-Worlitz Garden Realm and Schloss Luisium filling out ten hours. May to September is the stretch.

gem:gdynia.text: Gdynia is a modern port in northern Poland, part of the Tricity alongside Gdansk and Sopot. The tall ship Dar Pomorza is moored on the waterfront, Sea Towers rises behind it, and ten hours covers the city. June to August is the season.

gem:hildesheim.text: Hildesheim is a UNESCO listed cathedral city in Germany. Hildesheim Cathedral and the Roemer- und Pelizaeus-Museum lead, and the churches around them fill a day. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:alcala-de-henares.text: Alcala de Henares, a UNESCO listed city in Spain, packs its old centre with colleges and churches. The Museo Casa Natal de Cervantes and the Archbishop's Palace lead, and the whole thing fills a day. April, May and September suit best.

gem:speyer.text: Speyer is a small cathedral city in Germany, on the UNESCO World Heritage list. Speyer Cathedral is the draw, with the Technik Museum Speyer and the Historisches Museum der Pfalz filling out a full day. May to September is the season.

gem:almeria.text: Almeria is a coastal city in Spain with a big fortress above the old centre. The Alcazaba y Murallas del Cerro de San Cristobal comes first, then the Museo de Almeria. March to May and October are the kind months.

gem:melilla.text: Melilla is a small Spanish coastal town in North Africa. Melilla la Vieja leads, followed by the Conventico Caves and the Melilla Museum. May to August is the season.

gem:liege.text: Liege is a working city in Belgium with a deep stock of churches and palaces. The Prince-Bishops' Palace and Liege Cathedral lead, and the Opera Royal de Wallonie is worth an evening. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:el-puerto-de-santa-maria.text: El Puerto de Santa Maria is a coastal town in Spain within reach of Cadiz. Cadiz Cathedral and the Monument to the Constitution of 1812 lead, and Playa de Valdelagrana is the local beach. May to September works.

gem:aranjuez.text: Aranjuez is a small UNESCO listed palace town in Spain. The Royal Palace of Aranjuez takes most of a day, with the Casa del Labrador and the Convento de San Pascual nearby. April and May are the months to come.

gem:ceuta.text: Ceuta is a Spanish town on the coast of North Africa, ringed by old fortifications. The Royal Walls and the climb up Monte Hacho are the main business, and Playa San Amaro handles the rest. May to August is the season.

gem:elche.text: Elche is a UNESCO listed city in Spain. The Palmeral of Elche leads, with the Santa Maria Basilica of Elche and La Alcudia filling out a day. April and May are the best months.

gem:witten.text: Witten is a city in Germany sitting inside a UNESCO Global Geopark. The German Mining Museum and Hardenstein Castle are the pull, with Hengsteysee and Harkortsee for a day outdoors. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:la-linea-de-la-concepcion.text: La Linea de la Concepcion, a coastal city in Spain, sits right at the Gibraltar border. The big sights are over the line, among them Gorham's Cave, St Michael's Cave and the Ibrahim-al-Ibrahim Mosque. May to September is the season.

gem:viareggio.text: Viareggio is a seaside city in Italy, with the Apuan Alps and Lago di Massaciuccoli in easy reach. Villa Puccini is the pick in town, and the sights add up to about eight hours. May to August is the season.

gem:bergisch-gladbach.text: Bergisch Gladbach, a city in Germany, holds about a day of sights. Schloss Bensberg is the set piece, with Monte Troodeloh, Tutberg and the Altes Rathaus Bergisch Gladbach after it. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:bremerhaven.text: Bremerhaven is a harbour city in Germany. The German Emigration Center and the Klimahaus Bremerhaven are the two to plan around, with Wilhelm Bauer and the Deutsches Auswandererhaus nearby. June to August is the season.

gem:kolding.text: Kolding is a coastal city in Denmark with a castle at its centre. Koldinghus leads, then the Trapholt Museet and the gardens at Geografisk Have. June to August is the season.

gem:paignton.text: Paignton sits on the coast of the United Kingdom inside a UNESCO Global Geopark. Paignton Zoo and Kents Cavern take a day between them, and Goodrington Sands is the beach. June to August is the season.

gem:tarnowskie-gory.text: Tarnowskie Gory is a mining city in Poland whose underground workings carry a UNESCO listing. The Historic Silver Mine in Tarnowskie Gory and the Black Trout Adit are the reason to come. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:leiria.text: Leiria is a city in Portugal with a castle at the heart of it. Leiria Castle and the Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception Cathedral cover the centre in a morning, and Praia da Vieira is the nearest beach. May to July is the window.

gem:vilanova-i-la-geltru.text: Vilanova i la Geltru, on the coast of Spain, keeps a good run of small museums. The Biblioteca Museu Victor Balaguer and the Can Llopis Romanticism Museum lead, with the Catalonia Railway Museum after them. May to August is the season.

gem:asti.text: Asti is a town in Italy with towers and churches packed into a small centre. Asti Cathedral leads, with the Torre Troyana and the Collegiata di San Secondo close by. May, June and September are the months.

gem:aviles.text: Aviles is a coastal city in Spain. Oscar Niemeyer International Cultural Centre draws most of the visitors, with the Palacio de Maqua and Balsera Palace after it. June to September is the season.

gem:ferrol.text: Ferrol is a naval port city in Spain. The Museo Naval and Ferrol Cathedral fill a morning, and the old quarter of Ferrol Vello is worth the walk. June to September is the season.

gem:castellammare-di-stabia.text: Castellammare di Stabia is a coastal town in Italy, and it makes a base for the ruins next door. Pompeii, Stabiae and Oplontis are all within reach, and Mount Vesuvius rises behind them. May to August is the season.

gem:san-fernando.text: San Fernando is a coastal town in Spain, close to Cadiz and its sights. Cadiz Cathedral and the Museum of Cadiz are the pick, and Playa de la Victoria is the beach. May to September works.

gem:hilversum.text: Hilversum is a town in the Netherlands known for its broadcasting studios. The Netherlands Institute for Sound and Vision and AVRO Studios tell that story, with Soestdijk Palace nearby. June to August is the season.

gem:saint-quentin.text: Saint-Quentin is a city in France on the UNESCO World Heritage list. Basilica of Saint-Quentin and the Hotel de ville de Saint-Quentin are the two to see, with the Canal de Saint-Quentin for a walk. June to September is the season.

gem:algeciras.text: Algeciras is a ferry port on the coast of Spain. The boats to Morocco take most of the traffic, but Gorham's Cave, the Moorish Castle and the Ibrahim-al-Ibrahim Mosque reward a stop. May to September is the season.

gem:mataro.text: Mataro is a coastal city in Spain. Nau Gaudi and Casa Coll i Regas lead, with the Basilica de Santa Maria de Mataro and Casa Puig i Cadafalch in the old centre. May to July is the window.

gem:bergen-op-zoom.text: Bergen op Zoom, a city in the Netherlands, is built around the Markiezenhof. The Sint-Gertrudiskerk, the Gevangenpoort and the Stadhuis van Bergen op Zoom fill out the old centre. June to September is the season.

gem:santa-cruz-de-tenerife.text: Santa Cruz de Tenerife is a historic town in Spain. Auditorio de Tenerife and the Museo de la Naturaleza y el Hombre lead, with San Cristobal de La Laguna and its cathedral nearby. April to September is the window.

EFL.text: Kefalonia is an island in Greece where buses are thin on the ground and a car pays off. Melissani Cave and Myrtos Beach are the draws, with Mount Ainos for a climb. May to July is the window.

CPH.text: Copenhagen is a large, walkable city in Denmark with about seventeen hours of sights in it. Amalienborg, Rosenborg Castle and Freetown Christiania make the core, and transport is excellent. June to August is the season.

VNO.text: Vilnius is a baroque city in Lithuania with a UNESCO listed old town. Vilnius Cathedral, the Gate of Dawn and the Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania lead, and Uzupis is the offbeat corner. May to August is the season.

gem:bohinj.text: Lake Bohinj is a quiet alpine lake in Slovenia on the edge of Triglav National Park. Triglav and the Julian Alps rise around it, and Lake Bled is an easy side trip. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:delphi.text: Delphi is a village in Greece set on the slopes of Mount Parnassus. Ancient Delphi, the Temple of Apollo in Delphi and the Charioteer of Delphi take about half a day between them. May, June and September are the months.

gem:naxos.text: Naxos is a large, quiet island in Greece. Mikri Vigla is the beach to aim for, the Archaeological Museum of Naxos fills a rainy hour, and Paros is a short hop away. May to September is the window.

gem:milos.text: Milos is a volcanic island in Greece where the coast does most of the work. Sarakiniko Beach and Firiplaka are the pick, with Kimolos and Polyaigos offshore. May to September is the window.

gem:killarney.text: Killarney, a town in Ireland, sits at the gate of its national park. Ross Castle, Muckross House and Muckross Abbey are inside Killarney National Park, with Lough Leane and MacGillycuddy's Reeks beyond. June to August is the season.

gem:soca-valley.text: Soca Valley is a mountain valley in Slovenia, cut through the Julian Alps. Bovec is the base for hiking, and Triglav National Park and Mangart fill the skyline above. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:nafplio.text: The fortress town of Nafplio sits on the Peloponnese coast in Greece, with Palamidi above it and Bourtzi out in the bay. Set aside 5 hours for the forts and for Tiryns nearby. April and May are the best months, and Karathona beach is close.

gem:mdina.text: Mdina is a walled medieval town on Malta, quiet behind its gates and home to barely 193 people. The cathedral anchors a 4 hour wander through the alleys. June to August is the season, and buses from the coast are easy.

gem:caceres.text: Caceres wears its medieval walls well, a UNESCO listed city in Spain where stone towers rise over the plazas. Torre de Bujaco and the cathedral fill much of a 10 hour visit. May is the month to come.

gem:albi.text: The red brick cathedral of Albi towers over this small city in France, with the Palais de la Berbie and the Musee Toulouse-Lautrec next door. Set aside 9 hours. May, June and September are the pick of the year.

gem:conques.text: Conques is a stone village of 811 people in France, wrapped around the Abbey Church of Saint Foy. The sights take about 3 hours, and with transport this poor a car helps. June to September is the window.

gem:kandersteg.text: Kandersteg is a mountain village in Switzerland, a base for walkers heading up to Oeschinen Lake and the peaks around it. The walking is the point, and 3 hours covers the rest. June to August is prime.

gem:ragusa.text: The baroque city of Ragusa climbs two hillsides in Sicily, Italy, with stairways linking the Duomo of San Giorgio to Santa Maria delle Scale. Set aside 10 hours for the full walk. May is the best month to come.

gem:weimar.text: Weimar is a small city in Germany with outsized cultural weight, from the Herzogin Anna Amalia Bibliothek to the Bauhaus University. Buchenwald concentration camp sits on its edge. The sights run to 10 hours, best from May to September.

gem:glencoe.text: Glen Coe is a mountain valley in the Scottish Highlands, walled by Buachaille Etive Mor and Bidean nam Bian, with Ben Nevis close by. The Pap of Glencoe is the short climb, and 7 hours covers the glen. June to August is the window.

gem:bergamo-alta.text: Bergamo is a walled hill city in Italy, its upper town a UNESCO listed tangle of medieval lanes above the modern streets below. The sights add up to about 10 hours. May to September is the best spread.

gem:saint-cirq-lapopie.text: Saint-Cirq-Lapopie is a cliff village of 778 people in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The village takes 3 hours; Pech Merle cave and Cahors Cathedral fill the rest of a day. May to September is the run.

gem:mystras.text: The Byzantine ruins of Mystras spill down a hillside below Taygetus, in the Peloponnese of Greece. The archaeological site takes about 3 hours, with the Pantanassa Monastery still in use. April and May are the months for it.

gem:reggia-di-caserta.text: The Royal Palace of Caserta is why people stop in this city in Italy, a baroque spread of state rooms and long formal gardens. The palace and the old hill town of Casertavecchia fill 10 hours. May, June and September suit best.

gem:bialowieza.text: Bialowieza Forest is the last big stretch of old growth woodland in Poland, protected as a national park and listed by UNESCO. The village itself takes 3 hours; the forest takes longer. May to August is the season.

gem:seven-rila-lakes.text: The Seven Rila Lakes lie high in the Rila mountains of Bulgaria, a chain of glacial pools linked by one long day on foot. The walk runs about 6 hours. July and August are the reliable months, and Rila Monastery is worth adding.

gem:cies-islands.text: The Cies Islands guard the mouth of the Ria de Vigo in Spain, protected as part of the Atlantic Islands of Galicia National Park. A day trip runs about 5 hours of walking and beach time. June to August is the only real season.

gem:bru-na-boinne.text: Newgrange is a prehistoric passage tomb in Ireland, the centrepiece of the Bru na Boinne group alongside Knowth. Add the Hill of Tara and 6 hours goes quickly. June to August is the best time, though getting here without a car is hard.

gem:gijon.text: Gijon is a big working port with a beach in the middle of it, out on the Asturias coast of Spain. The Palacio de Revillagigedo and the Museum of the Asturian People carry the sightseeing, about 10 hours of it. June to September is warmest.

gem:le-havre.text: The centre of Le Havre was rebuilt in concrete, and that reconstruction is what earned the city its UNESCO listing. The MuMa Museum of modern art and the Maison de l'Armateur lead 10 hours of sights. June to August is the time.

gem:lorca.text: A castle on the ridge watches over Lorca, an inland city in Spain with baroque churches and the Palacio de Guevara in its streets. The Colegiata de San Patricio is the other stop, and 7 hours covers both. April and May are the months.

VLC.text: Valencia pairs a medieval core with the white curves of the City of Arts and Sciences, out on the coast of Spain. The cathedral, the Torres de Quart and Malvarrosa Beach fill about 17 hours of sights. March to May is ideal.

LYS.text: Lyon is the food capital of France, and the old quarter of Vieux Lyon sits under the Basilica of Notre-Dame de Fourviere. Add the parc de la Tete d'Or and the sights run to 17 hours. May to September is the long good spell.

ARN.text: Stockholm spreads over islands where Lake Malaren meets the Baltic, the capital of Sweden and its largest city. Stockholm Palace and Skogskyrkogarden lead 17 hours of sights, with excellent transport between them. June to August is the season.

NYO.text: Stockholm spreads over islands where Lake Malaren meets the Baltic, the capital of Sweden and its largest city. Stockholm Palace and Skogskyrkogarden lead 17 hours of sights, with excellent transport between them. June to August is the season.

BMA.text: Stockholm spreads over islands where Lake Malaren meets the Baltic, the capital of Sweden and its largest city. Stockholm Palace and Skogskyrkogarden lead 17 hours of sights, with excellent transport between them. June to August is the season.

gem:utrecht.text: Utrecht is a canal city in the Netherlands with a big student population and the UNESCO listed Rietveld Schroder House on its edge. Museum Speelklok and the cathedral tower fill out 17 hours of sights. June to August is the best window.

gem:regensburg.text: Regensburg sits where the Danube turns in Bavaria, Germany, its medieval centre listed by UNESCO and crossed by the old Stone Bridge. The cathedral and Walhalla memorial round out 8 hours. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:garmisch.text: Garmisch-Partenkirchen sits under the Zugspitze in Bavaria, Germany, a winter sports town that works just as well for summer walking. Eibsee, Linderhof Palace and the Alpspitze fill about 6 hours. June to September is the green season.

gem:portofino.text: Portofino is a harbour of 406 people on the Liguria coast of Italy, better known for the yachts than for anything ashore. Castello Brown looks down on it, and the Christ of the Abyss sits offshore. May, June and September are best.

gem:colmar.text: Colmar is a wine town in Alsace, France, with a well kept old quarter of timbered houses like the Maison Pfister. The Unterlinden Museum and the musee Bartholdi round out about 10 hours. May to September is the stretch to pick.

gem:salamanca.text: Salamanca is a university city in Spain with a UNESCO listed centre and two cathedrals, old and new, joined side by side. The Casa de las Conchas and the Convento de San Esteban follow, 10 hours in all. May, June and September are the picks.

gem:gjirokaster.text: Gjirokaster stacks stone roofed houses up a steep hillside in southern Albania, under a long grey castle on the ridge. The Zekate House and the Ethnographic Museum are the two to enter, and 6 hours does it. May and June are the months.

gem:oxford.text: Oxford is a college city west of London in the United Kingdom, where the Radcliffe Camera and the Bodleian Library stand a minute apart. Add the Ashmolean Museum and Magdalen College for 10 hours of sights. June to September is the best run.

gem:isle-of-skye.text: The Isle of Skye lies off the coast of Scotland, a rugged island of ridges where Sgurr Alasdair and The Storr pull the walkers. The roads are slow, and 6 hours barely scratches it. June to August is the season.

gem:rovinj.text: Rovinj is a pastel fishing town on the Istria coast of Croatia, its old quarter packed onto a peninsula below the tower of Euphemia's Basilica. The lanes and Balbi's Arch take about 4 hours. May to July is the sweet spot.

gem:lubeck.text: Lubeck is a brick gothic port on the Baltic in Germany, still entered through the old Holstentor gate. The Buddenbrookhaus and the Heiligen-Geist-Hospital fill out 10 hours of sights. June to August is the best time.

gem:lago-maggiore.text: Lago Maggiore is a long lake in northern Italy, with the Eremo di Santa Caterina del Sasso clinging to the rock above the water. The climb up Mottarone gives the view down it. May to September is the season.

gem:tarragona.text: Tarragona was the Roman city of Tarraco, and those ruins are what earned it a UNESCO listing. The colonial forum and the cathedral lead a 10 hour list, with a beach below the old town. May to July is the pick, and PortAventura is close.

gem:collioure.text: Collioure is a fishing village in France where the Pyrenees meet the sea, built around the Chateau Royal and the bell tower of Notre-Dame-des-Anges. The village and its beaches take about 4 hours. May to August is the run.

gem:eguisheim.text: Eguisheim is a wine village in Alsace, France, listed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France and home to some 1543 people. The lanes take about 4 hours to work through. Colmar is next door, and May to September is the season.

gem:trier.text: Trier wears its Roman past openly, a walled Germany river city and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Porta Nigra leads, with the Cathedral of Trier and Liebfrauenkirche behind it. Ten hours covers the sights; May to September is the best stretch.

gem:modena.text: Modena, in Italy, puts a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a serious food reputation in one compact centre. The Ghirlandina and Duomo di Modena lead, with Galleria Estense next. Ten hours covers it, and April, May and September are the best months.

gem:torun.text: Torun is a Gothic brick town in Poland, its medieval core on the UNESCO World Heritage Site list. The Leaning Tower of Torun, Torun Castle and the Old Town Hall hold the centre. Ten hours covers it, and May to September is the season.

gem:kromeriz.text: Kromeriz is a small Baroque town in Czechia, built around a castle and its gardens and listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Kromeriz Castle and the Podzamecka zahrada take up most of a visit. Six hours is about right, May to September.

gem:reims.text: Reims is a Gothic cathedral city in France, and the coronation church is why most people come. Reims Cathedral leads, with the Palais du Tau and Basilique Saint-Remi beside it. Ten hours covers the centre; May to September is the window.

gem:sorrento.text: Sorrento is a coast town in Italy, small enough to walk and set up for trips out. Piazza Tasso is the hub, with Capri and Villa Jovis a boat ride away. Six hours covers the town itself, and May to August is the peak.

gem:vicenza.text: Vicenza is a Renaissance city in Italy whose villas and civic buildings carry UNESCO World Heritage Site status. Teatro Olimpico and the Basilica Palladiana anchor the centre, with Villa Capra a little way out. Ten hours covers it, April to October.

gem:chartres.text: Chartres, in France, is a town that lives around one Gothic cathedral on the UNESCO World Heritage Site list. Notre-Dame de Chartres and its glass are the draw, with the Musee des Beaux-Arts nearby. Six hours is enough, best June to September.

gem:helsingor.text: Helsingor is a coastal town in Denmark with a castle on the UNESCO World Heritage Site list. Kronborg Castle takes top billing; the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art is the other reason to come. Six hours is enough, and June to August is the season.

gem:lednice-valtice.text: Lednice-Valtice is a designed landscape of castles, parkland and vineyards in Czechia, on the UNESCO World Heritage Site list. The Minaret in Lednice and the Palava Protected Landscape Area lead, and four hours covers them. May to September is the season.

gem:le-puy-en-velay.text: Le Puy-en-Velay is an old pilgrimage town in France, listed among Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. Le Puy Cathedral and the chapel of Saint Michel d'Aiguilhe lead, with the musee Crozatier after them. Six hours is enough, June to September.

gem:fontainebleau.text: Fontainebleau is a town in France wrapped around a royal palace and its forest, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Palace of Fontainebleau is the main event, and the forest of Fontainebleau fills the rest. Six hours covers both, May to September.

gem:ancient-olympia.text: Ancient Olympia is the ruined games sanctuary of Greece, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in quiet countryside. The Philippeion, Leonidaion and Pelopion stand among the stones, and the museum keeps Hermes and the Infant Dionysus. Six hours is enough, April or May.

gem:orta-san-giulio.text: Orta San Giulio is a small lakeside village in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Basilica di San Giulio sits on an island just offshore, and Mottarone rises behind. The village takes about four hours; June to August is the season.

gem:batalha.text: Batalha, in Portugal, is a village built around one monastery on the UNESCO World Heritage Site list. The Monastery of Batalha is the reason to stop, and Alcobaca Monastery lies a short drive on. The pair takes about three hours, best in May or September.

gem:sete-cidades.text: Sete Cidades is a lake and hiking area on Sao Miguel Island in Portugal. Lagoa das Sete Cidades is the centrepiece, with the Sete Cidades Massif rising around it and Santa Clara Lighthouse on the coast. Six hours covers it; July and August are the months.

gem:montserrat.text: Montserrat is a mountain in Spain with a working monastery on its flank. Santa Maria de Montserrat and the Museum of Montserrat fill most of the four hours here, and trails run into the natural park around it. May to August is best.

gem:aiguestortes.text: Aiguestortes National Park covers lake-strewn high mountains in Spain, with paths linking one tarn to the next. Estany de Contraix, Pic de Peguera and Gran Encantat are the names to know. The walking runs to about seven hours; July and August are reliable.

GRO.text: Girona is a walled medieval city in Spain, listed as a conjunto historico and easy to reach. Catedral de Girona heads the list, with Sant Pere de Galligants and Casa Maso behind it. Ten hours covers the old town; May to August is the stretch.

PDL.text: Ponta Delgada is the main town on Sao Miguel Island in Portugal and the base for its volcanic interior. Lagoa do Fogo, the Sete Cidades Massif and Agua de Pau are the drives worth making. Six hours covers the highlights, June to August.

SBZ.text: Sibiu is a medieval city in Romania and a former European Capital of Culture. The Brukenthal National Museum and the ASTRA National Museum Complex take up most of a day, with Liars Bridge in between. Ten hours covers it, May to September.

gem:antwerp.text: Antwerp is a port city in Belgium built on art and trade. Rubenshuis, the Koninklijk Museum voor Schone Kunsten and the Plantin-Moretus complex are the core, with Het Steen on the water. Two days suits it better than one, May to September.

gem:st-moritz.text: St Moritz is a high resort village in Switzerland, known for skiing and for the lakes below it. Piz Nair and Muottas Muragl give the views, and the Bernina Pass and Maloja Pass are the drives out. The village takes about four hours, June to August.

gem:ronda.text: Ronda stands either side of a gorge in Andalusia, in Spain. Puente Nuevo spans the gap and gets most of the photographs; Plaza de Toros de Ronda and Palacio de Mondragon follow. Six hours covers the town, June to August.

gem:berat.text: Berat is a UNESCO World Heritage Site town in Albania, its old quarters stacked up a hillside under a castle. Kalaja e Beratit crowns it, and the Bachelors' Mosque and Hysen Pasha Mosque sit below. The sights run to nine hours, best in April or May.

gem:york.text: York is a walled medieval city in the United Kingdom with Roman foundations under it. York Minster dominates, and the National Railway Museum is the surprise second act. Ten hours covers it, June to August.

gem:mykines.text: Mykines is a remote island in the Faroe Islands, open to visitors only in the summer months. The cliff walk is the whole reason to make the crossing, and Sorvagsvatn on nearby Vagar is worth adding. The island takes about four hours, June to August.

gem:myvatn.text: Lake Myvatn is a volcanic lake district in Iceland, with craters and lava formations around its shore. Krafla, Hverfjall and Dimmuborgir are the stops that matter. The circuit takes about five hours, and June and July are the best months.

gem:dinan.text: Dinan is a walled medieval town in Brittany, in France, with ramparts above the Rance. The Chateau de Dinan and the Eglise Saint-Malo de Dinan lead, and the canal d'Ille-et-Rance runs below. Six hours is enough, June to September.

gem:erice.text: Erice is a medieval stone village in Italy, up on Monte Erice with the coast spread out below. Mozia and the Madonna of Trapani are the pieces worth seeking out. The village takes about three hours; June to August is best.

gem:zamosc.text: Zamosc is a planned Renaissance town in Poland, its grid and ramparts intact enough for UNESCO World Heritage Site status. The Old City of Zamosc and Zamosc Fortress hold the centre, and the sights run to nine hours. May to September is the season.

gem:la-maddalena.text: La Maddalena is an island group off Italy, a national park ringed with beaches. Caprera and the Compendio Garibaldino hold the history; Spiaggia del Relitto and the Pink Beach hold the swimmers. The day runs to about seven hours, April to June.

gem:snowdonia.text: Snowdonia is a mountain national park in the United Kingdom, big enough to lose a week in. Snowdon is the summit everyone aims for, with Cadair Idris quieter and Harlech Castle down on the coast. The big walks run to seven hours, June to August.

gem:samaria-gorge.text: Samaria Gorge is a long walk down through a national park in Greece, open in summer only. The route drops from the Lefka Ori range to the sea and takes about five hours. May to September is the window, and transport at both ends needs planning.

gem:pulpit-rock.text: Preikestolen is a flat cliff top above the Lysefjord in Norway, reached on a walk up from the road. The view down the fjord is the whole point, and the top itself needs only a couple of hours. June to August is the season.

gem:erfurt.text: Erfurt keeps one of the largest intact medieval centres in Germany, with a UNESCO World Heritage Site among its churches. The Erfurter Dom and the Kramerbrucke lead, and the Alte Synagoge and Zitadelle Petersberg follow. Ten hours covers it, May to September.

gem:schwerin.text: Schwerin is a lake-ringed town in Germany built around a castle, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Schwerin Castle leads, with Schwerin Cathedral and the Staatliches Museum Schwerin close behind on the Schweriner See. Ten hours covers it, May to September.

gem:puy-de-dome.text: Puy de Dome is the high point of the Chaine des Puys in France, a line of old volcanoes on the UNESCO World Heritage Site list. Vulcania and Clermont-Ferrand Cathedral lie within reach below. The summit and its surrounds take about four hours, June to August.

gem:piazza-armerina.text: Piazza Armerina is a hill town in Italy, visited mostly for the Roman mosaics just outside it. Villa Romana del Casale and its Mosaico della Grande Caccia are the reason to come, with Morgantina nearby. The site takes about four hours, and May is the month.

gem:ponta-de-sao-lourenco.text: Ponta de Sao Lourenco is a bare coastal headland in Portugal, walked end to end on an exposed trail. The path out to the Farol da Ponta de Sao Lourenco takes about three hours there and back. Machico is the nearest town, May to September.

gem:burgos.text: Burgos is a cathedral city in Spain, with UNESCO World Heritage status. Burgos Cathedral comes first, then Las Huelgas and the Castillo de Burgos above it. Ten hours covers the lot, and June to September is the easy season.

gem:antequera.text: Antequera is a town in Spain with a UNESCO listed set of dolmens on its edge. Dolmen de Menga leads, then Dolmen de Viera and the rock country of Torcal de Antequera. Six hours is enough, and May or September suit best.

gem:valldemossa.text: Valldemossa is a stone village high in the Serra de Tramuntana on Mallorca. The Valldemossa Charterhouse is what most people come for, and the village takes a few hours on foot. June to August is the settled stretch.

gem:lovcen.text: Lovcen is a mountain national park in Montenegro, above the Bay of Kotor. Its peaks and the Fortifications of Kotor fill about seven hours, with Sveti Stefan on the coast nearby. July and August are the months to come.

gem:valbona.text: Valbona Valley is a national park in Albania, set deep in the Accursed Mountains. Maja Jezerce and Zla Kolata stand over it, and five hours covers the walking near the road. June to August is the season, though getting in is slow.

gem:riomaggiore.text: Riomaggiore is a village stacked above the sea on the Cinque Terre coast of Italy. Porto Venere and the islands of Palmaria and Tino sit close by, and seven hours covers the area. May to August is the warm stretch.

gem:sunderland.text: Sunderland is a coastal city in northeast England. Monkwearmouth-Jarrow Abbey carries a UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List entry, and Hylton Castle and the Stadium of Light fill out ten hours. June to August is the best window.

gem:prato.text: Prato is a cathedral city in Tuscany with a compact old centre. Prato Cathedral and the Basilica di Santa Maria delle Carceri lead, then the Castello dell'Imperatore. Ten hours covers it, best in April, May or September.

gem:a-guarda.text: A Guarda is a coastal town in Spain below Monte de Santa Trega. The Castro of Santa Trega on the hill is the reason to climb, and seven hours covers the town and the beaches. June to August is the season.

gem:bromley.text: Bromley is a market town in the United Kingdom, long since swallowed by the capital. Kew Gardens and Richmond Park are the pick nearby, a train ride across the city. June to September is the best stretch, and seven hours fills a day.

gem:enfield.text: Enfield is a market town in the United Kingdom, at the northern edge of the capital. Alexandra Palace Theatre is the draw nearby, with Cockfosters and Arnos Grove on the line in. Ten hours fills a day, easiest from June to September.

gem:barking.text: Barking is a market town in the United Kingdom, folded into the east of the capital. Greenwich Park, the Royal Observatory Greenwich and Cutty Sark are the sights nearby, about ten hours in all. June to September is the mildest stretch.

gem:bonn.text: Bonn is a city in Germany with more to see than its size suggests. Bonn Minster leads, then Villa Hammerschmidt, Palais Schaumburg and the Akademisches Kunstmuseum, some seventeen hours in all. May to September is the long season.

gem:sanlucar-de-barrameda.text: Sanlucar de Barrameda stands on the coast of Spain where the Guadalquivir reaches the Atlantic. Castillo de Santiago and the Palacio de Orleans-Borbon head a nine hour list, with Las Covachas along the old front. April and May are the months.

gem:noia.text: Noia is a coastal town in Spain at the end of a long inlet. Castro of Barona on its headland and the Dolmen de Axeitos are the pick, with Mount Pindo further out. Six hours covers it, best from June to September.

gem:sonntag.text: Sonntag lies in the mountains of Austria, inside a UNESCO Man and the Biosphere reserve. Lunersee, the Rote Wand and the Schesaplana are what walkers come for, about seven hours of it. June to August is the season, though buses are poor.

gem:aalst.text: Aalst sits in East Flanders, Belgium, halfway between Ghent and Brussels. Affligem Abbey and the Beguinage of Aalst lead a ten hour list, with the Kravaalbos woods for a break. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:terrassa.text: Terrassa is a city in Spain known for the church complex of Sant Pere de Terrassa and the Masia Freixa. Sant Llorenc del Munt gives the walking close by, and ten hours covers both. May and June are the pick.

gem:gardone-riviera.text: Gardone Riviera is a lakeside village on the Garda shore in Italy. Il Vittoriale degli Italiani is the set piece, with Salo along the water and Monte Pizzocolo above, about seven hours in all. May, June and September are the calm months.

BLQ.text: Bologna is a brick coloured university city in Emilia-Romagna, and a food town before anything else. Palazzo Re Enzo and the Basilica di San Domenico sit in the centre, seventeen hours of sights in all. April, May and September are kindest.

GOA.text: Genoa is a working port on the Ligurian coast of Italy, with the Palazzi dei Rolli behind the waterfront. Le Strade Nuove, the Aquarium of Genoa and the Lanterna di Genova fill seventeen hours. May, June and September are the best months.

NIM.text: Nimes is a city in southern France built around Roman stone. Maison Carree and the Arena of Nimes lead, and the Tour Magne rounds them off. Ten hours covers the lot, best in April, May or September.

gem:loire-valley.text: Loire Valley is wine country in France, with Tours at the centre of it. Tours Cathedral, the chateau de Tours and the Chateau de Plessis-lez-Tours make the short list. Ten hours covers them, and May to September is the season.

gem:evora.text: Evora is a walled city in the Alentejo of Portugal, on the UNESCO World Heritage list. Capela dos Ossos and the Roman Temple of Evora are what people come for, with ten hours enough for the centre. April and May are the best months.

gem:korcula.text: Korcula is an Adriatic island in Croatia with a compact old town at its tip. Korcula Cathedral and Our Lady of Angels are the sights, and five hours covers the walk around. May to July is the window, before the heat.

gem:mostar-ba.text: Mostar stands in Bosnia and Herzegovina, a city built around one arched bridge. Stari Most is the reason to come, and the Karadzozbey Mosque and the old town fill nine hours. May, June and September miss the worst heat.

gem:vik.text: Vik sits on the south coast of Iceland below Katla. Reynisfjara, Reynisdrangar and Dyrholaey are the stops, and four hours covers them. June to August is the easy season.

gem:connemara.text: Connemara is mountain and moor country in the west of Ireland. Connemara National Park and Kylemore Abbey are the fixed points, with Mweelrea and Bencorr for walkers. Six hours covers a drive through, best from June to September.

gem:high-tatras.text: High Tatras is a small alpine range in Slovakia, most of it inside Tatra National Park. Rysy, Krivan and Gerlachovsky stit are the peaks that lead, and seven hours covers a day on the trails. July and August are the sure months.

gem:trogir.text: Trogir is a medieval town on a small island off the coast of Croatia, UNESCO listed. Split and Diocletian's Palace lie a short ride away, and five hours covers Trogir itself. May and June are the best months.

gem:cuenca.text: Cuenca is a small city in Spain with a UNESCO World Heritage old town. Casas Colgadas and Cuenca Cathedral lead, then the Museo de Arte Abstracto Espanol. Ten hours covers it, best in May, June or September.

gem:gjogv.text: Gjogv is a small village on Eysturoy in the Faroe Islands. Slaettaratindur rises nearby and Kalsoy and Vidoy lie across the water, with three hours enough for a stop. June to August is the season, but transport is poor.

gem:snaefellsnes.text: Snaefellsnes is a volcanic peninsula in Iceland, with Snaefellsjokull at one end. Kirkjufell is the mountain everyone photographs, and Bjarnarfoss and Grundarfoss sit close to the road. June and July are the months for it.

gem:perast.text: Perast is a baroque village on the Bay of Kotor in Montenegro. Our Lady of the Rocks is the short boat trip everyone makes, and three hours is plenty for the waterfront. May and June come before the crowds.

gem:gozo.text: Gozo is the quieter island of the Maltese group in the Mediterranean. Ggantija and the Megalithic Temples of Malta are the draw, with Comino a boat ride off. May to August is the swimming season, and seven hours covers Gozo.

gem:sibenik.text: Sibenik is a coastal town in Croatia with a UNESCO listed cathedral at its heart. Krka National Park is the day trip, and the islands of Zlarin and Prvic lie offshore. May to August suits it, with five hours for the town.
