gem:hondarribia.text: Hondarribia is a walled fishing town on the Basque coast of Spain, close to the border with France. Cabo Higuer and Pheasant Island lie just outside, and the Camino del Norte passes through. June to September is the best run.

gem:santillana-del-mar.text: Santillana del Mar is a medieval village in Cantabria, Spain, on the UNESCO World Heritage list. The Colegiata and the Cave of Altamira outside the village are the two stops. June to September is the best run.

gem:saint-paul-de-vence.text: Saint-Paul-de-Vence is a hill village above the coast in France, full of galleries. Fondation Maeght just outside holds the art that matters, and four hours covers the lanes. May and June are the months to come.

gem:rocamadour.text: Rocamadour is a medieval pilgrimage village in the Lot, in southwestern France. Chapelle Notre-Dame de Rocamadour draws the visitors, with Padirac Cave a short drive on, and three hours covers the village. May to September is the long season.

gem:saint-emilion.text: Saint-Emilion is a medieval wine village in France, its jurisdiction listed by UNESCO. The Jurisdiction of Saint-Emilion, Chateau Ausone and Chateau Canon take about three hours. May to September is the season, and public transport is poor.

gem:civita-di-bagnoregio.text: Civita di Bagnoregio is a tiny hill village in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Two hours covers it. Lake Bolsena and the Gardens of Bomarzo lie close by, and May and June are the months to come.

gem:roros.text: Roros is an old mining town in the mountains of Norway, listed by UNESCO. Roros Church stands at its centre, and the Roros Mining Town and the Circumference holds the listing. July is the month to come, and two hours covers the sights.

gem:senja.text: Senja is a big island off northern Norway, wild country for hiking and northern lights. Anderdalen National Park leads, with Grytoya and Dyroya close by, and four hours of sights. July and August are the months, though transport is limited.

gem:vestmannaeyjar.text: Vestmannaeyjar is a remote volcanic island group off Iceland. Heimaey holds the town, Eldfell rises behind it and Surtsey sits offshore, about five hours of sights. June to August is the season, and transport is limited.

gem:odda.text: Odda is a fjord town in Norway and a base for serious walking. Trolltunga and Folgefonna stand close by, with Latefossen and Buarbreen a short trip, and two hours covers the town. July and August are the months.

gem:jurassic-coast.text: The Jurassic Coast is a protected shoreline in the United Kingdom, listed by UNESCO. Lyme Regis Museum, Shute Barton and Musbury Castle break up the walk, and Monmouth Beach and Charmouth Beach lie alongside. Its sights run to seven hours, best June to August.

gem:burg-eltz.text: Burg Eltz is a fairytale medieval castle in Germany. Eltz Castle is the reason to come, with Burg Pyrmont and Reichsburg Cochem a short drive away, and three hours is plenty. May to September is the season, and public transport is poor.

gem:aletsch-glacier.text: The Aletsch Glacier is the great ice stream of the Alps in Switzerland, listed by UNESCO. Aletschhorn, Jungfrau and Eiger ring it, and seven hours of walking gets the best of it. June to August is the window, and public transport is poor.

gem:porto-vecchio-palombaggia.text: Porto-Vecchio is a coastal town in France, best known for the beach at Palombaggia. Araghju, Casteddu di Tappa and Ceccia add old stonework inland, about four hours of sights. May to August is the season, and transport is limited.

gem:gorges-du-verdon.text: The Gorges du Verdon is a deep canyon in France, walking and adventure country. Verdon Gorge, the Lake of Sainte-Croix and Pont de l'Artuby lead, and five hours covers them. May and June are the best months, and public transport is poor.

gem:cirque-de-gavarnie.text: The Cirque de Gavarnie is a mountain amphitheatre in France, listed by UNESCO. Monte Perdido, Vignemale and the Pyrenees National Park fill the skyline, and seven hours of walking does it justice. June to August is the season.

gem:la-roque-gageac.text: La Roque-Gageac is a small village in France, listed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Chateau de Beynac, Chateau de Castelnaud-la-Chapelle and Sarlat Cathedral are all close by, about four hours. May to September is the season.

gem:epidaurus.text: Epidaurus is a village in Greece wrapped around one of the great ancient sites. The Ancient Theatre of Epidaurus leads, with the sanctuary of Asclepius and the Archaeological Museum beside it; three hours. May, June and September are best.

gem:balos-lagoon.text: Balos Lagoon is a shallow sand lagoon on the coast of Greece. Gramvousa, Agria Gramvousa and Phalasarna are the sights close by, about four hours. April to June and September are the best months, and transport is limited.

gem:alpe-di-siusi.text: Alpe di Siusi is a high meadow in the Alps of Italy, also known as Seiser Alm. Sassolungo and Marmolada fill the view, with Sella Pass and the Schlern-Rosengarten Nature Park close by. Its sights run to about four hours, best June to August.

gem:paestum.text: Paestum is a quiet archaeological village in Italy, listed by UNESCO for its Greek temples. The Temple of Hera and the Museo archeologico nazionale di Paestum take about three hours. April to June and September are the best months.

gem:cala-gonone.text: Cala Gonone is a small coastal village in Italy, set up for walking and swimming. Cala Luna and Cala Fuili are the beaches, while Grotta di Ispinigoli and Tiscali add three hours inland. April and May are the best months.

gem:flores-azores.text: Flores is a green, remote island in the Azores, part of Portugal. Rocha dos Bordoes, Morro Alto and the Cascata do Poco do Bacalhau are the landmarks, about seven hours in all. July and August are the months, and transport is limited.

gem:retezat.text: Retezat National Park protects a wilderness of peaks and mountain lakes in Romania, a UNESCO biosphere reserve. Peleaga and the Retezat Mountains rise above Bucura Lake, with five hours of walking. July and August are the months.

gem:gaztelugatxe.text: San Juan de Gaztelugatxe is a dramatic stretch of coast in Spain, best taken on foot. Bilbao lies close by, with the Vizcaya Bridge and the Bilbao Fine Arts Museum, and Anboto and Gorbea inland. Sights nearby run to seven hours, best June to September.

gem:ubeda.text: Ubeda is a compact town in Spain full of Renaissance palaces, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Vazquez de Molina Palace and the Casa de las Torres lead, and six hours covers the centre. April and May are the best months.

gem:hadrians-wall.text: Hadrian's Wall is a Roman frontier line across the United Kingdom, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Housesteads Roman Fort and Vindolanda are the best of it, with the Robin Hood Tree along the way. Six hours walks the main stretch, best June to August.

gem:toulon.text: Toulon is a port city on the coast of France with a big old harbour. Mont Faron looks down on it, and Toulon Cathedral, the Tour Royale and Toulon Opera fill the centre. Ten hours covers the sights, and June to August is the season.

gem:logrono.text: Logrono sits on the River Ebro in northern Spain, the capital of La Rioja. The Co-cathedral of Santa Maria de la Redonda and the Church of San Bartolome lead, about nine hours of sights. Best months run May to July, plus September.

gem:l-ametlla-de-mar.text: l'Ametlla de Mar is a small coastal town in Spain. The Delta de l'Ebre Natural Park lies close by, with Tortosa Cathedral and the Castell de Miravet inland. Six hours covers the area, and April and May are the best months.

gem:vila-nova-de-cerveira.text: Vila Nova de Cerveira is a small town in Portugal with an art streak. Sao Pedro da Torre and the Ponte de Rubiaes sit close by, and Monte Aloia and the Castro of Santa Trega are a little further. Six hours covers them, best June to August.

BRU.text: Brussels is a large city in Belgium, strong on art, food and architecture. The Grand Place leads, with the Atomium, Manneken Pis and the Stoclet Palace after it. The city holds seventeen hours of sights, transport is excellent, and May to September is best.

ACE.text: Lanzarote is a volcanic Canary island in Spain and a UNESCO biosphere reserve. Timanfaya National Park and La Geria lead, with Papagayo Beach and Playa Blanca for the sea. Six hours covers the sights, and April to September is a long season.

SPC.text: La Palma is a steep, green island in Spain, quieter than its Canary neighbours. Caldera de Taburiente National Park, Cumbre Vieja and Roque de los Muchachos are the walks, about six hours. April to September is the long season.

RHO.text: Rhodes is a large Greek island where a walled medieval city meets the beaches. The Medieval City of Rhodes and the Palace of the Grand Master lead, with Kameiros further out. Its sights take about four hours, and April to June is the best stretch.

WRO.text: Wroclaw is a large medieval city in Poland, busy with culture. The Centennial Hall carries the UNESCO listing, with Wroclaw Cathedral, the White Stork Synagogue and Iglica after it. The city needs seventeen hours, and May to September is best.

LUX.text: Luxembourg is a small fortress city and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Grand Ducal Palace, Fort Thungen, the Gelle Fra and Pont Adolphe are the landmarks, about ten hours in all. June to September is the season, and transport is excellent.

ZAD.text: Zadar is a coastal city in Croatia, old at its core and lively along the waterfront. The Sea organ and the Greeting to the Sun sit by the water, with the Church of St Donatus in the centre. Its sights fill eight hours, and May to August is the season.

gem:ghent.text: Ghent is a medieval city in Belgium, gothic in style and compact enough to walk. Gravensteen, Saint Bavo Cathedral and the Museum of Fine Arts Ghent are the leaders, about ten hours of sights. May to September is the season.

gem:rothenburg.text: Rothenburg ob der Tauber keeps its medieval walls and towers intact, a fairytale town in Germany. Its old centre, the Tauber Bridge and the Mittelalterliches Kriminalmuseum take about six hours. June to September is the season.

gem:piran.text: Piran is a medieval coastal town in Slovenia, tight lanes ending at the sea. Tartini Square is the centre, and the Secovlje Saltworks and Izola are short trips. The old town takes about four hours, and May to July is best.

gem:nice-villefranche.text: Villefranche-sur-Mer is a quiet village and beach on the French Riviera. Nice Observatory is close, and Monaco-Ville, La Condamine and Fontvieille are an easy trip along the coast. Sights nearby add up to four hours, best June to August.

gem:appenzell.text: Appenzell is a quiet village in the hills of Switzerland, with the Appenzell Alps behind it. Santis and Seealpsee are the walks close by, and the Abbey of Saint Gall is a short trip. The village and its walks fill about four hours, best June to August.

gem:lagos-pt.text: Lagos is a beach town on the coast of Portugal with a loud night scene. Ponta da Piedade leads, with Praia da Luz and Praia dos Tres Irmaos for sand. Six hours covers the sights, and May to September is the season.

gem:banska-stiavnica.text: Banska Stiavnica is a quiet medieval town in the Stiavnica Mountains of Slovakia, on the UNESCO list. The Kalvaria and the peak of Sitno stand over it. Its sights take about five hours, best between May and September.

gem:eze.text: Eze is a small coastal village in France, on the Cote d'Azur between Nice and Monaco. The village and the Parc de la Grande Corniche fill about four hours, with Mala beach below; June to August is the season.

gem:orvieto.text: Orvieto is a medieval hill town in Umbria, known for its cathedral and its wine. The Orvieto Cathedral leads, with Pozzo della Cava cut into the tufa below. Its sights take about four hours, and May or June is the time to come.

gem:peja.text: Peja is a mountain town in Kosovo at the mouth of the Rugova Canyon, best known for its UNESCO listed monasteries. The Patriarchate of Pec and Visoki Decani lead, with Gjeravica rising behind. Its sights take about four hours, May to July.

gem:nesebar.text: Nesebar is a UNESCO listed medieval town on the Black Sea coast of Bulgaria. The Ancient City of Nessebar and the Church of Christ Pantocrator lead, with Sunny Beach next door. Its sights take about five hours; May, June and September are best.

gem:cangas-de-onis.text: Cangas de Onis is a small town in Spain at the edge of the Picos de Europa National Park. The basilica at Covadonga and Lake Ercina are the draw. Its own sights take about three hours, best from June to September.

gem:procida.text: Procida is a quiet little island off Naples, in Italy, with the nature reserve of Vivara alongside and Ischia a short hop away. Its harbour, beaches and walks fill about six hours, best from May to August.

gem:camogli.text: Camogli is a quiet seaside village in Italy, on the edge of the Parco Naturale Regionale di Portofino and a short ride from Genoa. Its waterfront and the coast paths take about four hours; May, June and September are best.

gem:fort-william.text: Fort William sits below Ben Nevis in Scotland, a town given over to walkers and climbers. Aonach Mor, Carn Mor Dearg and Inverlochy Castle are all close. Six hours covers the sights, and June to August is the season.

gem:portrush.text: Portrush is a seaside town in the United Kingdom, known for its surf beaches. Dunluce Castle, the Carrick-a-Rede Rope Bridge and Old Bushmills Distillery are all nearby. Its own sights take about two hours, best from June to August.

gem:conwy.text: Conwy is a walled medieval town on the North Wales coast, its castle listed by UNESCO. Conwy Castle and the Smallest House in Great Britain stand by the river. Its sights take about four hours, best from June to August.

gem:cairngorms.text: Cairngorms National Park protects a spread of high, bare summits and plateau in the United Kingdom. Ben Macdui, Braeriach and Cairn Toul lead, with Loch Insh below. Six hours gets a taste; June to August is the season.

gem:aachen.text: Aachen is a cathedral and spa city in Germany, close to the corner where Belgium and the Netherlands meet. The UNESCO listed Aachen Cathedral leads, with the Ponttor gate after it. Ten hours fills a long day, best May to September.

gem:langhe.text: The Langhe is wine country in Piedmont, a run of vineyard hills in Italy on the UNESCO list. Castello di Grinzane Cavour and the Museo del Vino are the set pieces. Its cellars and villages fill about five hours, best May, June or September.

gem:yvoire.text: Yvoire is a walled medieval village on the shore of Lake Geneva in France. The Chateau d'Yvoire stands over the harbour, and Nyon lies across the water. Its lanes and lakefront take about four hours, best from June to September.

gem:sixt-fer-a-cheval.text: Sixt-Fer-a-Cheval is an alpine village in France, set in the Reserve naturelle de Sixt-Passy. Mont Buet rises above it, with the Aiguille du Midi and the Mer de Glace nearby. Its walks take about four hours; June to September is the season.

gem:nancy.text: Nancy is a baroque city in Lorraine, in eastern France, listed by UNESCO for its linked squares. Place Stanislas leads, with the Place d'Alliance and the musee de l'Ecole de Nancy after it. Ten hours covers the centre, best May to September.

gem:amiens.text: Amiens is a cathedral city in the north of France, on the UNESCO list. The Amiens Cathedral dominates, with the Musee de Picardie a few streets away. Ten hours fills a day here, best from June to September.

gem:patmos.text: Patmos is a quiet Greek island in the Dodecanese, known above all for its monastery. The Monastery of Saint John the Theologian and the Cave of the Apocalypse draw pilgrims. Its sights take about four hours, best from May to September.

gem:lago-di-braies.text: Lago di Braies is an alpine lake in South Tyrol, Italy, also known as the Pragser Wildsee. The Naturpark Fanes-Sennes-Prags rises behind it, with Kronplatz nearby. Its shore walk and the trails above fill about seven hours, best June to August.

gem:scilla.text: Scilla is a small coastal village in Italy, looking across the strait of Messina. The Castello Ruffo stands above the beach, with the Parco Nazionale dell'Aspromonte inland. Its sights take about three hours, best from May to August.

gem:stromboli.text: Stromboli is an active volcano in the Tyrrhenian Sea, one of the Aeolian Islands north of Sicily. The Sciara del Fuoco runs down to the water, and Panarea and Strombolicchio sit offshore. Its trails take about five hours; July and August are the months.

gem:trollstigen.text: Trollstigen is a mountain road of tight hairpin bends in Norway. Trollveggen, Romsdalshornet and Store Trolltinden rise around it, with Mongefossen falling nearby. Its viewpoints take about three hours; July and August are the months.

gem:jotunheimen.text: Jotunheimen is a wilderness of high peaks and long lakes in Norway, largely national park. Galdhopiggen and Glittertinden are the great summits, with Gjende and Tyin below. Six hours gets a first taste, best in June or July.

gem:alcobaca.text: Alcobaca is a small town in the west of Portugal, on the UNESCO list for its monastery. The Alcobaca Monastery leads, with the castle above it and Nazare beach a short drive away. Its sights take about five hours, best from May to July.

gem:danube-delta.text: The Danube Delta is a maze of channels, reed and shallow lakes in Romania, protected by UNESCO. Letea Forest and Popina Island are the places to aim for. Its waterways take about four hours, best in May, June or September.

gem:harris-luskentyre.text: The Isle of Harris is a remote island of wide beaches and bare rock in the Outer Hebrides. Clisham is the high point, with Berneray and Scalpay close by. Its beaches take about four hours, and June to August is the season.

gem:st-michaels-mount.text: St Michael's Mount is a castle crowning a small island off the Cornwall coast, in the United Kingdom. The Lizard NNR, Tate St Ives and Men-an-Tol are all within a drive. Its castle and the wider coast fill about seven hours, best June to September.

gem:woodstock.text: Woodstock is a stone market town in the United Kingdom, best known for Blenheim Palace at its edge. The palace is the reason to come, with Oxford and the Ashmolean Museum nearby. Its own centre takes about three hours, best June to September.

gem:llanberis.text: Llanberis is a village in North Wales at the foot of Snowdon, the starting point for the walk up. Dolbadarn Castle stands by the lake, and Caernarfon Castle is close. Its sights take about four hours, best from June to August.

gem:cromford.text: Cromford is a small village in the Derwent valley in Derbyshire, with UNESCO listing. Derby is the nearest city, with the Museum of Making and Derby Cathedral there. Its sights take about four hours, best from June to August.

gem:bakewell.text: Bakewell is a market town inside the Peak District National Park, in Derbyshire. Haddon Hall and Chatsworth House lie just outside, and Thornbridge Hall is close too. Its own centre takes about four hours, best from June to August.

gem:germoe.text: Germoe is a small village in Cornwall, United Kingdom, inside the UNESCO listed mining landscape. St Michael's Mount and Longrock Beach are close, with Men-an-Tol not far. Its sights take about three hours, best from June to September.

gem:montsoreau.text: Montsoreau is a small village on the Loire in France, its chateau standing at the water's edge. The Chateau de Montsoreau is the set piece, with Fontevraud and Chinon Castle nearby. Its centre takes about three hours, best May to September.

gem:san-felice-circeo.text: San Felice Circeo is a coastal village in Italy, set below Mount Circeo inside the Circeo National Park. The Guattari Cave and Torre Paola are the things to see. Its beaches and the village take about three hours, best from June to August.

gem:chelmsford.text: Chelmsford is a cathedral city and market town in the United Kingdom, with good public transport. Chelmsford Cathedral leads, with the Palace of Beaulieu and Boreham House nearby. Its sights run to about nine hours, best June to September.

gem:hardegg.text: Hardegg is a tiny village in Austria, set inside the National Park Thayatal below its castle. Hardegg Castle and Schloss Ruegers are the two things to see, with Podyji National Park alongside. Its walks take about four hours, best May to September.

gem:subiaco.text: Subiaco is a small town in Lazio, Italy, where the Benedictine order began. The Monastery of Saint Scholastica is the reason to come, with the Ponte di San Francesco nearby. Its sights take about three hours, best in May, June or September.

gem:pienza.text: Pienza is a small Renaissance town in the Val d'Orcia, in Tuscany, on the UNESCO list. The Duomo di Pienza and the Palazzo Piccolomini are the set pieces. Its centre takes about four hours, best in May or June.

gem:kortrijk.text: Kortrijk is a city of the Flanders region in Belgium, listed in the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. The Broeltorens stand over the water, with the Begijnhof and the Sint-Michielskerk in the centre. Ten hours covers it, best June to September.

gem:gradara.text: Gradara is a village of 1533 people in Italy, known for its castle and listed among the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Two hours covers it. Pesaro Cathedral, the Arch of Augustus and Tempio Malatestiano lie nearby; May and June are best.

gem:sabbioneta.text: Teatro all'Antica is the reason most visitors come to Sabbioneta, a village of 1624 people in Italy. Set aside three hours for the theatre, the Synagogue and the cathedral. Best months run April to June, plus September.

gem:vimbodi.text: Vimbodi is a village of 1030 people in Spain, and Poblet Monastery next door is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The monastery with a climb to Punta del Curull fills about four hours. Best months are May, June and September.

gem:knebel.text: Knebel is a village of 603 people in Denmark, set inside Nationalpark Mols Bjerge. The park and the beach at Skodshoved Strand fill about three hours, with Aarhus Cathedral and ARoS Aarhus Kunstmuseum nearby. Best in June, July or August.

gem:fuengirola.text: Castillo Sohail looks over Fuengirola, a coastal city of 71482 people in Spain. The castle, Torre del Muelle and the beach fill about eight hours, and buses run well. Best months stretch from May to September.

gem:petronell-carnuntum.text: Petronell-Carnuntum is a village of 1245 people in Austria, and Carnuntum beside it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The visit takes about four hours. Bratislava and its Old Town sit close by; May to September is the window.

gem:halle-saale.text: Halle is a city of 237865 people in Germany, on the Saale. Moritzburg, the Market Church of Our Dear Ladies and Giebichenstein Castle head a list worth about ten hours. May to September is the easiest time, and transport is good.

gem:high-wycombe.text: High Wycombe is a market town of 133204 people in the United Kingdom. Cliveden House, West Wycombe Park and Hughenden Manor sit around it and make up most of a ten hour visit. June to September is the best run, and transport is good.

gem:castel-san-pietro-romano.text: Castel San Pietro Romano is a village of 411 people in Italy and one of the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The sights take about three hours. Villa d'Este, the Alban Hills and Lake Nemi are all nearby; May and June are the months.

gem:livorno.text: Livorno is a port city of 157017 on the coast of Italy, in Tuscany. Fortezza Vecchia, the Duomo di Livorno and the Museo Civico Giovanni Fattori fill most of a ten hour visit. April to June and September are the kinder months.

gem:hoek.text: Hoek is a village of 1100 people in the Netherlands, well served by public transport. Leeuwarden nearby holds the Oldehove, Keramiekmuseum Princessehof and Grote of Jacobijnerkerk, about four hours in all. Best in June, July or August.

gem:sankt-andreasberg.text: Sankt Andreasberg is a village of 2037 people in Germany, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site with the Upper Harz Water Regale. The Brocken, Rammelsberg and Grosser Knollen fill about four hours. Best in June, July or August.

gem:forte-dei-marmi.text: Forte dei Marmi is a beach village of 7656 people on the coast of Italy, with the Apuan Alps behind it. Monte Pisanino and Massa Cathedral are the trips inland, and the sights take about three hours. May to August is the season.

gem:la-roche-guyon.text: La Roche-Guyon is a village of 583 people in France, on the Les Plus Beaux Villages de France list. Its castle church, the eglise Saint-Samson, and the Fondation Claude Monet at Giverny fill about four hours. May to September is the run.

gem:vigo.text: Vigo is a port city of 293642 people in Spain, spread along the Ria de Vigo. The concatedral, the Museo Quinones de Leon and Praia de Samil are the pick, with about ten hours of sights. June to August is the time, and buses are good.

gem:spitz.text: Spitz is a wine village of 1270 people in Austria, in the Wachau on the Danube and inside a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Melk Abbey, Burgruine Aggstein and Stift Durnstein make up about four hours. May to September is the stretch.

gem:porto-ercole.text: Porto Ercole is a coastal village of 2676 people in Italy, part of Monte Argentario and one of the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Cosa, the Laguna di Orbetello and the Tarot Garden sit close by. May and June are the best months.

gem:san-ildefonso.text: San Ildefonso is a village of 5426 people in Spain, and the Royal Palace of La Granja de San Ildefonso is why people come. The palace with a walk in Guadarrama National Park makes about three hours. Best in May, June or September.

gem:castel-gandolfo.text: Castel Gandolfo is a village of 3694 people in Italy, above Lake Albano and one of the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Its lake and the papal summer residence take about four hours, and Lake Nemi is next door. June to August is the warm stretch.

gem:arqua-petrarca.text: Arqua Petrarca is a village of 878 people in Italy, set in the Euganean Hills and on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. Monte Venda and Villa dei Vescovi are the stops around it, about four hours. April to June and September suit best.

gem:beynac-et-cazenac.text: Beynac-et-Cazenac, a village of 535 people in France, is one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Chateau de Beynac above it leads a four hour round, with Chateau de Castelnaud-la-Chapelle and Sarlat Cathedral close by. Best from May to September.

gem:aquileia.text: Aquileia is a village of 2939 people in Italy and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The basilica and the National Archaeological Museum take about three hours. May and June are the best months, and public transport is poor.

gem:capo-di-ponte.text: Capo di Ponte is a village of 2067 people in Italy, set in Val Camonica where prehistoric rock carvings hold a UNESCO World Heritage Site listing. The carvings and Mount Adamello above fill about four hours. June to September is the window.

gem:lavrio.text: Lavrio is a coastal village of 7078 people in Greece, listed on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List. Cape Sounion and the Theatre of Thorikos are the two to see, about three hours between them. May to September is the season.

gem:plouharnel.text: Plouharnel is a village of 1812 people on the coast of France, next to the Carnac stones and their UNESCO World Heritage Site listing. Kerzerho, the Geant du Manio and Gavrinis add about four hours. Best from June to September.

gem:ivanovo.text: Ivanovo is a village of 1031 people in Bulgaria, and the Rock-hewn Churches of Ivanovo above it are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Two hours covers the churches and a look at Rusenski Lom Nature Park. Best in May, June or September.

gem:mustair.text: Mustair is a village of 795 people in Switzerland and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Stelvio Pass, Stelvio National Park and Ortler fill about four hours, though public transport is poor. Best in June, July or August.

gem:middenbeemster.text: Middenbeemster is a village of 4070 people in the Netherlands and part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Amsterdam is the day out: the Rijksmuseum, the Van Gogh Museum and Anne Frank House, about four hours. Best in June, July or August.

gem:worms.text: Worms is a city of 81099 people in Germany. Worms Cathedral leads, with the Jewish Cemetery, Worms Synagogue and the Nibelungenmuseum filling out roughly ten hours. May to September is the pleasant stretch, and transport is good.

gem:colunga.text: Colunga is a village of 3868 people on the coast of Spain, listed as a conjunto historico. The Sierra del Sueve rises behind it and Playa de Rodiles is the beach, about three hours in all. Best from June to September.

gem:helsingborg.text: Helsingborg is a coastal city of 104250 people in Sweden, with the Karnan tower over its centre. Kronborg Castle and Sankt Olai Kirke are across the water at Helsingor, and ten hours covers the pair. June to August is the best run.

gem:guildford.text: Guildford is a market town of 71873 people in the United Kingdom. Guildford Cathedral on its hill, the Watts Gallery and the Shah Jahan Mosque are the pick, and the North Downs start at the edge of town. Ten hours, best June to September.

gem:noli.text: Noli is a coastal village of 1673 people in Italy, one of the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Chiesa di San Paragorio, Castel Gavone and the Caverna delle Arene Candide add to about four hours. Best in May, June, July or September.

gem:biot.text: Biot is a village of 7737 people near the coast of France, on the Les Plus Beaux Detours de France list. Fondation Maeght, Chateau Grimaldi and Antibes Cathedral are the nearby stops, about four hours. May and June are the months to pick.

gem:greve-in-chianti.text: Greve in Chianti is a village of 3792 people in Italy, one of the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Florence is close by for the Ponte Vecchio, the Bargello National Museum and Basilica of San Lorenzo, about four hours. Best in May, June or September.

gem:frantiskovy-lazne.text: Frantiskovy Lazne is a spa town of 5607 people in Czechia, one of The Great Spa Towns of Europe. Komorni hurka and Soos are the walks nearby, and the sights run to about four hours. Best from June to September.

gem:savona.text: Savona is a port city of 61345 people on the Liguria coast of Italy. Fortezza del Priamar guards the harbour, with Palazzo Della Rovere and the Oratorio di Nostra Signora di Castello nearby, about ten hours in all. Best in May, June or September.

gem:vallon-pont-d-arc.text: Vallon-Pont-d'Arc is a village of 2337 people in France, next to Pont d'Arc and the cave of Grotte Chauvet, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Grotte Chauvet 2 and Aven d'Orgnac round out about three hours. Best in May, June or September.

gem:benevento.text: Benevento is a city of 58418 people in Campania, Italy. The Arch of Trajan is the one everyone comes for, with Santa Sofia Church and the Rocca dei Rettori filling out about ten hours. April, May and September are the best months.

gem:zernez.text: Zernez is a village of 1053 people in Switzerland and the way into the Swiss National Park. Piz Quattervals rises above it and the Albula Alps are close, about three hours of sights. Best in June, July or August.

gem:lark-hill.text: Lark Hill is a village in the United Kingdom living in the shadow of Stonehenge, with Woodhenge and Durrington Walls nearby. Salisbury Cathedral rounds out about three hours of sights. Best months run June to September.

gem:luso.text: Luso is a village in Portugal set against Bucaco Forest. The Old Cathedral of Coimbra and Biblioteca Joanina lie a short way off, and three hours covers the lot. May and June are the best months.

gem:matalascanas.text: Matalascanas is a small beach village in Spain on the edge of Donana National Park. Torre de la Higuera stands above the sand, and two hours covers the village sights. April and May are the best months.

gem:divaca.text: Divaca is a village in Slovenia and the gateway to the Skocjan Caves. Jama Vilenica and Lipica Stud Farm round out about four hours above and below ground. June to August is the season.

gem:blaenavon.text: Blaenavon is a village in the United Kingdom with a UNESCO World Heritage listing and coal in its past. Big Pit: National Coal Museum leads, with Raglan Castle and Llangorse Lake nearby. The sights take four hours, best June to August.

gem:saintes-maries-de-la-mer.text: Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer is a coastal village in France at the heart of the Camargue. The Church of the Saintes Maries de la Mer anchors the centre, and the Camargue Regional Natural Park surrounds it. Two hours in town, best May or June.

gem:achicourt.text: Achicourt is a village in France beside Arras, whose cathedral and Fortifications of Vauban head the list. Louvre-Lens is the other draw nearby. The sights add up to four hours, best June through September.

gem:clermont-ferrand.text: Clermont-Ferrand spreads under the Chaine des Puys in central France, with Puy de Dome rising over it. Clermont-Ferrand Cathedral and the Basilica of Notre-Dame du Port anchor the centre. Ten hours of sights, best June to September.

gem:montefalco.text: Montefalco is a small village in Umbria, listed among the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Cattedrale di San Feliciano and Mevania are the local sights, with the Basilica of San Francesco d'Assisi nearby. The whole takes three hours.

gem:ponte-arche.text: Ponte Arche is a village in Italy below the Brenta group, inside a UNESCO Man and the Biosphere reserve. Cima Tosa, Campanile Basso and Lake Molveno lie close by. The sights run to three hours, best June to September.

gem:santo-stefano-di-sessanio.text: The village of Santo Stefano di Sessanio sits in Italy inside the Gran Sasso e Monti della Laga National Park, with barely a hundred residents. Corno Grande rises above it and Peltuinum lies nearby. June to August is the season.

gem:lednice.text: Lednice is a village in Czechia at the heart of the Lednice-Valtice Cultural Landscape. The Minaret in Lednice and the Palava Protected Landscape Area fill out four hours. May to September is the long season.

gem:jaujac.text: Jaujac is a village in France inside a UNESCO Global Geopark. Mazan Abbey and the Chateau de Ventadour lead, with Col de l'Escrinet a short drive away. The sights come to three hours, best in May or June.

gem:bad-grund.text: Bad Grund is a village in Germany, part of the UNESCO listed Upper Harz Water Regale. The Hubichenstein rises above it, with Rammelsberg and Gandersheim Abbey within reach. Best months are June to August.

gem:le-touquet-paris-plage.text: Le Touquet-Paris-Plage is a beach village on the coast of France. Parc Bagatelle and the Phare de Berck are close by, along with Quentovic and Gesoriacum. The sights fill four hours, best June to August.

gem:la-cabanasse.text: La Cabanasse is a small village in France on the Ligne de Cerdagne, whose Pont Gisclard and Pont Sejourne are sights in themselves. Puigmal rises above, and Lac de Matemale is close. Best months are June to August.

gem:messel.text: Messel is a village in Germany with a UNESCO World Heritage listing. Frankfurt am Main is the nearest big city, and the Artists' Colony in Darmstadt is close too. The sights around it take four hours, best May to September.

gem:malcesine.text: Malcesine sits on the shore of Lake Garda in Italy, with Castello Scaligero over the water and Monte Baldo behind. The village takes three hours, and June to September is the season.

gem:norre-vorupor.text: Norre Vorupor is a small coastal village in Denmark inside Thy National Park. Lodbjerg Lighthouse and Vestervig Abbey are the main sights, about three hours in all. July and August are the months for it.

gem:vejle.text: Vejle is a city in Denmark and the base for Jelling nearby, where the Jellingestenene and Jelling Kirke stand. Kongernes Jelling and the Vejle Museum of Art fill out a long day, about nine hours. Best months are June to August.

gem:loro-ciuffenna.text: Loro Ciuffenna is a village in Italy listed among the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Vallombrosa Abbey and the Arboreti di Vallombrosa lie in the hills above, with Ponte Buriano a drive away. Best months are May, June and September.

gem:barletta.text: Barletta is a coastal city in Italy where the Colossus of Barletta stands in the old centre. Barletta Cathedral, Palazzo della Marra and the Pinacoteca De Nittis fill much of a day, eight hours in all. May and June are best.

gem:buonconvento.text: Buonconvento is a village in Italy set in the Crete senese. Santa Maria di Monte Oliveto Maggiore and the Abbey of Sant'Antimo are short trips out, with Duomo di Pienza beyond. Best months are April to June, plus September.

gem:sutri.text: Sutri is a village in Italy between Lake Bracciano and Lake Vico. Villa Farnese and Falerii Novi are close by, with the Cimini Hills above. The sights take three hours, best in May or June.

gem:moret-sur-loing.text: Moret-sur-Loing is a village in France beside the forest of Fontainebleau, four hours of sights in all. The Palace of Fontainebleau leads, with Chateau de Moret and Chateau de Nemours closer to hand. Best months are May to September.

gem:glorenza.text: Glorenza is a small village in Italy below the Ortler, one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Stelvio Pass and Reschen Pass climb away on either side, with Reschensee close by. June to August is the window.

gem:lagrasse.text: Lagrasse is a village in France on the Plus Beaux Villages list. Lagrasse Abbey leads, with the Chateau de Termes and Montagne d'Alaric in the hills around. The sights take three hours, best May, June or September.

gem:le-croisic.text: Le Croisic is a coastal town in France, one of the Petites Cites de Caractere. Manoir de Kervaudu, the chateau de Careil and the Croix de Kervaudu are the sights, four hours in all. Best months are June to September.

gem:moneglia.text: Moneglia is a small beach village on the coast of Italy, one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Punta Baffe and Monte Gottero rise behind it, and Baia del Silenzio is close. Best months are June to August.

gem:grazie.text: Grazie is a small village in Italy near Mantua, listed among the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Palazzo Te and the Camera degli Sposi in Mantua are the main draw, four hours in all. Best months are April, May and September.

gem:forlev.text: Forlev is a village in Denmark near the Great Belt Fixed Link. Antvorskov Kloster and Soro Klosterkirke are the historic stops close by, about three hours in all. Best months are June to August.

gem:milano-marittima.text: Milano Marittima is a beach village in Italy. The Basilica of San Vitale, the Mausoleum of Theodoric and Sant'Apollinare in Classe are all a short trip inland, about three hours of sights. May to August is the season.

gem:civitella-del-tronto.text: Civitella del Tronto is a village in Italy below Montagna dei Fiori. Castel Manfrino stands nearby, with Ascoli Piceno Cathedral a short drive off. The sights come to three hours, best June to August.

gem:jena.text: Jena sits in Germany with the JenTower over its centre and the Zeiss-Planetarium close. Schillerkirche and the Fuchsturm fill the rest of a full day, about ten hours. May to September is the best stretch.

gem:varese.text: Varese is a city in Italy between Lake Varese and Lake Lugano, close to the mountains. Monte Generoso and Mottarone are within reach, and the smaller towns of Arcisate and Bisuschio lie nearby. Ten hours of sights, best May to September.

gem:lido-di-castel-fusano.text: Lido di Castel Fusano is a beach village on the coast of Italy beside Lido di Ostia. Ostia and Portus are the sights to plan around, about four hours in all. May to August is the season.

gem:le-bar-sur-loup.text: Le Bar-sur-Loup is a small village in France on the Plus Beaux Villages list. Grasse Cathedral is close by, with the Lerins Islands and Juan-les-Pins on the coast. The sights come to three hours, best May to August.

gem:palena.text: Palena is a village in Italy inside the Maiella National Park, below Monte Porrara. Caldora-Cantelmo Castle and Lago di Bomba are the nearby stops, with Sulmona Cathedral further off. The sights take three hours, best May or June.

gem:nodebo.text: Nodebo is a village in Denmark beside Gribskov, in the Par force hunting landscape in North Zealand. Frederiksborg Palace and Kronborg Castle are close, along with the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art. Best months are June to August.

gem:ramatuelle.text: Ramatuelle is a coastal village in France on the Plus Beaux Villages list, with the beach at Pampelonne nearby. Port Grimaud and the massif des Maures are close. The sights take three hours, best June to August.

gem:vielha.text: Vielha sits in the Val d'Aran, a Pyrenees village in Spain of about five thousand people. Aneto and Maladeta rise close by, with the Aiguestortes national park beyond. June to September is the season, and four hours covers the sights.

gem:la-spezia.text: A working port city in Liguria, La Spezia is the mainland base for Cinque Terre. Museo civico Amedeo Lia holds the art indoors, and boats cross to Porto Venere and Isola Palmaria. Ten hours covers the sights, best May to July.

gem:barruera.text: Barruera is a village of some seven hundred people in the Vall de Boi, Spain. The Catalan Romanesque Churches of the valley are UNESCO listed, and Sant Climent de Taull leads them. Best months are June to September; four hours covers it.

gem:ares-del-maestre.text: Ares del Maestre is a hilltop village of barely two hundred people in Spain, a Conjunto historico. Muela de Ares looms above and the Church of Santa Maria la Mayor anchors the centre, with Morella Castle a drive off. Its sights take three hours.

gem:jarvso.text: Jarvso is a village in Halsingland, Sweden, where the Decorated Farmhouses of Halsingland hold a UNESCO World Heritage listing. Jarvzoo and Jarvso Church round out a short stop. Two hours is enough, and June and July are the months.

gem:maikammer.text: Maikammer sits where the Palatinate Forest meets the plain in Germany, a village holding the European Heritage Label. Kalmit rises above it, with Villa Ludwigshohe on the slope below. Public transport is good, and four hours covers the sights.

gem:pacentro.text: The Caldora-Cantelmo Castle towers over Pacentro, a village in Maiella National Park in Italy and one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Monte Amaro and Lago di Scanno are both close. Set aside three hours, in May or June.

gem:castiglione-del-lago.text: Castiglione del Lago is a walled village above Lake Trasimeno in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Isola Maggiore sits offshore, with Montepulciano and Cortona a drive inland. May, June and September are best; three hours covers it.

gem:castellabate.text: Castellabate is a medieval village above the Cilento coast in Italy, on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. The temples of Paestum and the ruins of Velia are the draw close by, with Monte Stella behind. Two hours covers the village, in May or June.

gem:sorano.text: Sorano is a hill village in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Concattedrale dei Santi Pietro e Paolo anchors it, and Pitigliano with its synagogue is next door. Lake Bolsena and Monte Amiata are close; four hours covers the sights.

gem:colares.text: Colares is a coastal village in Portugal inside a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Cabo da Roca lies close, with the Pena National Palace and Sintra National Palace a short drive away. The sights need four hours, May to September.

gem:castello-del-matese.text: Castello del Matese is a small village of the Matese in Italy, set inside a national park. Saepinum, Alife Cathedral and Santa Maria della Ferraria are the sights, and none takes long. Two hours does it, ideally May or June.

gem:ponte-di-legno.text: Ponte di Legno is a mountain village in Italy below Mount Adamello and Presanella. The Gavia Pass and Mortirolo Pass climb away from it, with the Parco naturale dell'Adamello alongside. Sights run to three hours, June to August.

gem:palmanova.text: Palmanova is a fortress town in Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Palmanova Fortress and the Basilica of Our Lady of the Assumption stand inside the walls, with Palazzo Antonini nearby. Add four hours.

gem:njegusi.text: Njegusi is a village on the slopes of Lovcen in Montenegro, above the Bay of Kotor. The Fortifications of Kotor, Sveti Stefan and Our Lady of the Rocks all lie on the coast below. Set aside three hours, June to August.

gem:litochoro.text: Litochoro is the village at the foot of Mount Olympus in Greece, where walks up the mountain begin. Ancient Dion and Platamon Castle are the other calls, with the beach at Skotina close. The sights need three hours, in May, June or September.

gem:rovigo.text: Rovigo is a quiet city in Italy where the sights are mostly palaces. Palazzo Roverella carries the art, with Palazzo Roncale, Palazzo Angeli and the Duomo di Rovigo filling out the rest. Its sights run to nine hours, best April to June or September.

gem:bad-muskau.text: Bad Muskau, a spa town in Saxony, is known above all for Muskau Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Rhododendron Park Kromlau and the Englische Brucke are close enough to add. Set aside three hours, May to September.

gem:pettorano-sul-gizio.text: Pettorano sul Gizio is a village of five hundred on the edge of Maiella National Park in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Corfinium and Sulmona Cathedral are close, with Lago di Scanno a drive away. Its sights take three hours.

gem:holte.text: Holte is a leafy suburban area in Denmark just north of Copenhagen, with Fureso and Sjaelso on its doorstep. The bigger sights are a train ride away in the city: Amalienborg, Rundetaarn and Assistens Cemetery. Set aside seven hours, June to August.

gem:fazana.text: Fazana is a small port village in Istria, Croatia, where boats leave for the Brijuni islands. Pula Arena, the Temple of Augustus and the Arch of the Sergii lie just down the coast. Sights run to three hours, May to July.

gem:worlitz.text: Worlitz is a village in Germany in the Dessau-Worlitz Garden Realm, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Worlitzer Park and the Worlitz Synagogue stand here, with Wittenberg and its Castle Church close by. The sights need three hours, May to September.

gem:fiumaretta-di-ameglia.text: Fiumaretta di Ameglia is a small coastal village in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Tino, Palmaria and Tinetto lie offshore, with Cinque Terre National Park and the Apuan Alps within reach. Set aside four hours, May to July.

gem:tavarnelle-val-di-pesa.text: Tavarnelle Val di Pesa sits in Chianti, in Tuscany, Italy, a village of some seven thousand people. The Florence Charterhouse, Torre Grossa and the Collegiate Church of San Gimignano are all a short drive away. Its sights take four hours.

gem:ossuccio.text: Ossuccio is a village on Lake Como in Italy, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Bellagio, Menaggio and Villa Carlotta at Griante are all a boat ride across the water. The sights need four hours, May to September.

gem:kassiopi.text: Kassiopi is a harbour village on Corfu in Greece, under Mount Pantokrator. Butrint and the Islets of Ksamil lie across the water, with Ali Pasha Castle beyond. Two hours covers it, and April and May are the best months.

gem:salins-les-bains.text: Salins-les-Bains is a village in France where the Salines de Salins-les-Bains hold a UNESCO World Heritage listing. Mont Poupet stands above it and the Forest of Chaux is close. Set aside three hours, June to September.

gem:dannewerk.text: Dannewerk is a village in Germany beside the Danevirke, which with Hedeby forms a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Danevirke Museum explains the site, and Schleswig Cathedral is a short hop away. Its sights take four hours, June to August.

gem:schonau-am-konigssee.text: Schonau am Konigssee is a village in Germany inside a UNESCO Man and the Biosphere reserve. Watzmann and Jenner rise above Konigssee itself, with Eisriesenwelt and Hohenwerfen Castle further off. The sights need four hours, May to September.

gem:markov-grad.text: Markov Grad is a village in North Macedonia below Markovi Kuli, within a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Treskavec and Babuna are the other draws, with the Memorial Museum 11th October nearby. Sights run to four hours, in May, June or September.

gem:dubravice.text: Dubravice is a village in Croatia at the edge of Krka National Park. Sibenik Cathedral is the nearest landmark, with the islands of Prvic, Zlarin and Krapanj offshore. Two hours is enough, in May or June.

gem:schwabisch-gmund.text: Schwabisch Gmund is a city of sixty thousand in Germany, built around the Holy Cross Minster. Museum im Prediger holds the art, and Hohenstaufen Castle and Hohenrechberg lie outside the city. Ten hours covers the sights, June to September.

gem:puebla-de-sanabria.text: Puebla de Sanabria is a hill village in Spain, a Conjunto historico crowned by the Castle of Puebla de Sanabria. Nuestra Senora del Azogue stands below, and Sanabria Lake is a short drive. Two hours covers the village, June to September.

gem:coulon.text: Coulon is a village in France on the Marais Poitevin, one of the Petites Cites de Caractere. Maillezais Cathedral and the Eglise Sainte-Eulalie de Benet are close by. Two hours does it, May to September.

gem:ile-aux-moines.text: Ile-aux-Moines is an island village in the Gulf of Morbihan, France. Gavrinis is close across the water, with the Carnac stones and Vannes Cathedral on the mainland. Its sights take four hours, June to September.

gem:ager.text: Ager is a village of five hundred people in Spain, under the Serra del Montsec and listed as a Conjunto historico. The Canelles Reservoir and the Panta de Santa Anna lie close. Sights run to four hours, best in May, June or September.

gem:ibeas-de-juarros.text: Ibeas de Juarros is a village in Spain next to Atapuerca, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Gran Dolina and Sima de los Huesos belong to it, and Burgos Cathedral is a short drive. Set aside three hours, June to September.

gem:laxenburg.text: Laxenburg is a village in Austria whose draws are the castles and abbeys around it. Liechtenstein Castle and the Burgruine Modling stand close, with Heiligenkreuz Abbey and Baden a short drive. The sights need four hours, April to September.

gem:tobed.text: Tobed is a tiny village in Spain with the Sierra de Algairen and Sierra de Vicort close by. The Collegiate church of Santa Maria carries a UNESCO World Heritage listing, and Augusta Bilbilis is within reach. Two hours is enough, best in May or June.

gem:almere-stad.text: Almere Stad is a city in the Netherlands between the Gooimeer and the Markermeer. Lepelaarplassen lies at its edge, with Muiderslot and Pampus across the water. Set aside nine hours, June to August; public transport is good.

gem:san-millan-de-la-cogolla.text: Two monasteries, Yuso in the valley and Suso on the slope above, earn this small village in La Rioja its UNESCO World Heritage Site listing. The pair takes about two hours. June to September suits a visit best.

gem:burgh.text: Burgh is a coastal village in the Netherlands, a base for Walcheren, Neeltje Jans and the Zeeland Bridge. Set aside three hours for the sights around it. June to August is the season here.

gem:lipnice-nad-sazavou.text: Lipnice nad Sazavou is a small castle village in Czechia, with the Muzeum Jaroslava Haska and the Selske muzeum Michaluv statek nearby. Orlik Castle and the Zeliv monastery round out about four hours. June to August is best.

gem:libesice.text: Libesice is a small village in Czechia carrying a UNESCO World Heritage Site listing. Zatec, the Nechranice Reservoir and St Nicolas Church in Louny lie nearby and make up about four hours. May to September is the window.

gem:darp.text: Darp is a small village in the Netherlands ringed by national parks, with Dwingelderveld and Drents-Friese Wold both a short drive off. The walking fills about four hours. June to August is the season.

gem:de-cocksdorp.text: De Cocksdorp is a beach village on Texel in the Netherlands, with the Eierland Lighthouse and the Dunes of Texel National Park close by. Ecomare is worth an hour of the three most people need. June to August is the season.

gem:raksta.text: Raksta is a small village in Sweden set between the lakes Drevviken and Magelungen. Stockholm is the draw, with Skogskyrkogarden and the Thiel Gallery about four hours of sightseeing. July and August are the months to come.

gem:palaia-epidavros.text: Palaia Epidavros is a small coastal village in Greece, a base for the site of Epidaurus just inland. The Ancient Theatre is the sight that leads, and three hours covers it. April and May are the best months.

gem:lappi.text: Lappi is a small village in Finland known for Sammallahdenmaki, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Two hours covers it, with Old Rauma and the Church of the Holy Cross close by. June to August is the season.

gem:gars-am-kamp.text: Gars am Kamp is a village in Austria inside a UNESCO Global Geopark, and the Rosenburg is its landmark. Altenburg Abbey and Burgruine Senftenberg add up to about four hours. May to September is the stretch to visit.

gem:vrboska.text: Vrboska is a small harbour village on Hvar in Croatia, next to the Stari Grad Plain, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Set aside three hours, and add Zlatni Rat on Brac if there is time. May to July is the window.

gem:trevi.text: Trevi is a hill village in Italy, one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Museum of San Francesco and Palazzo Lucarini sit in the old centre, with the Tempietto del Clitunno nearby. May, June and September are the best months.

gem:vietri-sul-mare.text: Vietri sul Mare is a coastal village in Italy, one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Salerno next door holds the Castello di Arechi and the Giardino della Minerva, about four hours in all. May and June are the months.

gem:gradisca-d-isonzo.text: Gradisca d'Isonzo is a village in Italy on the Borghi piu belli d'Italia list, with Sabotin rising close by. The Chiesa di San Gottardo and Lago di Doberdo fill about four hours. May and June are the best months.

gem:bevagna.text: Bevagna is a village in Italy and one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia, its old centre laid over Mevania. Spello and the Cattedrale di San Feliciano are the nearby stops, about four hours together. April to June and September are best.

gem:montaione.text: Montaione is a hill village in Italy, one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Collegiata dei Santi Lorenzo e Leonardo and the Museo di Santa Verdiana are the main calls, about three hours. May and June are the months to come.

gem:bettona.text: Bettona is a small hill village in Italy on the Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. Two hours covers it, with the Pinacoteca Comunale di Deruta and the Museo regionale della Ceramica nearby. May, June and September are the best months.

gem:monzambano.text: Monzambano is a village in Italy on the Borghi piu belli d'Italia list, with Castellaro Lagusello close by. Forte Ardietti and Ponti sul Mincio round out about four hours. April to June and September are the best months.

gem:castelnuovo-di-porto.text: Castelnuovo di Porto is a village in Italy gathered below the Castello ducale Orsini. Two hours is enough, with Lucus Feroniae and Lake Martignano close by. May, June and September are the best months.

gem:percile.text: Percile is a tiny village in Italy inside the Parco Regionale Naturale dei Monti Lucretili. Two hours covers the village, with Horace's Villa and the Castello di Mandela nearby. May and June are the months to come.

gem:guarene.text: Guarene is a hill village in Italy and one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia, with Barbaresco close by. The Chiesa della Maddalena is the stop inside the village, and three hours covers the rest. May, June and September are best.

gem:portobuffole.text: Portobuffole is a small village in Italy on the Borghi piu belli d'Italia list, built around Piazza Grande. Villa Varda and Villa Toderini are the nearby houses to see, three hours in all. April to June and September suit best.

gem:cherasco.text: Cherasco is a village in Italy between the Langhe and Montferrat, carrying a Bandiera Arancione. The Castello di Pollenzo and the Chiesa di Sant'Andrea fill about three hours. May, June and September are the best months.

gem:verucchio.text: Verucchio is a hill village in Italy on the Borghi piu belli d'Italia list, close to Monte Titano over the border. The Three Towers of San Marino and the Guaita are a short drive off. May to July is the best stretch.

gem:summonte.text: Summonte is a mountain village in Italy, one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia, sitting under Monte Vergine. The Territorial Abbey of Montevergine leads, with Avellino nearby, about three hours in all. May and June are the months.

gem:orvinio.text: Orvinio is a village in Italy inside the Parco Regionale Naturale dei Monti Lucretili, with Monte Cervia close by. Santa Maria del Piano and Horace's Villa are the calls, and two hours is plenty. May and June are the months.

gem:montefiore-conca.text: Montefiore Conca is a hill village in Italy crowned by the Rocca di Montefiore. The village is one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia, and three hours covers the Rocca and the San Biagio Church. May to August is the season.

gem:san-giovanni-in-marignano.text: San Giovanni in Marignano is a village in Italy and one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Chiesa di San Pio V and the San Biagio Church lead, three hours in all, with Aquafan a short drive away. May and June are best.

gem:monte-grimano.text: Monte Grimano is a small village in Italy on the Borghi piu belli d'Italia list, close to Monte Titano. San Marino is the day out, with the Basilica di San Marino and the Guaita, about three hours. June to August is the season.

gem:aigueze.text: Aigueze is a stone village in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The caves lead here: Grotte de la Madeleine, Grotte de Saint-Marcel and Aven Marzal, about three hours. May, June and September are the best months.

gem:scandolara-ravara.text: Scandolara Ravara is a village on the plain in Italy, listed among the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Cella Dati, Motta Baluffi and Gussola make a loop of about three hours. April to June and September are the best months.

gem:villefranche-de-conflent.text: Villefranche-de-Conflent is a mountain village in France under Canigo, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Fort Liberia looks down on it and the Eglise Saint-Jacques stands in the centre, four hours in all. May and June are best.

gem:dartford.text: Dartford is a market town in the United Kingdom with good rail links and about ten hours of sights around it, from Hall Place and Gardens to Eynsford Castle. Rainham Marshes suits a slow morning. June to September is the season.

gem:la-roque-sur-ceze.text: La Roque-sur-Ceze is a hillside village in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, with the Pont Charles-Martel below. The Chartreuse de Valbonne is the other call, three hours in all. May, June and September are the months.

gem:montclus.text: Montclus is a small village in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, gathered under the Chateau de Montclus. Aven d'Orgnac and Goudargues are the nearby stops, about three hours. May, June and September are the best months.

gem:castelnou.text: Castelnou is a village in France under Canigo, listed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Chapelle de la Trinite and the Porte de Millars are the calls, about four hours with the drive. April to June and September are best.

gem:seguret.text: Seguret is a village in France on the slope under the Dentelles de Montmirail, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Vaison Cathedral and Mont Ventoux are close, and three hours covers the village. May, June and September are best.

gem:staines-upon-thames.text: Staines-upon-Thames is a market town in the United Kingdom on the Thames, with good rail links. Windsor Castle and Saint George's Chapel are the nearby draw, and the sights around add up to about ten hours. June to September is the season.

gem:romford.text: Romford is a market town in the United Kingdom, well served by rail. Valentines Park, Hare Hall and Rainham Marshes spread about ten hours of sights around it, with Barking close by. June to September is the best stretch.

gem:san-donato-in-poggio.text: San Donato in Poggio is a village in Italy in the hills of Chianti, one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Pieve di Sant'Agnese and the Chiesa di San Pietro a Cedda are the calls, about four hours. May, June and September are best.

gem:limone-sul-garda.text: Limone sul Garda is a lakeside village in Italy, home to barely more than a thousand people. Its short list of sights centres on Chiesa di San Giorgio and runs to about four hours, with Tremosine sul Garda on the cliff above. June to September is the season.

gem:crespi-d-adda.text: Crespi d'Adda is a historic village in Italy, listed by UNESCO and home to some six thousand people. Its streets take about four hours to walk, and Trezzo sull'Adda sits next door. May, June and September are the easiest months.

CTA.text: Catania is a baroque city on the coast of Sicily, in the shadow of Etna and on the UNESCO list. Castello Ursino, Palazzo Biscari and Teatro Massimo Bellini lead, and seventeen hours of sights means two full days. April and May are best.

ZTH.text: Zakynthos is a beach island in the Ionian Islands, with a marine park in its waters. Navagio draws the crowds, while Laganas and the islet of Marathonisi fill the rest of a short stay. May through July is the window.

GRZ.text: Graz is a university city in Austria with a UNESCO listed old town. Schlossberg rises over the roofs, and Eggenberg Castle and Grazer Dom round out seventeen hours of sights. Public transport is excellent, and May to September is the stretch.

TOS.text: Tromso is an Arctic town in Norway, some forty thousand people on the island of Tromsoya. Tromso Bridge, Tromsdalen kirke and Tromso Cathedral add up to six hours. July is the summer peak, and winter brings the northern lights.

HEL.text: Helsinki is a seafront city in Finland, modern and historic by turns. The sea fortress of Suomenlinna leads, with Helsinki Cathedral and Ateneum close behind, and seventeen hours of sights means two days. July and August are the months.

gem:dresden-saxon.text: Saxon Switzerland is walking country in Germany, sandstone towers in the Elbe Sandstone Mountains. Konigstein Fortress and Saxon Switzerland National Park lead about four hours of fixed sights. May to September is the season, and public transport is poor.

gem:zell-am-see.text: Lake Zell gives Zell am See its name, an alpine village in Austria with skiing on Kitzsteinhorn above. Castle Saalhof and the lakefront make three hours in town, and Schmittenhohe takes the rest of a day. June to August is the best stretch.

gem:interlaken.text: Interlaken is a village of five thousand between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz in Switzerland. Eiger, Monch and Jungfrau stand above it, and four hours covers the sights in town and in Unterseen. June to August is the peak.

gem:lecce.text: Lecce is a baroque city in the Puglia region of Italy, about eighty thousand people. Basilica di Santa Croce and Lecce Cathedral lead ten hours of sights, with Porta Rudiae marking the old edge of town. May and June come before the heat.

gem:paros.text: Paros is an island in the Cyclades, known for its beaches. Panagia Ekatontapyliani is the main monument, and Golden Beach and a hop across to Antiparos fill five hours or more. May to September is the run of good months.

gem:skaftafell.text: Skaftafell is a national park area in Iceland, set below the peaks of Vatnajokull. Svartifoss is the walk most people make, with Hvannadalshnukur and Oraefajokull behind it, five hours of marked sights. June to August is the season.

gem:sighisoara.text: Sighisoara is a medieval town in Romania with a UNESCO listed old centre. The Clock Tower of Sighisoara, the School on the Hill and Vlad Dracul House make about five hours. May to September is the run of good months.

gem:dingle.text: Dingle is a coastal village in Ireland, two thousand people under Mount Brandon. Conor Pass and Gallarus Oratory make the short list, three hours in all, with the Blasket Islands offshore. June to August is the season.

gem:auschwitz.text: Auschwitz is a memorial in Poland, a UNESCO site that people come to out of remembrance rather than sightseeing. Six hours covers a visit, often paired with Wieliczka. May to September are the usual months.

gem:lugano.text: Lugano is a lake city in Switzerland of some sixty thousand people. Monte San Salvatore looks down on it, the village of Gandria sits along the shore, and ten hours of sights fill a long weekend. May to September is the best run.

gem:postojna.text: Postojna Cave is the main sight of a small town in Slovenia, with Predjama Castle a short way off. The two make about six hours, and Lake Cerknica is an easy add. May to August is the season, and public transport is poor.

gem:bohemian-switzerland.text: Bohemian Switzerland is a national park of sandstone gorges in Czechia. Pravcicka brana leads about seven hours of walking, and Saxon Switzerland National Park lies next door. June to September is the season, and buses are few.

gem:menton.text: Menton is a quiet coastal town in France, right up against the border with Italy. Its own sights take an easy afternoon, and Monaco-Ville, La Condamine and the Oceanographic Museum are minutes away, six hours in all. April to June and September suit it best.

gem:avila.text: Avila is a medieval city in Spain, ringed by the Walls of Avila and listed by UNESCO. Avila Cathedral and the Real Monasterio de Santo Tomas fill most of nine hours of sights. May, June and September are the months to pick.

gem:beaune.text: Beaune is a wine town in France, in the middle of the Burgundy vineyards. Hospices de Beaune is the set piece, with Chateau de Savigny-les-Beaune and six hours of sights around it. May to September is the run, and trains and buses are thin.

gem:symi.text: Two thousand people live on Symi, an island in the Dodecanese near Rhodes. The Monastery of Saint Michael Archangel of Panormites is the set piece, and four hours covers the island sights. May to July and September are the best months.

gem:vis.text: Vis is a quiet island in Croatia, further out than the famous ones and known for its food. The Blue Grotto on Bisevo and the cove at Stiniva are the outings, about five hours of set sights. June to August is the season.

gem:tarifa.text: Tarifa is a windy town at the southern tip of Spain, with Africa in view across the water. Surf brings most people, along with Playa de Los Lances, the Castle of Tarifa and El Estrecho Natural Park, five hours in all. May to September is the run.

gem:otranto.text: Otranto is a small seaside town in Puglia with five thousand residents. Cattedrale di Otranto and Castello di Otranto stand a few steps apart, three hours of sights, and Spiaggia Alimini is up the coast. May to August is the season.

gem:stevns-klint.text: Stevns Klint is a UNESCO listed piece of coast in Denmark, walkable in an afternoon. Hojerup old church stands at the edge, with Stevns Lighthouse and Sankt Katharina Kirke close by, three hours in all. June to August is the season.

gem:orange-vaucluse.text: Orange is a town in France built around its Roman remains, thirty thousand people strong. The Roman Theatre of Orange and the Triumphal Arch of Orange carry the UNESCO listing and about six hours of sights. April, May and September are best.

gem:vezelay.text: Vezelay is a village in France of barely five hundred people, built around an abbey on the UNESCO list. Vezelay Abbey takes most of the three hours here, with Chateau de Bazoches a short drive on. June to September is the season.

gem:carnac.text: Carnac is a village on the coast of France, known for the standing stones lined up around it. The Carnac stones, Tumulus Saint-Michel and the Geant du Manio make about four hours, and the beaches are a short walk. June to September is the season.

gem:mycenae.text: Mycenae is an ancient site in Greece with a village beside it, on the UNESCO list. The Lion Gate and the Treasury of Atreus are the two things to see, three hours at most, and Tiryns and Nemea lie nearby. April and May are the best months.

gem:elba-portoferraio.text: Elba is an island in the Tuscan Archipelago, a national park on land and at sea. Monte Capanne rises over beaches such as Calamoresca, and Villa di San Martino adds the history, seven hours in all. June to August is the season.

gem:maratea.text: Maratea is a small coastal village in Italy, under three thousand people, with the Cristo Redentore statue standing above it. Its beaches and the Romito Cave fill about three hours. May and June are the months to come.

gem:landmannalaugar.text: Landmannalaugar is a hiking area in the mountains of Iceland, with Hekla and Torfajokull on its edges. Brennisteinsalda and Blahnjukur are the short climbs, Ofaerufoss and Eldgja the longer day, five hours of walking. June to August is the season.

gem:peneda-geres.text: Peneda-Geres National Park is a mountain park in Portugal, walked more than driven. Vilarinho das Furnas, Santuario de Sao Bento da Porta Aberta and Termas do Geres are the fixed points, about five hours. May, June and September are best.

gem:corvin-castle.text: Hunedoara is a city in Romania of about seventy thousand, built around Hunyad Castle. The castle takes up most of six hours, with Strei Church a short drive away. May to September is the run of good months.

gem:calella-de-palafrugell.text: A fishing village of fewer than a thousand people, Calella de Palafrugell sits on the coast in Spain. Port Bo and Platja del Canadell are where everyone gathers, and four hours covers the coves. May to July is the season.

gem:zumaia.text: Zumaia is a coastal town in Spain, at the centre of the Basque Coast Geopark. Its beaches lead, with Zarautz next along the shore and the Ekain cave inland, six hours of sights. June to September is the season.

gem:llanes.text: Llanes is a coastal town in Spain, thirteen thousand people between the Sierra de Cuera and the sea. Playa de Gulpiyuri and the Tower of Llanes lead six hours of sights, with Picos de Europa under thirty km inland. June to September is the season.

gem:as-catedrais.text: Praia das Catedrais is a protected beach in Spain, a natural monument on the shore. Its sands and the Ouro River take about four hours, with the Basilica of Saint Martin de Mondonedo inland. June to September is the season.

gem:trujillo.text: Trujillo is a medieval town in Spain, its skyline dominated by the Castillo de Trujillo and Alcazar de los Bejarano. The Rollo de Trujillo and Palacio de Carvajal-Vargas complete the old quarter. Its sights take four hours, best in May.

gem:guadalupe.text: Guadalupe is a small village in Spain, built around the Royal Monastery of Saint Mary of Guadalupe. Two hours is enough for the monastery and the village, best done in May. Villuercas and the Sierra de Altamira lie nearby for those with more time.

gem:caminito-del-rey.text: Caminito del Rey is a village in Spain built around hiking and nature, with Cueva de Ardales and Bobastro leading its sights. Two hours covers the highlights, best in April or May.

gem:cabo-de-gata.text: Cabo de Gata is a coastal area in Spain, its shoreline protected as the Cabo de Gata-Nijar Natural Park. Playa de Monsul and Playa de los Genoveses are the beaches to see. Six hours covers a full loop of the park, best in April, May, June or September.

gem:deia.text: Deia is an art village in Spain, set within the Serra de Tramuntana mountains. Son Marroig is the sight to see in the village itself, with Palma Cathedral, Bellver Castle and Port de Soller nearby. The sights take four hours, best from June to August.

gem:sutjeska.text: Sutjeska is a mountainous area in Bosnia and Herzegovina, protected as Sutjeska National Park. Perucica and Maglic lead the sights, with Zelengora and Black Lake nearby. Set five hours aside for the highlights, best from June to August.

gem:eisenach.text: Eisenach is a historic town in Germany, with the Wartburg as its landmark sight. Lutherhaus Eisenach and Bach House add to the heritage, and Sankt Georg and Hainich sit nearby for more time. Six hours covers the sights, best from June to September.

gem:gaeta.text: Gaeta is a coastal town in Italy, its skyline marked by Gaeta cathedral and the Aurunci Mountains behind it. Santissima Annunziata, the Villa of Tiberius and Monte Petrella round out the sights. The sights take six hours in all, best from May to August.

gem:ripon.text: Ripon is a market town in the United Kingdom, built around Ripon Cathedral. Fountains Abbey and Studley Royal Park lead the sights nearby, with Knaresborough Castle and Brimham Rocks further out. Six hours covers it all, best from June to August.

gem:lanark.text: Lanark is a historic town in the United Kingdom, with New Lanark as its best known sight. Craignethan Castle and Douglas Castle add two more, with the Falls of Clyde and Cleghorn Glen nearby. Its sights take six hours, best from June to August.

gem:oviedo.text: Oviedo is a city in Spain, its top sights led by Santa Maria del Naranjo and San Miguel de Lillo. San Tirso and the Fuente de Foncalada round out the old town. Ten hours takes in all the sights, best from June to September.

gem:kingston-upon-thames.text: Kingston upon Thames is a market town in the United Kingdom, close to Hampton Court Palace and Kew Gardens. Twickenham Stadium, Richmond Park and Kew Palace add variety nearby. The sights take six hours, best from June to September.

gem:bruhl.text: Bruhl is a town in Germany, best known for Phantasialand among its sights. Cologne Cathedral, the Hohenzollern Bridge and the Wallraf-Richartz Museum lie nearby in Cologne, along with Lanxess Arena. Six hours covers it all, best from May to September.

gem:richmond.text: Richmond is a market town in the United Kingdom, with Richmond Castle at its center. Middleham Castle, the Georgian Theatre Royal, Aske Hall and Easby Abbey fill out a visit nearby. Set five hours aside for the sights, best from June to August.

gem:portoferraio.text: Portoferraio is a coastal town in Italy, the main port of Elba in the Tuscan Archipelago. Mount Capanne rises above the island, and Palmaiola and Spiaggia Di Sansone give reason to stay near the water. Six hours covers the sights, best in May or June.

gem:wissembourg.text: Wissembourg is a historic town in France, with Chateau du Fleckenstein and Berwartstein Castle nearby. Burg Guttenberg, Hohe Derst and Bobenthaler Knopf add three more nearby stops. The sights take six hours, best from May to September.

gem:saltaire.text: Saltaire is a historic town in the United Kingdom, recognized as a UNESCO site. The National Science and Media Museum, Bradford Cathedral and Leeds Cathedral lie nearby, along with Bramley. Six hours covers the sights, best from June to August.

gem:l-escala.text: L'Escala is a coastal town in Spain, next to Empuries. Montgri and the Medes Islands add to the sights, with Cala Montgo the beach to choose from. The sights take six hours, best from May to July.

gem:denia.text: Denia is a coastal town in Spain, overlooked by the Castell de Denia. The Church of Saint Bartholomew and Hemeroskopeion add historic interest, and Platja de la Marineta Cassiana is the beach nearby. Six hours covers the sights, best in May or June.

gem:franeker.text: Franeker is a historic town in the Netherlands, home to the Eise Eisinga Planetarium. Museum Martena and Harlingen Lighthouse are worth the stop, with Arkens and Achlumer Molen further out. Six hours takes in the sights, best from June to August.

gem:santa-eularia-des-riu.text: Santa Eularia des Riu sits on the island of Ibiza, a coastal town in Spain. Ibiza Cathedral overlooks the old town, and Cala Llonga and Es Canar are the beaches most visitors choose. Its sights take five hours, best from May to August.

gem:torrevieja.text: Torrevieja is a coastal city in Spain, with the Torre del Moro among its historic sights. Torre de La Mata and Cabo Roig extend along the coast, and the Museo del Mar y de la Sal sits nearby. Its sights take eight hours, best in May or June.

gem:piombino.text: Piombino is a coastal town in Italy, near Populonia and its archaeological museum. Palmaiola, Cerboli and Topi Rock lie offshore, and Calamoresca is the beach nearby. The sights take six hours, best in May or June.

gem:caernarfon.text: Caernarfon is a historic town in the United Kingdom, built around Caernarfon Castle. Snowdon and Llyn Llydaw lie nearby, and the Menai Suspension Bridge and Britannia Bridge are close by too. Six hours covers the sights, best from June to August.

gem:perigueux.text: Perigueux is a historic town in France, centered on Perigueux Cathedral. Vesunna and the Musee d'art et d'archeologie du Perigord add depth, with Chateau des Bories further out. Six hours covers the sights, best in May, June or September.

gem:naumburg.text: Naumburg is a historic town in Germany, built around Naumburg Cathedral. Rudelsburg and Burg Schonburg lie nearby, and the Romanisches Haus in Bad Kosen and Nietzsche-Haus round out the sights. Six hours is enough for the sights, best from May to September.

gem:rochester.text: Rochester is a market town in the United Kingdom, dominated by Rochester Castle and Rochester Cathedral. Upnor Castle and Snodland are within reach, and Canvey Island makes for a longer day out. The sights take six hours, best from June to September.

gem:amersfoort.text: Amersfoort is a historic city in the Netherlands, with the Koppelpoort marking the old center. Onze Lieve Vrouwetoren and Mondriaanhuis add to the sights, with Soestdijk Palace a short trip away. Ten hours takes in it all, best from May to August.

gem:grottammare.text: Grottammare is a coastal town in Italy, its Santa Maria della Marina cathedral facing the sea. Teatro Luigi Mercantini and Ripatransone Cathedral add to the old town, with Porto d'Ascoli nearby. Its sights take five hours, best in May, June or September.

gem:frome.text: Frome is a market town in the United Kingdom, close to Stourhead. Longleat, King Alfred's Tower, Nunney Castle and Beckington Castle fill out a visit to the area. Six hours covers the sights, best from June to September.

gem:villajoyosa.text: Villajoyosa is a coastal town in Spain, with Platja de Llevant as its main beach. Terra Mitica and the Canelobre Caves make for a longer day, with Puig Campana and Aitana rising inland. The sights take six hours, best from May to July.

gem:calatayud.text: Calatayud is a historic town in Spain, with Bilbilis nearby among its sights. San Pedro de los Francos and the Collegiate church of Santa Maria anchor the old town, with Segeda further out. Six hours covers the sights, best April, May, September or October.

gem:waltham-abbey.text: Waltham Abbey is a market town in the United Kingdom, with Cheshunt Lake and Highams Park Lake close by. Alexandra Palace and the Copper Box Arena lie further afield for a longer day out. Six hours covers the sights, best from June to September.
