gem:sant-antoni-de-portmany.text: Sant Antoni de Portmany is a coastal town in Spain, on the island of Ibiza. Es Vedra and Cala Salada are the sights to seek out, with Sa Talaiassa rising inland and Cala Comte a short trip along the coast. Its sights take five hours, best from May to August.

gem:arendal.text: Arendal is a coastal town in Norway, on the water near Tromoya. Tromoy Church and Hisoy Church are the sights to see, and Merdo and Lille Torungen fyr lie further out on the coast. Six hours covers the sights, best in June or July.

gem:salou.text: Salou is a coastal town in Spain, home to Ferrari Land and the Shambhala roller coaster. Torre Vella de Salou overlooks the old port, with Colonia Iulia Urbs Triumphalis Tarraco beneath it. Six hours covers the sights, best from May to July.

gem:karlsruhe.text: Karlsruhe is a city in Germany, its art scene centered on the Staatliche Kunsthalle Karlsruhe. The Center for Art and Media adds to the cultural sights, with Karlsruhe Zoo and Durlach nearby. Ten hours takes in it all, best from May to September.

gem:riccione.text: Riccione is a coastal town in Italy, with Villa Mussolini among its own sights. Tempio Malatestiano, the Arch of Augustus and Ponte d'Augusto lie nearby, along with Colombarone. Set five hours aside for the sights, best in May or June.

gem:clausthal-zellerfeld.text: Clausthal-Zellerfeld is a historic town in Germany, known for the Upper Harz Water Regale. Rammelsberg and Lichtenstein Cave add to the sights, with the Gustav-Adolf-Stabkirche and Hubichenstein nearby. Six hours covers the sights, best from June to August.

gem:saint-remy-de-provence.text: Saint-Remy-de-Provence is a historic town in France, next to Glanum. The Monastery of Saint-Paul-de-Mausole and Alpilles add to the sights, with Chateau des Baux and Mont Gaussier further afield. Six hours covers the sights, best in April, May or September.

gem:tabor.text: Tabor is a town in Czechia, part of a UNESCO Global Geopark. Chynovska jeskyne, Kozi Hradek and the Stadlec Suspension Bridge lead six hours of sights, best planned between May and September. Jordan lake sits by the old town, but transport is poor.

gem:castro-urdiales.text: Castro-Urdiales is a coastal town in Spain, listed as a Conjunto historico for its historic center. The Church of Santa Maria de la Asuncion and the Casa de los Chelines lead five hours of sights, best kept to June through September.

gem:noyers.text: Noyers is a village in France, honored among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Fosse Dionne and the Chateau d'Ancy-le-Franc lead three hours of sights, best visited June through September despite poor public transport.

gem:estepona.text: Estepona is a city on the coast of Spain, its old watchtowers led by Torre del Padron and Torre del Salto de la Mora. Sierra Bermeja adds a scenic finish, and the sights take about seven hours, best planned for May, June or September with good transport links.

gem:zdar-nad-sazavou.text: Zdar nad Sazavou is a town in Czechia and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Pilgrimage Church of Saint John of Nepomuk anchors six hours of sights amid the Zdarske vrchy hills, best seen in June, July or August with good public transport.

gem:otley.text: Otley is a town in the United Kingdom, with Harewood House and Bradford Cathedral among the sights nearby. Six hours cover the area, best timed for June, July or August thanks to good public transport.

gem:grassington.text: Grassington is a village in the United Kingdom, within a national park landscape. Pen-y-ghent and Skipton Castle lead three hours of sights, best kept to June, July or August given poor public transport.

gem:beroun.text: Beroun is a town in Czechia and a UNESCO Global Geopark, anchored by Karlstejn and the Koneprusy Caves. Tetinske skaly and Doutnac round out six hours of sights, best planned for May through September despite poor public transport.

gem:menerbes.text: Menerbes is a village in France, part of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Pont Julien and Senanque Abbey headline three hours of sights nearby, best fit into May, June or September.

gem:cesenatico.text: Cesenatico is a coastal town in Italy, with the Cesena Cathedral and Biblioteca Malatestiana among the sights nearby in Cesena. The area takes about five hours to see, best visited in May or June despite limited public transport.

gem:taggia.text: Taggia is a town in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Sanremo Casino and Teatro Ariston lie nearby, and six hours cover the sights, best planned for May through September despite poor public transport.

gem:zwolle.text: Zwolle is a historic city in the Netherlands. Sassenpoort and the Peperbus lead ten hours of sights, with the Veluwemeer and Ketelmeer lakes nearby, best timed for June through August given good public transport.

gem:cambrai.text: Cambrai is a town in France and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Cambrai Cathedral and the Abbaye de Vaucelles lead six hours of sights, best planned between May and September with good public transport.

gem:carrara.text: Carrara is a city in Italy, recognized in the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. Carrara Cathedral and the Chiesa del Carmine lead ten hours of sights, with Massa Cathedral nearby, best visited May through August thanks to good public transport.

gem:lorsch.text: Lorsch is a town in Germany and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, centered on the Abbey and Altenmunster of Lorsch. Worms Cathedral and Worms Synagogue lie nearby, and six hours cover the sights, best planned between May and September with good public transport.

gem:bellaria-igea-marina.text: Bellaria-Igea Marina is a coastal town in Italy, with the Tempio Malatestiano and the Arch of Augustus nearby in Rimini. Its own sights take about five hours, best visited in May or June, though public transport is limited.

gem:lovere.text: Lovere is a village in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia on the shore of Lake Iseo. Riva di Solto and Monte Pora lie nearby, and four hours cover the village itself, best kept to June through September despite poor public transport.

gem:chioggia.text: Chioggia is a coastal town in Italy. Chioggia Cathedral and the Museo Civico della Laguna Sud lead five hours of sights, with Pellestrina nearby, best visited May through August despite limited public transport.

gem:conegliano.text: Conegliano is a town in Italy and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Le Colline del Prosecco and CastelBrando lead six hours of sights, best visited in May, June or September with good public transport.

gem:zonnebeke.text: Zonnebeke is a town in Belgium and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, tied to the Third Battle of Ypres and the Menin Gate. Six hours of sights end with In Flanders Fields and Saint George's Memorial Church, best visited June through August.

gem:montegridolfo.text: Montegridolfo is a small village in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Monte Titano and the Cathedral of Urbino make good day trips nearby, and three hours cover the village itself, best visited in May or June, though public transport is poor.

gem:lerici.text: Lerici is a coastal town in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Porto Venere and the Isola Palmaria lie nearby, and six hours cover the sights, best visited May through July despite poor public transport.

gem:montagnana.text: Montagnana is a town in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Villa Pojana and Villa Pisani lie nearby, and four hours cover the town itself, best visited in April, May, June, September or October.

gem:alassio.text: Alassio is a coastal town in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Villa Grock and the Museo navale lead six hours of sights, with Albenga Cathedral and the Toirano Caves nearby, best visited May, June, July or September.

gem:bad-ems.text: Bad Ems is a spa town in Germany, part of The Great Spa Towns of Europe. Marksburg and Burg Lahneck castles lie nearby, and six hours cover the sights, best planned between May and September with good public transport.

gem:montecatini-terme.text: Montecatini-Terme is a spa town in Italy, part of The Great Spa Towns of Europe. Pistoia Cathedral and the Paper Museum in Pescia lie nearby, and six hours cover the wider sights, best visited May, June or September with good public transport.

gem:tongeren.text: Tongeren is a town in Belgium, on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List. The Basilica of Our Lady and the Gallo-Roman Museum lead six hours of sights, best visited between May and September with good public transport.

gem:alta.text: Alta is a town in Norway and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Northern Lights Cathedral and Alta Museum lead four hours of sights, best visited in July with good public transport.

gem:saint-cyr-sur-mer.text: Saint-Cyr-sur-Mer is a coastal town in France, recognized among Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. Cap Canaille and Sainte-Baume lead five hours of sights, with Anse Gameou and Figuerolles beaches nearby, best visited June through August.

gem:bard.text: Bard is a small village in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Fort Bard anchors four hours of sights, with Issogne and Verres Castle nearby, best visited June through September despite poor public transport.

gem:nieuw-bergen.text: Nieuw-Bergen is a village in the Netherlands, on the edge of De Maasduinen National Park. Kasteel Bleijenbeek and the Overloon War Museum lead four hours of sights, best visited May through September despite poor public transport.

gem:sodertalje.text: Sodertalje is a city in Sweden, set on the edge of the Sodermanland region. Igelsta Bridge and the Marcus Wallenberg Hallen lead ten hours of sights, best visited June through August with good public transport.

gem:huskvarna.text: Huskvarna is a town in Sweden, part of a UNESCO Man and the Biosphere reserve. Sofiakyrkan and Bymarkskyrkan lead six hours of sights, with Jonkoping Catholic Church nearby, best visited June through August despite poor public transport.

gem:vila-do-conde.text: Vila do Conde is a coastal town in Portugal. The Monastery of Rates and Igreja Matriz de Vila do Conde lead six hours of sights, with Salgueira Beach and Rio Alto Beach nearby, best visited June through August despite limited public transport.

gem:gunzenhausen.text: Gunzenhausen is a town in Germany and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Grosser Brombachsee and Altmuhlsee lead six hours of sights amid the Franconian Jura, best visited June through September with good public transport.

gem:cerveteri.text: Cerveteri is a town in Italy and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Necropolis Banditaccia and Castello Orsini-Odescalchi lead five hours of sights, with Lake Bracciano nearby, best visited May through August with good public transport.

gem:baiona.text: Baiona is a coastal town in Spain, part of the Conjunto historico grouping. The Cies Islands and Monterreal Castle lead six hours of sights, with Praia de Samil and Playa de Rodas nearby, best visited June through August despite limited public transport.

gem:alfeld.text: Alfeld is a town in Germany and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, home to the Fagus Factory. Hildesheim Forest and Steinberg lie nearby, and six hours cover the sights, best planned between May and September with good public transport.

gem:hoxter.text: Hoxter is a town in Germany and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, centered on the Princely Abbey of Corvey. Solling and the Lippe Uplands lie nearby, and six hours cover the sights, best visited June through September with good public transport.

gem:marina-di-massa.text: Marina di Massa is a coastal town in Italy, beneath the Apuan Alps. Massa Cathedral lies nearby, and six hours cover the wider sights, including Carrara Cathedral and Pietrasanta Cathedral, best visited May through July despite limited public transport.

gem:saint-die-des-vosges.text: Saint-Die-des-Vosges is a historic town in France, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Saint-Die Cathedral and Col des Bagenelles lead the sights, with six hours enough to see them. It is best visited between June and September.

gem:chinchon.text: Chinchon is a historic village in Spain, designated a Conjunto historico. Royal Palace of Aranjuez and Casa del Labrador top the sights, about three hours in total. It is best visited in May or September, given the limited public transport.

gem:montesarchio.text: Montesarchio is a historic town in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Arch of Trajan and Santa Sofia Church top the sights, with Benevento Cathedral also nearby. It takes about five hours in all, best enjoyed in May or June.

gem:cambrils.text: Cambrils is a historic beach town on the coast of Spain. Ferrari Land and PortAventura Park lead the sights, with Torre Vella de Salou nearby in Salou. Six hours covers the rides, best planned for May, June or July.

gem:ballenstedt.text: Ballenstedt is a historic town in Germany, set among castle and nature sights. Falkenstein Castle and Teufelsmauer lead the list, with Quedlinburg Abbey a short trip away. Six hours covers the highlights, best from June to September.

gem:sedan.text: Sedan is a historic town in France, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Chateau de Sedan anchors the sights, with Bouillon Castle and the Canal des Ardennes also within reach. Six hours covers the highlights, best planned for June through September.

gem:luz-saint-sauveur.text: Luz-Saint-Sauveur is a small village in France, deep in the Pyrenees National Park. Col du Tourmalet and Pic du Midi de Bigorre top the sights, with Lac Bleu d'Ilheou and Lac d'Oredon nearby. It takes about three hours to see the village, best done from June to September.

gem:starigrad.text: Starigrad is a small coastal village in Croatia, on the edge of Paklenica. The Church of Holy Cross and the Novigrad Sea lead the sights nearby, with Vaganski vrh rising above. Two hours covers the village, best visited in May or June.

gem:la-ciotat.text: La Ciotat is a coastal town in France, close to Cassis and the Calanques National Park. Cap Canaille and the Cosquer Cave lead the sights, with the beaches of Port-Pin and En-Vau nearby. It takes about five hours to cover the highlights, best from June to August.

gem:semmering.text: Semmering is a small village in Austria, designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Schneeberg and Rax rise above the Semmering Pass, with Villa Wartholz among the sights. It takes about four hours to see the village, best visited from June to August.

gem:komarno.text: Komarno is a historic town in Slovakia, on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List. Fortress of Komarno and the Museum of Danube Komarno lead the sights. Six hours covers the highlights, best in May, June or September.

gem:calais.text: Calais is a historic coastal city in France. Les Bourgeois de Calais and the Calais Lighthouse lead the sights, with Cap Blanc Nez and the Eglise Notre-Dame de Calais also worth the trip. It takes about nine hours to cover the city, best from June to August.

gem:vlasim.text: Vlasim is a historic town in Czechia, part of a UNESCO Global Geopark. Vlasim Castle and Cesky Sternberk Castle lead the sights, with the Svihov Reservoir and Blanik mountain nearby. Six hours covers the highlights, best from May to September.

gem:pernes-les-fontaines.text: Pernes-les-Fontaines is a historic town in France, honored among Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. Carpentras Cathedral and its Arch lead the sights, with Senanque Abbey also within reach. Six hours covers the area, best in April, May or September.

gem:san-giljan.text: San Giljan is a historic beach town in Malta, on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List. Valletta and Mdina lie within reach, along with Golden Bay. Six hours covers the highlights, best from May to August.

gem:soesterberg.text: Soesterberg is a small village in the Netherlands, close to Utrecht and its Centraal Museum. Castle de Haar and Dorestad are also within reach, along with the Eemmeer and Henschotermeer lakes. It takes about four hours to see the village, best from June to August.

gem:alcoceber.text: Alcoceber is a small beach village in Spain, backed by the Serra de la Vall d'Angel. Platja del Carregador and Platja del Moro lead its beaches, with Peniscola Castle a short trip away. It takes about three hours to see the village, best from March to May or in October.

gem:breda.text: Breda is a historic city in the Netherlands, built around the Grote kerk and the Sint-Antoniuskathedraal. The Koepelgevangenis and the Begijnhof round out the sights, with Belcrum Beach nearby. Ten hours covers the city, best from May to September.

gem:le-locle.text: Le Locle is a historic town in Switzerland, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Col des Roches and the Creux du Van lead the sights, with Lake Neuchatel and Mont Racine also nearby. Six hours covers the highlights, best from June to August.

gem:laredo.text: Laredo is a historic beach town in Spain, designated a Conjunto historico. The Santona, Victoria and Joyel Marshes Natural Park lies nearby, along with the Monasterio de Montehano and the beach of Playa de Berria. Six hours covers the highlights, best from June to September.

gem:roquetas-de-mar.text: Roquetas de Mar is a historic beach city in Spain. Castillo de Santa Ana and Iglesia de San Benito lead the sights. It takes about seven hours to cover the highlights, best from March to May or in October.

gem:zuidhoven.text: Zuidhoven is a small village in the Netherlands, near Dordrecht, the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen and the Euromast, with De Biesbosch National Park and the Erasmusbrug also close by. It takes about four hours to see the highlights, best planned for June, July or August.

gem:burriana.text: Burriana is a historic beach town in Spain, designated a Conjunto historico. The Santa Quiteria Bridge and the Iglesia de San Jaime lead its own sights, with Castello Cathedral and El Fadri a short trip away. Six hours covers the highlights, best from April to June.

gem:vevey.text: Vevey is a historic town in Switzerland, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Montreux and Chillon lie close by, along with Lavaux and the villages of Puidoux and Rivaz. Six hours covers the area, best from May to September.

gem:lemmer.text: Lemmer is a historic town in the Netherlands, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Sloten and the Hervormde kerk lead the sights, with the Tjasker Zandpoel and Slotermeer lake nearby. Six hours covers the highlights, best from June to August.

gem:hornu.text: Hornu is a historic town in Belgium, home to the Major Mining Sites of Wallonia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Neolithic flint mines of Spiennes are also within reach. Six hours covers the highlights, best from May to September.

gem:somoskoujfalu.text: Somoskoujfalu is a small village in Hungary, part of a UNESCO Global Geopark. Somoska Castle and the Castle of Salgo lead the sights, with Karancs mountain and Salgotarjan also nearby. It takes about three hours to see the village, best from May to September.

gem:hinterbruhl.text: Hinterbruhl is a historic village in Austria, near Vienna and its Belvedere and Hofburg Palace. Baden and the Vienna State Opera house are also within reach, along with the Erlebnisbad Leobersdorf. It takes about four hours to see the village, best from May to September.

gem:torres-vedras.text: Torres Vedras is a historic coastal town in Portugal. Castelo de Torres Vedras and the Castro of Zambujal lead the sights, with the Leonel Trindade Municipal Museum and Praia do Guincho also nearby. Six hours covers the highlights, best from May to September.

gem:salasu-de-sus.text: Salasu de Sus is a small village in Romania, part of a UNESCO Global Geopark in the Retezat Mountains. Bucura Lake and Peleaga lead the sights, with Ulpia Traiana Sarmizegetusa also within reach. It takes about three hours to see the village, best from May to September.

gem:watford.text: Watford is a historic city in the United Kingdom, designated a Market town. Bhaktivedanta Manor and Hilfield Castle lead the sights, with Harrow & Wealdstone and Hatch End also nearby. Ten hours covers the area, best from June to September.

gem:ronciglione.text: Ronciglione is a historic village in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Palazzo Farnese and the Villa Giustiniani Odescalchi lead the sights, with Lake Bracciano and Lake Vico nearby. It takes about three hours to see the village, best in May, June or September.

gem:cervignano-del-friuli.text: Cervignano del Friuli is a historic town in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Aquileia and Palmanova draw visitors close by, along with the Museo Archeologico Nazionale. Six hours covers the area, best in May or June.

gem:neive.text: Neive is a small historic village in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Chiesa della Maddalena and Cattedrale di San Lorenzo lead its sights, with Barbaresco just next door. It takes about three hours to see the village, best in May, June or September.

gem:massa-martana.text: Massa Martana is a small historic village in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Santa Maria in Pantano and the Santuario dell'Amore Misericordioso lead the sights, along the Via Flaminia. It takes about three hours to see the village, best in May, June or September.

gem:valeggio-sul-mincio.text: Valeggio sul Mincio is a historic town in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Castello Scaligero and Castellaro Lagusello lead the sights. Six hours covers the highlights, best from April to June or in September.

gem:frontino.text: Frontino is a tiny historic village in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Monte Carpegna and Sasso Simone rise nearby, with Monte Titano also in view. Two hours covers the village, best in June, July or August.

gem:la-garde-adhemar.text: La Garde-Adhemar is a small historic village in France, honored among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Eglise Saint-Michel de La Garde-Adhemar sits near Saint-Restitut. It takes about three hours to see the village, best in May, June or September.

gem:la-roche-sur-foron.text: La Roche-sur-Foron is a historic town in France, honored among Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. Chateau de La Roche-sur-Foron leads the sights, with Pointe Percee and Le Mole rising nearby. Six hours covers the highlights, best from June to September.

gem:lussan.text: Lussan is a small historic village in France, honored among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Chateau de Lussan and the La Leque menhir lead the sights, with Fontareches and the Guidon du Bouquet nearby. Two hours covers the village, best in May, June or September.

gem:rochecorbon.text: Rochecorbon is a village of barely three thousand people in France, listed among the Petites Cites de Caractere. Tours sits next door, and its chateau and the Chateau de Plessis-lez-Tours are enough for four hours, best walked between May and September.

gem:castelfranco-piandisco.text: Castelfranco Piandisco is a village in Italy on the list of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Its four hours of sights run from the Monastero di San Salvatore a Soffena to the Palazzo Pretorio. May, June or September are the months, and transport is thin.

gem:bradford.text: Bradford is a city in the United Kingdom and part of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. Saltaire and Bradford City Hall head a list long enough to fill about seventeen hours, with Rodley Nature Reserve for a break. June to August is the season.

gem:frascati.text: Frascati is a small town in Italy with Lake Albano and Lake Nemi close by. Six hours covers the Papal summer residence, Villa Torlonia and the Church of the Gesu, and good public transport makes May, June or September easy going.

gem:purmerend.text: Purmerend is a city of eighty thousand in the Netherlands, ringed by smaller places such as Kwadijk, Beemster and Ilpendam. The Sint Nicolaaskerk and the Wormer- en Jisperveld fill about ten hours, and June through August is when it all opens up.

gem:porto-empedocle.text: Porto Empedocle is a port town in Italy, set beside the ancient ground of Akragas. The Temple of Concordia and Scala dei Turchi are the two that matter, about six hours between them, with April or May the months to pick.

gem:saint-savin.text: Saint-Savin is a village of a thousand people in France with a UNESCO World Heritage Site listing. The Abbey Church of Saint-Savin sur Gartempe is the reason to stop, with the Pont de Saint-Savin nearby, and three hours does it from June to September.

AGP.text: Malaga is a large coastal city in Andalucia, Spain, where the Alcazaba of Malaga and the Castillo de Gibralfaro look out over the beaches. The Centre Pompidou Malaga covers the modern side, and the sights run to seventeen hours across May to September.

BIO.text: Bilbao is the main city of the Basque Country in Spain, and the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao is what most people come for. Zubizuri, the Basilica of Begona and San Mames Stadium fill out seventeen hours, and June through September is the best stretch.

TER.text: Terceira is one of the volcanic islands of the Azores, out in the Atlantic and part of Portugal. Algar do Carvao and Monte Brasil handle the landscape, the Se Cathedral of Angra do Heroismo the history, and five hours does it, June through August.

SKG.text: Thessaloniki runs along the water in Greece, a UNESCO World Heritage Site layered with Roman and Byzantine remains. The White Tower of Thessaloniki, the Arch of Galerius and Rotunda and Hagia Sophia fill seventeen hours, and April and May stay mild.

HER.text: Heraklion is the main city of Crete, in Greece, with beaches close and ruins a short way inland. Knossos is the headline and the Heraklion Archaeological Museum the other half of the day. Ten hours covers it, anywhere from May to September.

BIQ.text: Biarritz is a surf town on the Atlantic coast of France, with a Basque accent and a luxury streak. The Hotel du Palais sets the tone, the Aquarium de Biarritz and Bayonne Cathedral fill the rest, and six hours does it. May through September for the sea.

AES.text: Alesund is a coastal city in Norway where the fjords begin. Jugendstilsenteret covers the art side, Alesund Church and Volsdalen kirke sit a short walk apart, and Slogen rises nearby, which adds up to nine hours between June and August.

gem:delft.text: Delft is a canal town in the Netherlands, known everywhere for its blue and white ceramics. The Nieuwe Kerk Delft is the landmark, with the Mauritshuis and Madurodam a short hop away in the neighbouring city. Ten hours, easiest June to August.

gem:bamberg.text: Bamberg is a town of seventy thousand in Upper Franconia, Germany, listed whole by UNESCO and serious about its beer. Bamberg Cathedral and the Altes Rathaus are the set pieces, eight hours in all, and May to September is the easy stretch.

gem:saint-malo.text: Saint-Malo is a walled port on the Brittany coast of France, and the first thing to do is walk the ramparts. Fort National, Solidor Tower and Saint-Malo Cathedral come next, then Cezembre out beyond them. Ten hours in all, June through September.

gem:cotswolds.text: The Cotswolds are hills and market towns in England, built from golden limestone. Arlington Row and Broadway Tower are the ones everyone photographs, with Chedworth Roman Villa for something older, three hours in all. June to September, and bring a car.

gem:galway-cliffs.text: Galway is a coastal city in Ireland with music at its centre and a European Capital of Culture title behind it. The Spanish Arch, Galway Cathedral and Menlo Castle fill eight hours, and the Cliffs of Moher draw people down the coast in high summer.

gem:montreux.text: Montreux is a lakeside town in Switzerland with mountains straight behind it. Chillon, the castle out on the water, is the one not to skip and Rochers de Naye handles the view. Six hours covers both, with May to September the best of it.

gem:krka.text: Skradinski Buk is the run of waterfalls at the heart of Krka National Park, a protected stretch of river in Croatia. It takes about four hours to walk, and May or June is the moment. Sibenik Cathedral and Zlarin are close by for a longer stay.

gem:honfleur.text: Honfleur is a harbour town in Normandy, France, on the list of Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. Maisons Satie is the oddest thing in it, and the Pont de Normandie runs across to Le Havre Cathedral and the MuMa, five hours in all from June to August.

gem:mons-klint.text: Mons Klint is a protected stretch of coast at Mon, in Denmark, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Liselund lies just inland, with Somarkedyssen, Nyord and Aborrebjerg all within reach. Six hours covers them, with June to August the pick of the year.

gem:cassis.text: Cassis is a fishing port in Provence, southern France, wedged between the headland of Cap Canaille and the Calanques National Park. Port-Pin and En-Vau are the coves worth the walk, about six hours all told. June to August, and a car helps.

gem:merida.text: Merida is a city in Spain built on top of Emerita Augusta, its Roman remains listed by UNESCO. The Puente Romano and the Acueducto de los Milagros lead, with the Alcazaba of Merida after them, nine hours in total. April or May suit best.

gem:ile-de-re.text: Ile de Re is a quiet island off the coast of France, reached by way of La Rochelle. Saint-Martin-de-Re, once besieged, holds the Ernest Cognacq Museum, and the Saint Catherine Church of Loix is worth the detour. Six hours, June to September.

gem:gorlitz.text: Gorlitz is an unusually intact old town in Germany, where the Gorlitz Department Store and the station are attractions in their own right. Landeskrone rises above it and Berzdorfer See is close. Ten hours, and May through September is the stretch.

gem:stein-am-rhein.text: Stein am Rhein sits on the Rhine in Switzerland, a medieval town kept almost whole. Reichenau Island and the Rhine Falls are both short trips out, and the town itself takes four hours. June through September is the pleasant run.

gem:bad-gastein.text: Bad Gastein is a thermal spa village in the Salzburg region of Austria, set high in the Alps. Hochalmspitze and Ankogel stand above it, the Tauernbahn runs through, and skiing fills the winter. Its own sights take three hours, best June to August.

gem:litomysl.text: Litomysl is a renaissance town of ten thousand in Eastern Bohemia, Czechia, carrying a UNESCO World Heritage Site listing. Portmoneum is the strangest thing in it, with Nedosinsky haj and Mastale close by. Six hours, and May to September is the season.

gem:transfagarasan.text: Transfagarasan is a mountain road in Romania, cut over the Fagaras Mountains and open only in the warm months. It runs past Lake Vidraru with Moldoveanu Peak and Negoiu Peak standing over the Southern Carpathians. Six hours of driving, July or August.

gem:peniscola.text: Peniscola Castle is the whole point here, a fortress over the water with the old town packed below it on the Castellon coast of Spain. Platja Nord runs north from the walls and Serra d'Irta rises behind, four hours in all, best May to July.

gem:trento.text: Trento is the capital of Trentino, an Alpine city in the north of Italy with mountains on either side. Castello del Buonconsiglio and the Cattedrale di San Vigilio carry the history and Torre Vanga the rest, ten hours in all. May to September is the run.

gem:keukenhof.text: Keukenhof is a patch of countryside in the Netherlands with Kasteel Keukenhof and its grounds at the centre. Noordwijk, Hartekamp and the Frans Hals Museum make up the rest of a six hour visit, easiest in the June to August window, with a car.

gem:tournai.text: Tournai is an old city in Wallonia, Belgium, listed by UNESCO. Tournai Cathedral and the Beffroi de Tournai are the pair, with the Pont des Trous on the river and the Musee des Beaux-Arts Tournai nearby. Ten hours, May through September.

gem:bellinzona.text: Bellinzona is the Italian speaking capital of Ticino, in Switzerland, and the Three Castles of Bellinzona earned it a UNESCO World Heritage Site listing. Castelgrande sits on the rock above the centre. Six hours is right, and the season runs May to September.

gem:saint-tropez.text: Pampelonne is the beach that made Saint-Tropez, a small harbour town on the coast of France. The village itself takes three hours, the Gendarmerie and Cinema Museum of Saint-Tropez included, and Port Grimaud is next door. May or June before the rush.

gem:saint-guilhem-le-desert.text: Saint-Guilhem-le-Desert is a medieval village in the Herault, France, listed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Abbaye de Gellone is its heart and the Grotte de Clamouse a short way down the valley, three hours between them. May or June, with boots.

gem:pic-du-midi.text: Pic du Midi de Bigorre is a summit in the mountains of France, crowned by the Observatoire du Pic du Midi de Bigorre. Col du Tourmalet and Col d'Aspin are the passes nearby and Lac d'Oredon lies below, three hours at the top. July or August only.

gem:montignac-lascaux.text: Montignac is a village in France at the edge of the Vezere Valley, where the Grotte de Lascaux keeps its painted caves. Chateau de Losse and Sarlat Cathedral are near enough to add on, and three hours covers the caves. May to September is open season.

gem:rethymno.text: Rethymno is a medieval town on the Greek island of Crete. The Fortezza and Arkadi Monastery lead a compact old quarter that takes about five hours to work through. May and June are calmer than high summer.

gem:val-di-funes.text: Val di Funes is a quiet alpine village in Italy, with Sas Rigais and the Rosengarten group among its draws. The trails are the point from June to August, and the valley sights themselves come to about four hours.

gem:courmayeur.text: Mont Blanc looms over Courmayeur, a resort village in the Western Alps of Italy. Skiing and walking fill most visits, with the Aiguille du Midi and the Great St Bernard Pass close by; four hours covers the village, and June to August is the season.

gem:sperlonga.text: One of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia, Sperlonga is a small village on the coast of Italy. Villa di Tiberio and the beaches fill a short stay of about two hours, and April through June comes before the heat.

gem:castelmezzano.text: Castelmezzano is a remote mountain village in Italy, set among the peaks of the Dolomiti lucane. Two hours covers the Cattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta and Monte Croccia, with May and June the months to pick.

gem:scala-dei-turchi.text: Scala dei Turchi is a beach and cliff landmark on the coast of Italy, worth about two hours on its own. The Valle dei Templi and the Temple of Concordia lie nearby at Agrigento; April and May bring the light without the crowds.

gem:modica.text: Modica is a baroque town in Sicily and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Duomo of San Giorgio and Chiesa di Santa Maria delle Scale head a long list of churches; ten hours is realistic, and May is the pick of the year.

gem:arrabida.text: Arrabida is a protected stretch of coast in Portugal, best known for its natural park. Figueirinha Beach and Albarquel Beach sit below it, with Castelo de Sao Filipe close by; five hours and a warm month between May and September do it justice.

gem:mafra.text: Mafra is a small baroque town in Portugal whose palace holds a UNESCO World Heritage listing. The Palace of Mafra and the Tapada Nacional de Mafra fill about six hours between them, with June through September the easiest months.

gem:pico-azores.text: Pico Island is a mountainous wine island in Portugal. Mount Pico stands over everything, and Gruta das Torres and Lagoa do Caiado round out roughly five hours of sights; July and August are when the weather holds.

gem:teruel.text: Teruel, an inland town in Aragon, Spain, is on the UNESCO World Heritage list. Torre de San Martin and Teruel Cathedral lead about six hours of sights, with Dinopolis the other draw; May, June and September avoid the extremes.

gem:las-medulas.text: Las Medulas is a Roman landscape in Spain, listed by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site. Castillo de Cornatel, Ponferrada Castle and the Monastery of Carracedo fill out five hours nearby, and anything from May to September works.

gem:porec.text: Porec is an old coastal town in Istria, Croatia. The Euphrasian Basilica is the reason most people stop, with Baredine Cave inland and Plava Laguna for swimming; four hours covers it, and May through July is the best run.

gem:nottingham.text: Nottingham, a large city in England, belongs to the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. Its castle museum, the Playhouse and Attenborough Nature Reserve add up to seventeen hours of sights, with June through September the best of the year.

gem:lyndhurst.text: Lyndhurst is a village inside the New Forest, a national park in the United Kingdom. Knightwood Oak and the Portuguese Fireplace lie out in the woods nearby, and Romsey Abbey is a short trip; three hours covers the village, best June to September.

gem:coleford.text: Coleford is a market town in the United Kingdom, right by the Forest of Dean. The forest takes most of the time; Monmouth Castle and Monnow Bridge sit nearby, and six hours covers both. June through August is the season.

gem:maussane-les-alpilles.text: Maussane-les-Alpilles is a small village in France at the foot of the Alpilles. Chateau des Baux and Glanum are the big sights close by, with the Barbegal aqueduct and mill a curiosity; four hours will do, and May or June is the sweet spot.

gem:tanumshede.text: Tanumshede is a small village in Sweden, known for the Rock Carvings in Tanum on the UNESCO World Heritage list. The carvings and the Ro runestone take about three hours, with Kosterhavet National Park close by; come June through August.

gem:ashbourne.text: Ashbourne is a stone market town in Derbyshire, in the United Kingdom. St Oswald's Church, Tissington Hall and Okeover Hall make up about six hours, with Alton Towers down the road; June through August is the time to come.

gem:scicli.text: Scicli is a baroque town in Sicily, in the province of Ragusa, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Santa Maria dell'Itria and the Duomo of San Giorgio anchor about four hours of churches; April or May is early enough to stay comfortable.

gem:keighley.text: Keighley is a market town in West Yorkshire, well placed for the Aire Valley. The Bronte Parsonage Museum, East Riddlesden Hall and Saltaire add up to ten hours of sights, and June through August is the driest stretch.

gem:kassel.text: Kassel, a city in Germany, is built around a huge hillside park. Bergpark Wilhelmshohe and Schloss Wilhelmshohe stand above the centre with the Fridericianum below, about ten hours in all, and June through September suits the walking.

gem:bras-sur-meuse.text: Bras-sur-Meuse is a tiny village in France, set among the Verdun memorials. Fort Douaumont, the Verdun Memorial and Verdun Cathedral make four sober hours, and June through September keeps the ground walkable.

gem:orpington.text: Orpington is a quiet market town in the United Kingdom. The Royal Observatory, Cutty Sark and the National Maritime Museum lie nearby and account for most of the six hours of sights, with June through September the pleasant half of the year.

gem:reggio-nell-emilia.text: Reggio nell'Emilia is a quiet city in Italy, large enough to have everything and small enough to walk. Its cathedral, the Basilica di San Prospero and the Collezione Maramotti carry ten hours; April, May and September are the kind months.

gem:pistoia.text: Pistoia, a city in Italy, gets passed over by the tour buses. The cathedral, the Ospedale del Ceppo and the Church of Sant' Andrea head ten hours of sights, and May, June or September brings the best weather.

gem:gottingen.text: Gottingen is a university city in Germany, walkable and full of student life. The Gottingen State and University Library and the Academy of Sciences are the serious stops, the Stadtfriedhof the quiet one; ten hours, June through September.

gem:folkestone.text: Folkestone, a seaside town in England, looks out from the Kent coast. Leas Cliff Hall, Folkestone Roman Villa and Lympne Castle spread nine hours across town and countryside, and June through August is when the beaches work.

gem:sanremo.text: Sanremo is a seaside resort town in Italy, close to the border with France. Villa Nobel, the Sanremo Casino, the Teatro Ariston and Monte Bignone add up to six hours; April through June and September are the pick.

gem:wattwiller.text: Wattwiller is a small village in France below the Grand Ballon. Hartmannswillerkopf holds the UNESCO World Heritage listing here, and with the Cite du train nearby it adds up to four hours; June through September is the season for walking.

gem:bad-schandau.text: Bad Schandau is the base for Saxon Switzerland, a spa village in Germany under the Elbe Sandstone Mountains. Konigstein Fortress and the paths into Bohemian Switzerland are the outings, four hours of sights; May through September is the stretch that works.

gem:foligno.text: Foligno is a workaday city in Italy with a compact old centre. Palazzo Trinci and the Cattedrale di San Feliciano lead nine hours of sights, with the Abbazia di Sassovivo out of town; April through June or September works best.

gem:hyeres.text: Hyeres is a coastal city in France with a historic centre and beaches at hand. Villa Noailles is the modern landmark, Port-Cros National Park the day out, and Plage de l'Argentiere the swim; nine hours in all, best May through August.

gem:pravia.text: Pravia is a small historic town in Spain, its centre a protected conjunto historico. Santa Maria del Naranjo, San Miguel de Lillo and the Oscar Niemeyer International Cultural Centre lie nearby at Oviedo; six hours, June through September.

gem:maury.text: Maury is a small village in France set among castle ruins. Chateau de Queribus and Peyrepertuse are the two worth the climb, roughly three hours between them; Arago cave is the wet weather alternative, and May, June or September keeps the heat off.

gem:huesca.text: Huesca, a provincial city in Spain, keeps a compact old quarter. The Holy Cathedral Church of the Transfiguration of the Lord and the Real Basilica de San Lorenzo carry most of nine hours; May, June, September and October all suit.

gem:miedzyzdroje.text: Miedzyzdroje is a Baltic beach resort in Poland on Wolin island. The beach and the forest do most of the work, with Swinoujscie and its lighthouse the outing along the coast; three hours of sights, best June through August.

gem:chambery.text: Chambery is a city in France hemmed in by mountains and lakes. Chateau de Chambery and the Elephants Fountain hold the centre, Lac du Bourget and Croix du Nivolet the escapes; ten hours of sights, and May through September is the window.

gem:arnhem.text: Arnhem, a city in the Netherlands, has a national park on its doorstep. The Netherlands Open Air Museum and Burgers' Zoo are the set pieces, Veluwezoom National Park and Posbank the green half; ten hours in all, May through August.

gem:lucignano.text: Lucignano is a medieval hill village in Italy, one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Tempio di Santo Stefano della Vittoria is the landmark here, with Montepulciano and Cortona a short drive off; four hours, and May or June is the moment.

gem:castelsantangelo-sul-nera.text: Castelsantangelo sul Nera is a village of 219 people in Italy, tucked under the Sibillini Mountains. Monte Vettore and Lago di Pilato are the draw rather than the streets, and June is the month; three hours and a car do it.

gem:monts-sur-guesnes.text: Monts-sur-Guesnes is a village of 688 in France, listed among the Petites Cites de Caractere. The Logis de la Haute Porte and the Manoir de Vayolles are the reason to stop, two hours at a slow pace, easiest between June and September.

gem:santa-margherita-ligure.text: Santa Margherita Ligure sits on the Liguria coast, a harbour town of 8,428 people. Cervara Abbey and the Christ of the Abyss offshore are the standouts, and six hours covers the town; May, June and September are the months to pick.

gem:ejby.text: Ejby is a village of 3,131 on Zealand in Denmark, three hours of looking at most. Roskilde Cathedral, the Viking Ship Museum and Borgring all lie nearby, and June through August is the season for it.

gem:chalkida.text: Chalkida is a coastal city of 59,125 in Greece, set where the Euripus Bridge crosses to Euboea. The ruins at Aulis and Lefkandi and the Emir Zade mosque round out a seven hour visit, best in April or May.

gem:casole-d-elsa.text: Casole d'Elsa is a small village of 1,024 in Italy, holder of a Bandiera Arancione. Its three hours of sights lean on the old centre, with the Guarnacci Museum and San Gimignano close by, and the quiet months are May, June and September.

gem:cesena.text: Cesena sits in Emilia-Romagna, a city of 97,137 with the Biblioteca Malatestiana and the Rocca Malatestiana at its core. Palazzo del Ridotto and Cesena Cathedral round out about nine hours, easiest in May or June.

gem:emden.text: Emden is a city of 51,526 in Lower Saxony, strong on local history and art. The Ostfriesisches Landesmuseum Emden and the Leaning Tower of Suurhusen lead ten hours of sights, with June, July and August the reliable months.

gem:orihuela.text: Orihuela is a city of 101,321 in Alicante province, a declared Conjunto historico thick with churches. Orihuela Cathedral, the Castillo de Orihuela and the Museo de la Semana Santa fill nine hours; March to May and October suit best.

gem:choirokoitia.text: Choirokoitia is a village of 531 in Cyprus, known for the UNESCO World Heritage Site at Khirokitia just outside it. Two hours covers the ruins, and Stavrovouni Monastery and Governor's Beach make easy additions in April, May or October.

gem:tarcal.text: Tarcal is a village of 3,283 in Hungary, set in the Tokaj wine region inside a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Tokaji-hegy and Bodrogzug are the walks at hand and three hours suits the village, anywhere between April and September.

gem:luanco.text: Luanco is a coast town of 10,427 in Asturias, its old quarter a Conjunto historico around the Iglesia de Santa Maria. Gijon and the Oscar Niemeyer International Cultural Centre are close; give it six hours, June through September.

gem:kampinos.text: Kampinos is a village of 723 in Poland, sitting inside a UNESCO Man and the Biosphere reserve. Niepokalanow, the Church of the Assumption in Kampinos and the Palace in Teresin add up to about three hours, best between May and September.

gem:pardubice.text: Pardubice is a city of 88,520 in East Bohemia, gathered around Pardubice Castle. Kunetice Mountain Castle crowns Kuneticka hora just outside town; ten hours covers the pair and the streets between, May through September.

gem:chudenice.text: Chudenice is a village of 699 in Czechia with Zamek Lazen and Bolfanek right above it and Orlovicka hora behind. Horsovsky Tyn Castle is a short drive off, four hours in all, and June through September is when it looks best.

gem:pomponesco.text: Pomponesco is a village of 1,415 in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Its centre takes three hours at most; Viadana, Dosolo and the Museo Peppone e Don Camillo are nearby, and April to September suits.

gem:cison-di-valmarino.text: Cison di Valmarino is a village of 1,178 in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia set among the Prosecco hills. The Molinetto della Croda and the Eremo di San Gallo fill three hours, with any month from May to September doing well.

gem:macerata-feltria.text: Macerata Feltria is a village of 1,456 in Italy, on the list of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Rocca Ubaldinesca is the set piece and two hours does it; Monte Carpegna and Pietrarubbia are the country around, best May to August.

gem:elefsina.text: Elefsina is a town of 24,910 in Greece, named a European Capital of Culture. The ruins of Eleusis and its Telesterion are the reason to stop, four hours at a steady pace, and April or May before the heat.

OVD.text: Asturias fills the far north of Spain, mountains at its back and beaches below. Santa Maria del Naranjo, San Miguel de Lillo and Monte Naranco lead about seven hours of sights, and the season runs June to September.

MXP.text: Milan is a city of 1,371,498 in northern Italy and the country's financial heart. Milan Cathedral and Teatro alla Scala lead a list that runs to seventeen hours, with May, June and September the best months to work through it.

BGY.text: Milan is a city of 1,371,498 in northern Italy and the country's financial heart. Milan Cathedral and Teatro alla Scala lead a list that runs to seventeen hours, with May, June and September the best months to work through it.

LIN.text: Milan is a city of 1,371,498 in northern Italy and the country's financial heart. Milan Cathedral and Teatro alla Scala lead a list that runs to seventeen hours, with May, June and September the best months to work through it.

MUC.text: Munich, capital of Bavaria, runs to 1,505,005 people and a deep bench of museums. The Deutsches Museum, Alte Pinakothek and Nymphenburg Palace top seventeen hours of sights, and May through September is the long good season.

gem:rotterdam.text: Rotterdam is a modern city of 868,135 in South Holland, rebuilt tall and glassy. The Erasmus Bridge, Euromast and the Van Nelle Factory head a seventeen hour list worth spreading over two summer days in June, July or August.

gem:wurzburg.text: Wurzburg is a wine city of 133,731 in Franconia, where the Wurzburg Residence carries a UNESCO World Heritage Site listing. Festung Marienberg and the Kappele sit on the slope above; ten hours covers both banks, May through September.

gem:durnstein.text: Durnstein is a village of 322 on the Danube in the Wachau, wine country in Austria. Stift Durnstein leads, with Gottweig Abbey and Burgruine Senftenberg a short way off; four hours is the measure, and the season stretches from April to September.

gem:etretat.text: Etretat is a coast village of 1,658 in Normandy, known for the cliffs at Porte d'Aval. The walk along the top and the Eglise Notre-Dame d'Etretat take roughly three hours; June, July and August are busy and bright.

gem:kiruna.text: Kiruna is an arctic town of 17,037 in Sweden, paired with Abisko and the fells around it. Kiruna kyrka and Luossavaara are the sights close at hand, about four hours of them, and July and August are the recommended months.

gem:coimbra.text: Coimbra is a university city of 140,796 in Portugal, its Universidade de Coimbra a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Old Cathedral of Coimbra and the New Cathedral of Coimbra fill out ten hours, best walked in April, May or June.

gem:cadaques.text: Cadaques is a white village of 2,894 on the Cap de Creus, at the north end of the Costa Brava. The Portlligat Museum-House and the coves at Platja des Poal draw most visits, about four hours; May, June and July are the good months.

gem:saksun.text: Saksun is a village of 634 on Streymoy in the Faroe Islands, remote and very quiet. Vagar and Eysturoy are the neighbouring islands and Slaettaratindur the high point; three hours here, in June, July or August.

gem:jokulsarlon.text: Jokulsarlon is a wilderness stretch in the southeast of Iceland, glacier country under Oraefajokull. Hvannadalshnukur rises above it, Fjallsarlon and Breidarlon lie alongside, and four hours is a fair stop in June, July or August.

gem:slovak-paradise.text: Slovak Paradise is a national park in eastern Slovakia, hiking and scrambling country. Sucha Bela is the route people come for, with Klastorisko, Tomasovsky vyhlad and Dobsinska Ice Cave close by; five hours out, June to August.

gem:dinkelsbuhl.text: Dinkelsbuhl is a medieval town of 12,260 in Mittelfranken with its walls and gates still standing. Segringer Tor, the Deutsches Haus and the Stadtmuhle Dinkelsbuhl make six hours of slow walking, best from June to September.

gem:gura-humorului.text: Gura Humorului is a town of 15,728 in Southern Bukovina, the base for the painted monasteries. Voronet Monastery and Humor Monastery are the two to see, four hours between them, with May to September the open season.

gem:brecon-beacons.text: The Brecon Beacons are upland country in southern Wales, a UNESCO Global Geopark of long grass ridges. Pen y Fan and Corn Du are the walks that matter, six hours for the pair, with June, July and August the driest stretch.

gem:loch-lomond.text: Loch Lomond is the big water at the heart of a national park an easy run from Glasgow, which keeps it busy. Ben Lomond is the climb above it, Balloch Castle and Dumbarton Castle the easy stops; three hours, June to August.

gem:camargue.text: The Camargue is flat wilderness coast in southern France, held as the Camargue Regional Natural Park and on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List. Arles and its amphitheatre anchor two hours of built sights, best in May or June.

gem:spa-belgium.text: Spa is a town of 10,756 in Belgium and one of The Great Spa Towns of Europe. Franchimont Castle and the Waterfalls of Coo are the outings, with Signal de Botrange and Lake Robertville not far; six hours, June to September.

gem:logar-valley.text: Logar Valley is a glacial trough in the alps of Slovenia, open in practice only from June through August. Grintovec stands at its head and Potok Cave sits in the trees, seven hours of walking between them. Its population is 214 and the buses hardly come.

gem:ruegen-jasmund.text: Rugen is an island in Germany whose coast does all the work, Nationalpark Jasmund right at the door. Konigsstuhl is the headline, Jaromarsburg and Schloss Ralswiek the quieter stops, six hours in all. The buses are thin, so drive, June to August.

gem:st-gallen.text: Saint Gallen is a baroque city in eastern Switzerland that grew around the UNESCO listed Abbey of Saint Gall and its library. Museum im Lagerhaus adds a smaller collection, and ten hours covers the centre on foot, easiest June to August.

gem:gorges-de-lardeche.text: The Gorges de l'Ardeche is a river canyon in France laced with caves, at its best in May, June or September. Grotte Chauvet and Aven d'Orgnac are the big two underground, with Pont d'Arc down on the water, and seven hours covers them.

gem:haut-koenigsbourg.text: Chateau du Haut-Koenigsbourg is a hilltop medieval castle in France, about four hours including the climb and easy to reach without a car. Chateau de Saint-Ulrich, Chateau du Frankenbourg and Chateau de Bilstein stand nearby, June to August.

gem:elounda-spinalonga.text: Elounda is a coastal stretch in Greece looking across to the fortress islet of Spinalonga, with a long season from May to September. The boat over is the main event, and ruins at Gournia, Lato and Dreros fill out the rest of five hours.

gem:voidokilia.text: Voidokilia is a curved sand beach on the coast of Greece, quietest in April and May. The Palace of Nestor lies a short drive inland, and three hours covers the beach and the ruins together. The village behind is small, the buses limited.

gem:pitigliano.text: Pitigliano is a quiet old village in Tuscany, four hours of lanes and long views rather than a full day. Pitigliano Cathedral anchors the centre, with Sovana a short drive off and the Monti Volsini behind. May and June are the pick.

gem:castelluccio-di-norcia.text: Castelluccio is a mountain hamlet on a high plain in Italy, ringed by the Monti Sibillini. Monte Vettore and Cima del Redentore draw the walkers, and six hours makes a fair day out. Its season is short, June to August, and transport is poor.

gem:ischia.text: Ischia is a volcanic island in Italy where thermal water and beaches carry the day rather than monuments, at its peak in July and August. Cumae, Baia and the Phlegraean Fields lie across the water on the mainland, an easy add to six hours here.

gem:stintino-la-pelosa.text: Stintino is a fishing village turned beach town in Italy, known above all for Spiaggia della Pelosa. The boats run out to Asinara National Park, and five hours covers sand and island. Its beach months are June, July and August.

gem:westfjords.text: The Westfjords are a remote arm of Iceland, thinly settled and slow to drive. Dynjandi and Latrabjarg lead, with Isafjordur the town to sleep in and four hours of stops spread between long roads. June and July are the only practical months.

gem:dettifoss.text: Dettifoss is a powerful waterfall in the wilderness of Iceland, inside Jokulsargljufur National Park. Selfoss and Hafragilsfoss are its neighbours, Asbyrgi and Krafla not far, and four hours takes them in. The drive works June to August.

gem:porto-moniz.text: Porto Moniz is a coastal village on Madeira Island in Portugal, where the sea pools are why people come. Pico Ruivo, the Laurisilva of Madeira and 25 Fontes are within reach, and three hours covers the village itself. July to September is warmest.

gem:sucevita.text: Sucevita Monastery is a UNESCO listed church in rural Romania, counted among the Churches of Moldavia. Two hours covers it, which is why most visitors string it with Moldovita Monastery, Putna Monastery and Bogdana Monastery, any time May to September.

gem:tossa-de-mar.text: Tossa de Mar is a walled beach town on the Costa Brava in Spain, its medieval quarter rising straight off the sand. Far de Tossa crowns the headland and Lloret de Mar is the next bay along. Its four hours suit June to August, when the sea is warm.

gem:ribeira-sacra.text: Ribeira Sacra is a wine region in Spain, terraced above the Sil Canyon and listed as a UNESCO biosphere reserve. Monasterio de San Vicente del Pino and Pazo de Tor are the stops on a five-hour drive, best made in May, June or September.

gem:morella.text: Morella is a walled hill town in the mountains of inland Spain, with Morella Castle on the rock above it. The walls and the castle take about three hours, and Serra de Vallivana is close for a drive any time from May to August.

gem:calpe.text: Calpe is a beach town on the coast of Spain, sitting under the rock of Penyal d'Ifac. Salines de Calp and Serra de Bernia lie behind the town, and six hours fills a day between them. May to August is swimming weather.

gem:sa-calobra.text: Sa Calobra is a cove at the foot of the Serra de Tramuntana in Spain, reached by a long twisting mountain road. Puig Major and Gorg Blau sit above it and Lluc Sanctuary lies over the pass, seven hours once the driving counts. Go between June and August.

gem:glenfinnan.text: Glenfinnan is a Highland spot in Scotland where the Mallaig railway curves over the glen on the Glenfinnan Viaduct. Loch Shiel stretches below, with Sgurr Thuilm and Streap for hillwalkers and six hours in all. The trains and the light favour June to August.

gem:orkney.text: Orkney is a windswept island group in the United Kingdom, thick with prehistoric sites. Skara Brae and Maes Howe carry the UNESCO listing, with Hoy across the water from Mainland, and seven hours of sights. The ferries and the daylight favour June to August.

gem:kynance-cove.text: Kynance Cove is a beach on the Lizard in the United Kingdom, a walk down from the cliffs above. Lizard Lighthouse and Goonhilly Downs are nearby and Pendennis Castle further along, six hours for the lot. The season stretches June to September.

gem:essen.text: Essen is a former coal and steel city in Germany, now a museum town. Zeche Zollverein holds the UNESCO listing, Museum Folkwang the art and Essen Minster the old centre, seventeen hours of sights in all. May to September is the easiest stretch.

gem:hobro.text: Hobro is a small town at the end of Mariager Fjord in Denmark, best known for the Viking ring fortress at Fyrkat. The gas museum and Madum Lake round out about six hours, an easy stop by train between June and August.

gem:shrewsbury.text: Shrewsbury is an old market town in the United Kingdom with a castle, an abbey and a cathedral all within one walk. Viroconium Cornoviorum, the Roman city, lies just outside, and ten hours covers the two together, best June to August.

gem:eastbourne.text: Eastbourne is a seaside resort on the coast of the United Kingdom, with Beachy Head rising at one end of the front. Pevensey Castle and the Long Man of Wilmington make short trips inland, and ten hours covers them. The season holds from June into September.

gem:treviso.text: Treviso is a walled city of canals in northeastern Italy, often skipped on the way to the lagoon. Treviso Cathedral and the Palazzo dei Trecento anchor the centre, Church San Nicolo a short walk off. Ten full hours of sights, best May to July.

gem:hastings.text: Hastings is a fishing and seaside town on the coast of the United Kingdom, with a ruined castle above the old town. The West Hill Cliff Railway climbs to it, Hastings Pier runs out to sea and Battle Abbey waits inland. Ten hours of sights, June to August.

gem:krinides.text: Krinides is a farming village in Greece beside the UNESCO listed ruins of Philippi. Two hours does the site, and Kavala aqueduct and the Archaeological Museum of Kavala are the obvious add-ons. April, May, September and October are comfortable.

gem:pesmes.text: Pesmes is a quiet stone village in France, listed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Its medieval walls and Chateau Rouillaud fill a slow three hours, and Acey Abbey and Museum Baron Martin extend that into a day. May to September is open season.

gem:xanten.text: Xanten is a town in Germany grown up beside the ruins of Colonia Ulpia Traiana, part of the UNESCO listed Lower German Limes. Xanten Cathedral and Castra Vetera fill out six hours, and the trains make it an easy day from May to September.

gem:halifax.text: Halifax is a stone mill town in the United Kingdom built around The Piece Hall. Its ten hours of sights take in Halifax Minster, Halifax Town Hall and, a short ride away, the National Science and Media Museum. June to August is the driest.

gem:chippenham.text: Set in Wiltshire, Chippenham is a workaday town in the United Kingdom that earns its keep as a base. Lacock Abbey and Corsham Court are the reasons to stop, with Malmesbury Abbey and Sheldon Manor further out. Six hours, June to September.

gem:montepulciano.text: Montepulciano is a hill town in Tuscany known for its red wine. Palazzo Comunale looks over the main square and San Biagio stands below the walls, with Pienza and its Palazzo Piccolomini close by. May or June, and four hours is enough.

gem:loches.text: Loches is a walled town in France stacked below the Chateau de Loches. The Collegiale Saint-Ours stands inside the ramparts, and Chateau de Montpoupon and Chedigny are short drives away. May to September suits the four hours it takes.

gem:senigallia.text: Senigallia is a beach town on the coast of Italy, busier in the water than in the museums. Rotonda a Mare juts out over the sea, with Portici Ercolani and Palazzetto Baviera in the old centre. April to June and September are the pick, five hours in all.

gem:maidstone.text: On the River Medway in the United Kingdom, Maidstone is a market town best used as a base. Leeds Castle is the headline trip, with Allington Castle and All Saints Church closer in and ten hours of sights all told, easiest June to September.

gem:helmsley.text: Helmsley is a small market town on the edge of the North York Moors in the United Kingdom. Helmsley Castle and Duncombe Park sit in town, with Rievaulx Abbey and Castle Howard a short drive out, three hours in all. June to August is busiest.

gem:monpazier.text: Monpazier is a bastide village in France, laid out around one arcaded square and listed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Chateau de Biron, Chateau de Bonaguil and Cadouin Abbey lie close by. Its three hours suit May to July, or September.

gem:mellie-a.text: Mellieħa is a beach town in the northwest of Malta, busiest from May through August. Popeye Village sits just around the bay and Golden Bay is a short hop down the coast, with boats out to Gozo and Comino. Six hours covers the town.

gem:alcoy.text: Alcoy is an inland city in Spain with a protected old centre and two natural parks on its doorstep. Cocentaina Castle and Castell de Barxell head the list, and the Serra de Mariola suits walking in May, June or September. Ten hours fills a visit.

gem:roses.text: Roses is a fishing and beach town on the Costa Brava, at its best from May to July. The ruins at Empuries and the walled centre of Castello sit just inland, while Cala Montjoi and Cala Tamariua are the coves worth the walk; six hours takes it all in.

gem:wiesbaden.text: Wiesbaden is a spa city in Germany, large enough to need a full day. The Nerobergbahn climbs to the Neroberg, Museum Wiesbaden and the Hessisches Staatstheater hold the centre, and Mainz Cathedral stands nearby. The warm stretch runs May to September.

gem:liberec.text: Liberec is a city in northern Czechia, sitting below the Jested mountain and the tower on its summit. Liberec Town Hall leads the sights down in the centre, and the ski jumping hills are just above. The pair take a long day, best May to September.

gem:otterlo.text: Otterlo is a village of a couple of thousand people at the gate of Hoge Veluwe National Park in the Netherlands. The Kroller-Muller Museum inside the park holds the art, the heath of the Veluwe the rest. A half day is plenty, and buses are scarce.

gem:swindon.text: A railway city in Wiltshire, Swindon leads with STEAM, the museum of the Great Western Railway. Barbury Castle and the Broad Town White Horse sit out on the downs above, and nine hours covers the lot. June through September is the best stretch.

gem:szczawnica.text: Szczawnica is a spa village in the Pieniny mountains of southern Poland. The Dunajec River Gorge cuts through below the Trzy Korony peaks, with Lake Czorsztyn close by. June to September is the window, and four hours covers the sights.

gem:egersund.text: Egersund is a small port town in Norway, the centre of a UNESCO Global Geopark. Egersund Church is the landmark in town; the Eigeroy Lighthouse out on Eigeroya is the walk worth making. Its season is June to August, four hours in all.

gem:ciutadella.text: Ciutadella is the former capital of Menorca, a harbour town of Gothic streets and shaded lanes. The Cathedral of Minorca anchors the middle, with the Cala Morell Settlement and Punta Nati Lighthouse out along the coast. Six hours, May to August.

gem:gotha.text: Gotha is a town in Thuringia built around Friedenstein Castle, a huge baroque block above the old streets. The Orangerie gardens adjoin it and Burg Gleichen crowns a hill nearby. June through September is the time, and six hours is enough.

gem:kilsyth.text: Kilsyth is a small town northeast of Glasgow where the Antonine Wall, a World Heritage Site, runs past. The Campsie Fells rise just beyond the houses and Culcreuch Castle is a short drive off. Its best run is June to August, six hours in all.

gem:ourense.text: Hot springs line the river at Ourense, a working city in Galicia with an old quarter around its cathedral. Ourense Cathedral and the Ponte Vella, the Roman bridge, lead the way. Its best months are May, June and September; nine hours of sights.

gem:ogre.text: Ogre is a town in Latvia on the bank of the Riga Reservoir, inside a national park. The wooded ridges of Ogres Zilie kalni carry the walking trails and take up most of a short visit. June to August is the season; four hours is enough.

gem:den-helder.text: Den Helder is a naval port city at the northern tip of North Holland. Willemsoord, the old dockyard, keeps HNLMS Abraham Crijnssen afloat, while Fort Kijkduin and Lange Jaap stand out along the shore. Set aside nine hours, June to August.

gem:lleida.text: The old cathedral, la Seu Vella, stands on the hill above Lleida, a city in Catalonia with roots in the Bronze Age. Seu Nova, the Lleida Museum and the Auditori Enric Granados sit below. Ten hours; April and May are the kindest months.

gem:guardamar-del-segura.text: Guardamar del Segura is a beach town in Spain, with salt lagoons behind the sand and a castle on the rise. A half day covers Guardamar Castle, the Islamic Caliphate Rabita and El Fondo Natural Park. May and June are the pick of the year.

gem:le-bonhomme.text: Le Bonhomme is a tiny village on a pass in the Vosges Mountains of France. Hohneck and the Lac Blanc are a short drive up, and Chateau du Haut-Koenigsbourg is the big sight below. The roads are clear June to August; three hours takes in everything.

gem:caen.text: Caen, the biggest city in Calvados, keeps its castle and two great abbeys at the heart of Normandy. The Abbey of Saint-Etienne, the Abbey of Sainte-Trinite and the Church of Saint-Pierre make the round, with Pegasus Bridge and Juno Beach near the coast.

gem:chipiona.text: Chipiona is a Costa de la Luz beach town in Cadiz province, Spain. The tall Chipiona Lighthouse marks it from far out, with the Castillo de Santiago and the Palacio de Orleans-Borbon in the streets behind La Playa de Regla. Its season runs May to September.

gem:bordighera.text: Bordighera is a small coastal town in Italy where the historic quarter sits above the beach. The Hanbury botanical gardens and Balzi Rossi lie along the shore, Teatro Ariston further on. April to June and September are the months, six hours in all.

gem:castiglion-fiorentino.text: Castiglion Fiorentino is a medieval town between Arezzo and Cortona, holding a Bandiera Arancione for its centre. The great churches are nearby: Santa Maria della Pieve one way, Cortona Cathedral the other. Six hours, best in May, June or September.

gem:ria-sirach.text: Ria-Sirach is a small village in France under the peak of Canigo, on one of the Plus Beaux Detours routes. The abbeys of Saint-Michel-de-Cuxa and Saint-Martin-du-Canigou are minutes away, Serrabone Priory over the hill; four hours does it.

gem:taranto.text: Taranto is a working port on the Ionian shore of Apulia and the second city of the region. Castello Aragonese guards the way into the old town and Taranto Cathedral stands behind it, with the Cheradi Islands offshore; nine hours, April or May.

gem:ostseebad-binz.text: Ostseebad Binz is a beach resort on the island of Rugen in Germany, backed by national park. Hauptstrand is the sand, and Konigsstuhl, the Granitz Hunting Lodge and Vilm fill the four hours beyond it. June to August is the short season.

gem:tirrenia.text: Tirrenia is a quiet beach village on the coast of Italy, close to Pisa. The Leaning Tower of Pisa, Pisa Cathedral and the Baptistry of San Giovanni are a short ride inland, the Duomo di Livorno the other way; four hours, June to August.

gem:hameln.text: The Pied Piper tale belongs to Hameln, a town in Lower Saxony where the Hochzeitshaus and Hefehof hold the centre. Old houses line Osterstrasse, and Schloss Hamelschenburg and the Klutturm are short runs out. A full day, May through September.

gem:givet.text: Givet is a small border village in France, on one of the Plus Beaux Detours routes. The sights lie mostly over the line: the Collegiate Church of Our Lady of Dinant, Maredret Abbey and the Rochers de Freyr. The village itself is a three-hour stop.

gem:saint-nazaire.text: Saint-Nazaire is a port city on the Loire estuary in France, with standing stones and burial mounds on its edges. The Saint-Nazaire Bridge is the landmark; the Tumulus de Dissignac and Dolmen des Rossignols reward a detour. June to September, nine hours.

gem:montalcino.text: Brunello is the reason most visitors climb to Montalcino, a hill village in Tuscany. The Abbey of Sant'Antimo sits in the valley below and Monte Amiata fills the southern skyline. May and June are the best months; the streets take barely three hours.

gem:apricale.text: Apricale is a stone village stacked on a ridge in Italy, one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Monte Bignone and Monte Saccarello rise behind it, while Balzi Rossi and the Hanbury botanical gardens are a drive down to the coast, with three hours enough here.

gem:jawor.text: Jawor is a town in southwest Poland whose Peace Church carries a World Heritage listing. Bolkow Castle stands on a crag nearby and the site of the Gross-Rosen concentration camp is a sobering stop. The visit runs six hours, May to September.

gem:louveciennes.text: Louveciennes is a quiet village in France beside the Versailles estate. The Palace of Versailles, its Gardens and the Galerie des Batailles take up the four hours here, with Port-Royal-des-Champs a short drive off. The season runs June through September.

gem:ciudad-rodrigo.text: Ciudad Rodrigo is a historic town in western Spain, its cathedral and castle set inside the old walls. The Cathedral of Santa Maria and the Castle of Enrique II lead, and Siega Verde is the trip out of town. May, June and September are best; four hours.

gem:garderen.text: Garderen is a small village on the Veluwe, the heath and forest belt in the middle of the Netherlands. Het Loo Palace, the Kroller-Muller Museum and Hoge Veluwe National Park are all within reach, and the water at Veluwemeer too. May to August, four hours.

gem:durres.text: Durres is the chief port of Albania and its beach city, standing on the ancient site of Epidamnos. The Roman amphitheatre is the standout, with the Durres Archaeological Museum and the Fatih Mosque close by; eight hours, May to August.

gem:soultzeren.text: Soultzeren is a village strung along a valley in the Vosges Mountains of France. Hohneck, Kastelberg and the Grand Ballon are the walks, and the Unterlinden Museum is the wet-weather option. June to September, four hours.

gem:labastide-murat.text: Labastide-Murat is a village on the limestone causse of France, inside a UNESCO Global Geopark. The caves at Pech Merle and the Grottes de Cougnac are the reason to come, with Chateau de Vaillac a few minutes off; three hours in all.

gem:tatranska-lomnica.text: Tatranska Lomnica is a resort village in Slovakia under Lomnicky stit, in the Western Carpathians. Rysy, Krivan and Slavkovsky stit ring the valley, and the lake at Strbske Pleso is the easy outing. The season is short, June to August.

gem:lelystad.text: The pull of Lelystad lies out on the edges of the city rather than in its centre. Bataviawerf has the ships, the Aviodrome the aircraft, and the Oostvaardersplassen marshes the birds and wild horses; eight hours and June to August suit it.

gem:domme.text: Domme is a small historic village in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, at its best from May to September. The castles are the point: Castelnaud-la-Chapelle and Beynac first, then Jardins de Marqueyssac, four hours in all.

gem:de-koog.text: Texel keeps its beach crowds at De Koog, a village of a thousand on the coast of the Netherlands. Dunes of Texel National Park begins at the edge of the village and Eierland Lighthouse stands further up; three hours, June to August.

gem:dingli.text: Malta puts several of its oldest sites within reach of Dingli, a historic village of under four thousand. Mdina and the Megalithic Temples of Malta lie close by, Golden Bay closer still, and four hours covers the lot, June to August.

gem:buitrago-del-lozoya.text: Buitrago del Lozoya is a village of eighteen hundred in Spain, listed as a Conjunto historico and built around its castle. The Church of la Magdalena and the Sierra de la Cabrera beyond fill out three hours, best in May, June or September.

gem:moraira.text: Out of season Moraira is a quiet seaside village in Spain, home to fewer than two thousand. Castillo de Moraira and the Church of Saint Bartholomew fill a morning, Penyal d'Ifac rises up the coast, and three hours is about right.

gem:hoenderloo.text: The Kroller-Muller Museum is what brings most people to Hoenderloo, a village of seven hundred in the Netherlands. Hoge Veluwe National Park starts at its edge, Veluwezoom National Park lies further on, and four hours is the usual stay.

gem:avallon.text: A town of under nine thousand in France, Avallon carries a Les Plus Beaux Detours listing and good public transport. Vezelay Abbey and Chateau de Bazoches head the day, the caves of Arcy-sur-Cure fill the rest, and six hours is a fair plan.

gem:el-port-de-la-selva.text: A fishing village of under a thousand on the coast of Spain, el Port de la Selva sits on the Cap de Creus shore. The Monestir de Sant Pere de Rodes is the main call, Cala Tamariua the place to swim, and four hours covers it from May to July.

gem:luneville.text: Luneville, a town of twenty-one thousand in France, is built around its chateau and sits on the Les Plus Beaux Detours de France list. The Chateau de Luneville takes most of five hours; the Abbaye Saint-Remy and the synagogue take the rest.

gem:loon-op-zand.text: Efteling draws most visitors to Loon op Zand, a town of twenty-three thousand in the Netherlands. Aquanura adds to the day, De Loonse en Drunense Duinen lies alongside, and six hours is a fair plan from May through September.

gem:wijk-bij-duurstede.text: Wijk bij Duurstede is a castle town of seventeen thousand in the Netherlands, easy to reach and easy to walk. Dorestad and Museum Dorestad tell its older story, Amerongen Castle stands nearby, and six hours covers a visit from May to August.

gem:boijl.text: Set between national parks, Boijl is a village of barely five hundred in the Netherlands. Drents-Friese Wold National Park is the reason to come, Dwingelderveld National Park backs it up, and four hours in June or July is enough.

gem:koge.text: Koge, a coastal town of thirty-eight thousand on Zealand in Denmark, has more history than its size suggests. Sankt Nicolai Kirke and Koge Town Hall hold the centre, Vallo Castle and Borgring sit outside it, and six hours suits a summer day.

gem:warten.text: On the edge of De Alde Feanen National Park, Warten is a village of eight hundred in the Netherlands. The park and the lakes take up most of four hours, with Leeuwarden and its Grote of Jacobijnerkerk a short run inland.

gem:salamina.text: Salamis Island has one real town, and Salamina is it: twenty-five thousand people a short hop from the mainland in Greece. The Cave of Euripides is the thing to find, Daphni Monastery lies over the water, and four hours in April or May does it.

gem:eisden.text: Hoge Kempen National Park runs right up to Eisden, a town of ten thousand in Belgium on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List. The Bonnefanten Museum and Basilica of Saint Servatius are a short hop away; six hours between May and September.

gem:cambron-saint-vincent.text: Pairi Daiza is why most people come to Cambron-Saint-Vincent, a village of a thousand in Belgium. The Neolithic flint mines of Spiennes and the Mundaneum are nearby, the Grand Large is good for a swim, and three hours covers the rest.

gem:heijen.text: Two things bring visitors to Heijen, a village of sixteen hundred in the Netherlands: Kasteel Bleijenbeek and De Maasduinen National Park. Wereldmuseum Berg en Dal is further out, and four hours covers the lot, May to September.

gem:sobotka.text: Bohemian Paradise surrounds Sobotka, a village of two thousand in Czechia. Hrad Kost and Humprecht are the closest calls, Trosky stands a little further on, and four hours is enough, May to September.

gem:toul.text: Toul Cathedral is the anchor of Toul, a town of seventeen thousand in France on the Les Plus Beaux Detours de France list. The Collegiale Saint-Gengoult and the Porte de Metz round out six hours, best from June to September.

gem:limoux.text: Alet Cathedral and the Basilique Notre-Dame de Marceille are the pull at Limoux, a town of eleven thousand in France. Chateau de Pieusse adds a stop, six hours covers the sights, and May, June or September is the time to come.
