gem:san-benedetto-po.text: The Abbazia di San Benedetto in Polirone is the reason to stop at San Benedetto Po, a village of five thousand in Italy. Its abbey and the Conca del Bertazzolo fill three hours, best in April, May or September.

gem:soncino.text: Soncino is a village of five thousand in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Its neighbours Orzinuovi and Torre Pallavicina fill out a short stop. April, May and September are the easy months, and three hours is plenty.

gem:santa-fiora.text: Monte Amiata rises behind Santa Fiora, a village of thirteen hundred in Italy and one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Pieve delle Sante Flora e Lucilla and Palazzo Sforza Cesarini are the sights; four hours, May or June.

gem:cetona.text: Cetona is a village of thirteen hundred in Italy, on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list and in sight of Monte Amiata. The Tomba della Scimmia and Necropoli delle Pianacce are the finds here; four hours does it, May to September.

gem:castiglione-di-garfagnana.text: The Fortezza delle Verrucole is the set piece at Castiglione di Garfagnana, a mountain village of under five hundred in Italy. Casa Museo Pascoli is the quieter stop, three hours covers both, and May through August is the season.

gem:castagnole-delle-lanze.text: Barbaresco and Castello di Govone are short trips from Castagnole delle Lanze, a village of two thousand in Italy. The Chiesa di Sant'Andrea is in the village itself, and three hours suits a day in May, June or September.

gem:cocconato.text: Vezzolano and the Abbazia di Santa Fede are what bring people to Cocconato, a village of under nine hundred in Italy. Its own San Lorenzo takes little time, so three hours covers the lot, May through September.

gem:sant-ambrogio-di-valpolicella.text: Sant'Ambrogio di Valpolicella is a town of ten thousand in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Villa Serego and Monte Pastello take up much of six hours, with Monte Baldo close by; May, June and September are the months.

gem:saint-amand-les-eaux.text: Coal mining history shapes Saint-Amand-les-Eaux, a town of eighteen thousand in France on the Les Plus Beaux Detours de France list. The Abbaye de Saint-Amand and Mine de Wallers-Arenberg fill six hours, May to September.

gem:eus.text: Eus is a village of six hundred in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, looking across to Canigo. May, June and September are the good months, and the Prieure de Marcevol and the Eglise Saint-Pierre de Prades take four hours between them.

gem:mosset.text: Fort Liberia is the big draw near Mosset, a village of seven hundred in France below Canigo. The Eglise Saint-Pierre de Prades sits down the valley, and four hours covers a visit in May, June or September.

gem:gravesend.text: Old forts are the theme at Gravesend, a market town of fifty-four thousand in the United Kingdom. Tilbury Fort and New Tavern Fort lead, Gads Hill Place and Stone Castle follow, and ten hours makes a full day, June to September.

gem:vallefoglia.text: Two hours is all Vallefoglia asks, a village of four hundred in Italy on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. The Convento del Beato Sante and Montegiano Castle are the sights, with Spiaggia di Pesaro close for a swim in May or June.

gem:san-lorenzo-dorsino.text: San Lorenzo Dorsino is a village of three hundred in Italy under Cima Brenta, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Castello di Stenico is the nearest big sight and Lake Molveno the nearest water; four hours, June to September.

gem:haarlemmermeer.text: Haarlemmermeer is a city of a hundred and sixty thousand in the Netherlands, well served by public transport. Museum De Cruquius, Hartekamp and Huis te Manpad spread over ten hours, and Bloemendaal aan Zee is the beach, best in summer.

gem:riva-del-garda.text: Torre Apponale gives the best view over Riva del Garda, a lakeside town of seventeen thousand in Italy. The Chiesa dell'Inviolata is worth the detour, Monte Baldo stands across the water, and six hours does the centre, June to September.

gem:colle-di-val-d-elsa.text: Colle di Val d'Elsa is a town of sixteen thousand in Italy, well placed for the towers of San Gimignano. Torre Rognosa and Torre del Diavolo are the ones to find. April through September is the window, and six hours suits a day out.

gem:rocca-di-papa.text: Lake Albano sits below Rocca di Papa, a town of fifteen thousand in Italy. The Papal summer residence and the Church of the Gesu are the set pieces, Lake Nemi lies a short way on, and six hours covers a visit in May or June.

gem:certaldo.text: Certaldo is a town of thirteen thousand in Italy, an easy base for San Gimignano. The Chiesa di Sant'Agostino is the local stop, Torre Rognosa and the Santa Fina Chapel the reason to head up the road. Six hours, April to September.

PSA.text: The Leaning Tower draws the crowd, but the whole Piazza del Duomo, Pisa Cathedral included, rewards a slow morning in this Tuscany city. Ten hours covers the lot, and April to June or September suits best.

MST.text: Maastricht pairs a dense old core with a serious appetite, the Netherlands city where lunch runs long. The Bonnefantenmuseum and Museum aan het Vrijthof are the indoor half of ten hours, and the months to aim at run May through September.

gem:baden-baden.text: Thermal water made Baden-Baden, one of The Great Spa Towns of Europe, and the Friedrichsbad still runs. Lichtentaler Allee, Museum Frieder Burda and the Faberge Museum fill out ten hours, with May to September the pleasant half of the year.

gem:cambridge.text: The colleges run the show in Cambridge: King's College Chapel, the Mathematical Bridge and the Fitzwilliam Museum all sit within one walk. Ten hours makes a fair day, and June through September shows the gardens at their best.

gem:zakopane.text: Zakopane sits at the foot of the Tatra Mountains in southern Poland, half resort, half mountain town. Six hours does the town, but Morskie Oko and Kasprowy Wierch want a day each, and the trails are clearest June through August.

gem:monemvasia.text: Monemvasia packs a medieval fortress town onto one rock by the sea in Greece, with the Church of Agia Sofia above and the Monemvasia Mosque in the lanes below. Two hours walks the whole of it, and May right through September is warm.

gem:vaxholm.text: The Stockholm Archipelago is island country, all boat timetables, sailing and quiet family beaches. Gamla stan, Stockholm Palace and Skogskyrkogarden are the trip back into town, about seven hours of sights, and summer here means June through August.

gem:braga.text: Churches set the rhythm in Braga, a Portugal city of baroque stone with Braga Cathedral at its centre and Bom Jesus do Monte on the hill above. Ten hours fills the day, and May or June catches it before the heat.

gem:ostuni.text: White houses stack up the hill at Ostuni, a quiet Puglia town about four hours wide. Ostuni Cathedral tops the old centre, the dune coast lies a short drive below, and May or June lands before the beaches fill.

gem:ascona.text: Ascona sits on Lake Maggiore in Switzerland, a quiet resort village where the day gets measured in lake walks. The centre needs four hours, Locarno and its film festival sit next door, and the weather holds from May into September.

gem:sinaia.text: Peles Castle is the reason most people stop in Sinaia, a mountain town in the Carpathians with Sinaia Monastery a short walk on. Six hours takes in both; the Bucegi Mountains above are the reason to come June through September.

gem:belogradchik.text: The Belogradchik Rocks rise around this small Bulgaria town, with Belogradchik Fortress built straight into them and Magura Cave a short drive off. Two hours is plenty for the town, and the months that work are May through July plus September.

gem:kardamyli.text: Kardamyli keeps things small: a stone village on the Greece coast where the walking matters more than the sights. Two hours is enough for old Kardamyle, and the Taygetus trails above are why April and May are the months to book.

gem:dhermi.text: Summer is the whole point at Dhermi, a beach village on the Albania coast reached over the Llogara Pass. Two hours sees the village, Palasa Beach handles the swimming, and little happens outside June to August.

gem:rouen.text: Rouen stacks its gothic centre around Rouen Cathedral, with the Gros-Horloge arching over a lane nearby and the Musee des Beaux-Arts de Rouen close behind. Ten hours fills it, and June through September is the drier stretch in Normandy.

gem:bolzano.text: Bolzano is a mountain city in the Alps of northern Italy, and the South Tyrol Museum of Archaeology there keeps Otzi. Ten hours takes in Sigmundskron Castle and Ritten as well, and the town is at its best from May into September.

gem:bol-brac.text: Zlatni Rat is the picture here: a long spit of beach off Bol, on the island of Brac in Croatia. Vidova gora rises behind for the view down, four hours is plenty, and May, June or September beats the high season.

gem:bohemian-paradise.text: Bohemian Paradise is a landscape of rock and castles in Czechia, laid out for long walking loops. Trosky and Valdstejn Castle lead, with Hrad Kost in the valley below; seven hours of sights, and anything from May to September walks well.

gem:karlstejn.text: Karlstejn Castle stands over the village of the same name in Czechia, and good public transport makes it an easy day out. The castle and the Koneprusy Caves fill four hours between them, and the comfortable months run May to September.

gem:orava-castle.text: Orava Castle climbs a high rock in the Orava region of Slovakia, all towers and stairways stacked up the ridge. The tour runs about three hours, Mala Fatra National Park is the drive around it, and June to August is the time to go.

gem:hohenzollern-castle.text: Burg Hohenzollern sits on its own hill in Germany, the kind of silhouette that ends up on postcards. Six hours allows the castle and the walk out to Zeller Horn for the view back at it; the clear months are June through August.

gem:chiemsee.text: Lake Chiemsee is a broad Germany lake with two islands worth the boat: Herreninsel for Schloss Herrenchiemsee, Frauenchiemsee for the quiet. Six hours does both and the Chiemsee-Bahn, with May to September the best of it.

gem:rhine-falls.text: The Rhine Falls spreads across the whole width of the river near Schaffhausen, the biggest noise in this corner of Switzerland. Six hours takes in the falls and the Schaffhausen old town, and May to September is the obvious time.

gem:cannes.text: Cannes trades on film and seafront, a France coast city built around the Palais des Festivals et des Congres. Ten hours does the town; the Lerins Islands and Lerins Abbey are the boat trip out, and May or June lands ahead of the crush.

gem:porquerolles.text: Porquerolles is the quiet one among the Iles d'Hyeres off the France coast, sand and pine inside Port-Cros National Park. Six hours is a full day here, May through August is the run of good weather, and Levant Island lies next door.

gem:collonges-la-rouge.text: Red stone gives Collonges-la-Rouge its name, a medieval village listed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The lanes take three hours to work through, Chateau de Turenne and Obazine Abbey are the nearby stops, and May to September is open.

gem:ploumanach.text: Ploumanac'h is a coastal village in France, with the Oratoire de Saint-Guirec down on the shore and Chateau de Costaeres out on its islet. The coast path and Trestraou Beach fill four hours, and the months for it are June through September.

gem:cape-sounion.text: Cape Sounion closes off Attica at the water, a Greece headland where the old site of Sounion looks straight out to sea. The trip runs about five hours with the Theatre of Thorikos and Laurium on the way, any time from May to September.

gem:corvara-alta-badia.text: Corvara is a ski and walking village in Alta Badia, high in the Alps of Italy. Piz Boe rises straight above and Sassolungo fills the skyline; three hours sees the village, and the walking gets going June through August.

gem:merano.text: Spa water and mountain air built Merano, a town in the Alps of Italy where the pace stays slow. Tirol Castle and Trauttmansdorff Castle take up most of six hours, and the town holds up from May right through September.

gem:campo-imperatore.text: Campo Imperatore is a high empty plateau in the Apennines, inside Gran Sasso e Monti della Laga National Park in Italy. Corno Grande rises off one edge; six hours of walking makes a day, and June through August is the only reliable window.

gem:kjerag.text: Kjeragbolten is why people climb Kjerag, a Norway mountain with a very long drop below it. The route takes about four hours and only works June through August, with Kjeragfossen the other stop up there.

gem:loen-nordfjord.text: Mountains drop straight into the water at Loen, a small Norway village with Hoven above it and the Jostedal Glacier inland. Its sights run to about three hours, and July and August are the two months that really work.

gem:karpacz.text: Karpacz works both seasons, a resort on the Poland side of the Karkonosze with walkers in summer and skiers in winter. The Vang stave church sits above the town and Sniezka is the climb, four hours in all, June to August for the warmth.

gem:cascais.text: Boca do Inferno chews at the rocks on the edge of Cascais, a seaside town on the Portugal coast. Six hours is enough here; Pena Palace and Sintra National Palace make the trip inland, and May to September stays warm.

gem:arouca.text: Arouca sits inside a UNESCO Global Geopark in Portugal, where the walking is the point. Ponte 516 Arouca draws the crowds, the Monastery of Arouca and Pedras Parideiras take the rest of five hours, and May, June or September is the timing.

gem:santana-madeira.text: Santana sits on the northeast coast of Madeira Island, countryside rather than resort. The Laurisilva of Madeira runs behind it, Pico Ruivo and Pico do Arieiro are the climbs, about five hours of sights, and June to September to walk them.

gem:rabacal-25-fontes.text: Rabacal is a trailhead on the Paul da Serra plateau on Madeira Island, set in the Laurisilva of Madeira. The walks below take about three hours, and July through September brings the steadiest weather.

gem:madriu-valley.text: The Madriu-Perafita-Claror Valley takes up the wild quarter of Andorra, a UNESCO World Heritage Site of remote high country. Its trails fill about seven hours under Pic de la Colilla, and July and August are the only dependable months.

gem:biertan.text: The Fortified Church of Biertan sits on the hill above its village in Romania, ringed by its own walls. Two hours is the whole visit; the Lutheran churches at Atel and Copsa Mare are close by, and the months run May through September.

gem:vall-de-boi.text: Vall de Boi is a high valley in Spain, and its villages hold the Catalan Romanesque churches that earned the UNESCO listing. Sant Climent de Taull is the one to see first. The walk between them runs about four hours, best June to August.

gem:lugo.text: Walls built when Lugo was Lucus Augusti still ring the old town of this city in Galicia, and the circuit on top is a UNESCO site. Lugo Cathedral sits just inside them. Its walls and cathedral want a full day, easiest May through September.

gem:leon.text: Leon is a city in Spain whose cathedral is the reason most travellers stop. Casa Botines and the Basilica of San Isidoro follow it, with the Convento de San Marcos out at the edge. A long day, ten hours or so, and the weather holds May into September.

gem:grazalema.text: Grazalema is a Spanish mountain village of 2,160 inside a UNESCO biosphere reserve. The Sierra de Grazalema natural park is the draw, with Cueva de la Pileta and Acinipo in reach, and the village itself takes three hours. May, June and September suit it.

gem:guadalest.text: Guadalest is a mountain village of 454 people in Spain, gathered under El Castell de Guadalest. Puig Campana and the Sierra de Aitana stand behind it, and three hours covers the visit. June through August is the window, though a car helps.

gem:cap-de-formentor.text: Cap de Formentor is a bare cape on the island of Mallorca in Spain, and the lighthouse at the end of it is the point of the trip. Faro de Formentor takes about two hours with stops. Alcudia beach and S'Albufera de Mallorca lie back down the road.

gem:alcudia.text: Alcudia is a resort town on Mallorca in Spain, paired with the ruins of Pollentia at its edge. S'Albufera de Mallorca Natural Park is the other half of a visit, and five hours covers both. May, June and July are the best stretch.

gem:eilean-donan.text: Eilean Donan is a castle on a tidal islet in the United Kingdom, set where Lochs Duich, Long and Alsh come together. The castle and the run out to the Skye Bridge fill about five hours. June through August brings the light and the crowds.

gem:isles-of-scilly.text: The Isles of Scilly are a scatter of small islands in the Atlantic off the United Kingdom. St Mary's is the base, and Tresco Abbey Gardens is the one thing worth crossing water for, about seven hours ashore. Public transport is limited once there.

gem:achill-island.text: Achill Island is an island of 582 people off the coast of Ireland, better known for its cliffs than its villages. Slievemore and Croaghaun hold the walking, Old Head Beach the swimming, and four hours makes a first pass. June through September is the season.

gem:paklenica.text: Paklenica is a hiking park in Croatia cut into the Velebit massif. Vaganski vrh is the summit above it, and the trails below take about five hours. June, July and August are the months, though public transport is poor.

gem:castell-arquato.text: Castell'Arquato is a village of 2,392 in Italy, listed among the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Two hours is all it asks. Villa Verdi and Fidenza Cathedral are nearby for a longer day, and May, June or September suits it best.

gem:benidorm.text: Benidorm is a high-rise resort city on the coast of Spain, built around beaches and theme parks. Terra Mitica, Aqualandia and Mundomar fill a day, with Platja de Llevant below and Puig Campana behind. The sights run to nine hours, best May to July.

gem:palazzolo-acreide.text: Palazzolo Acreide is a UNESCO listed town in the Hyblaean Mountains of Italy. Akrai, the ruined settlement on its edge, is the main sight, with the necropolis of Pantalica further out. Best in May or June, and allow five hours.

gem:wittenberg.text: Wittenberg is a town in Germany where the Reformation began, and its sights stand within a few streets of each other. Castle Church and the Lutherhaus are the anchors, the Stadtkirche in between. The whole of it fits in six hours, mildest May to September.

gem:veenhuizen.text: Veenhuizen is a planned village of 950 people in the Netherlands, small but on the UNESCO list. Its lanes take about three hours to walk. The Drents Museum and Drents-Friese Wold National Park sit close by, though a car matters here, June to August.

gem:huddersfield.text: Huddersfield is a market town in the United Kingdom, large enough to pass for a city. Castle Hill and the Emley Moor transmitting station stand over it, while the Tolson and Colne Valley museums take the wet hours, nine in all. June through August is driest.

gem:wuppertal.text: Wuppertal is a German city in a narrow valley, and the Schwebebahn hangs above the river through the middle of it. Elberfeld is the old centre, the Engels-Haus and Skulpturenpark Waldfrieden after that. Two days rather than one, May through September.

gem:pontevedra.text: Pontevedra is a stone-built city in Galicia, Spain, and its old town rewards aimless walking. The Basilica of Santa Maria la Mayor and the roofless Ruins of San Domingos Convent lead a ten-hour list. Beach days at A Lanzada and Montalvo follow, June to August.

gem:buxton.text: Buxton is a spa town of 20,048 people in Derbyshire, in the United Kingdom. Kinder Scout, Peveril Castle and Lyme Park all want a car. Six hours in the town itself, and the hills around it are at their best June through August.

gem:langemark.text: Langemark is a village in Belgium among the cemeteries of the Ypres battlefields. The Menin Gate, In Flanders Fields and Saint George's Memorial Church all lie close by. Best between June and September, and four hours covers the ground.

gem:annelund.text: Annelund is a village of 503 in Sweden, next door to the UNESCO listed Engelsberg Ironworks. The works and the old oil factory beside it take about three hours. Amanningen lies at the door, and June through August is when it comes alive.

gem:sainte-enimie.text: Sainte-Enimie is a stone village in France on the Les Plus Beaux Villages de France list, and three hours sees all of it. Aven Armand and Cevennes National Park take the days out, Castelbouc the short walk. June to August, and a car for any of it.

gem:pescasseroli.text: Pescasseroli is a mountain village in Italy at the centre of the Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise National Park. Monte Meta is the walk, Lago di Barrea and Lago di Scanno the drives, and the village itself is a three-hour stop. Best in June, July or August.

gem:church-stretton.text: Church Stretton is a market town of 3,698 in the United Kingdom, better known for the hills around it than for anything in its streets. Ludlow Castle and Shrewsbury Abbey sit within reach, and three hours does the town. The hills fill from June to August.

gem:lido-di-jesolo.text: Lido di Jesolo is a long strip of sand and hotels in Italy, busy right through the summer. Caribe Bay is the family stop, the Laguna del Mort the quiet end, and four hours is a fair visit. May and June come before the worst of the crowds.

gem:lierganes.text: Lierganes is a small historic town in Spain, inland from Santander. The Cave of El Castillo and Cueva de La Pasiega lie close, and Cabarceno Natural Park makes an easy afternoon, about seven hours in all. Best from June into September.

gem:mitte.text: Mitte is the central district of Hannover in Germany, where the museums and the water are. The Sprengel Museum Hannover and the Landesmuseum Hannover lead, with the Kestnergesellschaft for newer work and Maschsee a walk away. Six hours, May to September.

gem:royal-tunbridge-wells.text: Royal Tunbridge Wells is a market town in the United Kingdom, useful above all as a base. Penshurst Place and Groombridge Place fill a day between them, with Bayham Old Abbey and the Trinity Theatre around the edges. Ten hours if the houses are done properly.

gem:abergavenny.text: Abergavenny is a market town in Wales with a castle of its own and three more within a short drive. Grosmont Castle, White Castle and Raglan Castle make the circuit, while Big Pit National Coal Museum is the other direction. The four together want six hours.

gem:wolverhampton.text: Wolverhampton is a city of 263,700 in the United Kingdom, industrial in its bones and light on tourists. Wightwick Manor and Moseley Old Hall make the better days out, with Dudley Castle a short way off. Ten hours of sights, best worked through June to August.

gem:kudowa-zdroj.text: Kudowa-Zdroj is a small town in Poland under the Stolowe Mountains, right on the Czech border. Szczeliniec Wielki in Table Mountains National Park is the day out, and the Skull Chapel in Czermna is the oddity. June through September is the walking season.

gem:palazzuolo-sul-senio.text: Palazzuolo sul Senio is a village of 880 people in the hills of Italy, on the Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. Two hours does the centre. The Futa Pass and the Raticosa pass are the drives in, and May or June is the time to take them.

gem:margate.text: Margate is a seaside town on the Isle of Thanet in the United Kingdom, half faded resort and half art town. Dreamland Margate and the Shell Grotto are the two to see, with Richborough Roman Fort inland. July and August fill the beach, nine hours of sights.

gem:la-manga-del-mar-menor.text: La Manga del Mar Menor is a thin bar of sand and hotels in Spain with water on both sides. Parque Regional de Calblanque is the wild coast next door, and Isla Grosa sits offshore. May through August, and four hours unless the beach holds.

gem:macclesfield.text: Macclesfield is a Cheshire market town at the point where flat country ends and the Peak District begins. Lyme Park is the grand day out, the old churches a quieter hour, and the list runs to ten hours. June to August is the time to walk.

gem:kivik.text: Kivik is a coastal village of 895 people in Sweden, with the King's Grave just outside it. Stenshuvud rises behind, and the beach at Havang is close. Best in June, July or August, and four hours is plenty.

gem:saint-geniez-d-olt.text: Saint-Geniez-d'Olt is a village of 2,068 in France, on the Les Plus Beaux Villages de France list. Bonneval Abbey and the Pont des Pelerins are the sights, with Lac de Saint-Andeol up in the hills. The village itself takes three hours, June into September.

gem:ullastret.text: Ullastret is a quiet inland spot in Spain within reach of the coast. Empuries and the lanes of Peratallada are the near ones, with Girona Cathedral and the Castle of Pubol further out. Transport is good here, and seven hours covers it, May through July.

gem:soko-banja.text: Soko Banja is a spa town in Serbia held between two mountains. Rtanj and Devica are the climbs, with Soko Grad standing over the town and Cerje cave nearby. Spa aside, five hours covers the sights, and May, June or September is the time.

gem:armacao-de-pera.text: Armacao de Pera is a beach village of six thousand on the coast of Portugal, three hours of sights in all. The cliffs at Praia da Marinha and the cove at Praia de Benagil draw the crowds, and the Castle of Silves waits inland. May through September.

gem:jaca.text: Jaca sits below the Pyrenees in northern Spain, a town of thirteen thousand with six hours of sights. The Citadel of Jaca and the Cathedral of Jaca stand within a few streets of each other, and the Royal Monastery of San Juan de la Pena repays the drive out.

gem:baarn.text: Two lakes, Eemmeer and Gooimeer, frame Baarn, a well-connected town in the Netherlands. Soestdijk Palace is the main call, with Singer Laren minutes away and six hours of sights between them. June through August is the pleasant stretch.

gem:mytikas.text: The village of Mytikas holds fewer than a thousand people on the coast of Greece. Nicopolis and its ruins lie close, Lefkada is within reach, and the sand at Monolithi is the local swim. May and June suit best; three hours of sights.

gem:ornans.text: The musee Courbet is what brings people to Ornans, a village in France listed among Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. Besancon and its Basilica of Saint-Ferjeux are a short drive off, four hours for the pair. June through September is the best of the year.

gem:karlstad.text: Karlstad is a city of sixty thousand in Sweden, where the Klaralven meets Lake Vanern. Karlstad Cathedral and the park at Mariebergsskogen carry a long day of ten hours. June to August is when the light lasts and the water warms.

gem:deruta.text: Deruta is a village in central Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia and a two-hour stop. The Basilica of San Francesco d'Assisi and Portiuncula are close enough to fold into the same day, best in April, May or September.

gem:ossana.text: Two hundred or so people live in Ossana, a mountain village in Italy on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. The Tonale Pass and Gavia Pass climb away on either side, with Presanella above. The village asks three hours, June to August.

gem:kasperske-hory.text: Kasperske Hory is a village of fifteen hundred in Czechia, set where Sumava National Park meets the Bohemian Forest. Kasperk Castle is the landmark, the lake at Laka the walk, four hours for both. The season is short, June through August.

gem:horsens.text: Horsens is a port city of sixty thousand in eastern Jutland, Denmark. Boller Slot and the grounds at Bygholm carry most of the nine hours of sights, and CASA Arena Horsens is the other landmark. June to August, with the lake at Mosso close by.

gem:appelscha.text: Appelscha is a village in the Netherlands between two national parks, Drents-Friese Wold National Park and Dwingelderveld National Park. Its own sights amount to three hours, so the heath takes the rest of a June to August day.

gem:vlissingen.text: Vlissingen is a port town of forty-five thousand on the coast of Zeeland, the Netherlands. Fort Rammekens holds the shore and Middelburg Abbey sits a short ride inland, six hours between them. June to August is the season, though buses are thin.

gem:noordwijk-binnen.text: Noordwijk-Binnen is the inland half of Noordwijk, a town behind the beach in the Netherlands. Keukenhof, the big name close by, and the Rijksmuseum van Oudheden over in Leiden make six hours easy, with Naturalis Biodiversity Centre in the same city.

gem:belves.text: Belves is a hill village of fifteen hundred in France, listed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Chateau de Beynac and Chateau de Castelnaud-la-Chapelle stand nearby, as does the Font-de-Gaume cave. Its sights run three hours, May to September.

gem:constantina.text: Constantina is a village in the hills of Spain, inside Sierra Norte de Sevilla Natural Park. The Castillo de la Hiedra looks down on it and Cerro del Hierro is a short drive off. April and May are the months; two hours of sights.

gem:pforzheim.text: Pforzheim is a city of over a hundred thousand where the Black Forest begins, in Germany. Ten hours is no stretch here: Burgruine Liebeneck, the Kollmar & Jourdan House, and the view from Buchenbronn Observation Tower. May through September.

gem:ruzova.text: Ruzova is a village of under six hundred in Czechia, in the sandstone country of Bohemian Switzerland. May through September, the walk to the arch at Pravcicka brana is the thing, with Saxon Switzerland National Park adjoining and four hours of sights in all.

gem:bad-langensalza.text: Bad Langensalza is a town of sixteen thousand in Germany, easy to reach by train. St Stephani and Schloss Altengottern anchor the six hours of sights, with more churches at St Vitus and St Andreas in the villages around. June to September is good.

gem:esbjerg.text: Esbjerg is a harbour city of seventy thousand on the west coast of Jutland, Denmark. Men at Sea stands over the water and the Esbjerg Water Tower over the town, with Fano and the beach at Hjerting close by. Ten hours of sights, June to August.

gem:miskolc.text: Miskolc is a city of over a hundred and fifty thousand below the Bukk mountains in Hungary. The Cave Bath is the signature stop, with the Castle of Diosgyor and the Synagogue of Miskolc after it. April to June and August are the months; ten hours of sights.

gem:obernai.text: Obernai is a town of twelve thousand in France, on the Les Plus Beaux Detours de France list. Mont Sainte-Odile on the hill above and the Chateau de Guirbaden are the pull, six hours in all. May through September, and trains are frequent.

gem:dormans.text: Dormans is a village of three thousand in France, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Chateau de Boursault and Chateau de Conde are the two houses to see, and the Oise-Aisne American Cemetery and Memorial is close; three hours, May to September.

gem:vouliagmeni.text: Vouliagmeni is a coastal village of four thousand near Athens, Greece, with the beach at Varkiza along the shore. Its own sights run two hours; the Acropolis of Athens and the Acropolis Museum are the reason to head into the city. April and May suit best.

gem:fredericia.text: The Little Belt Bridge lands at Fredericia, a coastal town of forty thousand in Denmark. Det Hvide Vandtarn and Hindsgavl Slot fill much of six hours, and Osterstrand is the town beach. June to August is the season.

gem:rokytnice-v-orlickych-horach.text: Rokytnice v Orlickych Horach is a village of two thousand in Czechia, under the ridge of the Orlicke hory. Velka Destna and Suchy vrch are the walks, with the Pastviny Reservoir below. June to August is the window, and four hours covers the village.

gem:lovas.text: Lovas holds barely five hundred people in Hungary, inside the Balaton Uplands National Park and its UNESCO Global Geopark. Tihany Abbey and the waterfront at Balatonfured are the near neighbours, a three-hour round in all. May, June and September are the pick.

gem:assen.text: Assen is a city of seventy thousand in the Netherlands, the seat of Drenthe. The Drents Museum is the strongest hour or two, and Drentsche Aa National Park runs alongside the town. Ten hours fills a day here, with June to August the best of it.

gem:cinfaes.text: Cinfaes is a country district in Portugal rather than a single town, five hours of sights spread across it. The Monastery of Arouca and the Castro of Monte Mozinho lead in May, June or September, with the Area Arqueologica do Freixo for anyone keen on ruins.

gem:moigrad-porolissum.text: Moigrad-Porolissum is a village of five hundred in Romania, built beside the ruins of Porolissum, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Zalau County Museum and the wooden church at Jac make up the rest, about three hours. May through September works.

gem:figueira-da-foz.text: Figueira da Foz is a beach town of forty-six thousand on the coast of Portugal. Serra da Boa Viagem rises behind the streets and Cabo Mondego Lighthouse marks the headland, six hours between them, with Praia de Quiaios up the coast. May to August is best.

gem:arinsal.text: Arinsal is a mountain village of fourteen hundred in Andorra, with Coma Pedrosa above it. The walk to Lake Engolasters and the Madriu-Perafita-Claror Valley are the outdoor draws, and Casa de la Vall is a short drive. June to August, four hours of sights.

gem:diever.text: Diever, a village of two thousand in the Netherlands, sits right at the edge of Drents-Friese Wold National Park. Dwingeloo Radio Observatory and Frederiksoord fill out a three-hour list, with Dwingelderveld National Park close by. June to August.

gem:hunnebostrand.text: Hunnebostrand is a coastal village of two thousand in Sweden. Nordens Ark is the one big stop, with Vaderoarna and Dyngo out in the water and Dynge Castle behind. June to August is the short season, and three hours covers the sights.

gem:candelo.text: Candelo, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, is a village of seven thousand in Italy. The sights sit mostly next door in Biella, the Museo del Territorio Biellese and the Cattedrale di Santo Stefano among them. The circuit runs three hours, May to September.

gem:trevoux.text: Trevoux is a village of seven thousand in France, on the Les Plus Beaux Detours de France list. The Chateau de Saint-Bernard and the Basilique d'Ars are the nearby calls, four hours between them. May to July, or September, and trains are easy.

gem:corciano.text: Corciano is a village of eight hundred in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia and a short drive from Lake Trasimeno. The big sights are in the city next door, the Fontana Maggiore and the Arco Etrusco among them, four hours in all.

gem:acquasparta.text: Acquasparta is a village of three thousand in Italy on the old Via Flaminia, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The ruins at Carsulae are the highlight, with the church of Santa Maria in Pantano nearby. April to June and September; three hours.

gem:paciano.text: Set near Lake Trasimeno in Italy, Paciano holds five hundred people and a place on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. San Silvestro and the Torre di Beccati Questo are the landmarks. May and June are the months, with three hours of sights.

gem:visso.text: Visso is a village of under eight hundred in the mountains of Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Monte Vettore and the Lago di Pilato rise above; the Collegiata di Maria Santissima is the stop in the village. May and June, three hours.

gem:gualtieri.text: The I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list includes Gualtieri, a village of three thousand in Italy. The Teatro comunale Ruggero Ruggeri is the set piece, with Pomponesco and the Duomo di Guastalla a few minutes away. April to June, or September; three hours.

gem:pandino.text: Pandino is a historic village of some seven thousand in Italy, on the roll of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Palazzo Pignano and Comazzo sit close by and fill out a half day. Best months are May, June and September, and transport is poor.

gem:follina.text: Follina sits among Le Colline del Prosecco di Conegliano e Valdobbiadene, a village of under two thousand in Italy. Monte Cesen and the Eremo di San Gallo are the walks worth making, and the village itself asks only three hours, May to September.

gem:rodemack.text: Rodemack, a village of fewer than a thousand in France, carries the Les Plus Beaux Villages de France label. The Schlass and Aspelt Castle make a half day of it. Best between May and September, and a car helps.

gem:flavigny-sur-ozerain.text: Flavigny-sur-Ozerain holds about seven hundred people, a village in France on the list of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Eglise Saint-Genest anchors the centre and the Alesia archeological excavations lie close by, three hours from June to September.

gem:la-couvertoirade.text: La Couvertoirade keeps its old walls whole, a small village in France on the Les Plus Beaux Villages de France list. The Presbytere and the church inside make an unhurried five hours, with Mont Aigoual rising close by. Best in June, July or August.

gem:saint-leon-sur-vezere.text: Saint-Leon-sur-Vezere is a village of some six hundred people in France, close to the decorated caves of the Vezere Valley. Grotte de Lascaux and Chateau de Losse are the two to book ahead, four hours for the pair, best May to July or in September.

gem:limeuil.text: Limeuil counts about two thousand people and a place on the Les Plus Beaux Villages de France list. Cadouin Abbey and Grotte de Cussac are the nearby stops in this corner of France. Its own streets take three hours, best in May, June or September.

gem:puycelsi.text: Puycelsi, a village of under six hundred people in France, belongs to Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Bruniquel Cave and Chateau de Bruniquel are a short drive off. The village itself takes three hours, May to September.

gem:nogent-le-roi.text: Nogent-le-Roi carries the Petites Cites de Caractere label, a village in France with unusually good transport. Tour du Pilori stands in the centre, and Maintenon Castle with its aqueduct sits close by, three hours of sights from May to September.

gem:noisiel.text: Noisiel carries the Villes et Pays d'art et d'histoire label, a town of about fifteen thousand in France. Chateau de Champs-sur-Marne and Chateau de Ferrieres are the grand houses close by. Six hours covers both, May to September.

gem:dawley.text: Dawley is a market town in the United Kingdom, historic and well connected. The Iron Bridge, Blists Hill Victorian Town and The Wrekin fill a long day close by, about nine hours, with June to August the best of it.

gem:grottaferrata.text: Grottaferrata is a town of some eighteen thousand in Italy, set between Lake Albano and Lake Nemi. Cattedrale di San Pancrazio and the Papal summer residence lead a six-hour visit, most pleasant in May, June or September.

AHO.text: Alghero sits on the coast of Sardinia in Italy, a historic town with a Catalan past and beaches on either side. Neptune's Grotto and Alghero Cathedral lead the sights, with spiaggia del Porticciolo close by, seven hours in all from June to August.

TRS.text: Trieste is a coastal city in Italy where the Slovenian border runs close to the centre, best seen May to July. Miramare Castle leads, with Grotta Gigante and the Risiera di San Sabba after it; ten hours of sights, and the transport is excellent.

SJJ.text: Sarajevo is the hill-ringed capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina, cheap to visit and easy on foot. Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque, the Latin Bridge and Sarajevo National Theatre lead; its sights run to seventeen hours, May through September.

gem:haarlem.text: Haarlem is a compact historic city in the Netherlands, with the sea at Zandvoort aan Zee just west. The Frans Hals Museum and Teylersmuseum are the reasons to linger, and Het Dolhuys adds a quieter hour. June to August is the time to come.

gem:brasov.text: Brasov is a medieval city under the Carpathians in Romania, usually paired with the castle at Bran. The Black Church and Catherine's Gate lead the old centre, with Tampa rising behind it. Ten hours of sights over a long May to September season.

gem:volterra.text: Volterra is a small walled town on a hill in Tuscany, Italy, Etruscan long before the medieval centre grew over it. Museo etrusco Guarnacci and Porta all'Arco are the two to see, plus piazza del Duomo, four hours in all from May to August.

gem:the-hague.text: The Hague is a coastal city in the Netherlands, seat of parliament and the courts though not the capital. Mauritshuis and the Peace Palace lead its seventeen hours of sights; Madurodam suits children and De Zandmotor is the beach, June to August.

gem:kitzbuhel.text: Kitzbuhel trades on snow and money, a ski town in Austria known for the Streif race on the Hahnenkamm. Six hours covers the town in summer, when the Kitzbuheler Horn and the Kaiser Mountains take over and the Schwarzsee is warm enough to swim.

gem:tubingen.text: Tubingen is a medieval university town in Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany, at its best from June to September. Schloss Hohentubingen looks over the old centre, Kunsthalle Tubingen handles the art, and the Schonbuch woods start at the edge, ten hours of sights.

gem:klaksvik.text: Klaksvik, the second town of the Faroe Islands, is the way on to the islands further north. Christianskirkjan is the one building to see and three hours covers the town, but the ferries to Kalsoy and Fugloy matter more, June to August.

gem:loket.text: Loket is a small medieval town in Czechia, wrapped around the castle that gives it its name. The rocks at Svatosske skaly and the woods of Kaiserwald are the walks close by, four hours in all, June to September.

gem:trebinje.text: Trebinje is a cheap, quiet town in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Ottoman in its centre with wine country around it. June to August is the season, and five hours takes in Hercegovacka Gracanica on its hill and Tvrdos Monastery down the road.

gem:parga.text: Parga is a coastal holiday town in Epirus, on the Greece mainland, with Valtos Beach around the headland. April and May are the months to come, before the heat; the Nekromanteion of Acheron is the trip inland worth making, four hours in all.

gem:tenby.text: Tenby is a walled seaside town on the coast of Wales, its harbour ringed by sandy bays and busy from June to September. Tenby Castle and the boat out to Caldey Island fill a three-hour morning, with Pembroke Castle and Manorbier Castle close by.

gem:glendalough.text: Glendalough gathers its monastery ruins in a quiet valley in Ireland, inside Wicklow Mountains National Park. The climbs up Tonelagee and Lugnaquilla start close by, and six hours covers the valley with one of them, June through August.

gem:st-davids.text: St Davids is the smallest city in Britain, a village-sized place on the coast of Wales. Its cathedral needs only three hours, but Pembrokeshire Coast National Park starts at the edge of town and boats run out to Ramsey Island from June to August.

gem:chester.text: Chester keeps Roman ruins under a medieval centre, an English city and the county town of Cheshire. Chester Zoo alone takes half a day, and Chester Cathedral and the Grosvenor Museum hold the history. Ten hours all in, best June to August.

gem:parma.text: Parma, in Emilia-Romagna in northern Italy, trades on food and art in equal measure and gave its name to both the ham and the cheese. Palazzo della Pilotta holds the Teatro Farnese and the galleries. Ten hours of sights, best in April, May or September.

gem:humlebaek-louisiana.text: Humlebaek is a small coastal town in Denmark with one reason to stop, the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art on the shore. Kronborg Castle and Frederiksborg Palace are close enough to add, making a six-hour day between June and August.

gem:hoge-veluwe.text: Hoge Veluwe is a national park of heath and woodland in the Netherlands, made for walking and cycling. The Kroller-Muller Museum stands in the middle of it, and three hours is the least the park deserves, from May to August.

gem:efteling.text: Efteling is a fairytale theme park in the Netherlands, built for families rather than thrill seekers. Six hours makes a full visit between May and September, and Aquanura closes the evening in water and light. De Loonse en Drunense Duinen lie close by.

gem:hillerod.text: Hillerod grew up around Frederiksborg Palace and its lake, a town of thirty-five thousand in Denmark. The baroque gardens and the Gribskov woods take the rest of a six-hour day, best from June to August.

gem:stralsund.text: Stralsund keeps a Gothic old town on the UNESCO World Heritage list, a coastal city in Germany. The Ozeaneum takes a couple of hours, the island of Danholm lies just offshore, and the whole place runs to ten hours in the June to August season.

gem:sankt-goar.text: Sankt Goar is a village of three thousand in Germany, under Rheinfels Castle in a UNESCO World Heritage stretch of valley. The Lorelei rises close by, and Oberwesel and Pfalzgrafenstein are a little further, four hours of sights between May and September.

gem:aiguilles-de-bavella.text: Aiguilles de Bavella is a line of sharp rock peaks in the mountains of France, crossed at the Col de Bavella. Monte Incudine is the long climb from there; two hours at the pass itself, June to August, and a car is the only way in.

gem:peyrepertuse.text: Chateau de Peyrepertuse is a ruined castle strung along a rock ridge in France, reached by a steep walk up. The climb and the walls take three hours; Chateau de Queribus stands on the next height and Pic de Bugarach rises behind, best June to September.

gem:cordes-sur-ciel.text: Cordes-sur-Ciel climbs a hillside in France, a fortified medieval village small enough to walk in an hour. Maison du Grand Veneur and the Jardin des Paradis are the stops in town, with Albi Cathedral a short drive away. Best from May to September.

gem:lille.text: Lille is a big city in the north of France with Flemish architecture, a student crowd and late nights. Ten hours of sights begin with the Vieille Bourse and the Citadelle de Lille, with Villa Cavrois out in the suburbs; May to September is the stretch.

gem:belle-ile.text: Belle Ile en Mer is a quiet island off the coast of France, seven hours of sights spread thinly across it. The Phare de Goulphar and the cliffs at Pointe des Poulains are the walks that matter, and the season runs June through September.

gem:elafonisi-crete.text: Elafonisi is a shallow beach area on the coast of Greece, easy going with children. Chrysoskalitissa Monastery stands inland and Kedrodasos Beach is a walk away, about four hours for the pair. April to June and September are the kind months.

gem:castel-del-monte.text: Castel del Monte is a UNESCO listed castle standing alone in the countryside of Italy. Alta Murgia National Park spreads around it and Trani Cathedral is nearby, four hours for all three. May, June and September suit best; public transport is poor.

gem:atlantic-ocean-road.text: The Atlantic Ocean Road hops from islet to islet along the coast of Norway, built as much for the view as the traffic. Storseisundet Bridge is the stop everyone makes, Kvernes Stave Church a short detour; four hours and a June to August visit do it.

gem:thorsmork.text: Thorsmork is a wilderness valley in Iceland, hemmed in by Eyjafjallajokull and Katla. June to August is the only sensible window, and the way in runs past Seljalandsfoss and Skogafoss, five hours of sights along it.

gem:berlengas.text: The Berlengas Islands lie off the coast of Portugal, a small group inside a UNESCO biosphere reserve where diving is the draw. Berlenga holds the Fort of Sao Joao Baptista and most of the four hours of sights, and the crossing is a June to August affair.

gem:furnas.text: Furnas is a spa village on Sao Miguel Island in Portugal, built around hot water and its own cooking. Furnas Lake is the walk to make and Agua de Pau Massif rises behind it, three hours all told. June to August brings the best of it.

gem:sao-jorge-azores.text: Sao Jorge is a steep, thin island in the Azores where walking is the reason to come. Pico da Esperanca runs along its spine and Faja do Ouvidor sits below, five hours of sights between them. July and August are the settled months.

gem:curral-das-freiras.text: Curral das Freiras is a quiet village sunk in a bowl of mountains on Madeira Island. Pico Ruivo and Pico do Areeiro rise straight above it, with Cabo Girao out on the coast; four hours and a June to September visit suit it well.

gem:piatra-craiului.text: Piatra Craiului is a hiking park in Romania set along one long ridge, with La Om at its top. Bran Castle stands nearby on the Rucar-Bran Pass and pairs well with a walk. July and August are the months, about four hours of sights.

gem:bardenas-reales.text: Bardenas Reales is a stretch of protected wilderness in Spain, empty enough that the tracks through it are the attraction. Tudela Cathedral is the nearest built sight, a short drive off. Two hours in the park is normal; April, May and September are kindest.

gem:laguardia.text: Laguardia is a medieval wine village in Spain, small and walled and walkable in an afternoon. Church of Santa Maria de los Reyes leads the sights, with the Bridge of Mantible out of town; three hours does it, May through September.

gem:brighton.text: The Royal Pavilion and Brighton Pier set the tone in Brighton, a beach city on the south coast of England, with Hove continuing west along the same front. Ten hours covers the sights, public transport is good, and June to September is the season.

gem:seven-sisters.text: The Seven Sisters Cliffs rise in a row along the coast of the United Kingdom, with Beachy Head at the far end and Eastbourne beyond it. The clifftop path is the whole point, seven hours at a walking pace; June to August is driest.

gem:rhossili.text: Rhossili sits at the end of the Gower Peninsula in the United Kingdom, a long sand bay with Burry Holms at its far tip. Oxwich Castle and Penrice Castle round out about six hours. June to August for the weather, and public transport is poor.

gem:studenica.text: Studenica Monastery sits in quiet countryside in Serbia, walled and listed by UNESCO. The day fills out with Zica, Gradac Monastery and Maglic all close by, five hours in total, and May to September is the easy stretch.

gem:roussillon.text: Roussillon is a hill village in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France and walkable in three hours. Senanque Abbey, Pont Julien and Village des Bories are all a short drive out. May, June and September are the months.

gem:fordingbridge.text: Fordingbridge is a market town at the edge of the New Forest in the United Kingdom, worth about three hours in itself. Breamore House and Rockbourne Roman Villa are the outings, with Salisbury Cathedral nearby and June to September the pleasant stretch.

gem:brescia.text: Brescia is a working city in Lombardy with two cathedrals side by side, the old Duomo Vecchio and the newer Duomo Nuovo. Palazzo della Loggia fronts the main square and Lake Iseo is close; ten hours of sights, best in May, June or September.

gem:bayonne.text: Bayonne is an old town in France, close to the coast without sitting on it. Its cathedral and the Musee Bonnat-Helleu make up much of six hours, and the beaches around Biarritz are a short hop. May to September is the stretch.

gem:pavia.text: Pavia is a brick university city south of Milan, with more churches than a day allows. The Certosa di Pavia outside town is the set piece, followed by San Michele Maggiore and the Visconti Castle; a full ten hours, and April to June or September.

gem:fabriano.text: Fabriano is a papermaking town in Italy, in the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. The Museo della Carta e della Filigrana tells that story, and the Grotta di Frasassi is the trip out; five hours of sights, May or June.

gem:jaen.text: Jaen is a provincial city in Spain, with a cathedral out of scale with the rest of it. The Arab Baths of Jaen and the Arco de San Lorenzo fill in around it, ten hours of sights in all. April and May are the months.

gem:aberdeen.text: Aberdeen is a granite harbour city on the northeast coast of Scotland. Ten hours of sights start with St Machar's Cathedral and the Aberdeen Art Gallery, and the beach runs right up to the centre. June to September is the best of the weather.

gem:ambleside.text: Ambleside is a small stone village at the top of Windermere, inside the Lake District National Park. Its walks go out to Scafell Pike and Helvellyn, or gentler by Elter Water; four hours in the village itself, June to August.

gem:nantwich.text: Nantwich is a Cheshire market town with its old centre still intact, Welsh Row included. Six hours covers it, longer with the drive out to Beeston Castle or Crewe Hall. Public transport is good, and June to August is the easy season.

gem:lourmarin.text: Lourmarin is a village in France with a chateau at its edge, listed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Silvacane Abbey and Apt Cathedral are near, and Mourre Negre rises behind for walkers; three hours here, April to June or September.

gem:tavistock.text: Tavistock is a market town on the western edge of Dartmoor, in Devon, at its best from June to September. Buckland Abbey and Cotehele are the houses worth the drive and Vixen Tor is up on the moor, five hours in all.

gem:umea.text: Umea is a university city on a river in northern Sweden, once a European Capital of Culture and thick with birch trees. Bildmuseet and Guitars, the Museum are the two to see, ten hours of sights in all. June and July are when the light lasts.

gem:sheffield.text: Sheffield is a large city in Yorkshire, steel by trade and edged by moors. The Crucible Theatre and Sheffield City Hall lead a long list, seventeen hours of it, with Ladybower Reservoir close for a day out. June to August is best.

gem:knaresborough.text: Knaresborough is a market town above a wooded gorge in North Yorkshire, its castle looking straight down on the river. Six hours is enough for the town itself, with Fountains Abbey, Studley Royal Park and Harewood House the outings from June to August.

gem:lloret-de-mar.text: Lloret de Mar is a resort town on the Costa Brava, busy in season and built around its beaches. Platja de Fenals and Platja de Canyelles are the calmer stretches, and the Jardin Botanico Marimurtra sits above the water; six hours, June to August.

gem:oulchy-le-chateau.text: Oulchy-le-Chateau is a village of a few hundred people in France, listed by UNESCO and quiet with it. The sights lie mostly outside it: Soissons Cathedral, Longpont Abbey and Saint-Yved de Braine, four hours between them and easiest from May to September.

gem:aschaffenburg.text: Aschaffenburg is a city in Lower Franconia, the usual way into the Spessart. Schloss Johannisburg stands over the Main with the Pompejanum beside it, and the Stadttheater Aschaffenburg is in the centre. Ten hours of sights, easiest May to September.

gem:skipton.text: Skipton is a market town where the Yorkshire Dales begin, castle above the high street and canal through the middle. The castle and Bolton Abbey fill most of six hours, with the Craven Museum for a wet one. June to August is easiest.

gem:halver.text: Halver is a small town in the hills of Germany, more about the water around it than the streets. The Aussichtsturm Karlshohe gives the view and Bevertalsperre is the walk, six hours of sights between them. June to August is the time, and a car helps.

gem:zamora.text: Zamora is a small city in Spain, its old centre listed as a conjunto historico. The Cathedral of Zamora and the Castillo de Zamora sit together at the top of town, with the Teatro Principal de Zamora below; ten hours if the churches are counted.

gem:castello-de-la-plana.text: Castello de la Plana is a city in Spain, its old quarter formally listed and El Fadri at the middle of it. The cathedral and the Basilica de la Mare de Deu del Lledo take up most of ten hours. May and June are the pick.

gem:coventry.text: Coventry is a rebuilt city in the West Midlands, known for the two cathedrals standing side by side. The cathedral and St Mary's Guildhall head a list that runs to seventeen hours, with Kenilworth Castle a drive out. June to September suits.

gem:meschede.text: Set in the wooded hills of North Rhine-Westphalia, Meschede is a quiet town with the Hennetalsperre reservoir on its doorstep. Konigsmunster Abbey and Burg Eversberg take up most of six hours, and June to August is the season for the water.

gem:fira.text: Fira is a clifftop village on Santorini in Greece, set high above the caldera. The ruins at Akrotiri and a boat out to Nea Kameni fill the three hours most visitors give it, best between May and September.

gem:terracina.text: Terracina is a beach town on the coast of Italy, backed by the ridges of the Monti Ausoni. April to June is the pick of the year, and about four hours takes in the Temple of Jupiter Anxur above and Terracina Cathedral below.

gem:aberystwyth.text: Aberystwyth is a market town on the Ceredigion coast of Wales, with a castle, a cliff railway and the National Library of Wales to its name. Six hours covers all three, and the town is at its best from June to September.

gem:newton-abbot.text: Newton Abbot sits inland on the River Teign in Devon, a market town better as a base than a destination. Buckfast Abbey and the caves at Kents Cavern are the draws nearby, with Bradley Manor closer in, six hours in all, best June through August.

gem:diksmuide.text: Diksmuide is a small town in Belgium with a UNESCO listing and good train links. The Yser Tower dominates it, the Ganzepoot locks sit at the edge, and the castles at Wijnendale and Beauvoorde round out a six-hour day.

gem:hawes.text: Hawes is a market village of under a thousand people in the Yorkshire Dales National Park. June through August is the window, and while three hours does the village, Pen-y-ghent, Whernside and Bolton Castle are all within reach.

gem:chinon.text: Chinon is a small town in France on the Loire, its castle strung out along the ridge above the river. Chinon Castle, the royal abbey of Fontevraud and Chateau de Montsoreau make up six hours of sights, and trains are good from May to September.

gem:hathersage.text: Hathersage is a small village inside the Peak District National Park. Kinder Scout and Lose Hill are the walks people come for, Ladybower Reservoir is close, and Peveril Castle a drive off, so allow four hours between June and August.

gem:lignano-sabbiadoro.text: Lignano Sabbiadoro is a beach resort on the Adriatic coast of Italy, busy all summer. The sand is the point, with two hours enough for the sights, among them the Faro di Punta Tagliamento and a trip inland to Aquileia. May to August is the season.

gem:solingen.text: Solingen is a city of steep wooded valleys in Germany, better connected than it looks. Burg Castle and the Mungsten Bridge are the landmarks, with Zoo Wuppertal and Elberfeld next door; ten hours is realistic, May to September.

gem:gelsenkirchen.text: Gelsenkirchen is a large industrial city in Germany, the Arena AufSchalke its best-known address. The heavyweight museums are next door in Essen, the Museum Folkwang and the Golden Madonna among them, so ten hours is easily filled.

gem:almunecar.text: Almunecar is a beach town below the Sierra de Tejeda on the Granada coast of Spain. The Castillo de San Miguel looks down over the old centre, and the Cueva de Nerja and the Acantilados de Maro-Cerro Gordo are close. Six hours does it, May to August.

gem:manilva.text: Manilva is a coastal town in Spain backed by the Sierra Bermeja. Its shore carries watchtowers at Punta Chullera and the Ciudad romana de Lacipo lies inland, four hours of sights in all, and May, June and September are the kinder months.

gem:dalby.text: Dalby is a village in Sweden with its woods protected as Dalby Soderskog National Park. Dalby Norreskog adds more walking and Lund Cathedral is a short hop away, which makes four hours between June and August about right.

gem:derby.text: Derby is an industrial city in Derbyshire with a strong line in museums. The Museum of Making tells the factory story, Derby Museum and Art Gallery and Pickford's House fill more of the ten hours, and June to September is easiest.

gem:stafford.text: Stafford is a market town in the middle of Staffordshire, its castle on a ridge above the town. Stafford Castle, Doxey Marshes and the halls at Milford and Ingestre add up to nine hours, best tackled June through August.

gem:leicester.text: Leicester is a large city in the East Midlands, its history packed into a compact centre. The King Richard III Visitor Centre, Leicester Cathedral and the Jewry Wall stand within a few streets, and there are seventeen hours of sights in all.

gem:marco-de-canavezes.text: Marco de Canavezes is a town in northern Portugal, strong on archaeology. The hillfort at Monte Mozinho and the dig at the Area Arqueologica do Freixo lead, and chapels such as Santo Isidoro fill out five hours; May or June is the time.

gem:tenno.text: Tenno is a village of barely five hundred people in the mountains of northern Italy. Lago di Tenno sits below it and Castello di Arco guards the valley, while Monte Bondone and Lago di Ledro are within reach; four hours in all, June to September.

gem:kurten.text: Kurten is a scattered town in the hills of the Bergisches Land in Germany. Altenberg Abbey is the set piece, Burg Castle and the Mungsten Bridge a short drive off and the Bevertalsperre nearer still; six hours in all, May through September.

gem:vuillafans.text: Vuillafans is a small stone village in eastern France, one of those on the Plus Beaux Villages list. The sights sit mostly downstream at Ornans, the musee Courbet and the Grand Pont among them, and four hours between June and September is plenty.

gem:scalea.text: Scalea is a beach town on the Tyrrhenian coast of Calabria, with an old quarter climbing the hill behind. Torre Talao stands over the sand, Dino island lies offshore and the Parco Archeologico di Laos is inland, a four-hour list in May or June.

gem:saint-lary-soulan.text: Saint-Lary-Soulan is a mountain village of about a thousand in the Hautes-Pyrenees. The Col du Tourmalet draws cyclists, Pic du Midi de Bigorre and Lac de Payolle the walkers, and four hours of sights leaves a June to September day free for the trails.

gem:kelsterbach.text: Kelsterbach is a small town on the Main in Hesse, quiet and well connected. The real sightseeing is next door in Frankfurt am Main, the Senckenberg Museum, Alte Oper and Goethe House among it, a good six hours from May to September.

gem:bad-homburg-vor-der-hohe.text: Bad Homburg vor der Hohe is a city in Germany below the wooded Grosser Feldberg. Saalburg Roman Fort is the standout, the Europaturm and Rodelheim are minutes away, and the ten hours of sights go easiest from May to September.

gem:spindleruv-mlyn.text: Spindleruv Mlyn is a mountain village in Czechia, tucked into the Krkonose National Park. Snezka and Lucni hora are the ridge walks, Wielki Staw the lake below them, and June to August is the time to be up there; four hours covers the marked sights.

gem:chauvigny.text: Chauvigny is a small town in the west of France, listed among the Plus Beaux Detours. Two hours covers St-Pierre and the Marche cave, with the abbey church at Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe and Chateau de Touffou short drives away, and May to September the pick.

gem:javea.text: Javea is a low-key beach town on the Costa Blanca in Spain. Six hours takes in the Church of Saint Bartholomew, the islets at Illa del Portitxol and Illa del Descobridor, and Castell de Denia up the coast; May and June are the kindest months.

gem:hasselt.text: Hasselt is the main city of Limburg in Belgium, compact and easy to walk. The Sint-Quintinuskathedraal and the old beguinage anchor the centre, the Japanese Garden is a short walk out, and ten hours fills a day from May to September.

gem:cullera.text: Cullera is a beach town on the coast of Valencia, the castle on the hill above it. Castell de Cullera and the Santuario de la Virgen del Castillo share that hill, the Torre del Marenyet stands on the shore, and five hours covers them in May, June or July.

gem:campo-ligure.text: Campo Ligure is a village of under three thousand in the hills behind Genoa. The Parco Naturale Regionale del Beigua and Monte Pracaban are on the doorstep and the coast at Pegli lies down the valley, so four hours from May to July suits it.

gem:combles.text: Combles is a village of about seven hundred in the Somme country of northern France. The Delville Wood South African Memorial and the Necropole nationale de Rancourt sit close by, the Musee Somme 1916 a little further, four hours in all.

gem:limin-mesoyaias.text: Limin Mesoyaias is a small coastal town on the Attica shore of Greece. The ruins at Brauron and the Archaeological Museum beside them are the reason to stop, and the Attica Zoological Park is close; four hours does it, best in April or May.

gem:bad-neuenahr-ahrweiler.text: Bad Neuenahr-Ahrweiler is a twin town in the Ahr Valley of Germany, easy by train. The Ludendorff Bridge and Apollinaris Church are the landmarks; Schloss Drachenburg and the Drachenfels lie a drive off, six hours in all from May to September.

gem:fougeres.text: Fougeres is a town in Upper Brittany, France, built around its castle. The Castle of Fougeres takes much of the six hours, and the Cordon des Druides and the Dolmen de la Pierre du Tresor lie just outside; June to September is the season.

gem:santa-pola.text: Santa Pola is a port and beach town on the coast of Alicante. The Castillo de Santa Pola holds the centre, the Ruinas del Portus Illicitanus sit at the edge and the Palmeral of Elche is inland; five hours is right, in May or June.

gem:sant-agata.text: Sant'Agata is a village of a few hundred in the hills of northern Italy. Medici villas bring people out this way, Villa del Trebbio and Villa Medici at Cafaggiolo among them, and Lago di Bilancino is close; four hours in May or June.

gem:tonnerre.text: Tonnerre is a small town in France built around the Fosse-Dionne spring. Chateau de Tanlay and Chateau d'Ancy-le-Franc are short drives out, Pontigny Abbey a little further, and three hours covers the town itself; come May to September.

gem:varberg.text: Varberg is a beach town on the west coast of Sweden, in Halland. Varberg Fortress sits right on the water, the Grimeton VLF transmitter stands inland, and the sand at Apelviken fills up from June to August; six hours of sights in all.

gem:nieuwpoort.text: Nieuwpoort is a town on the coast of Belgium with a UNESCO listing, good trains and a long beach. The Abbey of the Dunes and Raversijde lie along the coast, the Yser Tower stands a little inland, and six hours will do, June through August.

gem:o-grove.text: O Grove is a beach town on the Galicia coast of northwest Spain, at the neck of a peninsula in the Ria de Arousa. The harbour has boats out to Ons Island and the Atlantic Islands of Galicia National Park; six hours here, June through August.

gem:camigliatello-silano.text: Camigliatello Silano is a village of about 900 people inside Sila National Park in Italy, a UNESCO Man and the Biosphere reserve. Monte Botte Donato rises behind it and Lago Cecita lies below; three hours, and July or August for the cool air.

gem:bruniquel.text: Bruniquel is a small village in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, stacked under its castle on a limestone spur. The Bruniquel Cave draws the rest of the visitors; three hours covers both, best in May, June or September.

gem:gorinchem.text: The ramparts still ring Gorinchem, a river town of some 35,000 people in the Netherlands, with the Dalempoort standing at the water. Six hours is about right for the old centre, and Loevestein Castle across the river adds half a day.

gem:torrox.text: Sea and hills split Torrox in two, a coastal town in Spain with an old village uphill and a beach quarter by the Faro de Torrox. The Cueva de Nerja and the Sierra de Almijara are both nearby, five hours between them, with April and May the pick.

gem:wismar.text: Wismar is a Baltic port in Germany whose brick old town holds a UNESCO listing. St Nicholas Church rises over the harbour streets and the Schweriner See lies inland. Six hours covers the centre, with June, July and August the warmest.

gem:san-miniato.text: San Miniato is a ridge town of about 17,000 people in the province of Pisa, Italy, with towers and brick churches along one long street. The Leonardo Museum and a pair of Medici villas fill a six-hour visit, best made in May or June.

gem:barga.text: Barga is a stone hill village in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, looking across to Monte Tambura and Monte Prado. The Pascoli House-Museum is the thing to see indoors; three hours does it, ideally in May or June.

gem:konigswinter.text: Konigswinter sits on the Rhine below the Siebengebirge in Germany, a town of some 41,000 people. Drachenfels and Schloss Drachenburg are the climb, Heisterbach Abbey the quiet alternative; six hours for the pair, any month from May to September.

gem:aalsmeerderbrug.text: Aalsmeerderbrug is a village of barely 500 people in the Netherlands, strung along the water between lakes and polder. The sights are all nearby: the Frans Hals Museum, the Cathedral of Saint Bavo and the Grote Kerk, four hours of it, June to August.

gem:aguilas.text: Two bays and a castle shape Aguilas, a coastal town in Spain with a run of quiet coves either side. The Embarcadero del Hornillo marks the old harbour and El Fraile Island sits offshore; allow four hours, and aim for March to May while it is mild.

gem:hunnerberg.text: The high ground by the Waalbrug holds Hunnerberg, a leafy village of a few thousand people in the Netherlands. Kronenburgerpark and the Concertgebouw de Vereeniging are a walk downhill; the Royal Burgers' Zoo fills most of a four-hour day out.

gem:loos-en-gohelle.text: Loos-en-Gohelle is a village next to Lens in France, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Louvre-Lens gallery is the reason most people stop, with the Stade Bollaert-Delelis beside it and Arras Cathedral further on. Best months are June to September.

gem:oosterhout.text: Oosterhout is a city of just over 50,000 people in the Netherlands, built around the Grote kerk and the De Onvermoeide mill. Breda next door adds Kasteel van Breda and St Anthony of Padua Cathedral. Ten hours covers both, May to September.

gem:saint-raphael.text: Saint-Raphael is a resort town on the French Riviera, running along the shore next to Frejus. Frejus Cathedral, the Missiri mosque and the Ile d'Or offshore are the sights, about six hours; May and June come before the heat.

gem:naousa.text: Naousa is a fishing village on Paros, in the Cyclades, its old harbour lined with tavernas. Two hours covers the village; the rest of a stay goes to Golden Beach, Antiparos or Panagia Ekatontapyliani across the island, May to September.

gem:montargis.text: Montargis is a town of canals and small bridges in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. The Eglise de la Madeleine de Montargis, the locks at Buges and Ferrieres Royal Abbey come to five hours, good from May to September.

gem:rastatt.text: Rastatt is a baroque town at the northern rim of the Black Forest in Germany, grouped around Schloss Rastatt and its gardens. Schloss Hohenbaden and Baden-Baden are close by; six hours covers the town, and May to September is the season.

gem:norcia.text: Norcia is a walled village in Italy at the edge of the Sibillini Mountains National Park, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The monastery of St Benedict stands on its main square; three hours is plenty, and May or June is best for walking.

gem:quercianella.text: Quercianella is a village of a thousand people on the rocky coast near Livorno, Italy, with swimming off the rocks rather than sand. Livorno adds the Duomo di Livorno and the Four Moors; four hours, April to June or September.

gem:oberems.text: Oberems is a hamlet of some 700 people in the wooded Taunus of Germany, under the Feldberg. The Rossert ridge and the trails around it are the reason to come; four hours of walking, and the woods are at their best from June to September.

gem:paralia.text: Paralia is a beach village in Greece, a strip of sand with cafes and small hotels behind it. Ancient Dion and the Archaeological Museum of Dion are the trip inland, two hours all told, and April or May comes before the summer rush.

gem:zdar.text: Zdar is a village of barely 1,200 people in the Bohemian Paradise, the sandstone country of Czechia. Hrad Kost and Valdstejn Castle stand within a short drive, Kozakov rises above the woods, and the walking season runs May to September.

gem:torre-del-mar.text: Torre del Mar is a beach town on the Costa del Sol in Spain, a long promenade with the Axarquia hills behind it. Six hours takes in the Palacio de Beniel and the Iglesia de San Juan Bautista inland at Velez-Malaga, any time from May to September.

gem:garrucha.text: Garrucha is a working fishing port in Spain with a beach village behind the quay. Castillo de las Escobetas guards the shore and Mojacar is just up the coast, an easy three hours, with April to June the comfortable window.

gem:vresina.text: Vresina is a village of about 2,400 people in Czechia, on the edge of a UNESCO Global Geopark. The Silesian Museum, the Synagogue in Opava and the Poodri Protected Landscape Area are all within reach. May to September is the season, four hours of sights.

gem:vilamoura.text: Vilamoura is a marina resort on the Algarve in Portugal, with the ruins of Cerro da Vila beside the harbour. Falesia Beach and its cliffs are the walk to make; two hours ashore is about right, and the water is warm from May to September.

gem:chios.text: Chios is the port and main town of an island in the eastern Aegean, Greece. The Castle of Chios stands over the waterfront; inland, the mosaics of Nea Moni of Chios and the emptied village of Anavatos are worth the four hours.

gem:san-enrique-de-guadiaro.text: San Enrique de Guadiaro is a village of about a thousand people near the coast in southern Spain. The sightseeing is down the road at the Moorish Castle, Gorham's Cave and St Michael's Cave, three hours in all, easiest in May, June or September.

gem:theoule-sur-mer.text: Theoule-sur-Mer is a village of barely 1,400 people on a rocky stretch of coast in France. Its four hours of sights are mostly on the water: the Lerins Islands and Lerins Abbey by boat, the Palais des Festivals et des Congres up the shore.

gem:santa-uxia-de-ribeira.text: Santa Uxia de Ribeira is a fishing town of some 27,000 people on the Ria de Arousa in Spain. The Dolmen de Axeitos sits inland and the dunes and lagoons of Corrubedo run along the coast. Best from June to August, five hours in all.

gem:canet-d-en-berenguer.text: Canet d'En Berenguer is a beach village in Spain next to Sagunto, a wide flat strand backed by low-rise blocks. Sagunto Castle and the Roman Theatre of Saguntum are the sights, four hours in all, and May to August for swimming.

gem:pec-pod-snezkou.text: Pec pod Snezkou is a mountain village of about 700 people in Czechia, tucked under Snezka. The Krkonose National Park starts at the last houses, and the climb to the summit is a four-hour outing, best attempted between June and August.

gem:braine.text: Braine is a village of about 2,000 people in France with a UNESCO World Heritage listing to its name. Soissons Cathedral and the Abbey of St Jean des Vignes are the sights worth the drive, four hours in all, and the Lac de l'Ailette is close.

gem:heerlen.text: Heerlen is a city of over 90,000 people in the hills of South Limburg, the corner of the Netherlands with real slopes. The Thermenmuseum keeps a Roman bathhouse and Kasteel Hoensbroek stands just outside; ten hours fills the day, May to September.

gem:thale.text: The Harz hills of Germany drop into a river gorge at Thale, a town of some 13,000 people. Quedlinburg, with its abbey and the Stiftskirche St Servatius, is the day out from here, six hours of it, and the gorge is walkable May to September.

gem:murzasichle.text: Murzasichle is a village of wooden highland houses in Poland, just outside Zakopane and at the edge of the Tatra National Park. Morskie Oko and Kasprowy Wierch are the walks to make, four hours in all, and July or August up high.

gem:archidona.text: The rock of the Pena de los Enamorados looms over Archidona, a white town of about 8,500 people in Spain. Its protected old centre, the Convento de las Minimas and the Virgen de Gracia sanctuary fill four hours; May, June or September.

gem:oberwesel.text: The Rhine runs past Oberwesel, a village in Germany still ringed by the towers of its old wall. Its four hours of sights take in Pfalzgrafenstein and Rheinfels Castle, and the Lorelei rock is a short way downstream.

gem:ruinen.text: Two national parks meet near Ruinen, a village in the Netherlands surrounded by heath and pine. Dwingelderveld National Park is the one at the door, the Dwingeloo Radio Observatory the oddity beside it; three hours in June or July is enough.

gem:nideggen.text: Nideggen is a hilltop town in Germany, built around Burg Nideggen and edged by the Hurtgen Forest. Mariawald and Hill 400 round out about six hours of sights, and buses are reliable. Best months run June through September.

gem:caldas-da-rainha.text: Caldas da Rainha is a town of ceramics and churches in Portugal, listed on the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. Museu de Ceramica and Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Populo fill six hours, and the castle at nearby Obidos rewards a detour.

gem:s-arenal.text: s'Arenal is a beach town on the Mallorca coast in Spain, more about the sand than the sights. Palma Cathedral, Bellver Castle and the Palma Aquarium are a short ride away and make up most of a six hour day, easiest between May and July.

gem:gamzigrad.text: Gamzigrad is a village of a few hundred people in Serbia, and the reason to come is Felix Romuliana, its UNESCO World Heritage site. Two hours is enough there. Lazar's Cave and Zajecar lie close, best in May, June or September.

gem:olloniego.text: Olloniego is a small village in Spain, a Conjunto historico within easy reach of Oviedo. The cathedral there, Santa Maria del Naranjo and Fuente de Foncalada make up four hours of sightseeing, and June through September is the time to go.

gem:mijas.text: Mijas climbs the Sierra de Mijas in southern Spain, a whitewashed Conjunto historico looking down on the Costa del Sol. Castillo de Suel, Castillo Sohail and Torre del Muelle push the sightseeing to eight hours, busiest from June to August.

gem:santa-ponsa.text: Santa Ponsa sits on the Mallorca coast in Spain, a beach town with little history on show. Magaluf Beach and Isla de sa Porrassa are the draws nearby, and Bellver Castle is a ride off. Six hours, May to July.

gem:poza-de-la-sal.text: Poza de la Sal is a village of a few hundred people in Spain, listed as a Conjunto historico. The Salinas de Poza de la Sal and Castillo de los Rojas take about two hours between them, and Frias Castle makes an easy add from June to September.
