gem:hellevoetsluis.text: Hellevoetsluis is a coastal town in the Netherlands with a historic core, and HNLMS Buffel is its set piece. The rest is water: Grevelingen, Brielse meer and the Krammer all lie close. Six hours covers it, best from June to August.

gem:spisska-stara-ves.text: Spisska Stara Ves is a village in Slovakia at the edge of the Pieniny, the way in to the Dunajec River Gorge. Cerveny Klastor sits downstream, with Szczawnica and the Beskids close by; reckon four hours and a June to August visit.

gem:hradec-kralove.text: Hradec Kralove is a city of ninety thousand in Czechia, big enough for a full day at ten hours of sights. The Cathedral of the Holy Spirit, the Museum of Eastern Bohemia and Gocarovo schodiste lead, and May through September is the stretch to pick.

gem:lejre.text: Lejre is a village on Zealand in Denmark, a short hop from Roskilde. Roskilde Cathedral and the Viking Ship Museum are the draws, four hours together, and the islands of Oro and Elleore add a detour. The warm months run June to August.

gem:ede.text: Ede is a city in the Netherlands that works better as a base than a destination, with the woods and heath of the Veluwe starting at its edge. Planken Wambuis, the Grebbeberg and the Posbank are the reasons to head out; ten hours, May through August.

gem:podgorzyn.text: Podgorzyn is a small village in Poland under the peaks of Sniezka and Szrenica, with the Vang stave church as its curiosity. The climb toward Smogornia, Maly Szyszak and Wielki Staw fills four hours, and the walking season is June through August.

gem:appingedam.text: Appingedam is a small town in Groningen, in the north of the Netherlands. Raadhuis Appingedam, the Petrus en Pauluskerk and Museum Mohlmann make a six hour round, with Delfzijl and the Kerk van Eenum minutes away. June to August is the liveliest.

gem:zanka.text: Zanka is a village on Lake Balaton in Hungary, inside a UNESCO Global Geopark. Its own sights run to about two hours, so the day tends to go to Tihany Abbey, Balatonfured and the hill of Csobanc. May, June and September beat the crowds.

gem:srednja-vas-v-bohinju.text: Srednja Vas v Bohinju is a small village in the Julian Alps of Slovenia, inside Triglav National Park. Lake Bohinj lies minutes down the valley, Vogel rises above it and Lake Bled is the bigger name nearby. The village itself asks four hours, May to September.

gem:skj-rhalden.text: Skjaerhalden is a village of six hundred on Kirkeoy in Norway, the base for Ytre Hvaler National Park. Two hours covers the village itself, while the park, the Koster Islands and Svinesund Bridge take longer. June to August is the season.

gem:satov.text: Satov is a small village in Czechia on the edge of Podyji National Park, a few minutes from Znojmo. Znojmo Castle and the Ducal Rotunda of the Virgin Mary and St Catherine are the historic stops, four hours all told, best May to September.

gem:haaksbergen.text: Haaksbergen is a town in Overijssel, in the east of the Netherlands, and an easy base for a day out. Museum Buurtspoorweg and the Haarmuhle sit close, while Rijksmuseum Twenthe and Roombeek fill out six hours. May to September is the pick.

gem:valtice.text: Valtice gives its name to the Lednice-Valtice Cultural Landscape in Czechia, and the village sits inside it. The Minaret in Lednice is the set piece, with Palava Protected Landscape Area and Dolni Vestonice close by, four hours in all, May to September.

gem:militello-in-val-di-catania.text: Militello in Val di Catania is a UNESCO listed village in Italy, also one of the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Santa Maria Maggiore, Chiesa di San Rocco and the Santuario di Santa Maria della Stella make up its three hours of sights. May is the month.

gem:pontarlier.text: Pontarlier is a town of twenty thousand in France, on the Les Plus Beaux Detours de France list and watched over by Fort de Joux. Porte Saint-Pierre and Place Saint-Pierre hold the old centre, about five hours, and June to August is easiest.

gem:sperlinga.text: Sperlinga, six hundred people in Italy, sits below the Castello di Sperlinga. Two hours covers the castle and the Chiesa di Sant'Antonio Abate, while Nicosia next door adds San Nicola di Bari Cathedral. May through August is the best run.

gem:cella-monte.text: Cella Monte counts fewer than four hundred residents, a village in Italy on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. The Chiesa parrocchiale di San Bartolomeo leads a short round of churches, three hours at a stroll. May, June and September are kind.

gem:bienno.text: Bienno lies beside Val Grigna in Italy, one of the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The day spreads out to Piancogno, Berzo Inferiore, Cividate Camuno and Malegno, four hours together, and June through September is the window.

gem:nocera-umbra.text: Nocera Umbra is a village in Italy under Monte Pennino, on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. The Chiesa di Santa Maria Assunta is the main call and Parco Regionale del Monte Subasio the nearest big walk, three hours across the two, best in May or June.

gem:corinaldo.text: Corinaldo is a walled village in Italy, and the Mura di Corinaldo are what people come for. The walls and the Museo di rievocazione storica take three hours, with Suasa and the Domus dei Coiedii a short run out in May or June.

gem:passignano-sul-trasimeno.text: Passignano sul Trasimeno is a lakeside village in Italy, with Castello Guglielmi above the water of Lake Trasimeno. Campo del Sole and Lake Trasimeno Park take about three hours between them. May, June and September are the easy months.

gem:torgiano.text: Torgiano is a village in Italy where the museums do the work, chief among them the Museo dell'olivo e dell'olio. The Museo regionale della Ceramica and the Pinacoteca Comunale di Deruta are close, three hours in all, best in May, June or September.

gem:dozza.text: Dozza grew up around the Rocca Sforzesca in Italy, a village on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. The castle and the Santuario della Beata Vergine del Piratello are worth three hours, and May, June or September is the time to come.

gem:saint-claude.text: Saint-Claude is a town of twelve thousand in France, on the Les Plus Beaux Detours de France list. Saint-Claude Cathedral, the palais abbatial de Saint-Claude and Place de l'Abbaye come to five hours, with Lac de Vouglans a drive off. June to September.

gem:san-gemini.text: San Gemini is a small village in Italy, and the site at Carsulae is just up the road. Palazzo Cesi and the Chiesa dei santi Cosma e Damiano add up to three hours, and the shoulder months of May, June and September suit best.

gem:panicale.text: The village of Panicale, five hundred people in Italy near Lake Trasimeno, belongs to the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. San Michele Arcangelo and the Santuario della Madonna della Carraia carry three hours, and May or June is when to go.

gem:montechiarugolo.text: Montechiarugolo is a village of a few hundred in Italy, and the Fondazione Magnani-Rocca is what brings most people. Museo Renato Brozzi and Castello di Guardasone spread four hours across the area, with April, May and September the kindest.

gem:castiglione-di-sicilia.text: Castiglione di Sicilia stands on the slopes below Etna in Italy, one of the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Cuba Bizantina and Chiesa di Sant'Egidio anchor three hours, with the Gurne dell'Alcantara just below. May and June are the months.

gem:calascibetta.text: Calascibetta is a village in Italy a short way from Enna, inside a UNESCO Global Geopark and on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. The sights are mostly over there, Castello di Lombardia and Rocca di Cerere among them, three hours in May.

gem:monte-castello-di-vibio.text: Monte Castello di Vibio, a village of five hundred in Italy, is known for the Teatro della Concordia. Santa Maria della Consolazione and the Tempio di San Fortunato take the total to three hours, and May, June or September is the moment.

gem:beuvron-en-auge.text: Beuvron-en-Auge is a village in France on the Les Plus Beaux Villages de France list. Chateau de Crevecoeur-en-Auge and Chateau de Victot-Pontfol are the nearby stops, three hours with the churches, and anything from May to September works.

gem:cassinetta-di-lugagnano.text: Cassinetta di Lugagnano is a small village in Italy with the Chiesa prepositurale di San Vittore Martire at its heart. Abbiategrasso, Corbetta and Robecco sul Naviglio are minutes off and stretch the visit to four hours. May, June and September are quietest.

gem:buccheri.text: Buccheri is a village of under two thousand people in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Monte Lauro and the Grotta dei Santi fill about three hours; nearby Palazzolo Acreide is worth the detour in May or June.

gem:charroux.text: Charroux, a village of a few hundred in France, carries the Les Plus Beaux Villages de France label. The Viaduc de Rouzat and the Chateau de Veauce are the draws, three hours in all, with the season running May to September.

gem:millesimo.text: Millesimo is a small historic village in Italy, at its best in May, June or September and listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Lago di Osiglia and the Monastero di Santo Stefano take up most of the three hours here.

gem:sepino.text: Altilia, the archaeological site outside Sepino, is the main reason to stop; the village itself belongs to I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Paleolab and San Pietro di Cantoni round out a two-hour visit, best made in May or June.

gem:balazuc.text: Balazuc is a stone-built village in France on the Les Plus Beaux Villages de France list. The Eglise Notre-Dame de Balazuc and Maison Bastide are the set pieces; three hours is plenty, with May, June and September the easiest months.

gem:bondone.text: Bondone is a mountain hamlet of just over two hundred people in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Lake Idro sits below, and Rocca d'Anfo, Bagolino and Magasa are within reach; four hours of sights, June through September.

gem:chateauneuf.text: Chateauneuf is a hilltop village in France on the Les Plus Beaux Villages de France list, wrapped around its chateau. The Chateau de Chateauneuf and the Chateau de Commarin fill most of three hours, and the village is liveliest from June to September.

gem:mercatello-sul-metauro.text: Mercatello sul Metauro is a quiet village in Italy carrying the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia designation. Its churches do the work: San Francesco Church, Santi Pietro e Paolo and the Abbazia di San Michele Arcangelo, two hours in May or June.

gem:miglionico.text: Castello del Malconsiglio stands over Miglionico, a village in Italy on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. Two hours takes in the castle and Chiesa Madre Santa Maria Maggiore, with Lago di San Giuliano close by; come in May or September.

gem:cremieu.text: Cremieu is a historic village in France, listed among Les Plus Beaux Detours de France and easy to reach on public transport. Chaise du Seigneur and the Chateau de Trept are the pick of three hours here, any time from May to September.

gem:talmont-sur-gironde.text: Talmont-sur-Gironde is a village of under six hundred in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Eglise Sainte-Radegonde is the one everyone photographs; three hours does it, and Plage de la Grande-Conche is close.

gem:epernon.text: Epernon is a small historic town in France, one of the Petites Cites de Caractere, with good rail links. The Aqueduc de Maintenon nearby and Les Pressoirs in town make three hours, anywhere from May to September.

gem:dewsbury.text: June to August is the run of good weather in Dewsbury, a market town of some sixty thousand in the United Kingdom. Oakwell Hall, Morley Town Hall and the Adwalton Moor battlefield spread across about ten hours, all reachable by train.

gem:chertsey.text: Chertsey is a market town in the United Kingdom with good rail links and a great deal of parkland next door. Windsor Great Park, Cumberland Lodge and the Air Forces Memorial are the draws, about six hours in all, easiest June to September.

gem:beeston.text: Beeston is a market town in the United Kingdom absorbed into the edge of Nottingham. Attenborough Nature Reserve is the local pull; with Nottingham Castle Museum and Art Gallery nearby the area fills seventeen hours, best June to September.

gem:gradella.text: Gradella is a very small village in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia and walked in minutes. Its neighbours fill out the four hours: Palazzo Pignano, Arzago d'Adda and Truccazzano, all good in May, June or September.

gem:wellington.text: Wellington is a market town in the United Kingdom in the shadow of The Wrekin. Six hours takes in The Iron Bridge and Blists Hill Victorian Town a short way off; June, July and August are the usual months.

gem:lens.text: Lens is a town in France whose surroundings hold a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Canadian National Vimy Memorial and the Notre Dame de Lorette cemetery shape a visit of about six hours, reachable by train, and May to September suits it.

gem:fiumicino.text: Fiumicino is a town in Italy with good transport links and one great set of ruins. Ostia Antica is the reason to come, with Portus and the Basilica of Santa Aurea alongside; six hours covers them, and April or May is the sweet spot.

gem:αργος.text: Lerna and the House of the Tiles lie just outside this town of twenty-two thousand in Greece, with Tiryntha a short drive on. The sites need about five hours; Karathona and Arvanitia are the beaches, and April and May are the months.

gem:ponte-buggianese.text: Ponte Buggianese is a small village in Italy, close to Montecatini Terme and easy to reach. Santi Stefano e Niccolao sits in the village; Buggiano Castello and the Cattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta are nearby, four hours in all, best May to September.

gem:pescia.text: Pescia is a town of some eleven thousand in Italy, a cathedral town with Montecatini Terme next door. Six hours covers Villa Mansi and the Cattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta, and May, June and September are the months that work.

DRS.text: Dresden is a baroque city on the Elbe in Germany, heavy with art and music. The Semperoper, the Zwinger and the Gemaldegalerie Alte Meister anchor roughly seventeen hours; transport is excellent, and May to September is the easy stretch.

SVG.text: Stavanger is a fjord city on the coast of Norway, as much a base for walkers as a place in its own right. Stavanger domkirke and Sverd i fjell fill about ten hours, Preikestolen is the big walk, and June to August is the window.

PDV.text: Plovdiv is a hill city in Bulgaria, a European Capital of Culture layered with Roman remains. The Plovdiv Roman theatre leads, with the Dzhumaya Mosque and the Regional Ethnographic Museum close behind; seventeen hours, best April, May or October.

gem:olomouc.text: Olomouc is a baroque city in Czechia whose Holy Trinity Column is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Saint Wenceslas Cathedral and Hradisko Monastery round out about ten hours; May to September is the pleasant half of the year.

gem:st-ives.text: Art and beaches share St Ives, a small Cornwall town on the United Kingdom coast. Tate St Ives and the Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden take up most of three hours, and the place fills between June and September.

gem:tomar.text: The Convent of Christ is why Tomar exists, a UNESCO World Heritage Site above a town of nineteen thousand people in Portugal. Castelo de Tomar and the Sinagoga de Tomar fill the rest of five hours, and April or May is the time to walk it.

gem:spis-castle.text: Spis Castle is the draw here, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Slovakia paired with the old town of Levoca. Spisska Kapitula and St Martin's Cathedral sit between the two; three hours covers the ruins, June to August, and a car helps.

gem:cudillero.text: Cudillero is a quiet village on the coast of Spain, as much about the food as the view. Its outings are the Oscar Niemeyer International Cultural Centre and the Cave of Candamo, three hours in all, and the months to aim for are June to September.

gem:vejer-de-la-frontera.text: Vejer de la Frontera is a quiet old town in Andalusia, Spain, still ringed by its walls. Los Canos de Meca and Playa de la Hierbabuena are a short drive down; five hours covers the town, best from May to September.

gem:sitges.text: Sitges is a beach town in Spain with a busy nightlife and a museum or two worth the time. Museu del Cau Ferrat and the Biblioteca Museu Victor Balaguer are the pick; the Garraf Massif rises behind, and May to August is peak.

gem:s-hertogenbosch.text: Den Bosch, properly 's-Hertogenbosch, is a cathedral city in the Netherlands with a reputation for food. The Citadel and Kamp Vught are the sober stops; ten hours suits the centre, and May to September is the comfortable run.

gem:freiburg.text: Freiburg im Breisgau is a university city in Germany where the Black Forest begins. Freiburg Minster dominates the old centre, Schauinsland gives the view, and ten hours is a fair allowance, best taken between May and September.

gem:aeroskobing.text: Aeroskobing is a small island village in Denmark, quiet and storybook in feel. Tranderup Kirke and nearby Langeland fill about five hours; June, July and August are the months to come, and transport is limited.

gem:fjallbacka.text: Fjallbacka is a small coastal village in Sweden, given over to sailing, eating and quiet. The Rock Carvings in Tanum and Nordens Ark are the trips inland; three hours of sights, with June, July and August the busy stretch.

gem:sighetu-marmatiei.text: Sighetu Marmatiei is a town in the Maramures countryside of Romania, and its past is not a light one. Sighet prison, now the Memorial of the Victims of Communism, leads the visit; the Merry Cemetery is close by, four hours, May to September.

gem:folegandros.text: Folegandros is a small quiet island in Greece, romantic and short on crowds. Naos Episkopis and the Chrysospilia Cave are the main walks, four hours in all; Sikinos lies next door, and the island wakes up from June to September.

gem:ston.text: Ston is a small fortified town on the coast of Croatia, on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List and known for its food. Mali Ston is a short walk away, the Peljesac Bridge and Mljet are close; three hours, best in May or June.

gem:st-andrews.text: Golf and an old university define St Andrews, a coastal town in Scotland. St Andrews Cathedral and St Andrews Castle are the ruins, the Royal and Ancient Golf Club the pilgrimage; six hours covers them, and the town is at its best between June and September.

gem:ullapool.text: Ullapool is a small Highland ferry village on the northwest coast of Scotland. The Summer Isles and Stac Pollaidh pull most visitors straight back out, with Corrieshalloch Gorge a short drive inland. Two hours does the village itself; June to August.

gem:stirling.text: The castle on its crag is why most people stop in Stirling, a town in central Scotland with good trains. Add the National Wallace Monument and the Church of the Holy Rude, and six hours fills easily. The months to aim for are June to August.

gem:bayeux.text: Bayeux is a small medieval town in Normandy with a cathedral at its centre and a war cemetery on its edge. Omaha Beach and Gold Beach lie a short way north along the coast. Six hours in town, best between June and August.

gem:passau.text: Baroque churches and the hilltop Veste Oberhaus define Passau, a German city on the Inn. Sights here add up to about ten hours, so give it a full day rather than a stop between trains. May through September is the season.

gem:kranjska-gora.text: Kranjska Gora is an alpine village in northwest Slovenia, ringed by the Julian Alps. Triglav National Park begins up the valley and the ski jumps at Planica stand next door; the village itself needs about four hours. June to August is the walking season.

gem:adrspach-teplice-rocks.text: Adrspach-Teplice Rocks is a maze of sandstone towers and ravines in northeast Czechia, reached from the villages of Adrspach and Teplice nad Metuji. The marked circuits take the better part of a day, around seven hours. Go between June and August.

gem:trebic.text: Trebic is a Czech town with two UNESCO entries standing side by side: the Jewish Quarter and the basilica of St Procopius. Six hours takes in both and the lanes between them, and the trains are good. May to September suits it.

gem:marianske-lazne.text: One of the Great Spa Towns of Europe, Marianske Lazne sits among wooded hills in west Bohemia. Castle Kynzvart and Tepla Abbey make the obvious trips out, while the town and its parks fill about six hours. June to August is peak.

gem:hortobagy.text: Hortobagy National Park protects the Puszta, the open grass plain of eastern Hungary. Its landmark is the Nine-holed Bridge, with Lake Tisza nearby, and four hours will do for a first look. April, May and September are the good months.

gem:altaussee.text: A village of three hundred on a lake under the Dachstein Mountains, Altaussee sits in the Alps of Austria. The Loser rises behind it and Lake Toplitz hides in the woods beyond, an easy four hours all told. June to August is the season.

gem:antibes.text: Antibes is a walled coastal city on the French Riviera, half old town and half the resort strip of Juan-les-Pins. Chateau Grimaldi and Fort Carre head the list, with Plage de la Salis just below. May and June are the pick, and ten hours fills a day.

gem:mont-ventoux.text: Mont Ventoux is a mountain rising alone above the villages of Vaucluse in southern France. The road up passes Chalet Reynard and Mont Serein, with Brantes on the quieter far side. Its summit and the drive take about three hours, June through August.

gem:cauterets.text: Cauterets is a spa and walking base at the edge of the Pyrenees National Park in southwest France. The trails climb toward Vignemale, while the Col du Tourmalet and Pic du Midi de Bigorre lie a drive away. Six hours of sights, June to September.

gem:perouges.text: On a low hill in eastern France, Perouges keeps its ring of medieval walls, one of the Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Tilleul de Perouges on the square and the Maison Thibault are most of it, and four hours between May and September sees the lot.

gem:briancon.text: Briancon is a fortified town high in the French Alps, a short way from the Italian border. Six hours does the ramparts and the old streets, while the Col d'Izoard and the Serre Chevalier slopes wait outside. Go between June and September.

gem:provins.text: Provins keeps its medieval walls and upper town intact, a UNESCO site in the Ile-de-France countryside. Six hours is enough for the ramparts, the Maison de Saint-Thibault and the Demeure des Vieux Bains, any time from May to September.

gem:pointe-du-raz.text: Pointe du Raz is a cliff headland on the western coast of France, looking out to the ile de Sein. Ar Men and the other lights mark the tide race offshore, and the Baie des Trepasses curves away north. Its paths run to three hours, June to September.

gem:cogne-gran-paradiso.text: At the gate of Gran Paradiso National Park, Cogne is a village of under a thousand in the Graian Alps of northern Italy. The Grivola rises behind and Monte Emilius closes the view north; three hours covers the village and its meadows. July and August.

gem:spoleto.text: Spoleto is a hill town in Umbria with a Roman past and a cathedral on a sloping square. The Ponte delle Torri strides across the gorge behind it, and the Teatro Caio Melisso sits in the centre; six hours is about right. May, June and September.

gem:san-vito-lo-capo.text: San Vito Lo Capo sits at the end of a cape in southern Italy, built around one long beach. Two hours is all the village asks, but the Zingaro Nature Reserve down the coast and Monte Cofano to the west take longer. May to July for the water.

gem:sestri-levante.text: Two bays and the headland between them make Sestri Levante, a seaside town in Liguria. The Galleria Rizzi and the Basilica dei Fieschi are the indoor stops, and the Portofino marine reserve lies up the coast. May, June and September, six hours each.

gem:voringsfossen.text: Voringsfossen is a waterfall dropping into the Mabodalen gorge in western Norway. The Hardanger Bridge and the heights of Hardangerjokulen lie close by, five hours of road and viewpoints in all. July and August are the safe months.

gem:rjukan.text: Rjukan is an industrial town on a deep valley floor in Norway, its waterfall and power works carrying a UNESCO listing. The Krossobanen climbs out of the shade and Gaustatoppen rises above, and three hours is enough for both. Go in June or July.

gem:blue-lagoon.text: The Blue Lagoon is a geothermal bathing spot in the lava fields of Iceland, next to Svartsengi. Fagradalsfjall and Gunnuhver are a short drive on, and transport out here is easy; two hours in the water is the usual stay. June and July are the season.

gem:marvao.text: On a quartzite crag in the Alentejo of Portugal, Marvao is a walled village with its castle at the highest point. Ammaia lies below and Castelo de Vide is the next stop along, and three hours in May or September walks the walls and lanes.

gem:serra-da-estrela.text: Serra da Estrela is a mountain range and natural park in central Portugal, and the road over the top to Torre is about two hours of stops. Covao dos Conchos and the Vale do Rossim Reservoir sit below, best reached June to August.

gem:foz-coa.text: Vila Nova de Foz Coa is a small town in the Alto Douro wine country of northern Portugal. The draw is the prehistoric rock art of the Coa Valley, a UNESCO listing across several sites that takes three hours to see. May and June are best.

gem:buzludzha.text: Buzludzha Monument stands alone on a ridge in the mountains of central Bulgaria, reached by a long road up. Shipka Monastery and the Thracian Tomb of Kazanlak break the drive, and the whole outing runs about three hours, June to September.

gem:alquezar.text: Alquezar is a village of three hundred set above a canyon in Aragon, Spain, inside the Sierra y Canones de Guara Natural Park. Pena Falconera rises at its back and canyoning routes start below; three hours is plenty for the village. May and September suit it.

gem:comillas.text: Comillas is a small town on the Cantabria coast of Spain, with a cluster of nineteenth-century mansions and three hours that will see them. El Capricho and the Palacio de Sobrellano are the two to visit, with the Cave of Altamira inland. June to September.

gem:monfrague.text: Monfrague National Park covers hills and river gorges in western Spain, entered from Torrejon el Rubio or Serradilla. The lookouts over the gorge make about four hours, with the Arrocampo Reservoir just east. April and May are the months to come.

gem:zahara-de-la-sierra.text: A white village stacked on a rock cone, Zahara de la Sierra looks over a reservoir in Andalucia with a castle keep above. The Sierra de Grazalema Natural Park spreads out behind; three hours suits the lanes and the climb. May is the month to pick.

gem:altea.text: Altea is a whitewashed town on the Costa Blanca, its old quarter climbing a hill above the beaches. The Serra Gelada park runs south and the Sierra de Bernia stands inland, while Platja de Llevant is the walk from town. Six hours is the measure of it.

gem:isle-of-mull.text: The Isle of Mull is one of the Inner Hebrides, an island of sea lochs and single-track roads. Staffa and Fingal's Cave are the boat trip, Ulva sits across a narrow sound, and Ben More is the climb. Its main sights take five hours, June to August.

gem:windsor.text: Windsor is a town in the United Kingdom built around its castle, with Eton College across the river. Saint George's Chapel is the thing to see inside the walls, and Frogmore House lies a little further out. Six hours covers it, June to September.

gem:portmeirion.text: Portmeirion is a village of pastel towers and piazzas built on a wooded estuary in North Wales. Harlech Castle and Criccieth Castle stand along the same shore, with Snowdonia rising inland; four hours walks the village and its paths. June to August.

gem:slieve-league.text: Slieve League is a run of high sea cliffs on the coast of Ireland, and the path along the top is a five-hour outing. Glencolumbkille Church and Cloghanmore lie inland, Inishmurray sits offshore, and the months are June through September.

gem:visoki-decani.text: Visoki Decani is a small city in western Kosovo with a UNESCO listing, set below the peaks of the Bjeshket e Nemuna. Six hours allows the town and a first walk toward Gjeravica and its lake, any time from May to August.

gem:dundee.text: Dundee sits on the River Tay in northeast Scotland, a port city now better known for design. The RRS Discovery is moored beside the V&A Dundee on the waterfront, and Claypotts Castle is out on the edge. Ten hours makes a long, full day.

gem:sveti-vlas.text: Sveti Vlas is a small resort village on the coast of Bulgaria, a short way north of Sunny Beach. The old town of Nesebar and its Church of Christ Pantocrator are the reason to walk that way; three hours is the whole of it. May, June, September.

gem:basford-stoke-on-trent.text: Basford is a village on the edge of Stoke-on-Trent in the United Kingdom, with market town roots. Alton Towers and Heighley Castle sit within easy reach, and Keele Hall rounds out about four hours of sights. Best in June or July.

gem:san-pedro-alcantara.text: San Pedro Alcantara sits on the southern coast of Spain below the Sierra Blanca ridge, a town of beaches and old towers. Torre Ancon and the King Abdelaziz Mosque fill about five hours, and May, June and September are the months to aim for.

gem:aylesbury.text: Aylesbury is a market town in Buckinghamshire carrying a full nine hours of sights. Waddesdon Manor leads, followed by the Roald Dahl Children's Gallery and Halton House, and the town is at its easiest between June and September.

gem:oswestry.text: Oswestry is a border market town in Shropshire, a short drive from the Welsh border. Whittington Castle stands nearby, while Chirk Castle and the Pontcysyllte Aqueduct lie just across it. Six hours covers them, June to August.

gem:sherborne.text: Sherborne is a small market town in northwest Dorset, built around its abbey and a pair of castles. Six hours takes in Sherborne Abbey, Sherborne Castle and the older ruin, with the Cerne Abbas Giant a short trip away.

gem:brilon.text: Brilon is a small forest town in the German uplands, close to the Rothaar hills. Langenberg and Diemelsee take up roughly six hours between them, and Muhlenkopfschanze sits a short drive off. Best months are June to August.

gem:gabrovo.text: Gabrovo is a town set in the Balkan hills of Bulgaria and named to the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. Etar and Sokolski Monastery fill much of a five hour visit, with Shipka Pass and Bacho Kiro cave close by in May, June or September.

gem:wigan.text: Wigan grew from an industrial market town in Greater Manchester and holds ten hours of sights. The Orwell at Wigan Pier and the Museum of Wigan Life carry the history, while Toughsheet Community Stadium and Leigh Sports Village take the sport.

gem:marsberg.text: Marsberg is a quiet town in the wooded hills of Germany, with Eresburg on the ridge above it. Arolsen Castle, Bredelar and the water at Diemelsee round out about six hours. June through September is the easiest stretch.

gem:oia.text: Oia is a small village on Santorini in Greece, above the caldera. The village itself needs about three hours, with boats out to Nea Kameni and across to Therasia. Red Beach lies a short ride off, and the season runs May to September.

gem:chepstow.text: Chepstow stands where the River Wye meets the Severn in South Wales, an old port town under a Norman castle. Chepstow Castle is the pull, with Tintern Abbey upstream and the Severn Bridge in view, six hours in all between June and September.

gem:ligourion.text: Ligourion is a quiet village in Greece, minutes from the ruins at Epidaurus. Its draw is the Ancient Theatre of Epidaurus, about three hours all in, with Tiryns and the Kazarma Mycenaean Bridge close enough for the same day in May or June.

gem:betws-y-coed.text: Betws-y-Coed is a village in the Snowdonia hills of the United Kingdom, ringed by castles and trails. Dolwyddelan Castle and Conwy Castle sit within a short drive, Snowdon and Llyn Llydaw a walk beyond. The village itself asks three hours.

gem:reading.text: Reading is a large city in the United Kingdom whose sights add up to seventeen hours. Reading Abbey and the Minster Church of St Mary the Virgin hold the historic centre, with Mapledurham House and Madejski Stadium filling out a June visit.

gem:chatillon-sur-seine.text: Chatillon-sur-Seine is a riverside town in the Cote-d'Or of Bourgogne, one of the Plus Beaux Detours de France. The museum holds the Vix Grave finds and Mont Lassois rises just outside, four hours all told between June and September.

gem:kingston-upon-hull.text: Hull, formally Kingston upon Hull, is a Yorkshire city on the Humber Estuary. Hull Minster, the Hull Maritime Museum and the Ferens Art Gallery lead a seventeen hour list, with the Humber Bridge a short drive out. June to September is mildest.

gem:santa-teresa-gallura.text: Santa Teresa Gallura is a small resort town at the top of Sardinia, with ferries over to Corsica. Its harbour sends boats to the Maddalena archipelago and Budelli, the Pink Beach among them, and three hours ashore is plenty in April or May.

gem:turnhout.text: Turnhout is the main town of the eastern Antwerp province in Belgium. Begijnhof Turnhout and St Catherine's Church take up much of five hours, with the Taxandria museum close and Bobbejaanland out of town. May to September works.

gem:torgau.text: Torgau is a castle town in the north of Saxony, Germany, and sits on the UNESCO tentative list. Schloss Hartenfels and its Schlosskirche take the centre of a six hour visit, with Lichtenburg concentration camp a sober stop nearby.

gem:sparta.text: Sparta today is a low, modern town in Laconia, Greece, with far less standing than the name suggests. Mystras on the slope of Taygetus is the real draw, and the Archaeological Museum of Sparta and the tomb of Leonidas fill five hours in April.

gem:kastel.text: Kastel is a small town in Germany facing Mainz across the river. The town's own Drususstein aside, the sights sit next door: Mainz Cathedral, the Gutenberg-Museum and Museum Wiesbaden, about six hours in all, best from May to September.

gem:blankenberge.text: Blankenberge is a beach town on the coast of Belgium, busiest through June, July and August. The sand at Albertstrand is the local draw, while Bruges, the Groeningemuseum and the Belfry are a short trip inland, six hours of sights in all.

gem:olsberg.text: June to August is the walking season in Olsberg, a small town in the Rothaar hills of Germany. Bruchhauser Steine and Langenberg are the climbs worth making, six hours between them, and the Hennetalsperre lies below.

gem:winterberg.text: Winterberg sits high in South Westphalia and works as a base for the Rothaar tops. Kahler Asten and Langenberg are the summits worth the climb, Grafschaft Abbey the quiet stop, and the six hours pass fast in July or August.

gem:bad-kissingen.text: Bad Kissingen is a thermal resort in Lower Franconia, one of the Great Spa Towns of Europe. Kurtheater Bad Kissingen, the Pfarrkirche and the ruin at Burgruine Botenlauben make about six hours, with May through September the season.

gem:pergola.text: Pergola is a hill village in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Two hours does the village; the Frasassi Caves, Monte Catria and the monastery at Fonte Avellana fill the rest of a May or June day.

gem:gliwice.text: Gliwice is an industrial city in Silesia, southern Poland, with a restored old centre. Gliwice Radio Tower and Gliwice Cathedral head a ten hour list, and the Guido Mine and Coal Mining Museum lies close by, best seen between May and September.

gem:les-sables-d-olonne.text: Les Sables-d'Olonne is a wide beach town on the Vendee coast of France. La Tour d'Arundel and the L'Armendeche lighthouse stand over the water, Villa Mirasol among the seafront houses, and the five hours pass easily from June to September.

gem:mailly-maillet.text: Mailly-Maillet is a village of a few hundred people in the old Somme battlefields of France, on the UNESCO list. Pozieres Memorial is minutes away, with the Musee Somme 1916 and the Basilique Notre-Dame de Brebieres at Albert, four hours in all.

gem:prudhomat.text: Prudhomat is a small village in southwest France with about three hours of sights of its own. Padirac Cave pulls the crowds close by, while Carennac and the Abbaye Saint-Pierre de Beaulieu make an easy loop from May to September.

gem:termoli.text: Termoli is an Adriatic resort in Molise, Italy, and its old quarter still sits inside its walls. Castello Svevo and Termoli Cathedral are the two stops that matter, about four hours, and May, June or September is the time to come.

gem:vitre.text: Vitre is a walled town on the eastern edge of Brittany in France. Chateau de Vitre and the Fortifications of Vitre take up much of six hours, with the Chateau des Rochers-Sevigne just outside. Public transport is good and June suits.

gem:portimao.text: Portimao is the second city of the Algarve in Portugal, known for grilled sardines and the beach at Praia da Rocha. Praia do Vau and Praia da Marinha are close, the old site at Alcalar inland, and six hours covers it from May to September.

gem:sainte-maxime.text: Sainte-Maxime is a beach town on the coast of France, a short hop from Saint-Tropez. Its own sand fills a morning; Port Grimaud, Pampelonne and Frejus Cathedral round out five hours, and May and June come before the heat.

gem:montoire-sur-le-loir.text: Montoire-sur-le-Loir is a village on the Loir in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Chateau de Montoire stands over it and Chateau de Lavardin is a short way off, with Vendome and Trinity Abbey filling out three hours.

gem:mechernich.text: Mechernich is a town in the Eifel hills of Germany, with Burg Satzvey on the doorstep. Bruder-Klaus-Feldkapelle stands out in the fields nearby, while Ordensburg Vogelsang and the Eifel Aqueduct fill six hours in June or July.

gem:capoliveri.text: Capoliveri is a hill village on Elba in Italy, part of the Tuscan Archipelago and its national park. The lanes and the beaches below take four hours, Mount Capanne rises across the island, and June to August is when the water is warm.

gem:canillo.text: Canillo is a mountain parish in Andorra, up the valley from Andorra La Vella. Sant Joan de Caselles and Our Lady of Meritxell fill about four hours, and Coma Pedrosa and Pic de Tristaina wait above for anyone walking in June or July.

gem:fussen.text: Fussen is a town in the Allgau at the southern end of Bavaria, Germany. Schloss Neuschwanstein and Hohenschwangau Castle draw nearly everyone, and Tegelberg and the Alpsee add to a six hour day best taken in June or August.

gem:varazze.text: Varazze is a beach town on the coast of Italy, with the Beigua ridge rising straight behind it. Monte Beigua and its regional park take the walkers, Savona Cathedral and Priamar Fortress the rest of six hours. May and June are the pick.

gem:remscheid.text: Remscheid sits in the hills of Bergisches Land in Germany, an easy run on good public transport. Mungsten Bridge is the sight that leads, with Burg Castle and the old centre of Lennep behind it, ten hours in all. June to August is the window.

gem:palamos.text: On the Costa Brava in Spain, Palamos works as both a working port and a beach town. Platja de Castell is the sand to aim for, with La Fosca nearer the centre and the Illes Formigues offshore. Six hours and a car, best in May, June or July.

gem:follonica.text: Follonica is a beach town on the coast of Italy with a couple of small museums behind the front. Palazzo Guelfi and the Pinacoteca Civica Amedeo Modigliani take a morning, the sand at Cala Violina an afternoon. May and June suit it best.

gem:cazalla-de-la-sierra.text: Cazalla de la Sierra is a protected old town in Spain, on the edge of the Sierra Norte de Sevilla Natural Park. Cerro del Hierro and Embalse de El Pintado fill about four hours between them, and May is the month worth planning around.

gem:dortmund.text: Dortmund anchors the Ruhr area in Germany and rewards a long stay, some seventeen hours of sights on good public transport. Museum Ostwall holds the art and Zoo Dortmund the family day. May through September is the season to pick.

gem:altamura.text: Altamura is an inland city in Italy where the cathedral sets the tone. Altamura Cathedral leads, then Chiesa e chiostro di Santa Teresa and the Dinosaur Quarry of Altamura, nine hours in all. May, June and September are the good months.

gem:turenne.text: Turenne is a village of under a thousand in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Chateau de Turenne fills most of the three hours here, with Obazine Abbey a short drive on. Transport is poor, so come by car, June to September.

gem:auray.text: Auray is a town in France recognised for its art and history, and a good base for the megaliths. The Carnac stones lie a short way out, with Gavrinis and the menhir d'Er Grah close by. Six hours does it, and June to September is the run.

gem:amerongen.text: Amerongen is a village in the Netherlands on the edge of Utrechtse Heuvelrug National Park. Amerongen Castle leads, with Huis Doorn and the old site of Dorestad within reach. Its four hours go best between May and August, by car.

gem:hel.text: Hel is a coastal village in Poland known for lighthouses and wartime history. Hel Lighthouse and the Seal Sanctuary in Hel are the stops most people make, three hours all told. June to August is the season, and public transport is poor.

gem:middelkerke.text: Middelkerke is a beach town on the coast of Belgium with a short summer season and limited transport. Abdij Ten Putte and the Abbey of the Dunes add weight to the day, while the Royal Galleries of Ostend sit nearby. Six hours, June to August.

gem:helmond.text: Helmond is a city in North Brabant in the Netherlands, ten hours of sights and good transport to reach them. Kasteel Croy and the Cube Houses lead, with De Roosdonck and the Opwettense watermolen out in the country. May to September.

gem:calella.text: Calella is a resort town on the Costa del Maresme in Spain, with beaches at the front and hills at the back. Calella Lighthouse is the walk to make; Castell de Santa Florentina and Parc del Montnegre i el Corredor lie inland. May to July, six hours.

gem:timmendorfer-strand.text: Timmendorfer Strand is a seaside resort in Schleswig Holstein in Germany, busy for three months of the year. The Holstentor and Burgtor gates of nearby Lubeck fill a half day, and Hansa-Park is the other draw, six hours across the two.

gem:compiegne.text: Compiegne is a palace town in Hauts-de-France, on the UNESCO list and easy to reach. Chateau de Compiegne is the set piece, the Forest of Compiegne the walk, and the Castle of Pierrefonds a short drive off. May to September, six hours.

gem:rogoznica.text: Rogoznica is a village of about a thousand people on the coast of Croatia, with poor transport and a good beach. Mala Raduca is the sand; the islands of Zlarin, Krapanj and Drvenik Veli lie offshore. Two hours covers the place, in May or June.

gem:torre-de-la-horadada.text: Torre de la Horadada is a small beach village in Spain, quiet once the summer weeks pass. The lagoons of Lagunas de La Mata y Torrevieja Natural Park draw a trip, with Isla Grosa and Isla del Baron out in the water; three hours, May or June.

gem:castellar-de-la-frontera.text: Castellar de la Frontera is a protected old village in Spain with about two hours of its own. Gibraltar makes the obvious day out, with the Moorish Castle, the Gibraltar Museum and the Great Synagogue. April to June is the window, and a car helps.

gem:alle.text: Alle is a small village in Belgium, under a thousand residents and poor transport. Bouillon Castle is the near landmark, with Chateau de Sedan and the Canal des Ardennes a drive on. Its three hours sit best between June and September.

gem:covarrubias.text: Covarrubias is a protected village of about 600 in Spain, small enough for three hours. The Abbey of Santo Domingo de Silos and Monasterio de San Pedro de Arlanza are the trips out, with Santa Maria de Lara close by. May to September.

gem:hruba-skala.text: Hruba Skala is a village in the rock country of Bohemian Paradise in Czechia, thinly served by buses. Trosky, Hrad Kost and Hruby Rohozec are the castles within reach, four hours between them. May through September works best.

gem:neoi-poroi.text: Neoi Poroi is a beach village on the coast of Greece under Mount Ossa. Platamon Castle is the one built sight, with the sand at Skotina and Paralia Panteleimonos along the same stretch. Two hours does it, and April or May is the time.

gem:vila-real.text: Vila Real is a town in Portugal on the doorstep of Alvao Natural Park, with good transport in. Mateus Palace is the reason most people come, and the Cathedral of Vila Real and Santuario de Panoias round out five hours. May, June or September.

gem:tvrdosin.text: Tvrdosin is a small town on the Orava in Slovakia with a church on the UNESCO list. The Church of All Saints of Tvrdosin is the stop, with Oravice and Sivy vrch close by, four hours in all. June to August is the season.

gem:ouddorp.text: Ouddorp is a coastal village in the Netherlands with a beach and almost no public transport. Grevelingen lies close by, and Voorne-Putten, the Sint-Lievensmonstertoren and HNLMS Buffel make the trips out, three hours in all. June to August.

gem:golem.text: Golem is a beach strip in Albania, Plazhi i Golemit its own sand and the Beach of Durres close by. The sights lie elsewhere: the Roman amphitheatre of Durres, and Skanderbeg Square and the Et'hem Bey Mosque in Tirana. May to July, five hours.

gem:eisenstadt.text: Set in Burgenland in Austria, Eisenstadt is a town of about 9,000 built around a palace. Schloss Esterhazy is that palace, with Eisenstadt Cathedral nearby and the Leitha Mountains rising behind. Six hours suits it, April through September.

gem:egmond-aan-zee.text: Egmond aan Zee is a small beach village in North Holland, four hours of sights and poor bus links. Abdij van Egmond stands just inland, and Hortus Bulborum, the Stedelijk Museum Alkmaar and Zaanse Schans are the trips out. June to August.

gem:roermond.text: Roermond is a cathedral town in Limburg in the Netherlands, with the Maasplassen lakes at its edge. The Munsterkerk is the building to see and Meinweg National Park the walk to take, about six hours together. May through September.

gem:landskrona.text: Landskrona is a coastal town in Sweden with a citadel and an island offshore. Uraniborg on Ven repays the crossing, while Landskrona Citadel and Landskrona konsthall fill the rest of six hours. June to August is the run of best months.

gem:liapades.text: Liapades is a small village on Corfu in Greece, with Myrtiotissa beach nearby and little in the way of buses. The Achilleion, Pontikonisi and Mount Pantokrator are the island trips; the village itself takes two hours. May to July is best.

gem:vila-real-de-santo-antonio.text: Vila Real de Santo Antonio is a border town in the Algarve, with the Guadiana International Bridge crossing to Spain. Castelo de Castro Marim and the marsh reserve behind it are the local trips, and Praia Verde the beach. May to September.

gem:dadia.text: Dadia is a small village in Greece at the edge of the Dadia-Lefkimi-Soufli Forest National Park, which is the whole reason to come. Two hours covers the village, transport in is poor, and May or September is the time to plan for.

gem:arraiolos.text: Arraiolos is a small town in the Alto Alentejo in Portugal, close enough to Evora to make it the day out. The Cathedral of Evora, the Roman Temple of Evora and the Capela dos Ossos are the sights, five hours in all. April and May are the months.

gem:rimburg.text: Rimburg is a border village of about 600 in the Netherlands, quiet and thin on buses. Aachen Cathedral and the Palatine Chapel in Aachen lie a short way over the line, with Abdij Rolduc and the Vaalserberg nearer, four hours in all. May to September.

gem:seborga.text: One of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, Seborga is a village of under 200 people in Italy. Castello di Dolceacqua, the Giardini Lowe and Villa Nobel all sit a drive down the valley, and four hours covers the lot. May, June or September.

gem:san-casciano-dei-bagni.text: San Casciano dei Bagni is a village of just over 500 in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Santi Leonardo e Cassia, the Oratorio della Concezione and the Teatro Comunale fill three hours, with Monte Amiata on the skyline. May and June.

gem:stockport.text: Stockport is a market town in the United Kingdom at the edge of Manchester, sharing its sights and its trains. The Manchester Museum, the Pankhurst Centre and Maine Road are the pull, ten hours across the two. June to August.

gem:bagnara-di-romagna.text: Bagnara di Romagna is a village of under 2,000 in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Rocca di Bagnara comes first, then the Teatro Rossini and Chiesa di San Petronio Vescovo, three hours in all. April to June, or September.

gem:hunspach.text: Hunspach is a village in France on the list of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, three hours from end to end. Ancienne maison Muntz and Ferme-chateau Le Bel are the village pieces, with Ouvrage Schoenenbourg a short way off. May to September.

gem:fontainemore.text: Fontainemore is a mountain village in Italy of just 121 people, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Monte Mars and Monte Cresto rise behind the Basilica Superiore and the Giardino Botanico; four hours of sights, June to August.

gem:sassoferrato.text: Sassoferrato, a historic village of some 3,800 in Italy, carries the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia label. Its ruins at the Parco archeologico di Sentinum are the draw, backed by the Museo d'arte sacra San Clemente; three hours in May or June.

gem:acquapendente.text: Acquapendente sits above lake Bolsena in Italy, a village of about four thousand on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. The Cattedrale del Santo Sepolcro anchors a three-hour wander that also takes in the Cappella di Santa Maria; May and June are kindest.

gem:celle-ligure.text: Celle Ligure is a seaside village of about 4,500 in Italy, with the beach at Albisola Marina close by. Villa Faraggiana, the Fortezza del Priamar and the Orto botanico di Villa Beuca fill four hours; pick May, June or September.

gem:ferla.text: Ferla is a hill village of some 2,500 in Italy, on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. Pantalica and its rock-cut tombs lead, with Palazzolo Acreide a short drive on. May and June bring the best light, and three hours covers it.

gem:monterosso-almo.text: Monterosso Almo is a stone village of about 3,000 in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. A three-hour circuit takes in the Chiesa Madre di Santa Margherita, the Castello Santapau and the Grotta dei Santi outside town; May and June are the season.

gem:mondavio.text: Mondavio is a walled village of 914 in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Its centre holds the Museo di rievocazione storica, and the Parco archeologico di Suasa with the Domus dei Coiedii lies a short drive off; three hours in all.

gem:cisternino.text: Cisternino is a historic village of about 5,700 in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Basilica di San Martino leads, with the Chiesa Madonna della Greca and the Cripta Madonna Odegitria a few streets away; three hours in all.

gem:trivignano-udinese.text: Trivignano Udinese is a village of 944 in Italy, part of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Its own sight is the Chiesa del Santissimo Redentore, though the Palmanova Fortress next door takes most of a three-hour trip, best in May or June.

gem:vogue.text: Vogue is a village of 765 in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, best seen in May, June or September. A four-hour loop takes in the Chateau d'Aubenas, the Eglise Saint-Pierre de Sauveplantade and the Oppidum de Jastres-Sud.

gem:montreal-fr.text: Montreal is a village of 719 in France, one of the Petites Cites de Caractere. Collegiale Notre-Dame is the centrepiece, with the Maison des Goix nearby and the Chateau de Montjalin a short drive off; three hours, and public transport is good.

gem:chateldon.text: Chateldon is a village of 775 in France, one of the Petites Cites de Caractere. Two hours covers the Chateau de Chateldon and the Chateau de Maulmont, with the Abbaye cistercienne de Montpeyroux close by. May through September is the long season.

gem:mornac-sur-seudre.text: Mornac-sur-Seudre is a village of 689 in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Eglise Saint-Pierre is the main sight, and three hours covers the lanes; the beaches at La Palmyre and Grande-Conche sit a short drive off, best June to September.

gem:saint-amand-de-coly.text: Saint-Amand-de-Coly is a village of 520 in France on the Les Plus Beaux Villages de France list. Sights point outward: the Grotte de Lascaux and the decorated caves of the Vezere Valley, with the Chateau de la Grande Filolie closer; three hours.

gem:luynes.text: Luynes is a village of about 5,000 in France, one of the Petites Cites de Caractere. Aqueduct and chateau sit in the village itself, while the Chateau de Villandry and the Chateau de Plessis-lez-Tours are a drive away; four hours all told.

gem:epping.text: Epping is a market town of about 10,700 in the United Kingdom, best walked between June and September. Epping Forest runs right to its edge and fills most of a six-hour visit; Copped Hall and Hainault Forest take the rest.

gem:chester-le-street.text: Chester-le-Street is a market town of about 37,000 in the United Kingdom, with the Angel of the North just outside. Finchale Priory and Waldridge Fell round out six hours, comfortably done between June and August.

gem:east-grinstead.text: Wakehurst Place, just outside East Grinstead, is the reason most people come to this market town of 26,500 in the United Kingdom. Saint Hill Manor, Starborough Castle and Bolebroke Castle round out six hours, with June to August the pick.

gem:chesham.text: Chesham is a market town of about 20,600 in the United Kingdom, at its best from June to September. Six hours takes in Chenies Manor and Hodgemoor Wood, with Berkhamsted Castle, Shardeloes and Tring Park spread nearby.

gem:keynsham.text: Keynsham is a market town of about 19,600 in the United Kingdom whose sights lie mostly in Bristol next door: Bristol Cathedral, SS Great Britain and Bristol Temple Meads. Six hours, ideally June to September.

gem:morley.text: Morley is a market town of some 57,000 in the United Kingdom, with Leeds next door. Ten hours of sights sit mostly over that line: Headingley, the Leeds Corn Exchange, the Middleton Railway and the First Direct Arena, best seen June to August.

gem:leatherhead.text: Leatherhead, a market town of about 43,500 in the United Kingdom, is best in the long days from June to September. Box Hill and Westhumble draw walkers, while Polesden Lacey, Painshill and Betchworth Castle fill out six hours.

gem:pudsey.text: Pudsey, a market town of about 25,400 in the United Kingdom, keeps its own sightseeing short and borrows the rest from Leeds. Headingley, the Leeds Corn Exchange and the Middleton Railway make up much of a six-hour day; June to August.

gem:verbania.text: Verbania is a lakeside town of about 31,000 in Italy. The Giardini Botanici Villa Taranto are the set piece, with the Eremo di Santa Caterina del Sasso along the shore and Mottarone above; six hours, May to September.

gem:jouy-en-josas.text: Jouy-en-Josas is a town of about 8,400 in France, next door to the Palace of Versailles. Versailles takes most of a six-hour day, the Petit Trianon and Grand Trianon included; June to September, and getting there is easy.

gem:carpentras.text: Carpentras is a town of about 29,700 in France, in the shadow of Mont Ventoux. Carpentras Cathedral and the Hotel-Dieu lead six hours, with the Bibliotheque Inguimbertine and L'arc romain close by; April to June, or September.

gem:genzano-di-roma.text: Genzano di Roma is a town of about 20,600 in Italy, set between Lake Nemi and Lake Albano. Cattedrale di San Pancrazio is the town's own sight; six hours stretches to the museum of the Nemi ships and the papal summer residence, June to August.

gem:delfzijl.text: Delfzijl is a town of about 28,600 in the Netherlands. Nicolaikerk, the Grote Waterpoort and the Mauritiuskerk carry a six-hour visit, with Oldambtmeer and the beach at Midwolda for the rest of the day; June to August.

gem:nemi.text: Nemi is a village of just over a thousand people in Italy, perched above Lake Nemi. June to August suits it best, and four hours covers the museum of the Nemi ships, the papal summer residence and Lake Albano.

gem:san-giuliano-terme.text: San Giuliano Terme is a village of about 2,400 in Italy, just outside Pisa. Pisa Cathedral and the Leaning Tower take up the four hours, with the beach at Marina di Vecchiano a short run away; April, May, June and September are comfortable.

gem:wageningen.text: Wageningen is a town of about 35,400 in the Netherlands. Kasteel Doorwerth leads, with the Cunerakerk and the water at Rijkerswoerdse Plassen filling out six hours; May to August, and transport is good.

TRN.text: Turin is a large city in the north of Italy, baroque in look and heavy on museums. Museo Egizio and the Mole Antonelliana lead about seventeen hours of sights, with the Basilica of Superga above the rooftops; May, June, September and October.

BRS.text: Bristol is a harbour city of nearly half a million in the United Kingdom, at its liveliest from June to September. Clifton Suspension Bridge and SS Great Britain lead about seventeen hours of sights, with Bristol Cathedral and Leigh Woods close in.

WAW.text: Warsaw, the capital of Poland, is a big and fast-changing city with a UNESCO listed centre. Royal Castle, the Palace of Culture and Science and Wilanow Palace lead seventeen hours of sights; May to September, and the transport is excellent.

WMI.text: Warsaw, the capital of Poland, is a big and fast-changing city with a UNESCO listed centre. Royal Castle, the Palace of Culture and Science and Wilanow Palace lead seventeen hours of sights; May to September, and the transport is excellent.

PFO.text: Paphos is a coastal town on Cyprus with a UNESCO listing and a deep archaeological record. Paphos Archaeological Park and the Tombs of the Kings take up most of six hours, with Coral bay for the beach; April and May, before the heat.

gem:biarritz-coast.text: Saint-Jean-de-Luz is a beach town of about 14,500 on the basque coast of France. Pheasant Island sits in the river mouth and Larrun rises behind, with the Cote des Basques and Milady Beach at Biarritz a short drive off; six hours, June to September.

gem:veliko-tarnovo.text: Veliko Tarnovo is a hillside city of about 59,000 in Bulgaria, known for its medieval fortress. Tsarevets takes the lead, with the Holy Forty Martyrs Church and the Transfiguration Monastery after it; nine hours, and April to June or September.

gem:kinderdijk.text: Kinderdijk is a village of under a thousand in the Netherlands, on the UNESCO list for its windmills. Mill Network at Kinderdijk-Elshout is the whole point and takes about four hours; Dordrecht and the Erasmusbrug are close by. June to August.

gem:leiden.text: Leiden is a historic city of about 120,000 in the Netherlands, shaped by its university. Rijksmuseum van Oudheden, Museum De Lakenhal and the Hortus Botanicus lead a ten-hour list, with the Hooglandse Kerk between them; June to August.

gem:telc.text: Telc is a Renaissance town of under six thousand people in the Bohemian-Moravian Highlands, listed by UNESCO. Its main square and the castle at Rostejn come to four hours, and the town looks best between May and September.

gem:lausanne.text: Lausanne is a university city on Lake Geneva in Switzerland, with public transport good enough to skip the car. The Olympic Museum and the Palais de Rumine anchor a full ten hours, with Montreux along the lake and June to September the time to be here.

gem:trakai.text: Trakai Island Castle sits on an islet in Lake Galve, the heart of a medieval lakeside town in Lithuania. Add the Peninsula Castle and Uzutrakis Manor and the place fills three hours; come in June, July or August, and expect to drive.

gem:mljet.text: The island of Mljet lies off southern Croatia, much of it given over to Mljet Nacionalni Park. Set aside four hours for the park and the beach at Sunj; boats in are limited, and May through August is the window.

gem:motovun.text: Motovun crowns a hill in Istria, a village of under four hundred people in Croatia where wine is the local business. Two hours is plenty here, and the Euphrasian Basilica is a short drive away; go between May and August.

gem:prizren.text: Prizren spreads below its fortress in Kosovo, an Ottoman and medieval city where mosques and churches stand close together. Sinan Pasha Mosque and the Fortress of Prizren lead nine hours of sights, and May, June and September are the months to pick.

gem:troodos.text: The Troodos Mountains fill the middle of Cyprus, a range of wine villages, painted churches and monasteries. Kykkos Monastery and Mount Olympus lead five hours of driving and stops; May and June work, and so do September and October.

gem:vianden.text: Vianden Castle stands above a small Luxembourg village on the Our, and it is why most people come. Bourscheid and Brandenbourg add two more castles to the same four hours, best done between June and September.

gem:hydra.text: Hydra is a low-key island of under two thousand people in the Saronic Gulf, and it suits a romantic weekend. Its harbour is most of the visit, about four hours, with Poros and Dokos in easy reach; the season runs June to September.

gem:arcachon.text: Arcachon is a family beach resort in Nouvelle-Aquitaine, and the Dune of Pilat rises just down the coast. The bay, the villas and a boat out to the ile aux Oiseaux fill five hours, best in June, July or August.

gem:cochem.text: Cochem is a wine town on the Mosel in Rhineland-Palatinate, with Reichsburg Cochem on the hill above it. Eltz Castle and the Calmont slopes are near enough for the same four hours; the vines look their best from May to September.

gem:alpbach.text: Alpbach sits high in the Tyrol, a small village in Austria where hiking is the main business. Kundler Klamm and the Wiedersberger Horn take up much of four hours, with Achensee close by and the trails at their best from June to August.

gem:gudhjem.text: Gudhjem is a harbour town on Bornholm, a quiet island in Denmark. Hammershus, Osterlars Church and a boat out to Christianso in the Ertholmene make a seven-hour day, best taken between June and August.

gem:husavik.text: Husavik sits on the coast of Iceland, a town of three thousand built around the Husavik Whale Museum. Two hours takes in the museum, Husavikurkirkja and the walk up Husavikurfjall, and June, July and August are the only real months.

gem:makrinitsa.text: Makrinitsa clings to the slopes of Pelion above Volos, a village of under seven hundred people in Greece. The Theofilos Museum of Anakasia and the long views need only three hours, and the walking is best in June, July and August.

gem:golubac.text: The fortress is the whole reason to stop at Golubac, a village of some sixteen hundred people in Serbia. Two hours is all it takes for the Golubac Fortress and the Tuman monastery, and April through June, or September, are comfortable.

gem:whitby.text: Whitby is a harbour town on the North Yorkshire coast, with Whitby Abbey standing on the cliff above. The abbey, the lighthouse and a walk out to Robin Hoods Bay fill five hours; July and August are the warm months, and the busy ones.

gem:salisbury.text: Salisbury is a small cathedral city in the United Kingdom, and Stonehenge stands on the plain a short drive away. Salisbury Cathedral, Old Sarum and Wilton House round out six hours, with June through September giving the longest days.

gem:lefkada.text: Lefkada is an island in Greece where the beaches carry the day, Porto Katsiki and Egremni above all. Meganisi and Skorpios lie just offshore, and four hours covers the main stops; the island really only opens up in June, July and August.

gem:sagres.text: Sagres sits at the southwest end of the Algarve, a windswept village of forts, lighthouses and surf beaches in Portugal. The Cabo de Sao Vicente lighthouse and Ponta de Sagres take three hours, and May through September is the run of good weather.

gem:peak-district.text: The Peak District is upland country in England, nearly all of it national park. Kinder Scout, Mam Tor and Peveril Castle are the landmarks, with Ladybower Reservoir below; nine hours barely scratches it, and June to August is best.

gem:bacharach.text: Bacharach is a wine village of about two thousand people in Germany, with Burg Stahleck on the hill above. Burg Pfalzgrafenstein and the Lorelei are close by, Oberwesel closer still; four hours does it, at any point between May and September.

gem:han-sur-lesse.text: Han-sur-Lesse is a village in Belgium where the caves are the attraction, and it works well with children. The Caves of Han-sur-Lesse take most of three hours, with Rochefort Abbey and Ciergnon Castle nearby; come between June and September.

gem:high-fens.text: The High Fens is a stretch of moorland and peat bog in Belgium, wild by the standards of the country. Signal de Botrange is the high point, with Baraque Michel and Lake Robertville close by; three hours of walking suits it, June to August.

gem:mons-belgium.text: Mons sits in Wallonia and wears its history openly, a former European Capital of Culture. Saint Waltrude Collegiate Church, the Mundaneum and the Neolithic flint mines of Spiennes make ten hours of sights, and May to September is comfortable.

gem:pannonhalma.text: Pannonhalma Archabbey crowns a hill in the Hungary countryside, a UNESCO World Heritage Site set in wine country. Two hours covers it, and the cathedral at Gyor is an easy add-on; May through September is the pleasant stretch.

gem:aggtelek.text: Aggtelek is karst country in Hungary, and the caves under it are a UNESCO World Heritage Site shared with the Slovak Karst. Cave tours and the trails of Aggtelek National Park run to seven hours, and any month from May to September works.

gem:velika-planina.text: Velika Planina is a high, empty plateau in the Alps of Slovenia, walking country rather than sightseeing country. Kamnik lies below and Mala Planina next door; seven hours makes a full day, and July and August are the two months that work.

gem:maulbronn.text: Maulbronn Monastery is a medieval abbey complex in Germany, listed by UNESCO and quiet most of the year. Kloster Maulbronn and a loop out to the Rossweiher fill four hours, with May into September the obvious window.

gem:lavaux.text: Lavaux is a ladder of vineyard terraces above Lake Geneva in Switzerland, protected by UNESCO. Its slopes run from Rivaz up to Puidoux, roughly four hours on foot, with Chillon Castle and Vevey along the shore; June to September suits it.

gem:oberstdorf.text: Oberstdorf is a mountain town under the Allgau Alps in Germany, a base for hiking in summer and skiing in winter. The Rubihorn, the Schattenbergschanze and the Heini Klopfer Ski Jump add up to five hours; hiking suits June, July or August.

gem:verzasca-lavertezzo.text: The Verzasca Valley runs down towards Lake Maggiore in Switzerland, narrow, green and made for walking. The Ponte dei Salti and the hamlet of Corippo are the set pieces, and six hours covers the valley road; June to August is when it makes sense.

gem:morcote.text: Morcote lines the shore of Lake Lugano in Switzerland, a village of about seven hundred people. Monte San Giorgio rises behind it and Campione d'Italia sits across the water; four hours is enough, with May to September the kindest months.

gem:epernay.text: Epernay is a wine town in Champagne, France, and its hillsides, houses and cellars are on the UNESCO list. De Castellane and the Abbaye d'Hautvillers account for much of six hours, and the best of the year runs May to September.

gem:metz.text: Metz pairs a great cathedral with a modern art museum, a historic city in Lorraine near Luxembourg and Germany. Metz Cathedral, the Centre Pompidou-Metz and the Porte des Allemands lead ten hours, and the city is at its best from May to September.

gem:crozon.text: The Crozon Peninsula is a wedge of cliffs and coves on the coast of France, much of it inside the Armorique Regional Natural Park. The Tour Vauban at Camaret and the beach at Trez Rouz are worth six hours between them, best from June to August.

gem:locronan.text: Locronan is a medieval village in France, well kept and listed among the Plus Beaux Villages de France. Its square and parish close, plus the beach at Kervel, come to three hours, and June through August brings the weather and the crowds.

gem:skopelos.text: Skopelos sits in the Sporades in Greece, an island made for beaches and slow days rather than sights. Skiathos, Alonnisos and Tsougria lie a short hop away, and four hours covers the island itself; the season runs May to August.

gem:sithonia.text: Sithonia is one of the legs of Chalkidiki in Greece, a coast of coves, islets and clear water. Two hours of sights is the honest figure; swimming and the islets of Diaporos and Kelifos are the point, from June to August.

gem:vergina.text: The royal tombs at Vergina hold what was dug out of Aigai, the old capital under this Greece village and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Two hours covers the Museum of the Royal Tombs in Aigai, and April and May are the months to come.

gem:monte-isola.text: Monte Isola rises out of Lake Iseo, a quiet island of villages carrying the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia label. The boat lands at Peschiera Maraglio, and Marone and Riva di Solto round out seven hours. May, June and September are calmest.

gem:sacra-di-san-michele.text: Sacra di San Michele crowns Monte Pirchiriano, a medieval site set high above the Avigliana lakes in Italy. The climb and Castello di Avigliana together make about four hours, and the walking is easiest from June to September.

gem:monopoli.text: Monopoli is a coastal town in Italy where Lama Monachile works as both landmark cove and town beach. Monopoli Cathedral and the Castellana Caves inland fill about five hours, and the water is warmest from May through August.

gem:su-nuraxi.text: Su Nuraxi is a village in Italy whose stone towers, Su Nuraxi di Barumini, hold UNESCO World Heritage Site status. The site itself takes three hours, and Giara di Gesturi is the obvious pairing. April and May are the months to pick.

gem:nordkapp.text: Nordkapp is a remote cape on the coast of Norway, reached across the island of Mageroya. The cliff viewpoint, Gjesvaerstappan offshore and Skarsvag Church come to five hours between them, and only July and August are really workable.

gem:karlskrona.text: Karlskrona is a baroque port city on the coast of Sweden, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Marinmuseum, Amiralitetskyrkan and Fredrik Church lead a generous ten hours of sights, best taken between June and August.

gem:kerlingarfjoll.text: Kerlingarfjoll is a remote mountain area in Iceland, reached by way of Kjolur and poorly served by public transport. Snaekollur, Lodmundur and Ogmundur shape the walking, about five hours of it, and the season runs May through July.

gem:sopot.text: Sopot is a spa and beach town on the coast of Poland, built around Sopot Pier and Krzywy Domek. Gdansk next door adds Oliwa Cathedral and Westerplatte, six hours for both, with June to August the beach months.

gem:szczeliniec-wielki.text: The Table Mountains are a walking area and national park in Poland. Szczeliniec Wielki and Bledne Skaly are the two rock scrambles that matter, about four hours together, with Wambierzyce and its basilica close by. The season is June through August.

gem:fanal-madeira.text: Fanal Forest is a wilderness walking area on Madeira Island, Portugal. Pico Ruivo and Pico do Areeiro rise inland and Porto Moniz sits down on the coast, so a full outing runs about six hours. July through September is the window.

gem:faial-azores.text: Faial is an island in Portugal that rewards a full day outdoors, from Cabeco Gordo down to the coast at Capelinhos. Praia do Almoxarife and the Botanical Garden of Faial round out about seven hours, with July and August the reliable months.

gem:turda-salt-mine.text: Turda is a town in Romania built around Salina Turda, the sight that draws the crowds. Cheile Turzii lies just outside and the Reformed Church sits in the centre, five hours in all, and any month from May to September suits.

gem:viseu-de-sus.text: Viseu de Sus is a remote mountain town in Maramures, Romania, and the way in to the Vaser. Ieud Hill Church and Maramures Mountains Natural Park take about four hours between them, and the months from May to September are the ones that work.

gem:targu-jiu.text: Targu Jiu is a city in Romania whose sculpture ensemble holds UNESCO World Heritage Site status. The Endless Column, the Gate of the Kiss and the Table of Silence are the reason to come, and six hours covers them. May, June and September are kindest.

gem:getaria.text: Getaria is a fishing and wine village on the coast of Spain, protected as a Conjunto historico. Zarautz and its beach sit next door and La Concha Beach is not much further, so four hours covers the village, best taken between June and September.

gem:ribadesella.text: Ribadesella is a family beach town in Asturias, Spain, protected as a Conjunto historico. Cueva de Tito Bustillo leads, with La Cuevona and the small Playa de Gulpiyuri close by, and three hours covers it. June to September is the safe bet.

gem:la-alberca.text: La Alberca is a small mountain village in Spain carrying Conjunto historico protection. Pena de Francia rises above the rooftops, Monasterio de las Batuecas sits behind it, and three hours does the lot. Its best months are May, June and September.

gem:alpujarras-pampaneira.text: The Alpujarras are a set of quiet villages on the flanks of the Sierra Nevada in Spain. Capileira makes the natural base, with Mulhacen and Veleta overhead, and two hours is enough in any one village. The paths stay open May through September.

gem:cazorla.text: Cazorla is a small town in Spain pressed up against the Sierra de Cazorla. Castillo de la Yedra stands over the streets and Castillo de La Iruela crowns the rock next door, four hours between them, and May and September are the months to aim for.

gem:rock-of-cashel.text: The Rock of Cashel is a medieval cathedral and castle site standing over a small town in Ireland. Two hours does it, with Hore Abbey just below and Cahir Castle an easy add. Its season is June through August.

gem:kravice-falls.text: The Kravica Waterfalls are what most people stop for in this corner of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Narona and Mogorjelo lie a short way off and the Mustaj-bey Bridge is closer still, five hours in all, and May, June or September avoid the crowds.

gem:lake-koman.text: Lake Koman is a long, narrow lake walled in by the Accursed Mountains of Albania. Thethi National Park and Grykat e Hapeta lie beyond the far end, and four hours covers the water itself, with May, June and September the settled stretch.

gem:mavrovo.text: Mavrovo National Park covers a wide stretch of mountain country in North Macedonia, with Mavrovo Lake at its centre. Korab is the peak that dominates and Saint Jovan Bigorski Monastery the building worth a detour, six hours in all, best June to August.

gem:norrkoping.text: Norrkoping, a city in Sweden, belongs to the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. Arbetets Museum leads the sights, with the Norrkoping Synagogue and Braborg Castle after it, ten hours for a full day and June to August for the weather.

gem:chemnitz.text: Chemnitz is a large city in Germany and a European Capital of Culture. The Karl Marx Monument is the landmark, Museum Gunzenhauser holds the art, and ten hours covers the centre plus the Kuchwald. May through September is the comfortable stretch.

gem:anghiari.text: Anghiari is a small hill village in Italy, one of the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The day fills out in Arezzo nearby, where Arezzo Cathedral and Casa Vasari stand close together, about four hours in all. Go in May or June.

gem:colchester.text: Colchester is a market town and city in Essex, standing on the Roman ground of Camulodunum. Colchester Castle and the Hollytrees Museum sit in the centre, Beth Chatto Gardens out of town, and ten hours is a fair estimate, June to September for the best of it.

gem:cirencester.text: Cirencester is a Cotswolds market town with a serious Roman past, set out at the Corinium Museum. The Church of St John the Baptist and the Roman Amphitheatre take up the rest of six hours, easily done between June and September.

gem:rochefort.text: Rochefort is a town in France carrying the Villes et Pays d'art et d'histoire label. The Rochefort-Martrou Transporter Bridge leads the sights and Ile Madame lies just offshore, six hours in all, best between June and September.

gem:bolton.text: Bolton is a market town turned city in Greater Manchester, big enough to fill a long day. Hall i' th' Wood Museum and Turton Tower carry the history, Radcliffe Tower is close by, and ten hours is realistic. The window is June to August.

gem:forli.text: Forli is a working city in Emilia-Romagna with more art than its size suggests. Abbazia di San Mercuriale and Musei in San Domenico lead, the Cattedrale di Santa Croce follows, and ten hours fills a day. April, May, June and September are pleasant.

gem:cheltenham.text: Cheltenham is a city in the United Kingdom with the Pittville Pump Room at its heart. Cleeve Hill and Leckhampton Hill rise on the edge of town and Sudeley Castle lies out in the country, ten hours all told, and June to September is the pick.

gem:penzance.text: Penzance is a coastal town in Cornwall with the Jubilee Pool on its seafront and St Michael's Mount just along the coast. Chysauster Ancient Village and Men-an-tol lie inland, six hours between them, and June to September is the run of good weather.

gem:biella.text: Biella sits at the foot of the mountains in Piedmont, a town on the UNESCO Creative Cities Network list. Biella Cathedral and the Biella Synagogue are in the centre, Monte Mucrone and the Basilica Shrine of the Black Madonna just above, six hours in all.

gem:venosa.text: Venosa is a small town in Italy on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. The Abbey of the Santissima Trinita and the Jewish catacombs of Venosa are the two to see, four hours with the Castle of Melfi nearby and best done in May, June or September.

gem:leek.text: Leek is a market town in North Staffordshire with the Nicholson War Memorial over its centre. Alton Towers and Little Moreton Hall are the bigger draws nearby, and five hours covers the town itself, most pleasantly from June to August.

gem:toro.text: Toro is a historic town in Spain, one of the country's Conjunto historico sites. The Colegiata de Santa Maria la Mayor is the landmark, with the Alcazar de Toro close behind, and five hours does the town, ideally in May, June or September.
