gem:westerham.text: Westerham is a small market town in Kent whose main draw is Chartwell just outside. The other sights on its list sit up in London, so four hours here is plenty, and June to September is the pleasant stretch.

gem:saarbrucken.text: Saarbrucken spreads along the Saar in Germany, a state capital with a compact centre. Ludwigskirche is the set piece, Saarbrucken Castle and Schloss Halberg follow, and ten hours fills a day between May and September.

gem:knokke.text: Knokke is a beach town on the Belgian coast with an art streak behind the seafront. Albertstrand and Laguna Beach take the sunny hours, Zwin sits at the edge of town, and six hours is plenty. June to August is when it fills up.

gem:scarborough.text: Scarborough Castle crowns the headland of this Yorkshire resort city, with the Rotunda Museum and Stephen Joseph Theatre below. The sights run to about nine hours, and July and August are the months to come.

gem:blackpool.text: Blackpool Tower rises over the Lancashire seafront, with North Pier, the Winter Gardens and Pleasure Beach Resort strung along below it. Ten hours will fill a visit, and June through August is when the resort is busiest.

gem:berkhamsted.text: The ruins of Berkhamsted Castle anchor this Hertfordshire market town, and St Albans Cathedral and Whipsnade Zoo lie within easy reach. Six hours covers the local sights, best from June through September.

gem:devizes.text: A market town in Wiltshire, Devizes puts the Wiltshire Museum and the Kennet and Avon Canal Museum within a few streets of each other. Avebury lies close by, and five hours from June to September covers the lot.

gem:much-wenlock.text: Wenlock Priory stands in ruins at the heart of this small Shropshire market town, and the Iron Bridge and Ironbridge Gorge are a short drive off. The sights fill four hours; come June to August.

gem:fulwood.text: Fulwood is a quiet town within reach of Sheffield Cathedral, the Crucible Theatre and Hillsborough Stadium, with Ladybower Reservoir and the national park the other way. June to August is the window, and six hours covers the sights.

gem:villena.text: Atalaya Castle towers over Villena, an inland town in Spain listed as a conjunto historico. Its second fortress, Castillo de Biar, and the Sierra de la Villa fill out about six hours; May, June and September are kindest.

gem:medebach.text: Medebach is a small town in the German uplands, set below Langenberg and Kahler Asten. Muhlenkopfschanze and the Dommel round out about six hours, with June through August the season for walking here.

gem:bishops-stortford.text: Bishops Stortford, a Hertfordshire market town, keeps the remains of Waytemore Castle and the Rhodes Arts Complex. Stansted Mountfitchet Castle and Windmill stand just north, worth folding into the same six hours. June to September is the stretch to pick.

gem:sainte-suzanne.text: Sainte-Suzanne is a small village in France on the Plus Beaux Villages list, and three hours is plenty. Evron Abbey, Hauterive Castle and the Dolmen des Erves are the pick, with June to September the easiest months.

gem:mangalia.text: Mangalia is a beach town on the coast of Romania, where Geamia Esmahan Sultan and Mangalia Mosque stand near the water. Movile Cave and Parc Mangalia round out four hours, and May through September is the warm stretch.

gem:bestwig.text: Bestwig sits among the wooded hills of the German uplands, with Langenberg, Hoher Eimberg and Dreiskopf in walking range. Burg Eversberg and Konigsmunster Abbey supply the history, the Hennetalsperre the water; six hours, June to August.

gem:wakefield.text: Wakefield Cathedral rises over a Yorkshire city that also holds Sandal Castle and the Theatre Royal Wakefield. The Yorkshire Sculpture Park just outside is why many come, and ten hours is barely enough. June through August is the time.

gem:le-cap-d-agde.text: Le Cap d'Agde is a beach village on the coast of France where three hours covers the sights. Agde Cathedral, the Roman Bridge and The Youth of Agde sit inland, with Mont Saint-Clair further off; May and June are the pick.

gem:newbury.text: Newbury is a market town with Donnington Castle above it, Benham Park on its edge and the Watermill Theatre a short way out. Highclere Castle nearby is the bigger draw. Six hours covers the lot between June and September.

gem:josselin.text: Josselin Castle rises straight from the Nantes-Brest canal in this small village in France, with the Basilique Notre-Dame du Roncier a few steps uphill. The whole thing takes four hours, best June to September.

gem:eslohe.text: Eslohe is a small town in the German hills, ringed by the Homert, the Saalhausen Hills and the Lenne Mountains. The walking is the point, about six hours of it, with the Hennetalsperre close by and June to August the season.

gem:llandeilo.text: Llandeilo is a small town in Carmarthenshire with Dinefwr Castle standing right above it. Carreg Cennen Castle, Llandovery Castle and Aberglasney are all a short drive out. The town itself asks three hours, and June to August is the best of it.

gem:castiglione-della-pescaia.text: Castiglione della Pescaia is a beach village in Italy, with the sands of Cala Violina down the coast. Grosseto Cathedral and Piazza Dante are a short run inland, and three hours covers everything; May and June are the months.

gem:cangas-do-morrazo.text: Cangas do Morrazo is a coastal town in Spain looking across the water to Vigo, with the Cies Islands offshore as the main event. Playa de Rodas and Praia de Samil handle the beach days, and six hours ashore is about right in June, July or August.

gem:estella-lizarra.text: Estella-Lizarra is a historic town in Spain, its old quarter holding the Church of San Pedro de la Rua and the Church of San Miguel. The Monastery of Irache and Monastery of Iranzu are a short drive out, and six hours does it between May and September.

gem:benicassim.text: Benicassim is a beach town in Spain with the Desert de les Palmes rising behind it. Castello Cathedral, El Fadri and the Roman Arch of Cabanes are close in, six hours' worth all told. April through June is the pick.

gem:sommepy-tahure.text: Sommepy-Tahure is a small village in France whose sights are places of remembrance, chief among them the necropole nationale de Sommepy-Tahure and La ferme des Wacques. Two or three hours is enough, June to September.

gem:segorbe.text: Segorbe is an old town in Spain set between the ridges of Serra d'Espada and Serra Calderona. Segorbe Cathedral is the set piece, and about six hours covers the historic core; April, May and October are the comfortable months.

gem:amboise.text: Chateau d'Amboise sits above the rooftops of this small town in France, with Clos Luce a short walk up the street. Chateau de Chanteloup and Chateau de Valmer make easy trips out, and five hours covers the town from May through September.

gem:ponferrada.text: Ponferrada Castle dominates this city in Spain, and the Basilica de la Virgen de la Encina stands below it. Santo Tomas de las Ollas and the old Central termica add to a full eight hours; May, June and September are best.

gem:guadalajara.text: Guadalajara is a city in Spain built around the Palacio del Infantado and the Co-cathedral of Santa Maria de la Fuente la Mayor. Its sights run to about nine hours, and May and September are the two months worth aiming for.

gem:castelo-branco.text: Castelo Branco is an inland town in Portugal, a member of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. The Castle of Castelo Branco and the Cathedral of Castelo Branco hold the high ground, and five hours does the town. May and June are the months.

gem:mseno.text: Mseno is a small village in Czechia with three castles in reach: Kokorin Castle, Houska Castle and Bezdez Castle. Lake Macha lies close by and the Skoda Auto Museum a little further. The castles alone are four hours, and May to September is the season.

gem:seligenstadt.text: Seligenstadt is a small town on the Main in Germany, its old centre built around the Basilika St Marcellinus und Petrus. Schloss Johannisburg and the Pompejanum stand a short way along the river. Six hours covers both, any month from May to September.

gem:hellendoorn.text: Hellendoorn is a village in the Netherlands on the edge of Sallandse Heuvelrug National Park, which is the reason to come. The Schildkerk and Pelmolen Ter Horst over at Rijssen fill out three hours, best June to August.

gem:cala-millor.text: Cala Millor is a beach village on Mallorca, and the caves inland are what set it apart. Coves del Drac, Coves dels Hams and Coves d'Arta come first, with Capdepera Castle above them, three hours all in. May and June are the months to aim for.

gem:anzio.text: Anzio is a coastal town in Lazio south of Rome, laid over the Roman site of Antium. The Sicily-Rome American Cemetery and Memorial and Torre Astura along the shore are the other stops, five hours all told, and May to August is the season.

gem:medina-del-campo.text: The Castle of La Mota is the reason most people stop at Medina del Campo, an old town in Spain. The Hospital of Simon Ruiz and the Church of Santa Maria Magdalena take up the rest of four hours. May, June and September are the months.

gem:manciano.text: Manciano is a small village in Italy, one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Terme di Saturnia, the Tarot Garden and the ruins at Vulci and Poggio Buco are all short drives out; three hours in the village itself, June to August.

gem:le-poet-laval.text: Le Poet-Laval is a village in France on the Plus Beaux Villages list, small enough to cover in three hours. The Ancien temple protestant and the Chateau des comtes de Poitiers lead, with Aiguebelle Abbey nearby; May and June suit it.

gem:buer.text: Buer is a town in Germany built around Arena AufSchalke, with the Musiktheater im Revier close by. Museum Folkwang, Essen Minster and the Baldeneysee are a short ride off. Six hours covers them, May through September.

gem:giulianova.text: Giulianova is a beach town in Italy, and the Santuario Maria Santissima dello Splendore is its landmark. Chiesa Di San Flaviano and the pinacoteca civica are the rest of a five-hour visit, best in May, June or September.

gem:la-chaux-de-fonds.text: The International Museum of Horology sets the tone in La Chaux-de-Fonds, a town in Switzerland built on watch making. Vue-des-Alpes and Tete de Ran rise behind it and Neuchatel Castle is close by. Six hours covers the town, June to August.

gem:cuxhaven.text: The Kugelbake marks the tip of Cuxhaven, a resort city on the German coast where the Elbe meets the sea. Fort Kugelbake, Schloss Ritzebuttel and the Wrackmuseum Cuxhaven fill out nine hours, with June to August the season.

gem:oropesa-del-mar.text: Old watchtowers line the shore at Oropesa del Mar, a beach town on the coast of Spain. Torre de la Corda and Torre Colomera are the ones to find, with the ridge of Desert de les Palmes inland. April to June, about six hours.

gem:ravda.text: Ravda is a beach village in Bulgaria, a short hop from Nesebar and the sands of Sunny Beach. Its own corner takes about three hours, and the Church of Christ Pantocrator is close by. May, June and September stay warm without the crush.

gem:schmallenberg.text: Up in the Rothaar Mountains, Schmallenberg is a German town built for walking. The climb to Kahler Asten and the Saalhausen Hills fills much of six hours, with Grafschaft Abbey for a quieter stop. June through August is the season.

gem:de-reit.text: De Reit is a village in the Netherlands with big days out on its doorstep: Efteling and Safaripark Beekse Bergen are both close. Loonse en Drunense Duinen and Koningshoeven Abbey round out four hours. May to September all work.

gem:janov-nad-nisou.text: Set in the Czech hills below Jested, Janov nad Nisou is a quiet village. Slovanka rises behind the houses, and Liberec, with its town hall and the Harcov reservoir, lies down the valley. June to August, four hours.

gem:mavrovi-anovi.text: Mavrovi Anovi is a small village inside Mavrovo National Park in North Macedonia. Mavrovo Lake lies below, Saint Jovan Bigorski Monastery is worth the drive, and the ridges of Korab and Deshat close the view. June to August, three hours.

gem:coca.text: The castle is the reason to stop at Coca, a small village in Spain. Castillo de Coca, the walls of La muralla and the Tower of Saint Nicholas take about two hours between them. May, June and September are the comfortable months.

gem:maasdam.text: Maasdam is a small village in the Netherlands beside the Hollandsch Diep, best in the June to August stretch. Dordrecht, the Euromast and Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen are the nearby draws, and De Biesbosch National Park adds reed marsh to a four hour day.

gem:hooghalen.text: Two national parks sit within reach of Hooghalen, a village in the Netherlands: Dwingelderveld and Drents-Friese Wold. The heath and the low ridge of Hondsrug fill four hours, and the Drents Museum covers a wet day. June to August is best.

gem:brihuega.text: Brihuega is a historic village in Spain, set in La Alcarria. The Church of San Salvador and the Church of la Inmaculada Concepcion stand in the town, while the castles at Torija and Jadraque sit nearby. May, June and September suit three hours.

gem:culla.text: Culla is a hilltop village in Spain, three hours of lanes and views with the inland sierras all around. Penyagolosa and the Muela de Ares rise close by, the rock shelters of Cova dels Cavalls are a short trip, and May through August is the warm run.

gem:gouwsluis.text: Gouwsluis is a small village in the Netherlands, ringed by the Kagerplassen and the Reeuwijkse plassen. Its four hours are spent in the museums nearby, Naturalis Biodiversity Center and the Temple of Taffeh among them, from June to August.

gem:nyborg.text: Nyborg is a coastal town in Denmark at one end of the Great Belt Fixed Link. Nyborg Slot and the Juelsberg estate fill most of five hours, and the bridge runs out past Sprogo. June to August brings the beach weather.

gem:lindos.text: On the coast of Rhodes in Greece, Lindos is a village under a rock. The Acropolis of Lindos stands on top, the Theatre of Lindos sits below it, and three hours covers the pair. May, June and September keep the heat bearable.

gem:lanaye.text: Lanaye is a small village in Belgium under the slope of Sint-Pietersberg. Fort Eben-Emael is the landmark here, with Eijsden Castle and Fort de Barchon nearby and Liege Cathedral a short run away. Any month from May to September, four hours.

gem:vindeln.text: Vindeln is a village in Sweden inside the Vindelalven-Juhtatdahka Biosphere Reserve, a UNESCO Man and the Biosphere site. Vindelns kyrka and Sankt Mikaels kapell are the two stops, an easy two hours. June and July are the practical months.

gem:agios-nikolaos.text: Agios Nikolaos is a harbour town in Greece with ancient sites scattered around it. The boat out to Spinalonga is the one everyone takes, and Lato, Gournia and Olous fill the rest of four hours. May, June and September are the pick.

gem:winsum.text: Winsum is a village in the Netherlands among windmills and water, at its best from June to August. The Eise Eisinga Planetarium nearby is the marvel, with Aylvapoldermolen and Huinsermolen closer to hand and four hours to spend on them.

gem:ronse.text: Ronse is a town in Belgium at the foot of the short steep climbs cyclists know: Koppenberg, Paterberg, Taaienberg and Eikenberg. Anvaing Castle and Mont-Saint-Aubert round out six hours, and public transport here is good. May to September rides best.

gem:holb-k.text: Holbaek is a harbour town in Denmark and the hub for its stretch of coast. Holbaek Museum and Holbaek Teater sit in the old centre, the boat crosses to Oro, and the churches at Tuse and Undlose are a drive out. Six hours, June to August.

gem:polhov-gradec.text: Polhov Gradec is a village in the hills outside Ljubljana in Slovenia. Its three hours really belong to the city: the National Museum of Slovenia, the National and University Library of Slovenia and the remains of Emona, best from May to August.

gem:tulln.text: Tulln is an old town in Austria, full of parks and easy to reach. The Egon-Schiele-Museum is the one to see, with Greifenstein Castle, the Troppberg and Wagram around it. May to September, and six hours if all of that appeals.

gem:nykobing-sj-lland.text: Nykobing Sjaelland is a coastal village in Denmark on the Odsherred peninsula. Hojby Church, Birkehoj and Odden Church make a three hour round, Jaegerspris Castle is further off, and Trekanten is the beach through June, July and August.

gem:aleksinac.text: Aleksinac is an area of hill country in Serbia. Soko Grad and the Cerje cave are the set pieces, the mountains Ozren and Devica stand behind, and Bovansko Jezero is the place to swim. May, June and September suit four hours out.

gem:rostanga.text: Rostanga is a village in Sweden at the gate of Soderasen National Park. The park walks are the reason to come, and Skanes Djurpark, Knutstorp Castle and Bosjokloster fill out three hours. June to August is the stretch to pick.

gem:nowa-slupia.text: Nowa Slupia is a village in Poland at the foot of the Swietokrzyskie Mountains. The climb to Lysa Gora and the Holy Cross Monastery is the day's business, with Lysica higher still and three hours on the clock. June to September.

gem:hojer.text: In the marshland of Denmark, Hojer is a village lying low behind its dykes. Hojer Molle is the landmark, and Schackenborg Slot, Romo Church and Vongshoj make the circuit in three hours. June to August is the window.

gem:novigrad.text: Novigrad is a seaside village on the Istria coast of Croatia. The Church of Saint Pelage and Dajla Abbey belong to it, and the Euphrasian Basilica is a short drive along the coast. Two hours in town, May to July, Plava Laguna for swimming.

gem:chateaudun.text: Chateaudun is a town in France and one of Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. The Chateau de Chateaudun is the draw, with Eglise Saint-Valerien and the Hotel de ville below it. June to September, five hours, good public transport.

gem:nusco.text: Nusco is a small village in Italy where the Concattedrale di Nusco and the Teatro Adele Solimene sit close together. Abbazia del Goleto and Convento di San Francesco a Folloni are worth the drive out, three hours in all, from May to August.

gem:morimondo.text: Morimondo is a village of a few hundred people in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Vigevano, Abbiategrasso and Cassinetta di Lugagnano are the neighbours worth the ride, about four hours all in. May, June and September are kind.

gem:gangi.text: A village in Italy with churches at nearly every turn, Gangi keeps Santa Maria Maggiore and the Chiesa di Sant'Anna within a two hour walk of the lanes. Castello di Geraci is nearby, and May through August are the months to go.

gem:tagliacozzo.text: Tagliacozzo is a village in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Rocca Orsini looks down on it, and the Chiesa e Convento di San Francesco and the Museo Orientale fill out three hours. May and June are the two months to aim for.

gem:sesto-al-reghena.text: Sesto al Reghena is a village in Italy grown up around its abbey. Abbazia Santa Maria in Silvis and the Torre Sbrojavacca are the centre of it, the Duomo di Portogruaro is a short ride away, and three hours in May or June covers the lot.

gem:monteleone-d-orvieto.text: Monteleone d'Orvieto is a hill village in Italy, small and quickly walked. San Silvestro and the Teatro dei Rustici take a couple of hours between them, with Palazzo della Corgna and Lake Chiusi for the run out, best in May or June.

gem:neumarkt.text: Neumarkt is a village in Italy lined with old manor houses: Ansitz Freienfeld, Ansitz Strehlburg and Ansitz Eberlehof among them. Naturpark Trudner Horn rises behind and Kalterer See is close, enough for four hours any time from May to September.

gem:camerata-cornello.text: Camerata Cornello is a small mountain village in Italy. June to September opens the high ground, where Lago Colombo and the Laghi Gemelli sit under Grignone. San Pellegrino Terme and San Giovanni Bianco fill the other four hours.

gem:coaraze.text: Coaraze is a village in France on the Les Plus Beaux Villages de France list. The Chapelle Saint-Sebastien is its own, while Chateau de Luceram and the Canal de la Vesubie are the drives out, three hours all told, any time from May to September.

gem:borgo-valsugana.text: Borgo Valsugana is a village in Italy between the lakes and the high ridges. Santa Maria Assunta, Santa Apollonia and Castel Ivano are the close ones, while Monte Ortigara and Cima Dodici stand over the valley, four hours of it from May to September.

gem:saint-veran.text: Saint-Veran is a high mountain settlement in France, listed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Eglise Saint-Veran, Fort Queyras and the churches at Ceillac and Molines-en-Queyras make six hours of it. July and August are the only easy months.

gem:lapalisse.text: The Chateau de La Palice gives this village in France its shape, and two hours covers the castle plus the old bridges around it. Lapalisse is easy to reach on public transport, and May through September is the stretch worth choosing.

gem:aubeterre-sur-dronne.text: Aubeterre-sur-Dronne is a tiny village in France that needs three hours, most of them at the Eglise monolithe Saint-Jean, carved down into rock. Les Plus Beaux Villages de France and Petites Cites de Caractere both list it.

gem:saint-suliac.text: June to September suits Saint-Suliac, a Les Plus Beaux Villages de France stop where the Rance widens into its estuary. The Rance Tidal Power Station and Solidor Tower are close by, Plage des Chevrets closer still, and four hours covers the lot.

gem:l-isle-adam.text: L'Isle-Adam is a town in France carrying the Les Plus Beaux Detours de France label, a short way from the Seine. Auvers-sur-Oise next door holds the Auberge Ravoux and the Chateau d'Herouville, so six hours is realistic; May to September.

gem:sevenoaks.text: Sevenoaks is a market town in the United Kingdom, and six hours here mostly means the country houses around it. Knole House, Chartwell and Ightham Mote are the pick, and June to September shows them at their best.

gem:montpeyroux.text: The fortified gate and the Chateau du Marchidial are the sum of Montpeyroux, a village in France among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France; three hours with lunch covers it. Lac d'Aydat lies close, and the season runs June to September.

gem:mehun-sur-yevre.text: Two hours does Mehun-sur-Yevre, a small town in France under the walls of the Chateau de Mehun-sur-Yevre. The Porte de l'Horloge and the collegiale fill out the rest, trains stop here, and May to September is the easy half of the year.

gem:angles-sur-l-anglin.text: Angles-sur-l'Anglin is a village of a few hundred people in France, set below the Chateau d'Angles-sur-l'Anglin. The Roc aux Sorciers and the Abbatiale Notre-Dame fill out three hours; a car helps, and June to September is the window.

gem:cormicy.text: Cormicy is a village in France with the Petites Cites de Caractere label and war graves in the fields around it. La Ville-aux-Bois British Cemetery and Cote 108 Berry-au-Bac anchor a three-hour loop, with Lac de l'Ailette not far.

gem:beaconsfield.text: Beaconsfield is a market town in the United Kingdom that works best as a base for big houses: Cliveden House, Taplow Court and Hedsor House. Two of them make a full six-hour day, and the months to choose are June through September.

gem:reigate.text: June through August is when Reigate, a market town in the United Kingdom, earns the trip for the walking country behind it. Box Hill and Westhumble, Betchworth Castle and Juniper Hall add up to six hours of sights.

gem:shepton-mallet.text: Shepton Mallet is a market town in the United Kingdom, and the reason to stop is Wells, next door. Wells Cathedral and the Bishop's Eye are worth the six hours between them, best from June to September.

gem:verdun.text: The Douaumont Ossuary and Fort de Douaumont are the heart of Verdun, a town in France listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Verdun Cathedral sits in the centre, six hours takes in most of it, and June to September is the best run.

gem:saint-germain-en-laye.text: Saint-Germain-en-Laye is a town near Paris on the Seine, built around the Chateau de Saint-Germain-en-Laye. Six hours covers the castle and the Porte Saint-Antoine, with the Villa Savoye nearby; May to September is the easiest time.

gem:kranj.text: Kranj is a town in Slovenia with Grintovec and Velika planina filling the skyline. Skofja Loka next door is the prettier stop, and six hours covers both old centres; May through August brings the clearest weather.

gem:libourne.text: May, June, July and September are the months for Libourne, a town in France that works as a base for Saint-Emilion next door. The Jurisdiction of Saint-Emilion, Chateau Ausone and Chateau Canon fill the six hours.

gem:ladispoli.text: Ladispoli is a town in Italy whose real draw sits inland at Cerveteri. The Necropoli della Banditaccia and the Tomba dei Rilievi make five hours worthwhile, and the Museo Nazionale Cerite fills the gaps; May to August.

gem:poissy.text: Poissy is a town on the Seine in France, best known as the address of the Villa Savoye. The Chateau de Maisons and the Machine de Marly are close enough to fold into the same six-hour day, any time from May to September.

gem:marostica.text: Monte Grappa stands over Marostica, a small town in Italy. Villa Godi and the Museo Civico are the sights at hand, with the Ponte degli Alpini a short drive off. Six hours does it, in May, June or September.

gem:mezzano.text: Mezzano is a village in Italy on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list, ringed by peaks around Cima della Rosetta. Its churches take three hours, lago del Mis is a short drive, and the roads suit June through September.

TFS.text: Tenerife South is the sunny end of the island in Spain, where the resorts and the best beaches are. El Medano draws the wind, Costa Adeje the calm water and Siam Park the families; five hours of sights, March to September.

CAG.text: Cagliari is the capital of Sardinia, a port city with the Torre dell'Elefante and the Bastione di Saint Remy on the hill above. Ten hours makes a full day with time at Poetto, and May through August is the warm run.

SMI.text: Samos is a quiet island in Greece whose ancient sites outrank its beaches. The Tunnel of Eupalinos, the Heraion of Samos and Pythagoreion take about five hours between them; May, June and September are the months to aim for.

MRS.text: Marseille is a big, loud port city on the coast of France, with Notre-Dame de la Garde on the hill above it. The calanques begin at the city edge and the chateau d'If sits offshore; seventeen hours of sights, best in April, May or September.

TLS.text: Toulouse is a university city in the south of France, strong on food and art. The Basilique Saint-Sernin and the Capitole de Toulouse lead its seventeen hours of sights, with the Canal du Midi and Aeroscopia after them; May, June, September.

LRH.text: La Rochelle is a port city in France facing the Atlantic, walkable and well served by trains. The Aquarium de La Rochelle and the Musee du Nouveau Monde stand out, and ten hours covers the old harbour too; June through September.

DUB.text: Dublin is a compact capital with a loud night side, set on the east coast of Ireland. Dublin Castle, Kilmainham Gaol and Croke Park anchor seventeen hours of sights, and June through August brings the longest evenings.

ZRH.text: Zurich is a moneyed, orderly city on a lake in Switzerland, with the Alps close behind. The Grossmunster, the Fraumunster and the Kunsthaus Zurich head a seventeen-hour list; June to September is the time for the water.

gem:kutna-hora.text: Kutna Hora is a small UNESCO town in Czechia where two churches do the work: the Sedlec Ossuary, built out of bones, and St Barbara. Six hours takes in both plus the Italian Court, and May through September is the pick.

gem:polignano.text: Polignano a Mare is a small coastal town in Puglia, Italy. Lama Monachile is the cove that defines it, the Castellana Caves sit inland and Monopoli is close; five hours covers them, and May to August is the swimming season.

gem:dalarna.text: Dalarna is forest and lake country in Sweden, and its anchor is the Falun Mine, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Six hours covers the mine and the Lugnet Hills above Falun; June through August is the short, bright summer, and a car helps.

gem:mechelen.text: Mechelen is a calm medieval city in Belgium where St Rumbold's Cathedral towers over everything. The Groot Begijnhof Mechelen and Kazerne Dossin round out a ten-hour visit, and May through September is the mildest run of the year.

gem:aran-islands.text: The Aran Islands are three wind-scoured islands off the coast of Ireland: Inis Mor, Inis Meain and Inis Oirr. Dun Aengus is the sight nobody skips, Kilmurvey Beach the place to swim, and five hours suits a June to September day.

gem:bihac-una.text: Bihac sits on the Una in Bosnia and Herzegovina, green country built for rafting and waterfalls. The Fethija mosque and the Zeljava Air Base fill six hours, the Plitvicka lakes lie within reach, and May to July is when the river runs high.

gem:monsanto.text: Monsanto is a remote village in Portugal built around the Castelo de Monsanto, its pelourinho and steep lanes below. The castle and the lanes take three hours, a car is needed to get there, and May, June and September are the kindest months.

gem:elvas.text: April and May are the months for Elvas, a walled border town in Portugal whose ramparts are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Aqueduto da Amoreira and the Nossa Senhora da Graca Fort lead five hours of sights.

gem:lindau.text: Lindau is a lakeside town in Germany on the Bodensee, where the Lindau Lighthouse marks the harbour mouth. The old streets take about four hours, and Bregenz along the shore adds the Kunsthaus Bregenz, best done between May and September.

gem:viscri.text: Viscri is a farming village in Romania built around The Fortified Church of Viscri, a UNESCO site. Two hours covers the church and its museum collection, buses barely reach it, and May through September is when to try.

gem:visegrad.text: Visegrad is a small town on the Drina in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the Mehmed Pasa Sokolovic Bridge is why anyone stops. Two hours covers the bridge and Andricgrad beside it, and the season stretches from April to October.

gem:dunajec-gorge.text: Pieniny is a national park in Slovakia cut through by the Dunajec River Gorge. The gorge below Trzy Korony is the draw, with Cerveny Klastor at its mouth; four hours is about right, June through September.

gem:idrija.text: Idrija is a small town of under six thousand in western Slovenia, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Wild Lake, a short walk out, leads the sights and three hours covers them. Public transport is good; come May through August.

gem:goslar.text: A town of just over forty thousand in Germany, Goslar sits below the Harz. Rammelsberg and the Kaiserpfalz head six hours of sights, best between June and August, with Brocken and the national park beyond.

gem:blautopf.text: Blaubeuren is a quiet town in Germany set around the Blautopf, with UNESCO World Heritage caves at Hohler Fels and Geissenklosterle. Ulm Minster lies a short trip away. Best months run June to September, and public transport is poor.

gem:werfen-eisriesenwelt.text: Werfen is a small village in Austria beneath the Hochkonig. Eisriesenwelt and the Festung Hohenwerfen take about three hours between them. June to August is the practical window; Konigssee lies over the border.

gem:saas-fee.text: Saas-Fee sits high in Switzerland at the head of its valley, ringed by peaks. Mittelallalin and Weissmies lead about four hours of sights, with Alphubel and the Simplon Pass close. July and August are the months; getting here without a car takes patience.

gem:corte-restonica.text: Corte is an inland hill town in France, ringed by the mountains of the interior. Monte Cinto, Monte Cardo and the climb to Lac de Melu fill three hours and more, with Lac de Capitellu beyond. May to July is best, and a car helps.

gem:cap-corse.text: Cap Corse is a remote stretch of coast in France, thinly settled and short on buses. Nonza and the towers at Erbalunga and Albo are the stops, with Monte Stello above. Six hours of driving and stops, best between June and August.

gem:saint-jean-pied-de-port.text: A walled village in France, Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port sends pilgrims off toward the Roncevaux Pass. Its own sights take three hours, and it carries the Plus Beaux Villages label. Mount Okabe and Munhoa rise behind; May to September is the walking season.

gem:najac.text: Najac strings along a ridge in France beneath its castle, one of the Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Chateau de Najac and the church of Saint-Jean take about three hours. May to September is the run of good weather, and there is little public transport.

gem:salers.text: Salers is a medieval village in France on the Plus Beaux Villages list, with Puy Mary and the Plomb du Cantal rising nearby. Maison Bertrandy and the Chateau d'Anjony take up three hours. The season is short, June to August.

gem:megeve.text: Megeve is an alpine resort village in France with Mont Blanc filling the skyline. The Aiguille du Midi and Praz-sur-Arly are the near draws, three hours of sights before the trails take over between June and September.

gem:giverny.text: Giverny is a village of a few hundred people in France, and the Fondation Claude Monet is why nearly everyone comes. The Chateau des Tourelles and the Tour des Archives round out roughly four hours between May and September.

gem:rochefort-en-terre.text: Rochefort-en-Terre is a small village in France on both the Plus Beaux Villages and Petites Cites de Caractere lists. The Calvaire and the Dolmen des Follets fill three easy hours; the zoo at Branfere suits families. Best from June to September.

gem:amorgos.text: Amorgos lies out on the edge of the Cyclades in Greece, thinly settled and short on boats. The Hozoviotissa monastery leads, with Minoa and Keros beyond it, and four hours covers the sights. The boats are best between June and September.

gem:syros-ermoupoli.text: Syros is a lived-in island in Greece, more town than beach resort. Ano Syros on its hill and Saint George's Cathedral head about six hours, and Chalandriani lies further out. Tinos is a short hop away; May to September is best.

gem:karpathos.text: Karpathos is a long, thinly visited island in Greece, set between Rhodes and Crete. Apella is the beach people come for and Kali Limni the climb above it, about four hours of sights, and the season runs June to September.

gem:astypalaia.text: Astypalaia is a quiet island in the Dodecanese, ringed by small bays and topped by its castle. The Archaeological Museum and Agia Kyriaki fill part of four hours; the rest goes on the coast. May to September, with boats limited.

gem:skiathos.text: Skiathos is a green island in the Sporades, reached from the Greek mainland. Koukounaries and Lalaria are the beaches to know, and the Evangelistria Monastery sits inland; five hours of sights. The season is long here, May to September.

gem:kyrenia.text: Kyrenia is a harbour town on the north coast of Cyprus, its castle standing over the water. Saint Hilarion Castle and Buffavento Castle sit up in the Kyrenia Mountains, and four hours covers the lot. The season here is April to June.

gem:madonna-di-campiglio.text: Set high in Italy, Madonna di Campiglio is a resort under the Brenta peaks. Cima Tosa, Cima Brenta and Cima Falkner ring it, with the Adamello Brenta park alongside; six hours of sights. The summer is short: July and August.

gem:asolo.text: Asolo is a walled hill village in Italy, one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Villa Emo and the Tomba Brion are close by and take about three hours; Monte Grappa rises behind. May to September, and a car is needed.

gem:sirolo-conero.text: Sirolo is a small coastal village in Italy above the beaches of Monte Conero. Two hours covers the village itself; the Spiaggia Urbani and the Conero park take the rest of the day. The beaches fill from May to August.

gem:cortona.text: Cortona is a hill town in Italy looking down toward Lake Trasimeno. The Cortona Cathedral, the Basilica of Santa Margherita and the Tabula Cortonensis add up to four hours. May and June are the best months; Isola Maggiore sits out on the lake.

gem:gubbio.text: Gubbio climbs a mountainside in Umbria and has kept its medieval walls. The Palazzo dei Consoli and the Duomo are the set pieces, about five hours with the Basilica di Sant'Ubaldo above the town. May and June are the two months to pick.

gem:spello.text: Spello sits on the flank of Monte Subasio in Italy, a quiet village with Roman remains. The Cattedrale di San Feliciano anchors four hours; Assisi and its Basilica of San Francesco are a short run away. The best of it is May, June and September.

gem:locorotondo.text: Locorotondo is a hilltop village in Apulia, one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia and set in wine country. The old centre takes about three hours; the Castellana Caves and Gnatia are the trips worth making. Go between June and August.

gem:finale-ligure.text: Finale Ligure is a beach town on the coast of Italy, backed by cliffs and old stone villages. Castel Gavone, the Chiesa di San Paragorio and the Toirano Caves fill about six hours. May to September is the stretch to aim for.

gem:comino.text: Comino is the small island between the two bigger ones in Malta, with barely any permanent residents. Day boats come over for the water, while Ggantija, Mnajdra and Fungus Rock lie on the neighbouring islands; seven hours in all. Its season is May to August.

gem:slowinski-dunes.text: The Slowinski Dunes rise along the coast of Poland inside Slowinski National Park. Lake Gardno and Lebsko Lake lie behind them, with the Czolpino Lighthouse as a turning point; five hours on foot. The dunes are at their best June to August.

gem:iron-gates.text: The Iron Gates is a river gorge on the edge of Romania, a national park and UNESCO Global Geopark. The Tabula Traiana and what is left of Trajan's Bridge take two hours, with Derdap National Park across the water. April to June and September suit best.

gem:bicaz-gorge.text: Bicaz Canyon cuts through the mountains of Romania, with Red Lake sitting just above it. The pair take about five hours, and the Hasmas Mountains and Ceahlau National Park carry on from there. June to September is the time for it.

gem:begur.text: Begur stands above the Costa Brava in Spain, a village with a castle over it and coves below. Platja de Sa Riera and Platja Fonda are the beaches, with the Medes Islands out front; four hours of sights. May to August is when to come.

gem:ainsa.text: Ainsa is a medieval village in the Aragon hills of Spain, castle and old quarter set on a ridge. The two take about three hours, with Pena Montanesa and the Cotiella massif behind. May, June and September are the months.

gem:fisterra.text: Fisterra is a small coastal town in Spain at the end of a rocky cape. Cape Fisterra and the Faro de Finisterre are the walk everyone makes, about three hours with the Iglesia de Nosa Senora das Areas. July to September is the window here.

gem:avebury.text: The Avebury Stone Circle wraps around a working village in Wiltshire, and UNESCO lists the whole landscape. Silbury Hill and the West Kennet Long Barrow are near enough to walk; seven hours for the lot. June to September, with few buses.

gem:northern-velebit.text: Northern Velebit is a national park of bare ridges in Croatia, held by UNESCO as a biosphere reserve. Six hours is a modest day here; the trails run far longer, with Rab and Goli otok out to sea. July and August are the reliable months.

gem:brijuni.text: The Brijuni Islands are a national park off the coast of Croatia, reached by boat. A day trip runs to about six hours between May and July, and Pula with its arena and Temple of Augustus pairs well with it.

gem:herceg-novi.text: Herceg Novi rises in terraces above the Bay of Kotor in Montenegro, a fortress town more than a resort. Kanli Kula and the Savina monastery are the main stops, four hours or so, with Mamula out in the bay. May and June are the pick.

gem:keswick.text: Keswick is a market town at the top of the Lake District, a base for walkers more than a sight in itself. Skiddaw rises behind and Castlerigg Stone Circle sits above; four hours covers the town. June to August is the season.

gem:hebden-bridge.text: Hebden Bridge fills a narrow valley in West Yorkshire, a mill town turned arts town. The Picture House is the landmark and three hours covers the place, with the Bronte Parsonage Museum a short trip away. June to August is the best of it.

gem:emporeio.text: Emporeio is a village on Santorini, Greece, a short drive from Red Beach and Vlichada. Its own sights take about three hours; the rest of a day belongs to the caldera, Akrotiri and the boat out to Nea Kameni, best between May and September.

gem:bautzen.text: Bautzen is a town in Saxony and the centre of Sorbian life in Germany. The Cathedral of St Peter and the Sorbian Museum carry most of six hours, with Monchswalder Berg for the view and Bautzen Reservoir for a swim in June or July.

gem:swanage.text: Swanage is a resort town on the Isle of Purbeck in Dorset, with sand in its bay and Bournemouth Beach up the coast. Corfe Castle and Anvil Point Lighthouse are worth the six hours; June to September is when the town is properly open.

gem:triora.text: Triora is a mountain village of a few hundred people in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. June to September is the comfortable window; the village needs about three hours, and Punta Marguareis and Monte Saccarello stand over it.

gem:carlisle.text: A border city in Cumbria, Carlisle rewards more than the overnight stop most people give it. Carlisle Castle, the cathedral and Tullie House come to nine hours together, and Skiddaw stands south of town; June to August is the time.

gem:medinaceli.text: Medinaceli is a village of a few hundred people in Spain, a Conjunto historico best known for its Roman arch. Two hours is enough for the arch and the Church of San Juan Bautista, and Siguenza Cathedral with its castle is the next stop along.

gem:berwick-upon-tweed.text: Berwick-Upon-Tweed is a coastal town in the United Kingdom, built around a castle and crossed by two remarkable bridges. The Royal Border Bridge and the Union Chain Bridge are the set pieces; six hours covers them and Halidon Hill, June to September.

gem:sos-del-rey-catolico.text: Sos del Rey Catolico is a village of a few hundred people in Spain, protected as a Conjunto historico. The Church of Santa Maria la Real fills much of a two-hour visit, and the Castle of Xabier and the Monastery of Leyre are close by.

gem:pezenas.text: Pezenas is a town in Herault, France, with a historic core and a place on Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. Valmagne Abbey and the Roman Bridge are the pick of the sights, six hours in all, and May, June or September is the time to walk them.

gem:evesham.text: A market town in Worcestershire, Evesham sits in the vale that took its name, with Evesham Abbey and the Almonry at its middle. The Tithe Barn and the Fleece Inn are close and Broadway Tower a short drive; six hours, June to September.

gem:rothbury.text: Rothbury is a village at the edge of Northumberland National Park in the United Kingdom. Cragside, the estate above the village, is the reason to stop and takes most of three hours; Alnwick Castle and Warkworth Castle are nearby, June to August.

gem:market-drayton.text: Market Drayton is a Shropshire market town on the Shropshire Union Canal, long associated with gingerbread. St Luke and the halls nearby, Styche and Buntingsdale, make about five hours, and the Blore Heath battlefield is close, best seen June to August.

gem:arevalo.text: Arevalo is a small town in Spain whose old centre is protected as a Conjunto Historico. The Hermitage of la Lugareja stands a short way out and the Arevalo History Museum is in the town; three hours covers both, in May, June or September.

gem:vittorio-veneto.text: Vittorio Veneto is a town in Italy below the prosecco hills of Conegliano and Valdobbiadene. CastelBrando and the San Boldo Pass make up most of six hours, and Lago di Santa Croce is close; come in May, June or September.

gem:great-yarmouth.text: Great Yarmouth is a seaside resort on the Norfolk coast, busy from July into September. The Hippodrome, the Time & Tide Museum and the Minster fill most of nine hours, with Berney Arms Windmill and Burgh Castle Roman Site a short way out.

gem:stroud.text: Stroud sits in Gloucestershire, where the Five Valleys meet in the Cotswolds. Uley Long Barrow, Owlpen Manor and Selsley are spread around it, so a full day of ten hours is realistic; June to September is the stretch to take it on.

gem:yeovil.text: Yeovil is a Somerset town known for helicopters, and the Fleet Air Arm Museum tells that story. Montacute House is the other stop, with Sherborne Abbey and Sherborne School a short drive away; ten hours covers the lot.

gem:cardaillac.text: Cardaillac is a village of a few hundred people in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Tour de Sagnes and the Chateau de Puy-Launay come to about three hours, and Lac du Tolerme is close for a swim in July or August.

gem:wipperfurth.text: Wipperfurth is a town in the Bergisches Land in Germany, with two reservoirs on its doorstep. Schloss Gimborn and Huckeswagen Castle carry most of six hours; Bevertalsperre and Glortalsperre take the rest, best June to September.

gem:heilbronn.text: Heilbronn is a working city in Baden-Wurttemberg rather than a museum piece. Its centre holds the Siebenrohrenbrunnen, and Burg Stettenfels looks down from outside town; ten hours is a fair allowance, any time from May into September.

gem:villeloin-coulange.text: Villeloin-Coulange is a village of a few hundred people in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Its corroirie is the local sight and three hours covers the village; Chateau de Loches, Chateau de Montresor and ZooParc de Beauval are near.

gem:chatillon-sur-chalaronne.text: Chatillon-sur-Chalaronne is a village in the Dombes of France, on the Les Plus Beaux Detours list. Its chateau and the Parc des oiseaux take about three hours between them, and the Basilique d'Ars is a short drive. May to September suits it.

gem:alessandria.text: Alessandria is a city in Piedmont where the Cittadella is the set piece and the Marengo Museum tells of the battle fought outside town. Palazzo Ghilini and the cathedral take up the rest of eight hours; April to June, or September, is the time.

gem:lampedusa.text: Lampedusa is the main island of the Pelagian Islands, closer to Africa than to the rest of Italy. Rabbit Beach and the reserve around Isola dei Conigli are the draw; the built sights take two hours, and the season runs May to August.

gem:kulmbach.text: Kulmbach is a town in Franconia, Germany, long known for the number of breweries packed into it. The Plassenburg on the hill above is the main sight, with Kloster Himmelkron and the Rathaus Kulmbach after it; six hours, June to September.

gem:chur.text: Chur, the Graubunden capital in eastern Switzerland, is a compact old town with mountains on every side. The Cathedral of Saint Mary of the Assumption anchors it, and Haldensteiner Calanda and Hochwang are the climbs; six hours, May to September.

gem:noirmoutier-en-l-ile.text: Noirmoutier-en-l'Ile is the main village on the Isle of Noirmoutier in France, reached over the Pont de Noirmoutier. The Chateau de Noirmoutier is the one substantial sight and three hours covers the village; June to August is when the island fills.

gem:conil-de-la-frontera.text: Conil de la Frontera is a beach town on the coast of Spain, with Playa de los Bateles below the old centre. Playa de la Barrosa and the Pinar de Roche are further along the sand; five hours of sights, and May to July or September for the water.

gem:villafames.text: Villafames is a small village in Spain, a Conjunto historico with its castle on the hilltop. The Desert de les Palmes rises nearby, and Castello Cathedral and El Fadri are down in the city; three hours is enough here, May to July.

gem:les-eyzies-de-tayac-sireuil.text: Les Eyzies-de-Tayac-Sireuil is a village in France set among the decorated caves of the Vezere Valley. Les Combarelles, Le Moustier and La Ferrassie are within minutes, Lascaux a drive further; four hours of sights, May to July or September.

gem:castroreale.text: Castroreale is a village of a few hundred in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, set against the Peloritani. Its own sights take three hours, with Patti Cathedral and the Villa Romana di Patti nearby; May and June are the months to pick.

gem:leer.text: Leer is a town in East Frisia, Germany, with a cluster of small castles close together. The Evenburg, the Haneburg and the Harderwykenburg make up most of six hours, and the Weener railway bridge is worth the detour in June, July or August.

gem:halmstad.text: Halmstad is a city in Halland on the west coast of Sweden, busiest when the beaches fill in July and August. Halmstad slott, Martin Luthers kyrka and Wapno Castle make a long day of ten hours, with Tylosand Beach the reason most people come.

gem:greetsiel.text: Greetsiel is a small village in Germany, out on a flat coast with Memmert and Lutje Horn lying offshore. The Pilsum Lighthouse and the Leaning Tower of Suurhusen are the short circuit, about three hours, and June to August is the season.

gem:yevre-la-ville.text: Yevre-la-Ville is a village in France whose castle at Yevre-le-Chatel earns it a place on Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The church of Sainte-Brigide and La Cour-Dieu Abbey round out three hours, May through September.

gem:pola-de-somiedo.text: Pola de Somiedo is the village at the centre of Somiedo Natural Park in Spain, a UNESCO Man and the Biosphere reserve. Two hours covers the village itself; the rest goes to the park, the Leitariegos Pass and the valleys above, June to September.

gem:miltenberg.text: Miltenberg is a small town in Lower Franconia, Germany, on the line of the Upper German-Raetian Limes. Zum Riesen stands in the old centre, with Amorbach Abbey and Engelberg Abbey close by; six hours does it, May through September.

gem:gulpen.text: Gulpen is a village in the Heuvelland, the hilly corner of South Limburg in the Netherlands. Kasteel Valkenburg, the Cauberg and Fort Eben-Emael are all a short ride away, about four hours in total, and May to September is the stretch to come.

gem:joigny.text: Joigny is a town in France on the Les Plus Beaux Detours list, its three churches, Saint-Jean, Saint-Thibault and Saint-Andre, within a few streets. The Quartier Dubois-Thainville fills out five hours, May through September.

gem:hulst.text: Hulst is a small fortified town in Zeeland, near the border with Belgium in the Netherlands. The Sint-Willibrordusbasiliek and De Stadsmolen fill about three hours, with Roosenberg Abbey close by; June to August is best for walking the ramparts.

gem:navarrenx.text: Navarrenx is a small village in France, listed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Chateau Moncade and Chateau de Maytie fill about three hours, and Oloron Cathedral is a short drive off. Best from May to September; a car helps.

gem:sankt-polten.text: Sankt Polten is a cathedral town in Austria, easy to reach by train and good for about six hours between April and September. Herzogenburg Priory is the one to make time for, with Dunkelsteinerwald just outside for a walk.

gem:krivoklat.text: Krivoklat is a village in Czechia wrapped around its castle, inside a UNESCO Man and the Biosphere reserve. Krivoklat Castle takes most of the four hours any time from May to September; Koneprusy Caves and Tocnik Castle are the obvious add-ons.

gem:archangelos.text: Archangelos is a coastal village in Greece with barely two hours of sights of its own. Feraklos Castle and Tsambika Monastery are the two to see, Anthony Quinn Bay is the swim, and Rhodes and Kameiros lie nearby. May, June and September.

gem:tonsberg.text: Tonsberg is a coastal city in Norway, ten hours of sights and easy local transport. Tonsberg Cathedral and Tonsberg Fortress head the list, and Jarlsberg Manor and Notteroy sit close by. The window is narrow: June, July and August.

gem:batenburg.text: Batenburg is a village of about five hundred in the Netherlands, with a castle and a church at its core. Standerdmolen Batenburg and De Drie Waaien are in the village, Hernen and De Verrekijker just outside, four hours all in. May through August, and little reason otherwise.

gem:horstermeer.text: Horstermeer is a small village in the Netherlands with Gooimeer and Eemmeer close by. The sights are mostly its neighbours: Vesting Weesp, Naarden, Beth Haim and Castle de Haar, roughly four hours in total. June through August works best.

gem:heiligenblut.text: Heiligenblut is a mountain village in Austria under Grossglockner, inside a national park. The Grossglockner High Alpine Road starts here and the Pasterze Glacier is what most people come for; four hours covers the viewpoints. June to August, really.

gem:kalyves.text: Kalyves is a beach village in Greece with about three hours of sights and Lefka Ori rising behind it. Aptera and Kydonia are the sites worth a detour, Kournas the lake and Almyrida the next beach along. May to July, then September.

gem:hoogmade.text: Hoogmade is a village in the Netherlands on the edge of the Kagerplassen. It works better as a quiet base than a destination: Keukenhof, Mauritshuis and Madurodam are all day-trip distance, four hours between them, and June to August is the stretch that makes sense.

gem:montreuil-sur-mer.text: Les Plus Beaux Detours de France includes Montreuil-sur-Mer, a village in France that the trains still reach. The Citadelle de Montreuil is the main draw, with the Chartreuse Notre-Dame des Pres a short way out; three hours is enough, best in June, July or August.

gem:varallo-sesia.text: A Bandiera Arancione hangs on Varallo Sesia, a village in Italy. Sacro Monte di Varallo on the hill above is the reason to stop, and the Collegiata di San Gaudenzio fills out three hours. Lake Orta is close, and June through August is the season.

gem:etroubles.text: Etroubles is a village of a few hundred in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Great St Bernard Pass climbs away above it, the hospice sits at the top and the Museo della fontina is down in the village; three hours is plenty. June to August.

gem:issoire.text: Issoire is a town in France whose Abbatiale Saint-Austremoine is the reason to stop, one of Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. Chateau de Villeneuve-Lembron and Puy de Mercoeur make short trips out, and six hours covers town and both, any time from May to September.

gem:montone.text: Montone holds a place on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list, a village in Italy of fewer than six hundred people. Piazza San Francesco and La Rocca are the set pieces, with Chiesa della Madonna della Reggia close at hand; three hours does it. May and June.

gem:commercy.text: Chateau de Commercy is the centrepiece of Commercy, a village in France on the Les Plus Beaux Detours de France list. Mairie d'Euville and a scatter of village churches round out three hours. June through September, and the trains stop here.

gem:vallo-di-nera.text: Vallo di Nera, in Italy, holds fewer than a hundred and fifty residents and a place on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. Monte Coscerno rises behind it and the Ex Ferrovia Spoleto Norcia makes the walk; three hours covers the lanes. May and June.

gem:rosazza.text: Rosazza, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, is a village in Italy with under a hundred residents. The draw sits mostly outside it: Sacro Monte di Oropa, the Sanctuary of Oropa and Basilica Superiore, four hours in all, June through September.

gem:gromo.text: Gromo is a mountain village in Italy on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list, with Pizzo Coca overhead. Chiesa del Paradiso is the one set piece; the rest is walking, out to Laghi Gemelli or Lago Colombo, four hours or so, June through September.

gem:pieve-tesino.text: Pieve Tesino sits under Cima Dodici in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Museo Casa De Gasperi and the Grotta della Bigonda are what to plan around, four hours between them. June, July and August are the months.

gem:bleggio-superiore.text: Bleggio Superiore is one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, a village in Italy with Lago di Tenno close by. Pieve del Bleggio anchors it, and Castello di Stenico, Monte Brento and the Fiave pile-dwelling site are all inside four hours. June to September.

gem:sancerre.text: Sancerre is a village in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Detours de France, and three hours walks it between June and September. Tour des Fiefs and the Beffroi give the views, with the church Saint-Pierre in Sancerre and Saint-Satur just below.

gem:bury.text: Bury is a market town in the United Kingdom, big enough for a full day at around ten hours of sights. Heaton Park is the green heart, Radcliffe Tower and Turton Tower the history, Kersal Moor the walk. June through August, with good transport throughout.

gem:saint-come-d-olt.text: Saint-Come-d'Olt is a village in France and one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Its chateau and the Chapelle des Penitents are the set pieces, with Chateau de Calmont d'Olt and Espalion nearby; three hours does it, June through September.

gem:mirmande.text: Mirmande is a village of about five hundred and fifty in France, listed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Abbatiale Sainte-Marie crowns the lanes, with Chapelle Saint-Didier and Chateau de Chabrillan nearby. May, June and September suit it.

gem:monesties.text: Monesties carries the Les Plus Beaux Villages de France label, a village in France of quiet lanes and one fine church. Eglise Saint-Hippolyte de Monesties is that church; Chateau de Trevien and Lac de la Roucarie are close. May to July, or September.

gem:lautrec.text: Lautrec is a village in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, and two hours covers it. Eglise Saint-Remi de Lautrec is the main stop, with Chateau de Malvignol and the church at Saint-Germier a short way out. May, June or September.

gem:ollioules.text: Ollioules is a town in France that leans on nearby Toulon for its sights, one of Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. Toulon Cathedral, Fort de Balaguier and the Pont basculant at La Seyne-sur-Mer fill six hours between them, June through August.

gem:artonne.text: Artonne carries the Petites Cites de Caractere label, a village in France of eight hundred people. Eglise Saint-Martin d'Artonne is the one real monument; chateau de Villemont and the church at Aigueperse are short hops, three hours in all. May to September.

gem:helston.text: Helston is a market town in the United Kingdom with five hours of sights, best June to September, and Pentreath Beach within reach. Helston Museum sits in town, while Godolphin Estate, Pengersick Castle and the old Great Work Mine are the trips out.

gem:valvasone-arzene.text: Two hours is enough for Valvasone Arzene, a village in Italy on the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. The Duomo del Santissimo Corpo di Cristo and Chiesa di San Leonardo are the two stops that matter. May and June are the months.

gem:ruda-slaska.text: Ruda Slaska is a coal city in Poland where the mines are the attraction. Guido Mine and Coal Mining Museum takes visitors underground and Bielszowice Coal Mine sits nearby; a full day, near ten hours, is not too much. May through September.

gem:fucecchio.text: Fucecchio is a town in Italy of some fourteen thousand people, worth about six hours. Villa Medicea and the Collegiata di San Giovanni Battista are the anchors, with San Genesio just outside. April to June, or September again.

LCG.text: A Coruna is a coastal city in Spain built around a working harbour, with the Tower of Hercules, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, standing over it. Playa del Orzan and Playa de Oza are in town, and ten hours covers the rest. June through September.

LPA.text: Gran Canaria is an island in Spain with beaches at one end and mountains at the other. Roque Nublo and Pico de las Nieves are the high points, Maspalomas Dunes and Playa de Las Canteras the sands worth the trip. June through October, and a car helps.

NUE.text: Nuremberg is a medieval city in Germany, big enough that seventeen hours of sights barely covers it, and best from May to September. Germanisches Nationalmuseum is the anchor, with Kaiserburg on its rock above the old town and the house of Albrecht Durer nearby.

BRE.text: Bremen is a port city in Germany whose centre holds a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Bremen Roland. Town Musicians of Bremen stands close by, Schnoor is the lane to walk and Bottcherstrasse the street to see; seventeen hours of sights. May through September.

CLY.text: Calvi is a coastal town on Corsica in France, more a base than a sightseeing stop. Calvi Cathedral and San Parteo take an hour of the five; plage de Bodri and Monte Cinto explain the rest. May and June are the pick.

GVA.text: Geneva is a city in Switzerland on its lake, expensive and full of institutions. Jet d'eau marks the waterfront, Carouge is the quarter to wander and Bains des Paquis the place to swim. Ten hours, May through September, with Le Saleve above.

JER.text: Jersey is a quiet island in the United Kingdom with a national park and about seven hours of sights. Elizabeth Castle, Jersey Zoo and Samares Manor are the fixed points, with La Hougue Bie for something much older. June through September.

gem:karlovy-vary.text: Karlovy Vary is a spa town in Czechia, one of The Great Spa Towns of Europe. The Mill Colonnade and Grandhotel Pupp anchor a walk of about six hours, and good buses reach Loket Castle. Best from May to September.

gem:aix.text: Aix-en-Provence is a city of fountains and shaded squares in southern France. The Musee Granet and Hotel de Caumont hold the art; the Fontaine de la Rotonde marks the middle. Ten hours covers the centre, best in May, June or September.

gem:ksamil.text: Ksamil is a cheap, quiet beach village on the coast of Albania, at its best in April and May. The islets just offshore are the draw, and Buthrotum sits inside Butrint National Park a short way inland. Set aside three hours.

gem:st-wolfgang.text: St Wolfgang is a village on the Wolfgangsee in the Salzkammergut, Austria, with the Schafberg at its back. Attersee and Mondsee lie a short drive away, and the village itself needs only three hours. The season runs May to September.

gem:uvac.text: Uvac Canyon is a wilderness of tight river loops in Serbia, remote enough that a car is the only sensible way in. Ledena cave and the Mileseva monastery round out about four hours. June, July and August are the months that work.

gem:mokra-gora.text: Mokra Gora is a small mountain village in Serbia below the Tara range. The Sargan Eight and Kustendorf are the two things to see, and three hours covers both; Zlatibor and Zaovine Lake are close. Aim for May through September.

gem:ericeira.text: Ericeira is a surf and fishing town on the coast of Portugal, with Praia da Aguda and Praia da Vigia within reach. The town takes three hours; Sintra and its palaces make the longer day out. May to September is the season.

gem:gruyeres.text: Gruyeres is a small medieval village in Switzerland built around a castle. Moleson rises behind it and Bulle sits a few kilometres down the valley, so four hours covers the village and a walk. June to September is the stretch.

gem:kazimierz-dolny.text: Kazimierz Dolny is a small Renaissance town in Poland, quiet and low-rise, with an old Jewish cemetery among its landmarks. Magiczne Ogrody and Kazimierski Park Krajobrazowy lie in the countryside around; three hours does the centre. May to September suits.

gem:westport.text: Westport is a coastal town in Ireland and the base for climbing Croagh Patrick. Westport House and Murrisk Abbey take up the rest, two hours or so, and the Partry Mountains sit inland. June to August is the drier window.

gem:vieste.text: Vieste is a beach town on the Puglia coast in Italy. The Castello and Vieste Cathedral hold the old centre together, with the Faro di Isola Sant Eufemia offshore, and four hours is enough before the sand. May to August is peak.

gem:villasimius.text: Villasimius is a small beach town in Italy wrapped around the marine reserve at Capo Carbonara. Porto Giunco and Punta Molentis are the beaches to aim for, with Isola Serpentara offshore. Sights take three hours, and May to August is the warm run.

gem:figueres.text: Figueres is a market town in Spain built around one outsized draw, the Dali Theatre and Museum. Six hours takes in the museum and the old centre, and trains run on to Peralada and Castello d'Empuries. May to September is comfortable.

gem:waterloo-lions-mound.text: Waterloo is a town in Belgium given over to the battlefield around it. The Lion's Mound gives the overview, then La Haye Sainte and Hougoumont fill in the rest of six hours on the ground. June to September keeps the walking dry.

gem:fur-island.text: Fur is a quiet island in Denmark, low and green and easy to cross in a day. The Fur Museum holds the local finds, while Mors and Spottrup Borg sit close by; four hours covers the island. Go in June, July or August.

gem:egeskov.text: Egeskov Castle is a fairytale castle in the Funen countryside in Denmark, aimed squarely at families. Egeskov Slot and its grounds take about three hours, with Tasinge and Thuro nearby for a longer loop. June, July and August are the obvious months.

gem:jelling.text: Jelling is a small country town in Denmark whose UNESCO World Heritage Site sits at its centre. The Jellingestenene, Jelling Kirke and Kongernes Jelling take about three hours, and June to August is the time to come.

gem:krkonose.text: Krkonose is a mountain area in Czechia, walked in summer and skied in winter. Snezka is the high point, and trails through Krkonose National Park and Karkonosze National Park fill about seven hours. June to August is the walking season.

gem:slavonice.text: Slavonice is a quiet historic town in Czechia, off the main routes but easy to reach by bus. Landstejn Castle and the underground drainage system beneath the streets are the curiosities, and three hours does it, May to September.

gem:hluboka-castle.text: Hluboka Castle is the fairytale castle above a village of the same name in Czechia. The castle and its park take about four hours, and Ceske Budejovice with its Samsonova kasna makes the obvious next stop, May to September.

gem:mala-fatra.text: Mala Fatra is a mountain range in Slovakia, most of it inside a national park. Vratna dolina is the way in and Velky Krivan the high point; four hours of walking gets a decent taste. July and August are the reliable months.

gem:wernigerode.text: Wernigerode is a fairytale town at the edge of the Harz in Germany. Wernigerode Castle looks down from its hill, and the Brocken and Steinerne Renne pull walkers out of the centre. Six hours is about right, June to August.

gem:krimml-waterfalls.text: Krimml Waterfalls is a walk up a wooded gorge inside Hohe Tauern National Park in Austria. The path climbs beside the water and carries on towards the Venediger Group, so seven hours is realistic. June to August is the window.

gem:saint-florent-corsica.text: Saint-Florent is a small wine and beach town on the coast of Corsica, in France. Saint-Florent Cathedral anchors the old quarter, the Col de Teghime climbs away towards Bastia, and three hours covers the town. May, June and September are the pick.

gem:vaison-la-romaine.text: Vaison-la-Romaine is a historic town in France, Roman and medieval by turns. The Vaison-la-Romaine Roman Bridge and Vaison Cathedral take up most of three hours, with Mont Ventoux on the skyline. Its best months are May, June and September.

gem:uzes.text: Uzes is a quiet medieval town in France, small enough to see in three hours. The Tour Fenestrelle is its landmark, while the Pont du Gard stands a short drive off and Nimes with the Maison Carree lies beyond, best in May, June or September.

gem:baume-les-messieurs.text: Baume-les-Messieurs is a village of barely five hundred in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Abbaye and the Cascade des Tufs are the two stops, four hours with the walk between them. The valley is at its best from June to September.

gem:baie-de-somme.text: Baie de Somme is a wide tidal bay on the coast of France, quiet, easy with children and at its best from June to September. Parc du Marquenterre and Le Crotoy are the two stops, about three hours between them.

gem:vannes.text: Vannes is a medieval city on the Gulf of Morbihan in France. Vannes Cathedral, the Saint-Vincent Gate and the Lavoirs de la Garenne make the walking list, and the gulf itself asks for a boat. Ten hours covers both, June to September.

gem:puy-du-fou.text: Puy du Fou is a family attraction in the countryside of France, built on history rather than rides. The Chateau du Puy-du-Fou stands at its centre and three hours covers the grounds, with Les Herbiers the nearest town, June to September.

gem:koufonisia.text: Koufonisia is a cluster of small islands in the Lesser Cyclades, Greece, and the beaches are the point. Ano Koufonisi holds the village and most of the sand, with Keros and Schoinoussa across the water. Its beaches take four hours to walk, May to September.

gem:canazei.text: Canazei is a village in the Val di Fassa in Italy that skis in winter and walks in summer. The Marmolada and Sassolungo rise over it and Piz Boe makes a day out, though four hours covers the valley floor. June to August is when the trails are clear.

gem:breuil-cervinia.text: Breuil-Cervinia is a high ski resort in Italy sitting directly under the Matterhorn. The lifts carry walkers towards the Klein Matterhorn and the Dent d'Herens, and seven hours goes quickly on the high paths. Its summer runs June to August.

gem:cividale-del-friuli.text: Cividale del Friuli is a quiet medieval town in Italy with a UNESCO site at its heart. The Tempietto Longobardo is the reason to come, and six hours takes in the museum and the old streets. May and June are quietest.

gem:san-leo.text: San Leo is a village of about two hundred people on a rock in Italy, crowned by a fortress. The Rocca di San Leo is the whole point and takes most of three hours, with San Marino and Monte Titano in view next door, best from June to August.

gem:saturnia.text: Saturnia is a spa village in the countryside of Italy, built around the Terme di Saturnia. The pools take an hour or two, and Pitigliano and Monte Amiata fill out about six hours. May to August is warmest.

gem:scanno.text: Scanno is a quiet mountain village in Italy with Lago di Scanno just below it. The Eremo di San Domenico and the lake shore fill about four hours, and the Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise National Park begins nearby. Best between June and August.

gem:carloforte.text: Carloforte is a harbour town on Isola di San Pietro in Italy, quiet and known for its cooking. The Saline di Carloforte and the coast are worth five hours, with Porto Flavia and Isola di Sant Antioco nearby. Aim for June, July or August.

gem:azenhas-do-mar.text: Azenhas do Mar is a small village above the sea in Portugal, inside the Parque Natural de Sintra-Cascais. Cabo da Roca and the palaces of Sintra make the day out around it, roughly four hours. The months to come are May through September.

gem:amarante.text: Amarante is a river town in Portugal on the UNESCO Creative Cities Network list for its food and wine. The Ponte de Sao Goncalo and the church beside it are the picture, and three hours covers the centre. May and June are the months to pick.

gem:porto-santo.text: Porto Santo is a quiet Atlantic island in the Madeira group: one long beach, and volcanic peaks behind it. Pico do Castelo and Pico do Facho are the climbs, six hours of sights all told. The sea is warm from June to September.

gem:sapanta-merry-cemetery.text: The Merry Cemetery is why anyone stops in Sapanta, a village of some three thousand in Romania. Two hours covers it, and the buses are poor, so a car helps. May to September is the workable stretch.

gem:sarmizegetusa-regia.text: Sarmizegetusa Regia is a Dacian fortress and sanctuary high in the Orastie Mountains of Romania, listed by UNESCO. The stone circles and terraces need about five hours, and the road in is rough with no bus. June to August only, in practice.

gem:apuseni-scarisoara.text: Apuseni is a scattered village in the Bihor Mountains of Romania, a base for Apuseni Natural Park. Scarisoara Cave is the reason most people turn off the road, and two hours covers it. The tracks are clear from June to August.

gem:barsana.text: Wooden churches are the point of Barsana, a village in Romania where they carry a UNESCO listing. Ieud Hill Church and the Calinesti Susani church stand close by, and two hours does the round. May to September is the season.

gem:kazanlak.text: Kazanlak is a town of fifty thousand in Bulgaria, built beside the Thracian Tomb of Kazanlak, a UNESCO site. Up in the hills sits the Buzludzha monument, with Koprinka Reservoir the other way. The two together run to five hours, in May, June or September.

gem:san-vicente-de-la-barquera.text: The port town of San Vicente de la Barquera spreads along an estuary on the northern coast of Spain. Parque Natural de Oyambre starts three kilometres out and El Capricho is a short drive away. A half day is enough, best between June and September.

gem:pedraza.text: Pedraza is a medieval village of fewer than five hundred people in Spain. The castles of Castilnovo and Turegano are within a short drive, with Hoces del Rio Duraton Natural Park beyond. Two hours covers it; May, June and September are the pick.

gem:arcos-de-la-frontera.text: Arcos de la Frontera is a medieval town in Spain, still partly ringed by its old walls. Iglesia de Santa Maria de la Asuncion and the Castle of Arcos de la Frontera lead the sights. April and May are the months to go, and four hours is plenty.

gem:es-trenc.text: Es Trenc is a long undeveloped beach in the Balearic Islands, with Es Salobrar just behind it. Platja des Caragol lies further round the same shore and Cabrera National Park sits offshore. May and June are best, and four hours is as long as anyone needs.

gem:dunnottar-castle.text: Stonehaven is a harbour town in the United Kingdom, and Dunnottar Castle, a ruin on a headland just outside, is the great draw. Stonehaven Harbour and the cliffs at Fowlsheugh round out a day of about six hours, easiest from June to August.

gem:bamburgh.text: Bamburgh is a village on the Northumberland coast of the United Kingdom, under Bamburgh Castle on its rock above the sand. Lindisfarne Priory and a boat out to the Farne Islands stretch the day to about seven hours, June to August.

gem:glenveagh.text: Glenveagh National Park fills a long glen in the Derryveagh Mountains of Ireland, lake at its centre and mountain all around. Glenveagh Castle stands on the shore and Errigal rises close by. Set aside five hours; June to August is driest.

gem:kopaonik.text: Kopaonik is a mountain range and national park in Serbia, a ski centre in winter and walking country the rest of the year. Pancicev vrh is the summit, with Gradac Monastery and Koznik below. July and August are the months for the high paths.

gem:mulhouse.text: An industrial city in Alsace, Mulhouse holds two of the best transport museums in France. Cite du Train and Cite de l'Automobile take most of a ten-hour day, with the Musee des beaux-arts nearby. May through September is the pleasant stretch.

gem:cremona.text: Cremona is a Lombardy city on the Po plain of Italy, known for violin making. The Torrazzo and Cremona Cathedral hold the main square, and the Museo del violino tells the rest. A full day, April to June or September.

gem:auvillar.text: Auvillar is one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, a thousand people gathered around an old grain market. The Halle aux grains and the eglise Saint-Pierre d'Auvillar fill three hours, with Moissac Abbey a short drive off. May, June or September.

gem:gloucester.text: Gloucester is a cathedral city in the United Kingdom, laid out over the Roman town of Glevum. Gloucester Cathedral leads, with Prinknash Abbey and the Great Witcombe Roman Villa out of town. Ten hours makes a full day, June to September.

gem:darlington.text: Darlington is a town of ninety thousand in County Durham, in the United Kingdom. Walworth Castle and Skerne Bridge come first, while Piercebridge Roman Fort and its bridge lie outside town. The sights run to nine hours, June to August.

gem:luneburg.text: Luneburg is a historic town in Lower Saxony, Germany, on the River Ilmenau. St John's Church and St Nicolai rise over the old centre, with Lune Abbey at the edge of town. The town holds ten hours of sights, May through September.

gem:albacete.text: Albacete is a large provincial city in Castile-La Mancha, Spain, known for its clasp knives. The Cathedral of San Juan de Albacete, the Albacete Museum and the Passage of Lodares fill about nine hours, best in April, May or October.

gem:bova.text: Bova is a village of a couple of hundred people in the Aspromonte hills of Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Aspromonte National Park begins at its edge and the Bova Marina Synagogue sits below on the coast. Two hours does it.

gem:sisteron.text: Sisteron is a small town in Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, France, under the Citadelle de Sisteron on its rock. Sisteron Cathedral stands below it, and Ganagobie Abbey lies along the valley. The town takes three hours, best in May, June or September.

gem:savoca.text: Savoca is a village of under two hundred in the Peloritani hills of Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Santi Pietro e Paolo d'Agro stands below it, and the Ancient theatre of Taormina is a short drive away. An hour or two covers it, May to July.

gem:apsley.text: Apsley is a quiet village in the United Kingdom, useful mostly as a base. St Albans Cathedral, Berkhamsted Castle and Whipsnade Zoo are all within a short drive, together about four hours. June to September is the best stretch.

gem:lectoure.text: Lectoure is a town of four thousand people in France, listed among Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. Lectoure Cathedral and the Chapelle des Carmelites fill much of three hours, and Flaran Abbey is a drive away. May, June and October are best.

gem:burton-upon-trent.text: Burton upon Trent is a Staffordshire market town in England, and brewing made it. Burton Abbey and The Burton Cooper are in town, with Tutbury Castle and the Heath Wood barrow cemetery a short way out. The whole circuit runs to ten hours, June to August.

gem:langres.text: Langres is a walled town of under nine thousand people in France, its ramparts running right around the old centre. Langres Cathedral and the Porte des Moulins anchor a walk of about five hours, best made between June and August.

gem:angers.text: Angers is a mid-sized city in Pays de la Loire, France, built around its castle. The Chateau d'Angers and Angers Cathedral hold the centre, with the Jardin des Plantes for a break. Its sights add up to ten hours, May through September.
