gem:mondonedo.text: Mondonedo is a cathedral town of about four thousand people in Spain, its old centre under protection. The Catedral de Mondonedo and the Basilica of Saint Martin de Mondonedo take three hours, and As Catedrais beach is a drive away.

gem:skalanion.text: Skalanion is a village of about a thousand people on Crete, in Greece. Knossos Palace and the Heraklion Archaeological Museum are the reason to be here, four hours between them. May to September is the long season.

gem:hallenberg.text: Hallenberg is a village of under five thousand people in the Rothaar hills of Germany. Muhlenkopfschanze sits above it, and Langenberg and Kahler Asten are within reach. The walking runs to about four hours, June to August.

gem:norderney.text: Norderney is a resort island in the East Frisian Islands, off Lower Saxony in Germany. The beaches are the point, and St Mary's Church and Berum Castle fill an hour or two more. June to August is the season.

gem:palencia.text: A cathedral city in Castile and Leon, Spain, Palencia keeps old plazas in a modern centre. Palencia Cathedral and the Crypt of San Antolin lead, with Cristo del Otero on the hill outside. The full round takes nine hours, easiest in May, June or September.

gem:jerica.text: Jerica is a village of fifteen hundred people in Spain, between two ranges of low hills. Serra d'Espada and Serra Calderona rise on either side, with Segorbe Cathedral a short drive off. The village asks about four hours, best in April, May or October.

gem:kemmel.text: Kemmel is a village of a thousand people in Belgium, under the low ridge of the Kemmelberg. Spanbroekmolen British Cemetery is one of many war graves nearby, and Ypres with its Menin Gate is a short drive; four hours covers both, June to August.

gem:vaasa.text: Vaasa is a coastal city in Ostrobothnia, Finland, with the Old Vaasa ruins standing apart from the present centre. Vaasan kirkko and Mustasaaren kirkko fill out about eight hours. June to August is the short bright season.

gem:castelli.text: Castelli is a village of three hundred people in Italy, below Monte Camicia and among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Gran Sasso e Monti della Laga National Park spreads around it, with Corno Grande above. May to July is the window.

gem:zabrze.text: Zabrze is a coal city in Silesia, Poland, part of the sprawl around Katowice. The Guido Mine and Coal Mining Museum takes visitors underground and is the reason to come. Add the Gliwice Radio Tower and the day runs to ten hours, May to September.

gem:manresa.text: Manresa is a city in Catalonia, Spain, within sight of Montserrat. Santa Maria de Manresa stands above the river by the Pont Vell, and the Cave of Saint Ignatius sits below it. April to June and September are the good months, ten hours of sights.

gem:bolsward.text: Bolsward is a town of nine thousand in Friesland, ringed by working windmills such as the Aylvapoldermolen and Oegekloostermolen. Add the Eise Eisinga Planetarium nearby and the day runs to six hours, best between June and August.

gem:bar-sur-seine.text: Bar-sur-Seine is a village of under four thousand in France, one of the Petites Cites de Caractere. The Chateau de Bar sur Seine anchors a three hour visit, and the Orient Forest Regional Natural Park is the draw beyond it, June to September.

gem:herne.text: Herne sits in the Ruhr, a city of 172,000 where the German Mining Museum and Schloss Strunkede lead. Ten hours fills a day, taking in the Rathaus Herne and the Stadtische Galerie im Schlosspark Strunkede, with May to September the kindest run.

gem:winschoten.text: Molen Berg, Molen Dijkstra and Molen Edens stand over Winschoten, a town of 18,500 in the Netherlands. Six hours takes in the mills and the Ennemaborg estate; the Oldambtmeer is close, and June to August suits it best.

gem:sliven.text: Sliven is a city of 84,000 in Bulgaria, set below the Blue Stones ridge with Karandila on the heights above. Tuida and the Saint Nikola church round out a seven hour visit; May, June and September are the months to pick.

gem:place.text: A village of 958 people in North Macedonia, close enough to Skopje that Matka Canyon, Vodno and the Millennium Cross fill a four hour day. Scupi and the Skopje Aqueduct sit on the same route; May, June and September are the pick.

gem:szczawno-zdroj.text: Szczawno-Zdroj is a village of 5,600 in Poland at the foot of Waligora and Wielka Sowa. Ksiaz is the great castle nearby, with the Peace Church in Swidnica and Krzeszow Abbey within reach; four hours of sights, best June to August.

gem:launsdorf.text: Hochosterwitz Castle on its rock is the reason to stop at Launsdorf, a village of 1,200 in Austria. Gurk Cathedral and the Langsee are close, four hours in all, and the season runs May to September.

gem:drachten.text: Drachten is a town of 45,000 in Friesland and the handiest base for De Alde Feanen National Park. Museum Drachten and the Harinxmastate round out a six hour day; June to August is the stretch to aim for.

gem:quin.text: Quin is a village of 935 in Ireland, built around Quin Abbey. Bunratty Castle, Craggaunowen Castle and Ennis Cathedral all lie within a short drive, which turns a three hour stop into a full day out in June, July or August.

gem:christoupoli.text: Christoupoli is a village of 518 in Greece within reach of Athens, which is where its sights are. The Parthenon and the rest of the Acropolis of Athens, the Erechtheion and the Panathenaic Stadium take about three hours; May is the month.

gem:midsland.text: Midsland is a village of 915 in the West Frisian Islands, close to the Brandaris and to Formerum. Its sights amount to three hours, so most people come for the beach instead, between June and September.

gem:klausen.text: Klausen, or Chiusa, is a village of 2,500 in Italy under the cliff of Sabiona Monastery. Trostburg and Schloss Branzoll fill out four hours, with Sassolungo and Piz Boe on the skyline; June to September is the season.

gem:vitorchiano.text: Vitorchiano is a village of 2,000 in Italy, one of the Borghi piu belli d'Italia, and about four hours of sights. Piazza San Francesco and the Basilica di San Francesco alla Rocca come first, then Monte Cimino or Lake Vico in May or June.

gem:vogogna.text: Castello Visconteo looks down on Vogogna, a village of 1,400 in Italy on the Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. The village itself takes three hours; Lago di Mergozzo and the walks up Monte Massone are what fills the rest, June to September.

gem:varzi.text: The Borghi piu belli d'Italia list includes Varzi, a village of 2,300 in Italy with three hours of sights. Oramala, Zavattarello and Bagnaria are the outings worth adding, in May, June or September.

gem:cordovado.text: May and June suit Cordovado, a village of 2,600 in Italy on the Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. Its centre, the Chiesa di San Martino Vescovo and the Abbazia Santa Maria in Silvis make three hours; the Duomo di Portogruaro is nearby.

gem:preci.text: Preci is a village of fewer than three hundred in Italy, below Monte Vettore and on the Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. Its two buildings of note, the Collegiata di Maria Santissima and the Convento Sant'Agostino, fill a three hour stop in May or June.

gem:acerenza.text: The Cattedrale di Acerenza is the whole point of Acerenza, a village of 2,200 in Italy on the Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. Two hours covers the cathedral, the Museo Diocesano and the Castello Normanno; May and June are the pick.

gem:le-faou.text: Eglise Saint-Sauveur is the church at the heart of Le Faou, a village of 1,700 in France on the Petites Cites de Caractere list. Landevennec Abbey and Eglise Notre-Dame de Rumengol are worth the detour on a three hour visit, June to September.

gem:geraci-siculo.text: June to August is the window for Geraci Siculo, a village of 1,800 in Italy on the Borghi piu belli d'Italia list. Castello di Geraci, Santa Maria Maggiore and Chiesa di Sant'Anna are what there is to see, three hours in all.

gem:combourg.text: Combourg, a village of 5,400 in France, is on the Petites Cites de Caractere list, and its castle is the reason to stop. The Chateau de Combourg takes up most of a three hour visit; the Menhir La Pierre-Longue is a short walk beyond.

gem:gourdon.text: Gourdon, a village of 5,300 in France, made Les Plus Beaux Detours de France on the strength of its old centre, where Eglise Saint-Pierre de Gourdon and Maison Cavaignac stand. Add the Grottes de Cougnac and three hours is gone; May to September.

gem:la-grave.text: La Grave is a village in France set opposite La Meije, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Notre-Dame de l'Assomption is the sight in the village; the rest is mountain, from La Grande Ruine to Barre des Ecrins. July and August are the months.

gem:brousse-le-chateau.text: Brousse-le-Chateau is a village of 710 in France, one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, and three hours sees all of it. The Vieux Pont and Eglise Saint-Jacques-le-Majeur are the pair to walk to, with Chateau de Coupiac the detour, May to September.

gem:bazouges-la-perouse.text: Two chateaux, Bonnefontaine and La Ballue, are the reason to turn off for Bazouges-la-Perouse, a village of 1,800 in France on the Petites Cites de Caractere list. Its own streets take the rest of three hours, June to September.

gem:besse-et-saint-anastaise.text: Besse-et-Saint-Anastaise sits below the Puy de Sancy in France, a village of 1,600 on the Petites Cites de Caractere list. Grottes de Jonas and Murol castle are the outings worth the drive, and Lac Chauvet is close; three hours, June to August.

gem:camon.text: The Abbatiale de la Nativite-de-la-Vierge and the Maison haute are all Camon has, which was enough to put this village of 1,250 on Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Chateau de Lagarde is close; three hours, May, June or September.

gem:excideuil.text: Chateau d'Excideuil stands over Excideuil, a village of 1,400 in France on the Petites Cites de Caractere list. Abbaye de Tourtoirac and the Lanterne des morts de Cherveix-Cubas are the short drives that round out three hours, June to September.

gem:piriac-sur-mer.text: Piriac-sur-Mer is a village of 2,000 in France, one of the Petites Cites de Caractere. Its sights are modest, the Croix de Brogard and Croix du Requer among them, and three hours is generous; most arrive between June and September.

gem:sainte-croix-en-jarez.text: Sainte-Croix-en-Jarez, a village of 806 in France, takes its name from the Chartreuse de Sainte-Croix-en-Jarez and is on Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Tour de Doizieux and Chateau de Virieu are nearby; allow three hours, May to September.

gem:la-sauvetat.text: The Puy de Dome rises behind La Sauvetat, a village of 518 in France on the Petites Cites de Caractere list. Chateau du Marchidial is the sight in the village and the Porte fortifiee de Montpeyroux the one nearby, four hours for both, May to September.

gem:chanaz.text: Chanaz is a village of 510 in France near the Lac du Bourget, one of the Petites Cites de Caractere. Hautecombe Abbey is the main outing and Grand Colombier rises behind; plan on three hours, any time from May to September.

gem:ossett.text: Ossett is a market town of 21,900 in the United Kingdom, close enough to Wakefield to borrow its sights. Wakefield Cathedral, Sandal Castle and the Theatre Royal Wakefield make up most of six hours; June to August is the best of it.

gem:shifnal.text: Shifnal is a market town of 6,200 in the United Kingdom, handy for The Iron Bridge and Coalport Bridge. Blists Hill Victorian Town and the Jackfield Tile Museum take up most of four hours, best June to August.

gem:monfalcone.text: Monfalcone is a town of 26,700 in Italy, best used as the start of the Rilke trail along the Duino cliffs. The Isonzo battlefields and the Marano-Grado Lagoon fill out six hours; May and June are the months to pick.

gem:san-sebastian-de-los-reyes.text: San Sebastian de los Reyes is a city of 76,000 beside Madrid, with good public transport into the centre. Its own sights, the Ermita de Valverde and San Pedro Martir among them, run to seven hours, best in May or September.

gem:sagunto.text: Sagunto is a city of 66,000 in Spain under the Castell de Sagunt, with the Roman Theatre of Saguntum on the climb. Ten hours takes in the castle, the theatre and the beaches towards Valencia; May to August is the season.

gem:chianciano-terme.text: Chianciano Terme is a village of 6,200 in Italy whose sights sit close together, the Collegiata di San Lorenzo, the Palazzo Comunale and the Chiesa del Suffragio among them. Lake Chiusi is nearby; four hours, May or June.

gem:velez-malaga.text: Velez-Malaga is a city of 74,000 in Spain and a listed conjunto historico. The Castillo de Velez-Malaga looks over the old town, with the Palacio de Beniel and Iglesia de Santa Maria la Mayor below; nine hours, April and May.

gem:la-flotte.text: La Flotte is a quiet harbour village in France, listed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Ernest Cognacq Museum and Fort de La Pree fill about three hours, and June to September is the window; public transport is poor, so a car helps.

BRI.text: Bari is a port city on the Puglia coast, with roughly sixteen hours of sights to work through. The Basilica of Saint Nicholas leads, backed by Teatro Petruzzelli and Castello Svevo di Bari. May is the month, and transport is excellent.

PEG.text: Perugia is a hill city in Italy, medieval at its core. Palazzo dei Priori and the Fontana Maggiore hold the main square, with Rocca Paolina below and the Galleria nazionale dell'Umbria for paintings. Ten hours covers it, best in May or June.

BRQ.text: Brno is a city in Czechia where modern and historic sit side by side. Spilberk Castle holds the hill, Vila Tugendhat draws architecture pilgrims, and the Museum of Romani Culture is rare anywhere. Its seventeen hours suit May through September.

gem:st-anton.text: St Anton am Arlberg is a ski village in Austria, set below the Arlbergpass. The hills open up June through August, with Galzig, the Lechtal Alps and the lakes at Butzensee and Spullersee, roughly three hours of sights. Public transport is poor.

gem:jajce.text: Jajce is a walled medieval town in Bosnia and Herzegovina, best known for the Pliva Waterfall. The Jajce Fortress and the Jajce Mithraeum round out about five hours, and May through September is the reliable stretch; buses are decent.

gem:cartagena.text: Cartagena is a port city on the coast of Spain with a Roman layer under the modern one. The Roman Theatre of Cartagena is the headline, the cathedral stands beside it, and the Cueva de los Aviones is out of town. Ten hours, April to June.

gem:dragor.text: Dragor is a low, quiet harbour town on Amager in Denmark, an easy run out from Copenhagen. Six hours covers the old streets, the sand at Amager Strandpark and the view to the Oresund Bridge. June through August is the season; buses are thin.

gem:virpazar.text: Virpazar is a tiny village on Lake Skadar in Montenegro, and the lake is the whole point. Two hours covers the place itself, so pair it with Nacionalni park Skadarsko jezero or the coast at Sveti Stefan. May and June are the months to pick.

gem:kinsale.text: Kinsale is a harbour town in Ireland, known for eating well and for sailing. Two hours covers the centre with Desmond Castle and James Fort, while Spike Island and Haulbowline sit further along the coast. June through August, and buses are thin.

gem:oban.text: Oban is a ferry town on the coast in Scotland, the way out to the islands. McCaig's Tower looks over the bay, Dunollie Castle and Dunstaffnage Castle bracket it, and Oban Distillery sits in the middle of five hours. June through August is best.

gem:yorkshire-dales.text: The Yorkshire Dales are walking country in England, limestone hills cut by long valleys. Pen-y-ghent is the classic climb, with Bolton Castle and Middleham Castle for a change of pace and Semerwater to sit beside. Six hours out, June through August.

gem:christiansfeld.text: Christiansfeld is a small planned town in Denmark, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for the way it was laid out. The church and Christiansfeld Pharmacy fill three quiet hours; Koldinghus and Trapholt are close by. Best from June to August.

gem:zatec.text: Zatec is a small town in Czechia where beer is the local trade, and the brewery quarter carries a UNESCO World Heritage listing. Zatec Brewery and the Muzeum Homolupulu anchor six hours, with Nechranice Reservoir nearby. May through September.

gem:sumava.text: Sumava National Park is quiet forest country in Czechia, spread along the Bohemian Forest. Kvilda makes a base, with Plockenstein and Grosser Arber for height and Nationalpark Bayerischer Wald over the border. The walking runs to seven hours, best June through August.

gem:meersburg.text: Meersburg is a wine town stacked above Lake Constance in Germany, and Burg Meersburg holds the high ground. Mainau and Reichenau Island lie across the water, so the four hours here stretch easily. June through September is the season.

gem:oberammergau.text: Oberammergau is a mountain village in Germany ringed by big names. Linderhof Palace and the Wieskirche are the set pieces, Kloster Ettal sits down the valley, and the Zugspitze rises behind. The four hours here are best taken June through August.

gem:gosau.text: Gosau is a scattered valley village in Austria under the Dachstein Mountains. Hoher Dachstein and Gamsfeld are the walks, Hallstatter See and Wolfgangsee the water, and three hours covers what is signposted. June through August, and a car is needed.

gem:creux-du-van.text: Creux du Van is quiet walking country in Switzerland, wild enough to feel remote. Le Soliat is the high point of the circuit, with Motiers, Couvet and Boudry as the villages below. Six hours on foot, June through August; public transport is poor.

gem:sete.text: Sete is a working fishing port on the coast of France, more workaday than resort. Mont Saint-Clair gives the view, the Espace Georges Brassens the local hero, and the Lido de Thau the beach. Six hours does it, best in May or June.

gem:brantome.text: Brantome is a small, quiet village in France, listed among the Petites Cites de Caractere. Chateau de Bourdeilles and Villars Cave are the nearby draws, with Perigueux Cathedral a drive away. May through September, and three hours is enough.

gem:vichy.text: Vichy is a spa town in France and one of The Great Spa Towns of Europe. The Opera de Vichy, the Hotel des Ambassadeurs and the park kiosk make six unhurried hours, with Lac d'Allier alongside. Public transport is good; come May through September.

gem:dijon.text: Dijon is a city of old streets and good food in France, built around the Palace of the Dukes of Burgundy. Dijon Cathedral and the Musee des Beaux-Arts de Dijon take up much of ten hours. May through September is the spread, and trains are good.

gem:troyes.text: Troyes is a medieval city in France, compact and easy on foot. Troyes Cathedral leads, with the Basilica of St Urbain, the Musee des Beaux-Arts de Troyes and the musee d'Art moderne de Troyes close behind. Ten hours, May through September.

gem:deauville.text: Deauville is a seaside resort in France, smart and a little formal. The Casino de Deauville and the sand fill most of four hours, with the Pont de Normandie up the coast and Casino de Trouville-sur-Mer next door. Best from June to August.

gem:quiberon.text: Quiberon is a beach and surf town on the coast of France, busiest June through September. The Carnac stones are the local wonder, Belle Ile lies offshore, and plage de Sainte-Barbe handles the swimming. Sights take about three hours.

gem:guerande.text: Guerande is a medieval town on the coast of France, with the Marais salants de Guerande spread out beside it. Chateau de Careil, Manoir de Kervaudu and the Dolmen de Sandun add up to six hours. June through September; a car makes it easier.

gem:sifnos.text: Sifnos is a small island in the Cyclades, known in Greece for its cooking. The Archaeological Museum of Sifnos and the collection at Agios Andreas cover five hours, and Sarakiniko Beach is the swim. Best months run May through September.

gem:thasos.text: Thasos is an island in Greece that suits families, with beaches at Pefkari and Koinyra. The Archaeological Museum of Thasos and the Polygnotos Vagis Municipal Museum fill the rest of six hours, and Ypsario is the walk. Beaches stay busy June through August.

gem:ioannina.text: Ioannina is a lakeside city in Greece, with the old quarter still inside its castle. Ioannina Castle and the Fethiye Mosque look over Lake Pamvotida, and the National Resistance Museum of Ioannina is close by. May and June suit the seven hours it takes.

gem:brisighella.text: Brisighella is a medieval village in Italy, listed with I Borghi piu belli d'Italia and standing inside a UNESCO Global Geopark. The Rocca di Brisighella above the roofs is the climb, three hours in all. May, June and September are the months.

gem:ascoli-piceno.text: Ascoli Piceno is a historic town in Italy built around the piazza del Popolo. The Cattedrale di Sant'Emidio, the Ponte di Cecco and the Ponte Romano di Solesta make the walk, six hours with lunch. May and June are the best months.

gem:palinuro.text: Diving is what brings people to Palinuro, a quiet stretch of coast in Italy. Velia and Monte Gelbison lie inland inside Cilento, Vallo di Diano and Alburni National Park, and about four hours covers what is signposted. The season runs May through August.

gem:rocca-calascio.text: Rocca Calascio is a castle standing high in the Apennines in Italy, with almost nothing around it. Corno Grande and the Gran Sasso e Monti della Laga National Park take the rest of six hours, and Lake Campotosto lies below. The road up is best June through August.

gem:gerace.text: Gerace is a medieval town on a hill in Italy, listed with I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Co-Cathedral Basilica of the Assumption of Mary is the reason to climb, and two hours is enough before dropping to Locri Epizephiri below. May through July.

gem:caltagirone.text: Caltagirone is a baroque town in Italy that lives on ceramics. The Staircase of Santa Maria del Monte is the sight, backed by the Museo Regionale della Ceramica di Caltagirone. May or June, four hours.

gem:castelsardo.text: Castelsardo is a medieval village stacked on a headland in Sardinia, with Castello dei Doria at the top. Elephant Rock is a short drive out and Punta Tramontana is the beach, three hours in all. May through August, though buses are poor.

gem:bosa.text: Bosa is a quiet town on the coast in Sardinia, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Torre di Bosa looks down on it, the Concattedrale dell'Immacolata Concezione sits in the centre, and three hours is plenty. April and May are the pick.

gem:briksdalsbreen.text: Briksdalsbreen sits inside Jostedalsbreen National Park in Norway, a walk in from the road and back. Ramnefjellsfossen, Nigardsbreen and Lodalskapa are the other names here, five hours of them. July is the month that works, and there is no bus.

gem:sesimbra.text: Sesimbra is a fishing town on the coast of Portugal, Castelo de Sesimbra above it and Forte de Santiago on the front. Arrabida Natural Park runs along the coast to Ribeiro do Cavalo Beach and Figueirinha Beach. May through September, four hours.

gem:praia-da-falesia.text: Praia da Falesia is a beach town on the coast of Portugal, known for red cliffs above the sand at Falesia Beach. Albufeira, Paderne Castle and Cerro da Vila fill about five hours nearby, best reached May through September given limited transport.

gem:lamego.text: Lamego is a wine and baroque town in northern Portugal, its skyline led by the Our Lady of the Assumption Cathedral. Godim and the Chapel of Sao Pedro de Balsemao make for six hours of sightseeing, ideal in May, June or September.

gem:kaliakra.text: Cape Kaliakra is a fortress village on the Bulgaria coast, its clifftop ruins tied to the Naval Battle of Kaliakra and Admiral Fyodor Ushakov. Bolata beach sits close by, and two hours takes in the sights between June and August.

gem:olite.text: Olite is a castle village in Spain, its skyline held by the turreted Palacio Real de Olite. The Palacio de los Mencos and Castillo de Santacara stretch a visit to three hours, best planned for May through September since transport runs poor.

gem:siguenza.text: Siguenza is a quiet castle village in Spain, its center held by Siguenza Cathedral and the ruins of Castillo de Siguenza. Segontia and the Roman arch of Medinaceli bring the total to three hours; transport is good, and May, June or September suit it best.

gem:xativa.text: Xativa is a historic castle town in Spain, its hilltop Castle of Xativa visible for miles around. The Collegiate Basilica of Xativa and Cova Negra add up to six hours, best timed for March, April or May with good transport links.

gem:la-graciosa.text: La Graciosa is a remote island area in Spain, part of the Chinijo Archipelago beside Alegranza and Montana Clara. Monte Corona and Roque del Este add another five hours on foot, quietest May through September despite limited transport.

gem:torridon.text: Torridon is a wilderness area in the United Kingdom, ringed by the peaks of Liathach and Beinn Eighe above Loch Maree. Tom na Gruagaich and Beinn Liath Mhor extend the hiking to seven hours, best tackled June through August with little public transport.

gem:loch-ness.text: Loch Ness in the United Kingdom is known for the Loch Ness Monster legend and the ruined Urquhart Castle above the water. Boleskine House and the Caledonian Forest take the visit to about five hours, best seen June through August despite poor transport.

gem:tintagel.text: Tintagel is a coastal castle area in the United Kingdom, its ruined Tintagel Castle perched above the sea. Merlin's Cave and the Tintagel Old Post Office fill six more hours, best explored June through September though transport stays limited.

gem:porthcurno.text: Porthcurno is a coastal beach area in the United Kingdom, near the cliff-top Minack Theatre and the point at Land's End. St Michael's Mount and Porthgwarra stretch a coastal walk to seven hours, best done June through September with limited transport.

gem:white-cliffs-dover.text: The White Cliffs of Dover rise above the English Channel in the United Kingdom, with Dover Castle anchoring the sights. St Augustine's Abbey and South Foreland bring the total to seven hours, best timed June through August despite limited transport.

gem:pelister.text: Pelister National Park in North Macedonia centers on Lake Prespa and the ridgeline of Magaro Peak near Bitola. Golem Grad and Heraclea Lyncestis add historic stops to seven hours of hiking, best done June through August given poor transport.

gem:opatija.text: Opatija is a romantic coastal village in Croatia, near Rijeka on the Liburnia riviera. Vojak and the wooded ridge of Ucka rise behind Palace Modello, and two hours suffices for the sights, best enjoyed May through August despite limited transport.

gem:varazdin.text: Varazdin is a baroque town in Croatia, its Old Town centered on the Croatian National Theatre in Varazdin. Cakovec Castle and the ruins of Aquae Iasae fill out four hours, best seen May, June or September with good transport.

gem:stolac.text: Stolac is a quiet historic village in Bosnia and Herzegovina, close to Mostar and the ancient hillfort of Daorson. Badanj Cave and Hutovo Blato Nature park stretch a visit to three hours, with good transport making May, June or September the easiest choice.

gem:biogradska-gora.text: Biogradska Gora is a wilderness village in Montenegro, built around Lake Biograd inside its own national park. The Bjelasica range and Komovi range frame three hours of trails, best hiked June through August despite poor transport.

gem:cetinje.text: Cetinje in Montenegro holds the National Museum of Montenegro and Cetinje Monastery. Sveti Stefan and the peak of Lovcen lie within reach, and five hours covers the town, best planned for June through August with good transport.

gem:brecon.text: Brecon is a market town in the United Kingdom, its skyline held by Brecon Cathedral and the ridge of Pen y Fan. Brecon Beacons National Park and Brecknock Museum add up to six hours, best timed June through August with good transport.

gem:faenza.text: Faenza is a cathedral town in Italy, centered on Piazza Saffi and Faenza Cathedral. San Mercuriale abbey and Monte Poggiolo bring the sights to about six hours, best seen April, May, June or September with good transport.

gem:saint-etienne.text: Saint-Etienne is a city in France, home to Stade Geoffroy-Guichard and Saint-Etienne Cathedral. The Saint-Etienne Mine Museum and Chateau de Rochetaillee extend a visit to about ten hours, best planned June through September given good transport.

gem:faversham.text: Faversham is a market town in Kent, United Kingdom, with Canterbury Cathedral and St Augustine's Abbey among the nearby sights. Canterbury Castle and the Isle of Sheppey take the visit to six hours; June through September works best, and transport is good.

gem:fermo.text: Fermo is a cathedral town in the Marche region of Italy, its center marked by Fermo Cathedral and Palazzo dei Priori. Teatro dell'Aquila and the Church of Santissima Annunziata stretch a visit to five hours, best in May or June despite poor transport.

gem:nuoro.text: Nuoro is a town in Sardinia, Italy, overlooked by the peak of Ortobene and the Supramonte massif. Monte Corrasi and the Fonte sacra Su Tempiesu add another five hours, best seen May, June or September despite poor transport.

gem:voiteur.text: Voiteur is a village in France, near the Abbaye Saint-Pierre de Baume-les-Messieurs and its carved retable. Chateau de la Muyre and Chateau d'Arlay fill three more hours, best timed May through September with poor transport nearby.

gem:udine.text: Udine is a city in Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Italy, anchored by Udine Cathedral and Castello di Udine. The Loggia del Lionello and Museo Diocesano e Gallerie del Tiepolo stretch a visit to about nine hours, best in May or June with good transport.

gem:bishop-auckland.text: Bishop Auckland is a castle town in County Durham, United Kingdom, built around Auckland Castle and Escomb Church. Durham Castle and Raby Castle lie within reach, and six hours covers the sights, best timed June through August with good transport.

gem:romsey.text: Romsey is a market town in Hampshire, United Kingdom, centered on Romsey Abbey beside the River Test. Winchester Cathedral and Mottisfont Abbey lie nearby, and six hours fills a visit best timed June through September.

gem:cluny.text: Cluny sits in Saone-et-Loire, France, built around Cluny Abbey. The Rock of Solutre and Chapelle des Moines bring the sights to four hours, best seen May through September with good transport.

gem:radevormwald.text: Radevormwald is a town in Germany, near the Tuchmuseum Lennep and Huckeswagen Castle. Elberfeld and the Opernhaus Wuppertal add historic stops nearby, with six hours needed and June through August the easiest months.

gem:ayr.text: Ayr is a coastal town in the United Kingdom, home to Ayr Cathedral and within reach of Culzean Castle. Brig o' Doon and Lady Isle round out six hours, best timed June through August though transport stays limited.

gem:astorga.text: Astorga is a historic town in Castile and Leon, Spain, centered on Astorga Cathedral and the Palacio Episcopal de Astorga. The Muralla de Astorga and Plaza de la Catedral add five more hours, with good transport and May through September the kindest months.

gem:sutomore.text: Sutomore is a coastal village near Bar in Montenegro, within reach of Sveti Stefan and Sveti Nikola Island. Ratac Abbey and the peak of Rumija lie close by, and three hours covers the sights, best timed June through August despite poor transport.

gem:fontenay-le-comte.text: Fontenay-le-Comte is a historic town in France, near Maillezais Cathedral and the Hotel des eveques de Maillezais. The Maison de Francois Viete and Hotel dit Chateau-Gaillard add up to six hours, best seen May through September with good transport.

gem:plasencia.text: Plasencia is a cathedral town in the Extremadura region of Spain, seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Plasencia. Capera and the Parque de los Pinos round out six hours, best visited in May with good transport.

gem:cottbus.text: Cottbus is a city in Brandenburg, Germany, home to the Wendisches Museum and Spremberger Turm. Staatstheater Cottbus and the Kunstmuseum Dieselkraftwerk Cottbus stretch a visit to about ten hours; transport is good, best planned May through September.

gem:brandenburg-an-der-havel.text: Brandenburg an der Havel is a historic city in Germany, ringed by towers like Plauer Torturm and Steintorturm. Rathenower Torturm and the Neustadtischer Muhlentorturm add another ten hours of sights, best timed May through September with good transport.

gem:pomorie.text: Pomorie is a beach town on the Bulgaria coast, anchored by Anhialo and Lake Pomorie. Sunny Beach and Lake Atanasovsko lie close by, and four hours covers the sights, best timed May, June or September despite limited transport.

gem:chesterfield.text: Chesterfield sits in Derbyshire, United Kingdom, anchored by Bolsover Castle and Holy Trinity Church. Renishaw Hall and Sutton Scarsdale Hall bring the sights to nine hours, best seen June through August with good transport.

gem:southport.text: Southport is a coastal city near Liverpool in the United Kingdom, home to Meols Hall and St George's Church. The Atkinson and Birkdale round out nine hours of sights, with Crosby Beach and Formby Beach close by and good transport June through August.

gem:jyvaskyla.text: Jyvaskyla is a lake city in central Finland known for its student population. AaltoAlvari and the Alvar Aalto Museum head the sights, with ten hours enough time between June and August. Tuomiojarvi and Jyvasjarvi lie close by for a swim after.

gem:monchengladbach.text: Monchengladbach is a city in Germany with old castles and green space. Abteiberg Museum and the Basilica of St Vitus lead the sights, with Schloss Rheydt close behind. Ten hours suits a visit from May through September.

gem:long-eaton.text: Long Eaton sits in the United Kingdom, close to Derby and Nottingham. Derby Museum and Art Gallery and Nottingham Castle draw most visitors, with Pickford's House and the Museum of Making rounding out six hours. June through September suit it best.

gem:ablain-saint-nazaire.text: France lists Ablain-Saint-Nazaire, a village, as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Fortifications of Vauban and Arras Cathedral sit nearby in Arras and Lens, with the Abbey of St Vaast close behind. It takes about four hours, best between June and August.

gem:vernet-les-bains.text: Vernet-les-Bains, in France, is set below Canigou. The Abbaye Saint-Martin du Canigou and Saint-Michel-de-Cuxa top the sights, in about four hours. May, June and September are the best months, with Lac de Vinca for a swim.

gem:ceaulmont.text: Ceaulmont, in France, is listed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. Argentomagus and the Chapelle Saint-Benoit sit nearby in Argenton-sur-Creuse. A morning here runs about three hours, best from June to September, with Plage de Chambon nearby.

gem:greoux-les-bains.text: Greoux-les-Bains is a small spa village in France, listed among Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. Its own Chateau de Greoux-les-Bains anchors a visit, with the Plateau de Valensole a short trip away. Two hours suffices, best in May, June or September.

gem:falkenberg.text: Falkenberg is a coastal town in Sweden with a long beach history. Saint Lawrence Church and Falkenberg Bridge lead the sights, in about five hours. June, July and August suit it best, though public transport here runs limited.

gem:jonzac.text: Jonzac, in France, is recognized among Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. Chateau de Jonzac and Chateau de Meux headline the sights, with the church of Saint-Vincent de Reaux nearby. May through September works well, with about three hours enough time.

gem:luttringen.text: Luttringen sits in Germany near a national park and a reservoir. The Mohne Reservoir and Werl Pilgrimage Churches lead a visit, with the Wiesenkirche nearby in Soest. June through August works best, in about four hours.

gem:terezin.text: Terezin is a village in Czechia on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List. Ploskovice and Strekov Castle top the sights, with Radobyl and Hazmburk rounding things out. May through September brings the best weather, in about four hours.

gem:chiusi.text: Chiusi is a village in Italy between two lakes, Trasimeno and Chiusi. The Chiusi National Archaeological Museum and San Biagio anchor a visit, with Isola Maggiore nearby. May and June are the months to choose, in about four hours.

gem:go-weinstein.text: Gossweinstein sits in Germany, built around its basilica and nearby caves. The Basilica Gossweinstein and Devil's Cave draw most visitors, with Bing Cave close behind. June through September suits it, with about four hours enough time.

gem:imola.text: Imola is a historic city in Italy with a cluster of older sights near its center. The Santuario della Beata Vergine del Piratello and Palazzo Tozzoni lead them, with San Domenico nearby. April, May, June and September all work well, across roughly nine hours.

gem:oberhausen.text: Oberhausen is a city in Germany, home to the Schauinsland-Reisen-Arena. Essen sits next door with the Museum Folkwang, Essen Minster and the Golden Madonna of Essen. Ten hours covers both, best from May to September.

gem:villalago.text: Villalago is a village in Italy named among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Rocca di Villalago and the Eremo di San Domenico sit above Lago di San Domenico. June through August is the season, in about four hours, with Scanno nearby.

gem:santarem.text: Santarem is a town in Portugal above the Rio Tejo. The Our Lady of the Assumption Cathedral and Torre das Cabacas lead the sights, with Igreja da Graca rounding out six hours. April, May and June are the best months to come.

gem:lahti.text: Lahti sits on the shore of Vesijarvi in southern Finland, a city built for sport. Sibelius Hall and Lahti Stadium lead the sights, close to the Salpausselka ridge. June through August suits it best, across about nine hours.

gem:kuopio.text: Kuopio is a lake city in Finland, framed by water on three sides. Kuopio Cathedral and Puijon torni top the sights, with Kallavesi lake spreading out below Puijo hill. June through August is prime time, across roughly nine hours.

gem:poros.text: Poros is a village in Greece facing Hydra across the water. The Archaeological Museum of Poros and Kalaureia lead a visit, with the Methana Volcano visible beyond. Two hours covers it, best from May through September.

gem:bad-lauterberg-im-harz.text: Bad Lauterberg im Harz is a spa town at the foot of the Brocken in Germany. The Unicorn Cave and Walkenried Abbey lead the sights, with Grosser Knollen for hikers. Six hours suits June through August, and Juessee lake offers a break after.

gem:bauge-en-anjou.text: Bauge-en-Anjou, in France, is recognized as one of the Petites Cites de Caractere. Chateau de Bauge and Chateau de Montgeoffroy anchor the sights, with Louroux Abbey further out. May through September works well, in about three hours.

gem:ravensburg.text: Ravensburg is a town in Germany with three abbeys nearby: Weissenau, Baindt and Weingarten. Ravensburger Spieleland and the Gehrenberg hill round out a visit. Six hours suits May through September, with Illmensee and Stadtsee for a lake stop.

gem:bibione.text: Bibione is a beach village on the coast of Italy. Spiaggia di Ponente and Spiaggia di Levante draw most visitors, with the Caorle Lighthouse a short trip along the shore. Two hours covers it, best from May through August.

gem:neptun.text: Neptun is a small beach village on the coast of Romania. Lake Techirghiol and the Mangalia Mosque lead the sights, with Parc Mangalia rounding out the list. Two hours is plenty, best between May and September.

gem:pori.text: Pori is a coastal city in Finland known for the Juselius Mausoleum. Porin Teatteri and Keski-Porin kirkko round out the center, with Ulvilan kirkko further out. July and August are the months to go, across roughly nine hours.

gem:fiumefreddo-bruzio.text: Fiumefreddo Bruzio is a village in Italy named among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Coreca Caves and Coreca Reefs sit below it on the water, with Monte Cocuzzo further inland. May and June are the best months, in about three hours.

gem:sansepolcro.text: Sansepolcro is a town in Italy centered on its own cathedral. Sansepolcro Cathedral and the Museo Civico di Sansepolcro lead the sights, with the Cattedrale di San Florido e Amanzio nearby. Six hours suits May, June or September.

gem:ligatne.text: Ligatne is a village in Latvia inside a national park of caves and old castles. Gutmanis Cave and Turaida Castle lead a visit, with Sigulda Medieval Castle further along the valley. June through August works best, in about three hours.

gem:zwaagdijk-west.text: Zwaagdijk-West is a village in the Netherlands near the shores of the IJsselmeer and Markermeer. The Zuiderzeemuseum and Oostereiland sit a short drive away in Hoorn. June through August is the season, in about four hours total.

gem:zafra.text: Zafra is a town in Spain built around the Palacio de los Duques de Feria. The Plaza Grande and Museo Santa Clara are close behind, with the Hospital de Santiago further out. May is the month to come, with about four hours enough time.

gem:konstantinovy-lazne.text: Konstantinovy Lazne is a spa village in Czechia surrounded by abbeys and ruined castles. Tepla Abbey and Kladruby Monastery lead a visit, with Gutstejn Castle nearby. June through September suits it best, in about three hours.

gem:sare.text: Sare, in France, carries the Les Plus Beaux Villages designation, set below La Rhune. The Grottes de Sare and Pheasant Island lead the sights, with the Bayonne Cathedral further afield. June through September works well, in about three hours.

gem:oisterwijk.text: Oisterwijk is a town in the Netherlands next to the Efteling. St John's Cathedral and Koningshoeven Abbey add historic sights nearby, close to Safaripark Beekse Bergen. Six hours suits May through September.

gem:castrogeriz.text: Castrogeriz is a small village in Spain also known locally as Castrojeriz. The Castle of Castrojeriz and the Iglesia de Nuestra Senora del Manzano anchor the center, with the San Anton monastery nearby. June through September suits it, in about three hours.

gem:blankenburg.text: Blankenburg is a town in Germany at the foot of the Brocken. Quedlinburg Abbey and Halberstadt Cathedral lead the sights nearby, with St Cyriakus, Grossvaterfelsen and Volkmarskeller rounding out the area. Six hours suits June through September well.

gem:kreuzau.text: Kreuzau is a village in Germany on the edge of the Hurtgen Forest. Burg Nideggen and Hill 400 draw most of the history, close to Hambach Forest. June through September is the season, in about four hours.

gem:veroia.text: Veroia is a town in Greece with layers of history packed close together. The Archaeological Museum of Veroia and the Old Metropolis lead a visit, with the Medrese Mosque, Mieza and Aigai a little further out. Six hours suits April, May or September best.

gem:bendorf.text: Bendorf is a town in Germany close to Koblenz and the Rhenish Massif. Koblenz itself holds the Deutsches Eck, Ehrenbreitstein Fortress, the Basilica of St Castor and the Electoral Palace. Six hours covers them all, best from May through September.

gem:begunje-na-gorenjskem.text: Begunje na Gorenjskem is a small village in Slovenia beside Lake Bled. Bled Castle and the Bled Gorge lead the sights, with Lesce nearby. May through August is the season, in about four hours, with Camping Bled for those who stay longer.

gem:ansouis.text: Ansouis holds the Les Plus Beaux Villages de France label for its castle and old streets. Mourre Negre and Silvacane Abbey lead the sights, worth about three hours, best kept to May, June or September with public transport poor.

gem:hervas.text: Hervas is a historic village in Spain, grouped as a Conjunto historico for its castle and artisan streets. The Monastery of Yuste and Sierra de Bejar head three hours of sights, best planned for May, June or September.

gem:belleme.text: Belleme is one of the Petites Cites de Caractere in France, its historic core anchored by a castle and cathedral. The Parc naturel regional du Perche and Basilique Notre-Dame de Montligeon take up three hours, best from June through September.

gem:frederikshavn.text: Frederikshavn is a coastal town in Denmark with a cathedral and Palm Beach nearby. Hirsholmene and Frederikshavn Church fill six hours of sights, best kept to July and August since public transport runs limited.

gem:bejar.text: Bejar earns its Conjunto historico status from a historic center wrapped around nature trails in Spain. Sierra de Bejar and the Plaza de toros de Bejar share four hours, best from May, June or September with good transport links.

gem:shipka.text: Shipka is a village in Bulgaria known for the Battle of Shipka Pass and the Thracian Tomb of Kazanlak nearby. Shipka Monastery adds up to three hours near Koprinka Reservoir, best in May, June or September.

gem:hollum.text: Hollum sits among the West Frisian Islands in the Netherlands, a beach and coast village with old art on show. Ameland Lighthouse and the Maritiem Centrum Abraham Fock take about three hours, best from June through August.

gem:corofin.text: Corofin borders The Burren in Ireland, a village built around a castle and cave country. Poulnabrone dolmen and O'Dea Castle bring the total to three hours, with Ennis Cathedral nearby, best from June through August.

gem:hohenems.text: Hohenems in Austria pairs a hilltop castle with the Jewish Museum of Hohenems in its old town. The Rolls-Royce-Museum and Hohe Kugel fit into six hours, best May through September, with Saint Nicholas church in nearby Feldkirch.

gem:tripoli.text: Tripoli in Greece sits below Mainalo, its cathedral town serving as gateway to Tegea. Mantineia and the Temple of Athena Alea need four hours in all, best in May, June or September near Lake Taka.

gem:joensuu.text: Joensuu is a city in Finland on Hoytiainen lake, its cathedral and coast framing the historic center. Botania and the Joensuu railway station stretch to eight hours, best from June through August.

gem:mikkeli.text: Mikkeli pairs Mikkeli Cathedral with the Savilahti Stone Sacristy in a corner of Finland. Suur-Savon Museo and Mikkelin Tuomiokirkko round out nine hours of sights, best planned for June, July or August.

gem:tata.text: Tata centers on Tata Castle above Lake Oreg in Hungary, a town that mixes art with old stone walls. Szelim cave and Vertesszolos claim five hours of the day, best from May, June or September.

gem:angelholm.text: Angelholm mixes beach and cathedral town life below Kullaberg in Sweden. The UFO-Memorial Angelholm and Barkakra kyrka occupy six hours, best from June through August, though public transport runs limited.

gem:neuchatel.text: Neuchatel sits on Lake Neuchatel in Switzerland, its old town built around the Collegiale de Neuchatel and Neuchatel Castle. The Musee d'Art et d'Histoire and nearby Creux du Van settle at six hours, best June through September.

gem:gytheio.text: Gytheio is a coastal village in Greece near Apidima Cave and Cranae, with about four thousand residents. Alepotrypa cave and Diros cave near Mount Arabikias call for two hours, best kept to April or May since public transport is poor.

gem:baia-mare.text: Baia Mare pairs the Assumption of Mary Cathedral with Stephen's Tower in Romania. The Synagogue in Baia Mare and the Ethnographic and Folk Art Museum warrant seven hours, best May through September.

gem:trnava.text: Trnava is a cathedral city in Slovakia with a well kept City Tower and the Church of Saint Anne nearby. The Synagogue in Trnava fills out eight hours, best from May through September, near the Kralova Reservoir.

gem:silistra.text: Silistra holds a spot on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List in Bulgaria, a town of nearly thirty thousand. Medzhidi Tabiya and Island Vetren cover four hours, with the Roman Tomb close by, best in May or September near Srebarna lake.

gem:rakovica.text: Rakovica borders Plitvice Lakes National Park in Croatia, a small village anchored by Cetin Castle. The Caves of Barac and Stari Grad top out at two hours, best from May through August.

gem:hollviken.text: Hollviken combines beach walks with the Foteviken Museum on the coast of Sweden. Skanors Ljung Nature Reserve and Maklappen come to six hours in total, best from June through August.

gem:tempio-pausania.text: Tempio Pausania holds a place among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, its old town scattered with ancient dolmen sites. Dolmen di Ladas and Nuraghe Majori take up six hours, best from May through August, with Lake Coghinas close by.

gem:argentan.text: Argentan carries the Les Plus Beaux Detours de France title for its abbey and old churches. Argentan Abbey and the Eglise Saint-Martin d'Argentan run to about five hours, best from June through September.

gem:poppi.text: Poppi is listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, its skyline held by Castello dei Conti Guidi. The Pieve di Santa Maria Assunta and Museo dell'Arte della Lana take four hours, best in May, June or September.

gem:agira.text: Agira sits among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, its hilltop marked by the Basilica di San Leone. Two hours covers the Greek Theare of Agyrion and the Agira Canadian War Cemetery, best kept to May.

gem:greccio.text: Greccio belongs to I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, its Santuario di Greccio set above Lago di Piediluco. San Pastore and the Ciclovia della Conca Reatina hold the visit to three hours, best in May or June.

gem:kastelruth.text: Kastelruth opens onto Seiser Alm and the Schlern-Rosengarten Nature Park, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Prosels Castle and Sabiona Monastery keep the visit to four hours, timed for June through September, near Karersee.

gem:villefranche-de-rouergue.text: Villefranche-de-Rouergue carries the Les Plus Beaux Detours de France title, its center built around the Chartreuse Saint-Sauveur. The Abbaye de Loc-Dieu and Eglise de Toulongergues leave room for five hours, best May through September.

gem:sellano.text: Sellano is one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, home to just over two hundred people and ringed by Monte Costara and Monte Puro. Santa Maria Annunziata and San Lorenzo make for two hours, best in May or June, though public transport is poor.

gem:polcenigo.text: Polcenigo is listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, its skyline set by Castello di Polcenigo. Castello di Caneva and the Chiesa di San Giorgio add up to three hours, timed for April, May, June or September, near Lago di Santa Croce.

gem:barfleur.text: Barfleur belongs to Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, its old streets watched over by the Phare de Gatteville. Chateau du Tourps and the Eglise Saint-Martin de Reville pace out to three hours, best from June through August.

gem:allerona.text: Allerona counts among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, watched over by Castello di Torre Alfina and Castello di Viscardo. Santa Maria Assunta and the Museo del Fiore take about two hours, best in May or June, in a village of under four hundred.

gem:montescudaio.text: Montescudaio is a historic village in Italy, centered on the Chiesa di Sant'Andrea. Add the Chiesa di San Giovanni Evangelista and the Oratorio della Madonna delle Grazie for three hours in all, best in May or June.

gem:framura.text: Framura is a historic village in Italy, close to the Baia del Silenzio. Mura di Levanto and Monte Moneglia stretch the visit to four hours, with June to August the best window, near spiaggia di Fegina.

gem:mittelbergheim.text: Mittelbergheim ranks among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, watched over by Chateau d'Andlau and Andlau Abbey. Chateau du Landsberg and Chateau de Dreistein claim four hours, best May through September.

gem:la-chatre.text: La Chatre carries the Les Plus Beaux Detours de France title, tied to the Domaine de George Sand. Chateau de Sarzay and the Chateau de Saint-Chartier fill out three hours, best June through September.

gem:citerna.text: Citerna is a historic village in Italy, anchored by Castello Bufalini and the Piazza Santa Chiara. Museo Civico and Museo Bufalini bring the total to four hours, best in May or June, near Lago di Montedoglio.

gem:mondolfo.text: Mondolfo is a historic village in Italy, close to the site of the Battle of the Metaurus. Santa Maria delle Grazie and the Museo della mezzadria fit into two hours, best June through August, near Spiaggia di Fano.

gem:saint-jean-d-angely.text: Saint-Jean-d'Angely carries the Les Plus Beaux Detours de France title around its Lanterne des morts. The Eglise Saint-Germain de Varaize and hotel de Hausen need three hours, best May through September.

gem:fiumalbo.text: Fiumalbo is a historic village in Italy beneath Monte Cimone. The Orto Botanico Forestale dell'Abetone and Chiesa di San Leopoldo cap the day at three hours, ideally between June and August.

gem:morro-d-alba.text: Morro d'Alba is a hill village in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, home to just over 1,500 people. The Biblioteca comunale Planettiana and Santuario Madonna della Rosa top three hours of sights. Transport is poor, so come in May or June by car.

gem:brugnato.text: Brugnato is a small historic village in Italy, named both I Borghi piu belli d'Italia and Bandiera Arancione. The Concattedrale and Museo Diocesano fill three hours, with Guvano beach close by. Transport is poor, best May through August.

gem:aieta.text: Aieta is a hillside village in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Castello di Castrocucco and Grotta di Marina di Maratea take about two hours to see. Transport is poor, so visit in May or June with a car.

gem:fornelli.text: Fornelli is a village in Italy, recognized as one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Abbazia di San Vincenzo al Volturno and Fontana Fraterna fill three hours between them. Transport is poor, though May or June suit it best.

gem:borgo-valbelluna.text: Borgo Valbelluna carries the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia designation. The Castello di Zumelle and Chiesa di Santa Giustina fill about three hours, with the lago del Mis nearby for a walk after. Transport is poor, best May through September.

gem:fasano.text: Fasano is a town in Italy, its sights led by the Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Egnazia and the Tempietto Seppannibale. The Punta Torre Canne lighthouse and Fasanolandia round out about four hours. May through August suit it best.

gem:ars-en-re.text: Ars-en-Re is a small harbor village in France, ranked among the Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Phare des Baleines and the eglise Saint-Etienne fill about three hours. Transport is poor, so come by car June through September.

gem:estaing.text: Estaing is a riverside village in France with 650 residents, one of the Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Chateau d'Estaing and Chapelle de l'Ouradou make a three-hour visit. Transport is poor, best May, June, July, or September.

gem:bonneval-sur-arc.text: Bonneval-sur-Arc is a mountain village in France carrying Plus Beaux Villages de France status. The Eglise Notre-Dame-de-l'Assomption anchors it, and the Col de l'Iseran climbs nearby toward Gran Paradiso. Transport is poor, best July or August.

gem:castelnau-de-montmiral.text: Castelnau-de-Montmiral is a hilltop village in France with fewer than 1,000 residents, one of the Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Porte des Garrics and Place Publique fill two hours. May through September suit it best.

gem:saint-benoit-du-sault.text: Saint-Benoit-du-Sault is a village in France, home to 770 people, listed among the Plus Beaux Villages de France. The Chateau de Brosse anchors two hours, with Plage de Chambon lake close by. Transport is poor, best June through September.

gem:sauveterre-de-rouergue.text: Sauveterre-de-Rouergue is a bastide village in France, a Plus Beaux Villages de France entry. The Porte des Anglais and Eglise Saint-Christophe lead a three-hour walk through the square and arcades. Transport is poor, best June through September.

gem:sarrant.text: Sarrant is a circular walled village in France, one of the Plus Beaux Villages de France, with just under 1,900 residents. The Eglise Saint-Orens de Maubec and Halle de Solomiac fill three hours. May, June, September, or October suit it best.

gem:vouvant.text: Vouvant is a fortified village in France, ranked among the Plus Beaux Villages de France. Notre-Dame-de-l'Assomption and the Chateau de la Citardiere sit above the Vieux pont de Vouvant. Transport is poor, best May through September.

gem:carennac.text: Carennac is a riverside village in France carrying Plus Beaux Villages de France status. The Chateau de la Johannie sits right in the village, while Padirac is a short trip out, three hours in all. May, June, July, or September suit it best.

gem:beaugency.text: Beaugency is a town in France, named among the Plus Beaux Detours de France. The Pont de Beaugency and eglise Notre-Dame lead three hours of sightseeing. Transport is good, best May through September.

gem:revel.text: Revel is a town in France with close to 8,700 residents, one of the Plus Beaux Detours de France. The Halle and Clocher Saint-Martin anchor five hours, with the Bassin de Saint-Ferreol nearby. Transport is good in May, June, or September.

gem:montreuil-bellay.text: Montreuil-Bellay is a town in France, named both a Plus Beaux Detours de France stop and a Petites Cites de Caractere. The Chateau de Montreuil-Bellay anchors a three-hour visit. Transport is good, best May through September.

gem:pont-audemer.text: Pont-Audemer is a canal town in France with close to 9,700 residents, one of the Plus Beaux Detours de France. The Eglise Saint-Ouen and the Immeuble de la cour Canel fill five hours. Transport is good June through September.

gem:sezanne.text: Sezanne is a town in France, one of the Petites Cites de Caractere. The Eglise Saint-Denis and the Monument national de la victoire de la Marne fill two hours between them. Good transport suits May through September.

gem:malmesbury.text: Malmesbury, a United Kingdom market town, grew up around Malmesbury Abbey. St Saviour's Church and the Market Cross fill three hours, and Tetbury makes an easy add-on. June through September is the season to pick, with transport running well.

gem:amersham.text: Amersham, a United Kingdom market town, is home to close to 22,000 people. Shardeloes and Chenies Manor lead the sights, with Milton's Cottage filling out about six hours. Transport runs well, and June through September suit a visit.

gem:wincanton.text: Wincanton, a United Kingdom market town, has about 5,400 residents. King Alfred's Tower and Cary Castle lead the way, with Gants Mill filling a four-hour visit. Good transport suits June through September.

gem:chipping-sodbury.text: Chipping Sodbury, a United Kingdom market town, is home to about 5,500 people. Badminton House and Dyrham Park sit nearby, with Dodington Park rounding out roughly three hours. Transport is good June through September.

gem:west-malling.text: West Malling, a United Kingdom market town, has about 2,300 residents. Allington Castle and the Chestnuts Long Barrow lead the way, with East Farleigh nearby, about four hours total. Good transport suits June through September.

gem:wrotham.text: Wrotham, a United Kingdom market town, has just under 1,900 residents. Knole House and Ightham Mote stand out nearby, with Otford Palace rounding out about four hours. Transport is good June through September.

gem:rothwell-gb.text: Rothwell, a United Kingdom market town, sits near enough to Leeds to borrow its sights. Temple Newsam House and the Leeds Corn Exchange lead the list, worth about six hours. June through August suit it best.

gem:ashton-under-lyne.text: Ashton-under-Lyne sits in the United Kingdom, its sights leaning on nearby Manchester. The O2 Apollo and Manchester Piccadilly anchor a visit worth about six hours. Transport is good June through August.

gem:todmorden.text: Todmorden sits in the United Kingdom with close to 11,700 residents. Todmorden Town Hall and Dobroyd Castle anchor the town, and neighboring Hebden Bridge rounds out a six-hour day. Good transport suits June through August.

gem:royal-wootton-bassett.text: Royal Wootton Bassett sits in the United Kingdom with about 11,300 residents. Lydiard Park and Bradenstoke Priory lead the way, with Ringsbury Camp filling a six-hour visit. Transport is good June through September.

gem:thornbury.text: Thornbury sits in the United Kingdom, built around Thornbury Castle, with about 11,700 residents. The Severn Bridge and Aust Cliff sit close by, worth roughly five hours. Transport is good June through September.

gem:chipping-ongar.text: Chipping Ongar sits in the United Kingdom with close to 4,000 residents. Ongar Castle and Blake Hall lead the sights, with Saint Andrew church rounding out three hours. Cheshunt Lake sits nearby, transport good June through September.

gem:broughton-in-furness.text: Broughton in Furness sits in the United Kingdom, ringed by Coniston Water and Windermere. Millom Castle anchors a three-hour visit, with Scafell Pike rising nearby. June through August suit it best.

gem:katwijk.text: Katwijk is a coastal village in the Netherlands. The Rijksmuseum van Oudheden and Leiden Observatory sit just inland, with Noordwijk adding about four hours. Kagerplassen lake is close by, with transport running well June through August.

gem:meppel.text: Meppel is a town in the Netherlands with close to 30,700 residents, built around the Grote Kerk of Mariakerk. De Wieker Meule windmill fills out about six hours, with Bovenwijde lake close by. Transport runs well from June through August.

ALC.text: Alicante is a port city in Spain on the Costa Blanca. Santa Barbara Castle and Lucentum lead the sights, with San Juan Playa for the coast, about seventeen hours in all. Transport is excellent, best April or May.

SDR.text: Santander is a coastal city in Spain, capital of Cantabria, with close to 174,000 residents. Centro Botin and Santander Cathedral anchor the center, with El Sardinero beach nearby, about ten hours total. Transport is excellent June through September.

FUE.text: Fuerteventura is an island in Spain, part of the Canary Islands south of Lanzarote. Betancuria and the Montana de Tindaya lead the sights, with the Castillo de Fuste filling out about five hours. Transport is limited, best May through October.

FSC.text: Figari sits in South Corsica, a coastal area of France. The Lavezzi Islands and Cavallo lie just offshore, with The Pink Beach filling about four hours on land. Transport is limited, best May through August.

AJA.text: Ajaccio is a port city in France, capital of Corsica, with about 54,000 residents. Maison Bonaparte and the Ajaccio Cathedral anchor the old town, with the Citadelle d'Ajaccio nearby, about nine hours total. Transport is limited, best May or June.

ZAG.text: Zagreb is the capital of Croatia, compact and built for walking. The Museum of Broken Relationships and Zagreb Cathedral top the bill, with Mirogoj Cemetery worth the stop. Transport is excellent, and seventeen hours across May and June cover it well.

gem:obidos.text: Obidos is a walled medieval town in Portugal. The Castle of Obidos anchors its hilltop streets, and Caldas da Rainha makes an easy side trip. Six hours in June, July or August covers it; transport there is poor, so a car helps.

gem:san-marino.text: San Marino is a tiny republic inside Italy, its capital perched on Monte Titano. The Three Towers, Guaita and the Basilica di San Marino make up the sightseeing. Three hours covers it, best done May through August.

gem:leuven.text: Leuven is a lively university city in Belgium. Leuven Town Hall and Museum M come first on the list, and Park Abbey rewards the extra walk beyond downtown. Transport is good, and ten hours from May to September takes in the rest.

gem:giethoorn.text: Giethoorn is a small canal village in the Netherlands, where boats replace cars. Weerribben-Wieden National Park borders it, with De Sterrenberg and Grote of Sint-Clemenskerk nearby. It takes about four hours in June, July or August, and transit in is easy.

gem:bardejov.text: Bardejov is a UNESCO listed medieval town in eastern Slovakia. The Basilica of St Giles is the main sight, and the spa quarter at Bardejovske Kupele makes a relaxed add-on. It takes five hours between May and September, with good transport.

gem:roskilde.text: Roskilde is an ancient city in Denmark, once a Viking age capital. Roskilde Cathedral and the Viking Ship Museum draw the most visitors, and Lejre Museum rewards a longer stop. Ten hours over June, July or August covers it, helped by good transport.

gem:kuldiga.text: Kuldiga is a small fairytale town in Latvia, built along the Venta Rapid. Kuldiga Castle and the vaulted bridge anchor a short walk, and Riezupe Sand Caves suit a half day. Transport is good, so five hours over June, July or August will do.

gem:orheiul-vechi.text: Orheiul Vechi is a remote monastery village in Moldova. Old Orhei and Orhei National Park top the sightseeing, and Trebujeni is close enough for the same day. Its transport is poor, so bring a car for about two hours in May, June or September.

gem:sandomierz.text: Sandomierz is a quiet medieval town in Poland above the Vistula. Sandomierz Cathedral and Sandomierz Castle come first, and the Town Hall anchors the square. Transport is good, with six hours over May through September enough.

gem:ptuj.text: Ptuj is a small wine town in eastern Slovenia. Ptuj Castle is the main sight, and Lake Ptuj offers an easy afternoon away from the old streets. Its transport there is poor, so plan on a car and five hours between May and September.

gem:sylt.text: Sylt is a narrow island off Germany, its western shore one long stretch of white beach. Westerland anchors the sights, and Lakolk Strand offers quieter sand nearby. It takes seven hours over June, July or August, though transport is limited.

gem:rudesheim.text: Rudesheim am Rhein is a wine town in Germany on the Rhine, across from Bingen. Niederwalddenkmal and Mouse Tower top the sightseeing, and Burg Rheinstein is a short trip upriver. Transport there is poor; plan a car and six hours over May through September.

gem:bregenz.text: Bregenz is a lake town in Austria facing Lake Constance. Kunsthaus Bregenz and the Vorarlberg Museum are the main sights, and a cable car up Pfander adds wider views. Transport is generally poor; plan a car and six hours over May through September.

gem:minerve-herault.text: Minerve is a tiny medieval village in France, perched above river gorges in the Herault. It ranks among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, near the Haut-Languedoc Regional Natural Park. A car is needed for three hours in May, June or September.

gem:cap-frehel.text: Cap Frehel is a wild stretch of coast in France, its cliffs dropping into the sea. Fort la Latte, Cezembre and the Ilot Saint-Michel are the main sights. Its transport is mostly poor, so three hours between June and September covers the headland by car.

gem:tinos.text: Tinos is an island in Greece near Mykonos, known for its pilgrimage church. Our Lady of Tinos draws the pilgrims, and Saint George's Cathedral and Exomvourgo round out a stay. Transport is limited; plan a car and about five hours between May and September.

gem:samothrace.text: Samothrace is a remote island in Greece, shaped by one mountain dropping into the sea. The Samothrace temple complex and the Archaeological Museum hold the main sights, with Fengari looming above. It takes four hours between June and August to see it.

gem:preveli.text: Preveli is a quiet beach area on Crete in Greece. Preveli Beach and Arkadi Monastery top the sightseeing, and Kournas makes a good lake detour inland. Transport is limited, so a car and about five hours between May, June or September will cover it.

gem:prespa-lakes.text: Prespa Lakes is a remote corner of Greece built around two lakes. Lake Prespa and the Monastery of Saint Naum lead the sights, with Baba Mountain rising over the water. Transport is poor, so bring a car for seven hours across May, June or September.

gem:famagusta.text: Famagusta is a walled port city in Northern Cyprus, its center built inside medieval fortifications. Lala Mustafa Pasha Mosque, Othello Castle and Palazzo del Provveditore lead the sightseeing. It takes four hours in April or May to see it.

gem:san-martino-di-castrozza.text: San Martino di Castrozza is a quiet alpine resort in Italy, ringed by peaks. Cimon della Pala, Cima della Vezzana and Pale di San Martino offer long summer hikes. Transport there is poor; plan a car and six hours between June and August.

gem:favignana.text: Favignana, the biggest of the Aegadian Islands, sits a short ferry ride from Trapani off Sicily. Levanzo and Marettimo lie within sight across the water, and the Stagnone Lagoon lies to the north. It takes about four hours between May and July to see it.

gem:chia.text: Chia is a family beach area on the coast of Italy, backed by dunes. Spiaggia di Chia, Spiaggia di Sa Colonia, Nora and Bithia make for a short drive along the coast. Transport is limited; five hours across April, May, June or September should cover it.

gem:vesteralen-andenes.text: Vesteralen is a remote group of islands off Norway, wild and thinly settled. Andenes kirke and Andenes fyr anchor the main village, and Bleiksoya rises just offshore. Transport is limited, so around four hours in July or August is what most need.

gem:high-coast.text: High Coast is a UNESCO listed coastline in Sweden, still rising from the last Ice Age. Skuleskogen National Park, Skuleberget, Hogbonden and Mjalton lead the sightseeing. Transport is poor; five hours in July fits the short season.

gem:lund.text: Lund is a compact university city in Sweden, close enough to Malmo for a half day. Lund Observatory and Lunds domkyrka top the sightseeing, and Kulturen fits into the same day. Transport is good, so ten hours over June, July or August covers the city.

gem:bieszczady.text: Bieszczady Mountains form a wild, thinly populated corner of Poland, prized for ridge walks. Poloniny National Park, Lake Solina and Lopienka anchor the routes. Transport is poor; six hours between June and August suit the trails.

gem:ksiaz-castle.text: Ksiaz Castle rises above wooded hills near Swidnica in Poland. Ksiaz itself is the main sight, and the Peace Church in Swidnica and Cisy Castle are close enough to add on. Transport is good, with six hours over June through September enough.

gem:ojcow.text: Ojcow National Park is a small park in Poland, tucked into the Polish Jura. Pieskowa Skala, Maczuga Herkulesa, Zamek Korzkiew and Sigismund's Chapel lead the sightseeing. Transport is poor; plan a car for the seven hours needed between May and September.

gem:conimbriga.text: Conimbriga is a Roman era site near Coimbra, Portugal. Old Cathedral of Coimbra, the Monastery of Santa Cruz and Biblioteca Joanina lead the sightseeing nearby. Transport is poor; four hours between May and August covers the ruins.

gem:graciosa-azores.text: Graciosa is a small island in the Azores, part of Portugal and a UNESCO biosphere reserve. Caldeira da Graciosa, Ponta da Barca Lighthouse and Carapacho Lighthouse lead the sightseeing. Transport is limited; five hours in July or August is typical.

gem:mertola.text: Mertola is a small hilltop village in Portugal above the Guadiana Valley. Castle of Mertola, the Church of Nossa Senhora da Anunciacao and Pulo do Lobo lead the sightseeing. Transport is poor; a car and about two hours in April or May are enough.

gem:camara-de-lobos.text: Camara de Lobos is a small fishing town on Madeira Island in Portugal. Pico Ruivo and Pico do Areeiro dominate the skyline, and the Cathedral of Funchal is a short trip along the coast. Transport is poor; six hours between July and September cover the area.

gem:trigrad.text: Trigrad Gorge cuts through the Rhodope Mountains in Bulgaria, a canyon known for its caves. Uhlovitsa Cave, Yagodinska cave and Buynovsko Gorge combine easily in one trip. Transport is poor; five hours between June and September is enough.

gem:consuegra.text: Consuegra is a historic town in central Spain, its ridge lined with windmills. Molinos de Consuegra, the Castle of la Muela and the Church of Santa Maria la Mayor are the main sights. Transport is poor; four hours in May or September should be enough.

gem:lindisfarne.text: Lindisfarne is a quiet island off Northumberland in the United Kingdom. Lindisfarne Priory, Lindisfarne Castle, Bamburgh Castle and Dunstanburgh Castle line the shore. Transport is limited; six hours between June and August is enough.

gem:barafundle-bay.text: Barafundle Bay is a quiet beach in the Pembrokeshire Coast National Park, United Kingdom. Pembroke Castle, St Govan's Chapel, Manorbier Castle and Caldey Island line the coast nearby. Transport is limited; seven hours between June and September is typical.

gem:anglesey.text: Anglesey is an island in the United Kingdom, a UNESCO Global Geopark. Caernarfon Castle and Britannia Bridge link it to the mainland, with Holy Island and South Stack along the coast. Transport is limited; seven hours in June through August is typical.

gem:blue-eye-saranda.text: Blue Eye is a natural landmark in Albania, near the Port of Sarande. Gjirokaster Fortress, Lake Butrint and the Xhemahalle complex round out the sightseeing. Transport is limited; about three hours in May or June is enough.

gem:osum-canyon.text: Osum Canyon is a remote village in Albania built for hiking and canyon adventure. Pirogoshi Cave and Ostrovice lead two hours of sights, with Mount Trebeshine close by. Transport is poor, so visit in May, June or September with a car.

gem:djavolja-varos.text: Davolja Varos is a quiet natural area in Serbia on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List, centered on Devil's Town. Prolom and Batllava Lake round out four hours, best done May through September.

gem:penrith.text: Penrith is a market town in Cumbria at the edge of the Lake District. Brougham Castle and Penrith Castle fill about six hours, with Ullswater and Helvellyn close by. June through August suits it best.

gem:taunton.text: Taunton is a market town and cathedral city in Somerset, United Kingdom. Taunton Castle, Hestercombe Gardens and the Museum of Somerset lead about ten hours of sights. Dunkery Hill sits nearby, best kept to June through September.

gem:stara-zagora.text: Stara Zagora sits in Bulgaria, known for cathedral architecture and the Neolithic Dwellings Museum. Liliev house and Bunardzhievi House add texture to an eight hour visit. Buzludzha is a nearby side trip, best April, May, June, September or October.

gem:ostersund.text: Ostersund sits on Storsjon in Sweden, part of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. Jamtli and the Froso Runestone lead six hours of sights, with Ostersund Central Station a short walk from the lake. June and July are the months to visit.

gem:llandudno.text: Llandudno is a seaside town on the coast of Wales, built up in Victorian times. Great Orme and Conwy Castle top six hours, with Conwy Morfa beach and Carnedd Llewelyn close by. Transport is limited, so bring a car June through August.

gem:bobbio.text: Bobbio is a small village in Italy, one of the I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Bobbio Abbey and Ponte Gobbo need about three hours, with Monte Penice and Monte Lesima rising nearby. Its poor transport favors May, June or September by car.

gem:burnley.text: Burnley is a market town in Lancashire with nine hours worth of sights, from Turf Moor to Pendle Hill. Gawthorpe Hall and the Queen Street Mill Textile Museum add industrial history. June, July and August work best.

gem:monmouth.text: Monmouth is a historic town centered on its castle and the old Monnow Bridge. Drybridge House and the Forest of Dean add a further stop, filling about six hours. Good transport makes June through September easy.

gem:dorchester.text: Dorchester is a market town in Dorset with ties to Roman Britain and to Thomas Hardy. Maiden Castle and the Cerne Abbas Giant anchor about six hours, and Thomas Hardy's Cottage adds a stop. Best kept to June through September.

gem:warwick.text: Warwick is a historic town known above all for Warwick Castle, with Kenilworth Castle and Charlecote Park nearby. Coventry Cathedral and the Royal Shakespeare Theatre round out about six hours. June through September works best.

gem:perth.text: Perth is a cathedral town centered on Scone Palace, with Elcho Castle and Methven Castle nearby. St Ninian's Cathedral and McDiarmid Park round out about six hours. June through August suits it, with good transport.

gem:rovereto.text: Rovereto sits between Trentino and Veneto in Italy, a fortress town turned home to modern art. The Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art of Trento and Rovereto anchors about six hours. Monte Stivo and Monte Bondone suit May through September.

gem:de-panne.text: De Panne is a beach town on the coast of Belgium in West Flanders. Plopsaland Belgium and the Abbey of the Dunes lead six hours of sights, with Malo-les-Bains close by. Transport is limited, so plan June through August by car.

gem:paderborn.text: Paderborn is a cathedral city set in North Rhine-Westphalia, with ten hours worth of sights to fill. Paderborn Cathedral and Schloss Neuhaus lead, and the Historisches Rathaus fills out a long day. June through September is easiest.

gem:bedford.text: Bedford is a market town and administrative center for Bedfordshire, in eastern England. St Paul's and St Peter's Church anchor about ten hours of sights. Willington Stables and Willington Dovecote sit a short trip out, best June through September.

gem:vasteras.text: Vasteras sits in central Sweden, a city with ten hours worth of sights but few tourists chasing them. Vasteras Cathedral and Anundshog lead, with Arosvallen filling out the day. June through August is the season.

gem:st-austell.text: Par Beach and the china-clay works sit alongside St Austell, a South Cornwall town built around the Eden Project. The Lost Gardens of Heligan and Restormel Castle round out about five hours. Transport is limited, best June through September by car.

gem:carucedo.text: Carucedo is a small village in Spain, gateway to the red cliffs of Las Medulas. Castillo de Cornatel and Ponferrada Castle add stops within its two hour circuit. Its transport is poor, best May, June or September by car.

gem:stony-stratford.text: Stony Stratford is a market town with Milton Keynes as its larger neighbor next door. The Concrete Cows and National Bowl sit in Milton Keynes nearby, with Waddesdon Manor further out. Its seven hours combined suit June through September.

gem:balatonfured.text: Balatonfured is a lakeside town on Lake Balaton in Hungary, built for slow afternoons on the water. Tihany Abbey and the Balaton Uplands National Park lead a five hour visit. Transport is limited, best May, June or September by car.

gem:roissy-en-france.text: Roissy-en-France is a small village in France with four hours of its own sights and much more nearby. The Pantheon, ile de la Cite and Luxembourg Palace sit an easy trip away. Transport is poor locally, best May through September by car.
