gem:milnthorpe.text: Milnthorpe is a market town in the United Kingdom near Windermere. Sizergh Castle and Levens Hall take up about four hours of touring, and Arnside Tower with St Mark's Church round things out, June through August is the season.

gem:katerini.text: Katerini is a city in Greece near Mount Olympus. The Saint Mary Kondariotissa Church and the Folklore Museum of Katerini top a six hour list, and Olympiaki Akti gives it a stretch of water too. April and May lead the calendar, with good transport.

gem:molsheim.text: Molsheim is a historic town in France, home to the Chartreuse de Molsheim. Chateau d'Osthoffen and the Jesuit Church fill much of a six hour visit, with Eglise Saint-Etienne de Rosheim nearby and Lac du Baggersee for after, May through September.

gem:martina-franca.text: Martina Franca is a town in Italy known for its old center. The Castello medievale and Chiesa Santa Maria Assunta head the list, with Chiesa San Giuseppe close behind, about four hours in total, best in May or June.

ZAZ.text: Zaragoza is a historic city in Spain on the Ebro, holding UNESCO World Heritage status. The Basilica of Our Lady of the Pillar and the Aljaferia fill seventeen hours of sightseeing, best across the shoulder months of April, May, September and October.

TPS.text: Trapani is a coastal city in Italy. Trapani Cathedral and Monte Erice make up most of nine hours of sightseeing, and Playa San Vito Lo Capo lies close by for the beach, though public transport is limited, so May to July is the safer window.

PNL.text: Pantelleria is a remote island in Italy, protected in part as a national park. The Pantelleria National Park and Castello de Pantelleria fill about four hours, with Lago di Venere close by for a quieter stop, June to August, transport limited.

FDH.text: Friedrichshafen is a lakeside city in Germany on Lake Constance, known for its aviation history. The Dornier Museum Friedrichshafen and the Zeppelin Museum anchor about ten hours of sightseeing, with Pfander rising nearby, May through September.

NTE.text: Nantes is a city in France with strong ties to Brittany. The Chateau des ducs de Bretagne and Nantes Cathedral take up much of a full day, seventeen hours worth of sightseeing, with the Theatre Graslin close behind, May through September.

MAN.text: Manchester is a large city in the United Kingdom, known for music and nightlife as much as its past. Manchester Cathedral and the John Rylands Library run to about seventeen hours of sights, with the Etihad Stadium adding more. June to August is best.

NWI.text: Norwich is a city in the United Kingdom, unusual for having two cathedrals within reach. Norwich Cathedral and St John the Baptist Cathedral lead about ten hours of touring, with Norwich Castle Museum close behind, June through September.

KLU.text: Klagenfurt is a lakeside city in Austria, framed by the Alps with the Worthersee and Lake Ossiach close by. The Museum Moderner Kunst Karnten and the Stadttheater Klagenfurt fill about ten hours, best from May to August.

GOT.text: Gothenburg is a coastal city in Sweden with a strong food scene. Liseberg and the Gothenburg Cathedral stand out among about seventeen hours of touring, and the Museum of World Culture sits nearby, across June, July and August.

TRD.text: Trondheim is an old cathedral city in Norway. Nidaros Cathedral alone is worth much of its ten hours of sights, and the Trampe bicycle lift with Munkholmen offer something different, best in July or August.

KUN.text: Kaunas is a city in Lithuania holding UNESCO recognition for its heritage. Kaunas Castle and the M K Ciurlionis National Art Museum come to about ten hours of sightseeing, with Pazaislis Monastery further out, May through August.

IOM.text: The Isle of Man is a quiet island in the United Kingdom, with about seven hours of sights led by Tynwald and Snaefell. The Calf of Man and South Barrule add a wilder stop, though public transport is limited across June to September.

INV.text: Inverness is a city in Scotland, gateway to the Highlands. Inverness Castle and Culloden Battlefield make up most of six hours of touring, and Inverness Cathedral with Eden Court sit nearby, June through August is the season.

gem:budva.text: Budva is a coastal resort town in Montenegro, with Sveti Stefan just along the shore. Jaz Beach and Kotor Cathedral fill out about five hours, and Lovcen rises inland for a change of scene, best in May or June.

gem:monaco-mc.text: Monaco is a tiny wealthy city-state on the coast. Monaco-Ville and the Prince's Palace of Monaco add up to six hours between them, with the Rock of Monaco close behind, best kept to June, July and August.

gem:kilkenny.text: Kilkenny is a medieval town in Ireland, its old streets founded by the Normans. Kilkenny Castle and Saint Canice's Cathedral cover most of five hours, with Rothe House close by, at its best June to August.

gem:melk.text: Melk is a small town in Austria on the Danube, anchored by its baroque abbey. Melk Abbey and Artstetten Castle make for about three hours, with Aggstein Castle a bit further out, best April through September.

gem:balaton.text: Tihany is a quiet village on Lake Balaton in Hungary, known for its abbey and thermal appeal. Tihany Abbey and the Balaton Uplands National Park take about six hours to see, with Balatonfured nearby, best May, June or September.

gem:himara.text: Himara is a coastal village in Albania on the Albanian Riviera, backed by the Ceraunian Mountains. Porto Palermo Castle and Llogara National Park fill about two hours, and Palasa Beach sits nearby, best in May or June.

gem:vlkolinec.text: Vlkolinec is a UNESCO listed mountain village in Slovakia. Velka Fatra National Park and Hrad Likava run to about six hours, and the Choc Mountains with Liptovska Mara round things out, across June, July and August.

gem:setenil-de-las-bodegas.text: Setenil de las Bodegas is a village in Andalusia, Spain. Puente Nuevo and the Castillo de Olvera add up to about two hours between them, with Cueva de la Pileta further afield, and May is the only real window.

gem:esch-sur-sure.text: Esch-sur-Sure is a small castle village in Luxembourg, ringed by the Upper Sure Natural Park. Esch-sur-Sure Castle and Berg Castle make for about four hours, with the Upper Sure Lake close by for the water, June through September.

gem:klaipeda.text: Klaipeda is a coastal city in Lithuania, gateway to the Curonian Spit. Klaipeda Castle and Klaipeda Lighthouse take up about nine hours, and Pilsotas sits nearby for more history, June through August is the season.

gem:naantali.text: Naantali is a quiet coastal town in Finland, best known for Moomin World. Kultaranta and Nadendal Abbey account for its own five hours, with Turku Cathedral and Turku Castle a short trip away, best in July and August.

gem:viljandi.text: Viljandi is a hilly town in Estonia. Viljandi Castle and Lake Viljandi come to about six hours, and the Raudna Nature Reserve with Sinialliku sit further out, best kept to June, July and August.

gem:ios.text: Ios is an island in Greece, part of the Cyclades group near Santorini. The Chora of Ios and Panagia Gremniotissa take up about five hours, and Skarkos adds older ruins nearby, June through September.

gem:bourtange.text: Bourtange is a fortified village in the Netherlands. Bourtange Fortress and the Kerk van Bourtange amount to about three hours, and Vestingmolen Bourtange with the Kusten Canal sit nearby, at its best June to August.

gem:svendborg.text: Svendborg is a coastal town in Denmark on Funen, with Langeland and Tasinge close by as island stops. Egeskov Castle and Valdemars Slot span about seven hours, with Thuro Church nearby too, across June, July and August.

gem:domburg.text: Domburg is a beach village on the Zeeland coast in the Netherlands, known for spa and family stays. Walcheren, Veerse Meer and Neeltje Jans top the sights, four hours worth in all, with public transport limited outside June to August.

gem:marken.text: Marken is a quiet historic fishing village on a former IJsselmeer peninsula in North Holland, still reached by a causeway. The Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum and Concertgebouw sit nearby in Amsterdam, three hours combined, best June through August.

gem:heusden.text: Heusden is a fortified historic village in the Netherlands with good public transport, best explored May through September. Efteling and Kamp Vught head the sight list, plus De Loonse en Drunense Duinen woodland, roughly four hours in town.

gem:fano.text: Fano is a quiet island area in Denmark, close to beach villages. Esbjerg and Wadden Sea National Park head the sights, seven hours in total, best in July or August with Blavandshuk and Lakolk Strand beaches nearby.

gem:klitmoller.text: Klitmoller is a surf town in Denmark, built around beach days and adventure. Thy National Park and Hanstholm Lighthouse lead the sights, about five hours together, best from June to August since transport away from town runs poor.

gem:silkeborg.text: Silkeborg is a lakeside town in Jutland, Denmark, grown up around hiking trails and water. Museum Silkeborg, Museum Jorn and Himmelbjerget hill fill about six hours, best tackled June through August, with Bolling lake close by after.

gem:ceske-budejovice.text: Ceske Budejovice, also called Budweis, is a historic food city in South Bohemia, Czechia. Hluboka Castle and the Cathedral of St Nicholas lead a full day of sights, about ten hours, with good transport making May through September easy to visit.

gem:lillafured.text: Lillafured is a small spa town in Northern Hungary, near Miskolc, built for lake walks and romance. Bukk forest, the Castle of Diosgyor and Cave Bath fill about six hours, best from May to September when the poor transport matters less.

gem:goriska-brda.text: Goriska Brda is a wine village in Slovenia, its hills threaded with vineyards around Capriva, Medana and Kozana. The sights take about four hours, best fit into May or June before summer, though transport into the hills stays poor.

gem:rakotzbrucke.text: Rakotzbrucke is a quiet countryside village in Germany built around its arched bridge and the Rhododendron Park Kromlau nearby. Muskau Park and Barwalder See round out about three hours, best May through September, with poor transport making a car useful.

gem:lunersee.text: Lunersee is a high alpine lake area in Austria for quiet hiking above the Brandnertal. Schesaplana mountain anchors the views, seven hours worth, with Vaduz Castle and Vaduz Cathedral nearby, best June through August though transport stays poor.

gem:stoos.text: Stoos is an alpine family village in Switzerland near Schwyz. Rigi and Brunnen lead the sights, close to four hours in all, best from June to August, with Urnersee and Agerisee lakes close by though transport stays poor.

gem:verbier.text: Verbier is a ski resort village in Valais, Switzerland, backed by Mont Fort and the Grand Combin peaks. Saillon and Sembrancher add three hours nearby, with Lac de Mauvoisin close by, June through August the recommended window, transport still poor.

gem:triberg.text: Triberg is a family mountain village in the Black Forest of Germany, known for its waterfalls. Triberg Waterfalls and nearby Schonach im Schwarzwald fill about three hours, best from June to August, though transport around Triberg stays poor.

gem:nordlingen.text: Nordlingen is a medieval walled town in Swabia, Bavaria, sitting inside an old meteorite crater. Few towns in Germany keep such a complete circuit of walls, and Neresheim Abbey plus Ipf extend the sightseeing past five hours, best from June to September.

gem:hall-in-tirol.text: Hall in Tirol is a medieval town near Innsbruck in Tyrol, Austria, on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List. Ambras Castle leads its own sights, with the Golden Roof and Innsbruck Cathedral a short trip away, five hours combined, best May to September.

gem:cahors.text: Cahors is a medieval wine town in the Lot department of France. Cahors Cathedral and the fortified Pont Valentre lead about six hours of sights, with Chateau de Mercues nearby for a wine detour, best from May to September despite poor transport.

gem:concarneau.text: Concarneau is a fortified coastal town in Brittany, France, built for family visits along the water. Chateau de Keriolet and Fort du Cabellou anchor about six hours of sights, best June through September, though transport beyond town stays limited.

gem:marais-poitevin.text: Marais Poitevin is a quiet wetland area in France, good for countryside family days out. Maillezais Cathedral and the Croix hosanniere de Maillezais lead about five hours of sights, best from May to September, with transport into the marsh poor.

gem:lake-kerkini.text: Lake Kerkini is a wilderness lake area in Greece, kept quiet along its water year round. Belasica ridge and Smolare Falls fill roughly four hours, best kept to April, May or October since transport into the area stays poor.

gem:gavdos.text: Gavdos is a remote wilderness island in Greece with only thirty seven residents. Korfos and Potamos beaches anchor four hours of sights in all, best from May to September, with transport to the island limited outside that window.

gem:lake-plastiras.text: Lake Plastiras is a quiet mountain lake area in Greece, held back by the Plastiras Dam. Porta Panagia and the Portaikos Bridge round out four hours nearby, best May, June or September, with Meteora among the mountains close by, transport still poor.

gem:kastellorizo.text: Kastellorizo is a remote island in the Dodecanese, Greece, prized for its quiet coast. The Blue Cave and the Uluburun shipwreck site lead some four hours of sights, best from May to September, with transport to the island still limited.

gem:loutro.text: Loutro is a remote coastal village in Greece where public transport stays poor. Samaria Gorge and Frangokastello fill about two hours nearby, best kept to May or June, with the Lefka Ori peaks rising behind.

gem:elafonisos-simos.text: Elafonisos is a quiet beach island in Greece, near Pavlopetri and Kythira. The Church of Agia Sofia and Monemvasia Mosque round out about four hours of sights, best from May to September, with Sarakiniko Beach a short walk from town.

gem:vatheia-mani.text: Vatheia is a remote historic area in Greece named alongside the village of Vathia nearby. Diros cave and Alepotrypa cave lead about four hours underground, best in May, June, July or September, since transport in the region runs poor.

gem:nafpaktos.text: Nafpaktos is a castle town on the Gulf of Corinth in Greece, its harbor framed by the old Rio Castle above. Fethiye Mosque and the Rio-Antirrio bridge round out about four hours, best kept to April or May since transport stays limited beyond then.

gem:frasassi-caves.text: Frasassi Caves is an underground karst system in Italy, near Genga in the Marche area, built for family adventure. Grotta di Frasassi and the Monastery of Fonte Avellana fill about six hours, best in May or June, with transport in the area still poor.

gem:dolceacqua.text: Dolceacqua is a medieval wine village in Italy, quiet enough for a romantic stop between vineyards. Monaco-Ville and the Prince's Palace of Monaco make a nearby day trip, about four hours combined, best in May, June or September given poor transport.

gem:oland.text: Oland is an island area in Sweden, second largest in the country and linked to Kalmar by a bridge. Kalmar Castle and Borgholm Castle head about seven hours of sights, best June through August, though transport across the island stays limited.

gem:koster-islands.text: Koster Islands is a quiet coastal area in Sweden built around Kosterhavets nationalpark and the water around it. Ytre Hvaler National Park and Homlungen Lighthouse extend the sights past five hours, best June through August despite limited transport out.

gem:faro-gotland.text: Faro is a remote beach island in Sweden, anchored by the sights at Langhammars. Faro Church and Faro lighthouse round out about six hours, best kept to July or August, with Sudersand and Sigsarve strand beaches part of the day.

gem:sigtuna.text: Sigtuna is a quiet historic lake town in Sweden, ringed by castles like Skokloster Castle and Steninge Palace. Rosersbergs slott and the Nasby Runestone extend the sights past six hours, best June through August, with transport around town still poor.

gem:oulanka.text: Oulanka National Park is a wilderness hiking area in Finland, with trails near Ala-Kitka and Kiutakongas. Rukatunturi mountain rises close by, and about four hours of sights are best saved for July since transport into the park runs poor.

gem:seydisfjordur.text: Seydisfjordur is a remote art village on the coast of East Iceland, reached past Fardagafoss and Gufufoss. The Technical Museum of East Iceland rounds out about two hours, best June through August, with onward transport still poor.

gem:suduroy.text: Suduroy is a remote hiking island in the Faroe Islands. Beinisvord and Gluggarnir lead toward Litla Dimun and Stora Dimun, about six hours of sights, best June through August despite limited transport.

gem:ogrodzieniec.text: Ogrodzieniec Castle is a medieval countryside village in Poland, named for its own castle. Zamek Ogrodzieniec and Bobolice Castle anchor about three hours, best June through August, with the Bledow Desert a short, unusual detour despite poor transport.

gem:silves.text: Silves is a castle town in the Algarve, Portugal. The Castle of Silves and Praia da Marinha beach fill about five hours, best from May to September, with Foia mountain close by despite poor transport.

gem:cacela-velha.text: Cacela Velha is a quiet coastal village in Portugal, its fort overlooking the Ria Formosa Nature Park. Forte do Rato and Praia Verde beach round out about three hours, best from May to September, though transport out of the village stays poor.

gem:lousa.text: Lousa is a hiking town in the mountains of Portugal, its fairytale reputation built around Serra da Lousa. Castelo de Arouce and the Palacio dos Salazares fill about five hours, best in May or June, since transport through the hills stays poor.

gem:santa-maria-azores.text: Santa Maria is a quiet diving island in the Azores, part of Portugal. Barreiro da Faneca and Pico Alto top the sights, six hours in all. June to August bring the calmest seas, and buses run only rarely.

gem:soldeu.text: Soldeu is a small ski village high in the mountains of Andorra. The Andorra National Library and Our Lady of Meritxell head the visit, four hours total. July and August are quietest, since there is no real bus service.

gem:central-balkan.text: Central Balkan is a national park village deep in the mountains of Bulgaria. Vezhen and Sashtinska Sredna Gora dominate the wilderness, though two hours covers the main trails. June through August gives the clearest paths, and a car helps more than buses.

gem:ruse.text: Ruse is a baroque riverside city along the Danube in Bulgaria, near the crossing into Romania. The Sexaginta Prista and Danube Bridge open the visit, about nine hours in all. April, May, June, or September suit it best, and the trains here run smoothly.

gem:luarca.text: Luarca is a quiet coastal village in Spain, its houses stepped above the sea. The Faro de Luarca lighthouse leads the visit, about three hours around the village. June through September works best, though buses come only a few times a day.

gem:symonds-yat.text: Symonds Yat is a river gorge and countryside area in the United Kingdom, within the Wye Valley National Landscape. Goodrich Castle and Monmouth Castle top the sights, seven hours of walking. June through September suits the trails best.

gem:downpatrick-head.text: Downpatrick Head is a remote stretch of coast in Ireland, known for its cliffs. Ceide Fields and Bartragh Island head the visit, about four hours in all. June through September brings calmer weather, with Slieve League within reach for longer days.

gem:falmouth.text: Falmouth is a harbour town on the coast of the United Kingdom, known for its food scene. Pendennis Castle and St Mawes Castle guard the harbour mouth, six hours in all. June through September is when to come, though outlying buses run thin.

gem:newquay.text: Newquay is a beach and surf town on the coast of the United Kingdom, popular with families. Bedruthan Steps and Fistral Beach anchor the visit, filling about five hours. June through September brings the warmest water and busiest waves.

gem:dartmouth-devon.text: Dartmouth is a small, romantic harbour town in the United Kingdom, facing Kingswear across the water. Dartmouth Castle and Kingswear Castle guard the river mouth, four hours in total. June through August is prime time, though buses run rarely.

gem:lynmouth-exmoor.text: Lynton and Lynmouth are twin villages on the coast of the United Kingdom, close by Exmoor National Park. Wind Hill and Hollerday Hill rise above the harbour, an easy three hours on foot. June through August suits the coastal walks best.

gem:winchester.text: Winchester is a medieval cathedral city in the United Kingdom. Winchester Cathedral and Winchester Castle anchor the sights, six hours in all. June through September draws the crowds, and trains make it an easy day trip.

gem:isle-of-wight.text: Isle of Wight is a family beach island off the coast of the United Kingdom. Osborne House opens the visit, with Calshot Castle and Calshot Beach close together, seven hours in all. June through September is the busiest stretch, though buses run thin.

gem:beara-peninsula.text: Beara Peninsula is a remote finger of coast and countryside in Ireland. Hungry Hill and the Caha Mountains dominate the drive, about four hours without rushing. June through August is the calmest window, and a car is close to essential out here.

gem:trakoscan.text: Trakoscan Castle is a fairytale lakeside castle in Croatia. Veliki Tabor Castle and the Museum of Neandertals in Krapina pair well nearby, four hours between them. May through September suits it best, though a car matters more than any timetable.

gem:mali-losinj.text: Mali Losinj is a quiet island town on Losinj island in Croatia. The Croatian Apoxyomenos headlines the visit, with day trips out to Susak, about four hours in town. June through August is the season, though ferries keep their own schedule.

gem:krk-baska.text: Krk is a beach town on the island of the same name off Croatia. Krk Cathedral and Krk Bridge anchor the old town, with Paradise Beach close by, five hours for both. May through August draws the crowds, and a car covers the island better.

gem:omis.text: Omis is a small coastal town on the Adriatic in Croatia, known for adventure sports. Klis Fortress and Diocletian's Palace lie within reach nearby, though two hours covers Omis itself. May, June, and September suit it best, since buses run rarely.

gem:travnik.text: Travnik is a fortress town in Bosnia and Herzegovina, set below Vlasic. Travnik Castle and the Mosque Sulejmanija lead the visit, five hours total. May, June, and July are the best months, and buses connect it easily to nearby towns.

gem:hexham.text: Hexham is a market town in the United Kingdom, built around its cathedral and abbey. Hexham Abbey and Hadrian's Wall top the sights, about six hours to see them. June through August is the season, with trains making it a simple base for day trips.

gem:ledbury.text: Ledbury is a small market town in Herefordshire, in the west of England. Eastnor Castle and the Malvern Hills lead the visit, about six hours between them. June through September brings the best weather, and buses here run reliably.

gem:midhurst.text: Midhurst is a small market town set in West Sussex, in the United Kingdom. Arundel Castle and Chichester Cathedral head the sights, three hours around town. June through September suits it best, though a car is worth arranging in advance.

gem:solothurn.text: Solothurn is a baroque town on the River Aare in Switzerland. The Kunstmuseum Solothurn anchors the visit, with Weissenstein just outside town, six hours for both. June through September works well, and the rail connections could hardly be easier.

gem:bewdley.text: Bewdley is a small market town on the River Severn in Worcestershire, near Kidderminster. Bewdley Bridge leads the sights, a design of Thomas Telford, six hours total. June through August is prime time, and getting here by bus or train is straightforward.

gem:ruddington.text: Ruddington is a quiet historic village in the United Kingdom, close to Nottingham. Newstead Abbey and Attenborough Nature Reserve lie within reach nearby, about four hours together. June through September suits it best, though buses here are rare.

gem:kempten-allgau.text: Kempten is a cathedral city in Bavaria, on the Iller below the Allgau Alps. St Lorenz Basilica and Kempten Abbey anchor the old town, ten hours in all. June through August works well, with trains linking it easily to the surrounding valleys.

gem:peterborough.text: Peterborough is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, in the United Kingdom. Peterborough Cathedral opens the visit, with Flag Fen further out, about nine hours in all. June through September is the season, and trains reach it easily.

gem:narni.text: Narni is a hill town in Umbria, in Italy. San Francesco and the Ponte d'Augusto lead the visit, three hours around the old town. April, May, and September are quietest, since buses to the hill town run infrequently.

gem:choustnikovo-hradiste.text: Choustnikovo Hradiste is a small village in Czechia, on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List. Kuks Hospital and the Church of Holy Trinity lead the visit, four hours between them. May through September suits it best, though buses here run only rarely.

gem:vic.text: Vic is a cathedral town in Spain. Vic Cathedral and the Roman temple of Vic lead the visit, six hours between them. May, June, and September are best, with good rail service into the town.

gem:kaysersberg.text: Kaysersberg is a castle village in Alsace, in France. Chateau de Kaysersberg leads the sights, with Hohlandsbourg further into the hills, about four hours together. May through September suits it best, though buses here run only rarely.

gem:bran.text: Bran is a tiny castle village in Transylvania, in Romania. Bran Castle guards the old pass and leads the visit by far, two hours for the castle itself. June through August is busiest, since buses run only a few times a day.

gem:arta.text: Arta is a town in Greece, built over the ancient site of Ambracia. The Bridge of Arta and the Church of the Parigoritissa lead the visit, about six hours in all. April and May are the best months, with buses connecting it well to the region.

gem:freising.text: Freising is a cathedral town in Bavaria, not far from Munich. Freising Cathedral and Weihenstephan Abbey lead the visit, six hours between them. May through September works well, and trains to Munich run frequently.

gem:bukkszentkereszt.text: Bukkszentkereszt is a tiny village in the Bukk hills of Hungary. The Cave Bath and Anna-barlang cave head the sights, four hours between the closer two. May through September suits it best, though a car is far more reliable than the buses.

gem:altenburg.text: Altenburg is an art town in Germany, gathered around its castle. Altenburg Castle and the Residenzschloss Altenburg anchor the visit, six hours total. May through September brings the best weather, and rail links make it an easy stop.

gem:gressoney-saint-jean.text: Gressoney-Saint-Jean is a small mountain village in Italy, beneath the Monte Rosa Massif. Dufourspitze and Lyskamm rise in view of the village, three hours for a walk around. July and August are the only real window, since buses up the valley are few.

gem:auxerre.text: Auxerre is a cathedral town on the Yonne River in France. Auxerre Cathedral and the Royal Abbey of Saint-Germain d'Auxerre lead the visit, six hours between them. May through September works best, and the vineyards nearby suit a side trip.

gem:oulmes.text: Oulmes is a modest village in France, among the Petites Cites de Caractere. The Maillezais Cathedral and the Marais Poitevin wetlands lie within reach nearby, about three hours for both. May through September suits it best, since buses are scarce.

gem:galati.text: Galati is a cathedral city in Romania. The Precista fortified church leads the visit, with the Archdiocesan Cathedral St Andrew close behind, six hours in all. May and September are the best months, and rail connections here are solid.

gem:leba.text: Leba is a small beach village on the Baltic coast of Poland. Slowinski National Park sits right beside it, with dunes among the tallest in Europe, and Lebsko Lake spreads to the east. Two hours is enough for the village itself, ideally in July or August.

gem:didymoteicho.text: Didymoteicho is a castle town in Greece. The Celebi Sultan Mehmed Mosque and the Castle of Didymoteicho anchor the old quarter, with the Hamam of Feridun Ahmed Bey nearby. For about three hours, April and May suit it best.

gem:almagro.text: Almagro is a historic town in Spain, protected as a Conjunto historico. The Corral de Comedias de Almagro, a rare surviving theatre, headlines the sights alongside the Museo Nacional del Teatro. Its four hours of sights suit May best.

gem:eenrum.text: Eenrum is a little village in the Netherlands. Lauwersmeer National Park lies close by, with the Groninger Museum and the wild island of Rottumeroog also within reach. Few places need less than four hours, best planned for June through August.

gem:avernes.text: Avernes is a quiet village in France, set inside the Parc naturel regional du Vexin francais. Maubuisson Abbey and Pontoise Cathedral sit within day-trip range. Not much time is needed, about four hours, best from May to September.

gem:pisek.text: Pisek is a historic town in South Bohemia, Czechia, built around the country's oldest stone bridge. The Pisek Stone Bridge leads the sights, followed by Zvikov Castle. Six hours covers the town, best between May and September, on the way to Cesky Krumlov.

gem:ustka.text: Ustka is a beach town in Pomorskie, Poland, popular with domestic summer visitors. The lighthouse, Latarnia morska Ustka, tops the list, with Salvator church and Lake Gardno close by. June through August works best, with about four hours needed.

gem:jelenia-gora.text: Jelenia Gora is a historic city in Lower Silesian Voivodship, Poland, and a gateway to the Giant Mountains. Chojnik Castle tops the sights, with Cieplice Slaskie-Zdroj close behind. Ten hours covers it all, best from May through August.

gem:korenov.text: Korenov is a little village in Czechia, set among mountains such as Kozakov and Wielki Szyszak. Frydstejn Castle and Rotstejn Castle headline the sights, with Lysa hora nearby. June through August is the best window, and four hours takes in both castles.

gem:lidkoping.text: Lidkoping is a town on Lake Vanern in Vastergotland, Sweden. Husaby Church anchors the old town, with Villa Giacomina and the old parish of Hovby socken close by. The town takes about six hours to see properly, best in June through August.

gem:zlin.text: Zlin is a historic city in South Moravia, Czechia, built on the legacy of the Bata shoe company. Bata's Skyscraper and Zlin Castle headline the sights, with the Vizovice Highlands nearby. The round takes about nine hours, from May to September.

gem:skovde.text: Skovde is a town in Vastergotland, Sweden. Varnhem Abbey opens the list of sights, with the old parish churches of Vambs kyrka and Forsby kyrka nearby. The whole visit runs about six hours, best in June through August.

gem:roma.text: Roma is a small village on Gotland, Sweden. Roma Abbey is the first stop, with Ganthem Church and, in nearby Visby, the City wall of Visby. July and August are the months to come, with four hours covering the abbey and the church.

gem:snezne.text: Snezne is a small village in the Upper Svratka Highlands of Czechia. The Pilgrimage Church of Saint John of Nepomuk comes first among the sights, with the hills of Zdarske vrchy close by. The four hours needed suit June through August, near Velke Darko.

gem:tolmin.text: Tolmin is a little village in Slovenia, within reach of Lake Bohinj and the peak of Triglav. Vogel rises above the lake as a favorite viewpoint, while Krn draws hikers further out. May, June, and July all work, and three hours takes in the peaks.

gem:vastervik.text: Vastervik is a coastal town in north-eastern Smaland, Sweden, part of the Tjust archipelago region. The ruined castle of Stegeholm tops the sights, with Sankt Petri kyrka nearby. June through August is the season, and five hours covers the old town easily.

gem:rauna.text: Rauna is a small area in Latvia, best known for Rauna Castle and its place within Gauja National Park. Cesis Castle and the Church of Saint John the Baptist sit nearby. June through August works well, with four hours covering both castles.

gem:megchelen.text: Megchelen is a small village in the Netherlands, close to the Lower German Limes. Xanten Cathedral and Colonia Ulpia Traiana sit just across the border. Its sights take about four hours, best from May through September, with Villa Bouchina closer to home.

gem:ruurlo.text: Ruurlo is a modest village in Berkelland, Gelderland, the Netherlands. Kasteel Huize Ruurlo headlines the village, with the Kristalmuseum and De Wildenborch nearby. The estate and museum take about four hours, best from May through September.

gem:vransko.text: Vransko is a small village in Slovenia, among the hills near Velika planina. The surrounding villages of Braslovce and Kokarje make for quiet detours, near the peak of Kum. May through August suits it, with about three hours enough for the detours.

gem:trutnov.text: Trutnov is a town in Czechia, gateway to the Adrspach-Teplice Rocks. The restored Synagogue in Trutnov anchors the built sights, with the forest of Dvorsky les close by. Six hours suits it, best kept for June through August.

gem:balassagyarmat.text: Balassagyarmat sits on the Ipoly river in Nograd county, within Northern Hungary. The Janossy Gallery and the Paloc Museum top the list of sights, with the Balassagyarmati zsinagoga nearby. The five hours needed fit April, June, or September.

gem:sloup-v-cechach.text: Sloup v Cechach is a quiet village in Czechia, between the Lusatian and Zittau Mountains. The rock formation of Mariina skala is the standout, near Ceske Svycarsko National Park. May through September suits it, and four hours takes in the rocks.

gem:faliraki.text: Faliraki is a beach village on Rhodes, Greece. Nearby, the Medieval City of Rhodes holds the Palace of the Grand Master of the Knights of Rhodes. Two hours covers the village itself, with Anthony Quinn Bay closer to home, best in April, May, or June.

gem:valmiera.text: Valmiera sits in Vidzeme, Latvia, straddling both banks of the Gauja river. The ruins of Valmiera Castle crown the sights, with the Valmiera Drama Theatre nearby. The four hours needed suit June through August, inside Gauja National Park.

gem:mladenovac.text: Mladenovac is a rural area in Serbia, around the wooded hill of Kosmaj. Pavlovac Monastery is the main draw, with the Despot Stefan Lazarevic Memorial nearby. April, May, and September are the best months; four hours covers both.

gem:decin.text: Decin is a town in North Bohemia, Czechia, set on the River Elbe. The Elbe Sandstone Mountains rise around it, with Bohemian Switzerland just beyond and Decin Zoo closer to town. Six hours covers the surroundings, best from May through September.

gem:seborga-it.text: Seborga, in Italy, is a little village above the Fiume Roia valley. The Istituto Internazionale di Studi Liguri and Villa Nobel make up the local sights. May, June, and September suit it best, with about four hours enough to see it all.

gem:usseaux.text: Usseaux is a tiny village in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Forte di Fenestrelle opens the list, with the peaks of Monte Albergian and Bric Rosso nearby. June through August suits it, and three hours takes in the fort and the peaks.

gem:offida.text: Offida sits in Italy as a village, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Teatro Serpente Aureo fronts the sights, with the Concattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta close by. Two hours covers the village, with May or June best for a visit.

gem:boville-ernica.text: Boville Ernica sits in Italy as a village, another of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Concattedrale di Sant'Andrea and the San Pietro Ispano church anchor the old center, with Abbazia Casamari nearby. Two hours is plenty, timed for May, June, or September.

gem:oratino.text: Oratino is a village in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Castello Monforte is the highlight, with Santa Maria Maggiore and, in nearby Campobasso, Campobasso Cathedral. May and June suit it best, with three hours covering the churches easily.

gem:caramanico-terme.text: Caramanico Terme is a village in Italy, in the Majella mountains. The hermitage of Eremo di San Bartolomeo in Legio tops the list, with Castello di Salle nearby. May and June suit it best; three hours takes in the hermitage and the castle, below Monte Amaro.

gem:monteprandone.text: Monteprandone is a village in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Torre dei Gualtieri stands first, with the lighthouse at San Benedetto del Tronto nearby. May and June work best; three hours covers the tower and the lighthouse.

gem:specchia.text: Specchia is a village in Italy, another entry among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Castello dei Trane dominates the old center, with the Cripta della Madonna del Gonfalone close by. May and June are best, and three hours takes in the crypts and the castle.

gem:scapoli.text: Scapoli is a small village in Italy, holder of the Bandiera Arancione. The Abbazia di San Vincenzo al Volturno ranks first, with the Museo internazionale delle guerre mondiali nearby. Two hours takes in the abbey and the museum, best in May or June.

gem:l-argentiere-la-bessee.text: L'Argentiere-la-Bessee is a village in France, on the edge of Ecrins National Park. The Eglise Saint Apollinaire is the first stop, with the Cellier de la maison Planche close by. June through August suits it, with three hours covering both.

gem:castelvecchio-di-rocca-barbena.text: Castelvecchio di Rocca Barbena, in Italy, is a tiny village beneath the Rocca Barbena peak. The Toirano Caves top the list, with the church of San Pietro in Varatella close by. June through August works best; three hours takes in the caves and the church.

gem:servigliano.text: Servigliano is a village in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. The Palazzo comunale and the Chiesa di Sant'Agostino lead the sights, with the Casa museo di Osvaldo Licini nearby. Two hours suffices, with May or June the better months.

gem:allegre.text: Allegre is a village in France, listed among the Petites Cites de Caractere. The ruined Chateau d'Allegre headlines the walk, with the Hotel de Bar close by. Two hours does it, best from June through August, with Mont Bar nearby.

gem:valencay.text: Valencay pairs its chateau with a quieter side, the SOE Memorial and two parish churches. It is one of the Plus Beaux Detours de France villages, with sights that take about two hours. Transport is easy, and May through September is the best stretch to visit.

gem:la-roche-derrien.text: La Roche-Derrien belongs to the Petites Cites de Caractere, a stop in France near Treguier Cathedral. The cathedral and the gardens at Kerdalo take about three hours, with Trestrignel Beach nearby. June through September is best, with good public transport.

gem:saint-urcize.text: Saint-Urcize is part of the Petites Cites de Caractere network, a tiny stop in France. Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Michel and Puy de Gudette fill a compact two hours, with Lac du Moulinet close by for a walk. June to August is the season to come.

gem:jugon-les-lacs.text: Jugon-les-Lacs is one of the Petites Cites de Caractere, a stop in France. Chateau de la Hunaudaye and Manoir de Vaumadeuc anchor three unhurried hours, rounded out by St-Pierre and Beaulieu. Public transport runs well June through September.

gem:saint-sauvant.text: Saint-Sauvant is among the Petites Cites de Caractere, a stop in France. Abbaye de Fontdouce and haras national de Saintes lead three unhurried hours, with two Saint-Martin churches nearby. Transport is reliable, best used May through September.

gem:mouchamps.text: Mouchamps belongs to the Petites Cites de Caractere, a stop in France with three chateaux to its name. Its chateaux and the tomb of Georges Clemenceau make for three unhurried hours. June through September is the season, with smooth transport connections.

gem:saint-calais.text: Saint-Calais is one of the Petites Cites de Caractere, a village worth a detour in France. Chateau de Courtanvaux and Halle aux grains lead a tight two hours, alongside Notre-Dame. Transport connections are good, best used June through September.

gem:parne-sur-roc.text: Parne-sur-Roc, among the Petites Cites de Caractere, is a stop in France built around a menhir. Menhir de la Hune and parish churches across Parne-sur-Roc, Force and Laval fill about three hours. Public transport is reliable, best used May through September.

gem:le-coudray-macouard.text: Le Coudray-Macouard is one of the Petites Cites de Caractere, built around Chateau de Montreuil-Bellay. The chateau and St Florent Abbey headline four hours, with Pierre couverte du Mousseau nearby. Transport links are good, best used May through September.

gem:saint-pierre-sur-erve.text: Saint-Pierre-sur-Erve, among the Petites Cites de Caractere, is a stop in France. Grotte Mayenne-Sciences and Moulin de Thevalles join Chapelle Saint-Pierre for a three-hour visit. May through September brings good weather and reliable transport.

gem:northallerton.text: Northallerton is a market town in the United Kingdom. Its sights, worth five hours in all, run from the site of the Battle of the Standard to All Saints Church and St Helens. June through August is best, helped by good public transport.

gem:wallingford.text: Wallingford Castle and Dorchester Abbey lead a six-hour visit in this United Kingdom market town. Hinksey Lake and Caversham Lock lie within reach for a break from the ruins. June through September is the season, with good transport throughout.

gem:blaison-gohier.text: Blaison-Gohier, in France, is part of the Petites Cites de Caractere and centers on two chateaux. Chateau de Brissac and Chateau de Montsabert headline a four-hour circuit past Moulin de Bourgdion. Transport runs well, best used May through September.

gem:newport.text: Newport is a market town in the United Kingdom. Lilleshall Hall, Puleston Cross and St Peter and Paul Church anchor a five-hour visit, with Forton Hall and Aqualate Hall close by. June through August works best, with good public transport.

gem:stow-on-the-wold.text: Stow-on-the-Wold, site of the Battle of Stow-on-the-Wold, is a United Kingdom market village. Sezincote House, Chastleton House and Birdland Park and Gardens fill a four-hour visit. June through August is the season, with good transport.

gem:darwen.text: Darwen is a market town in the United Kingdom. Blackburn Cathedral and St Mark's Church lead a six-hour visit, joined by Turton Tower, Round Loaf and Ewood Aqueduct. Transport links are good, best used June through August.

gem:neston.text: Neston sits on the Dee Estuary, a market town in the United Kingdom. Lady Lever Art Gallery and Flint Castle headline a six-hour visit, with Basingwerk Abbey and Dibbinsdale close behind. June through August suits it best, and getting around is easy.

gem:bedale.text: Bedale is a market village in the United Kingdom. Snape Castle, Bedale Hall and Hornby Castle fill out a three-hour visit, with St Gregory's Bedale and Leeming Bar nearby. Transport is reliable, and June through August is the recommended window.

gem:highbridge.text: Highbridge is a market village in the United Kingdom. St Andrews and St Peter & All Hallows lead a three-hour visit, with the moors at Catcott and Edington nearby. June through September works well, and connections are good.

gem:retford.text: Sloswicke's Hospital and Milton Mausoleum lead a six-hour visit in Retford, a market town in the United Kingdom. Mattersey Priory and Holy Trinity Hospital fill the rest of the list. June through September is best, with good public transport.

gem:fresnay-sur-sarthe.text: Fresnay-sur-Sarthe, among the Petites Cites de Caractere, is a stop in France. Its chateau and Notre-Dame church anchor a three-hour visit, with Commanderie du Gue-Lian close by. June through September suits it best, and it is easy to get around.

gem:sowerby-bridge.text: Sowerby Bridge is a market town in the United Kingdom, close to Halifax. Halifax Minster, The Piece Hall and Wainhouse Tower lead a six-hour visit, with Hebden Bridge nearby. Good transport makes June through August the easiest season.

gem:giglio-castello.text: Giglio Castello, among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, centers on Rocca aldobrandesca. Torre del Saraceno and Torre di Campese round out a two-hour visit, with Faro di Capel Rosso close by. Transport is poor, so plan around June through August.

gem:corinth.text: Corinth is a city in Greece built around its ancient ruins. Ancient Corinth and Acrocorinth lead a five-hour visit, with the Diolkos and the Battle of Lechaeum site nearby. Transport runs well, and April and May bring the best weather.

gem:ventimiglia.text: Ventimiglia is a town on the coast in Italy. The Jean Cocteau Museum and Balzi Rossi lead a six-hour visit, with Plage du Buse and Larvotto beach close by after. April, May, June or September suit it best, with good public transport.

gem:lievin.text: Lievin, a town in France, is shaped by its war memorials. The Canadian National Vimy Memorial and the Lantern Tower and Ossuary at Notre Dame de Lorette lead a six-hour visit. Public transport runs well, best used June through September.

gem:agropoli.text: Agropoli is a town in Italy near the ruins of Paestum. The Second Temple of Hera and the Tomb of the Diver headline five unhurried hours, with Museo d'arte sacra in nearby Castellabate. Transport is reliable, and April through June is the season.

gem:settimo-vittone.text: Settimo Vittone, near Ivrea, centers on Santo Stefano and Torre di Pramotton. The pair lead a three-hour visit, joined by the Ecomuseum of Treby dairy and Museo della vite e del vino. Lake Sirio sits nearby, best seen May through September.

gem:monte-san-savino.text: Monte San Savino sits in Italy, built around two churches. Santuario della Madonna della Querce and Tempio di Santo Stefano della Vittoria lead a three-hour visit, with Santissima Annunziata nearby. Transport is easy, best used May, June or September.

MJV.text: Murcia is a city on the coast of Spain, a Conjunto historico. Murcia Cathedral leads its museums, including Bellas Artes and Salzillo, filling seventeen hours. Public transport is excellent, best used March, April, May or October.

EXT.text: Exeter is a cathedral city on the coast of the United Kingdom, in the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. Exeter Cathedral and the Royal Albert Memorial Museum anchor a ten-hour visit. June through August is best, with excellent transport.

RVN.text: Rovaniemi sits on the Arctic Circle in Finland, home to Santa Claus Village and Santa Park. Arktikum and Ounasvaara round out a seven-hour visit. July is the best month, with excellent public transport nearby.

gem:rundale.text: Rundale Palace is a baroque estate in the countryside in Latvia, on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List. Bauska Castle and Bornsminde Manor lead a five-hour visit, with Svitene Manor nearby. Transport is poor, so plan around May through August.

gem:ulcinj.text: Ulcinj is a coastal town in Montenegro with Ottoman era sights, on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List. Pasha's Mosque and the Church-Mosque of Ulcinj lead a four-hour visit, with Velika Plaza close by. Transport is limited, so aim for May or June.

gem:novi-sad.text: Novi Sad sits on the Danube in Serbia, once a European Capital of Culture. Petrovaradin Fortress and the Novi Sad Synagogue lead a ten-hour visit, with Danube Park nearby. It is easy to get around, and April through June or September works well.

gem:heviz.text: Heviz is a spa town in Hungary built around Lake Heviz. Festetics Palace and the thermal lake lead a three-hour visit, with Keszthely and Badacsony within reach. Transport is poor, so May, June or September make the easiest visit.

gem:subotica.text: Subotica is a city in Serbia known for its Art Nouveau architecture. Subotica Cathedral and the Subotica Synagogue lead an eight-hour visit, with Palic Lake nearby. It stays affordable, with good transport April through June or September.

gem:lefkara.text: Lefkara sits in the Larnaca district of Cyprus, a historic village. Khirokitia and the Painted Churches in the Troodos Region lead a short two hours, with Pano Lefkara and Stavrovouni Monastery nearby. Transport is poor, so April, May or October work best.

gem:ninglinspo.text: Ninglinspo Valley is a hiking area in the Ardennes, Belgium. Signal de Botrange and the High Fens lead a seven-hour stretch, with Franchimont Castle and Lake Robertville within reach. Transport is poor, so plan around June through September.

gem:durbuy.text: Durbuy is a medieval town in Belgium, set among countryside good for a slow visit. Chateau de Deulin and Villers-Sainte-Gertrude lead a five-hour visit, with Menhir Danthine nearby. Transport is poor, so June through September is the easiest season.

gem:zierikzee.text: Zierikzee is a quiet medieval town in Zeeland, Netherlands. Sint-Lievensmonstertoren and the Zeeland Bridge draw the most attention, with Nobelpoort and Zuidhavenpoort close behind; six hours takes in all four, best in June, July or August.

gem:de-haan.text: De Haan is a quiet beach town on the coast of Belgium, popular with families. Oostende and Blankenberge sit within easy reach, while Klein Strand and the Spuikom stay closer to home; six hours covers De Haan itself, easiest June through August.

gem:remich.text: Remich is a small wine village in Luxembourg, quiet and rural. Schengen Castle and Villa Borg sit a short drive away, and Wincheringen and Wintrange Castle add to the list; four hours covers the village itself, best May through September.

gem:faaborg.text: Faaborg is a quiet coastal village in Denmark. Egeskov Castle stands out first, Hvedholm and the island of Lyo second, and four hours takes in all three; Bojden Nor lake lies close by for a quieter stop, best June through August.

gem:romo.text: Romo is a remote island in Denmark, known for its wide beaches. Romo Church and the Wadden Sea National Park anchor a four-hour visit, Lakolk Strand supplies the sand, and Mando sits visible offshore; June to August is the easiest season.

gem:koszeg.text: Koszeg is a medieval town in Hungary. Jurisics Castle draws visitors first, Sacred Heart Church second, and the Geschriebenstein peak rises just beyond; five hours covers the town, and good public transport makes May through September an easy trip.

gem:godollo.text: Godollo is a baroque town in Hungary, built around its royal palace. Godollo Palace leads the way, with Our Lady Basilica and Mariabesnyo close by; five hours is enough, and April, May, June or September all work well.

gem:meissen.text: Meissen is a historic town in Germany, home to a hilltop castle and cathedral. Albrechtsburg and Meissen Cathedral come first, Moritzburg Castle and the village of Niederau after, across six hours in all; May through September suits it best.

gem:klontalersee.text: Klontalersee is a lake area in Switzerland, ringed by peaks and popular with hikers. Glarnisch and Rautispitz rise above the water, Glarus and Ennenda sit nearby, and six hours covers the area well; come in June, July or August.

gem:usedom.text: Usedom is an island area in Germany, known for its beach resorts and spas. Seebad Heringsdorf and Schloss Pudagla lead the list, with Karsibor and Swinoujscie close by; seven hours covers it, best from June to August.

gem:edessa.text: Edessa is a small town in Greece, known for a park built around its waterfalls. The Waterfalls Park and Yeni Mosque top the list, with Lake Agra not far off; four hours is enough, and May, September or October are the calmer months.

gem:leros.text: Leros is a quiet island in Greece, part of the Dodecanese. Vromolithos beach and nearby Kalymnos fill most of a four-hour visit, while Leipsoi and Farmakonisi stay visible across the water; May through September is the season to come.

gem:kythnos.text: Kythnos is a quiet volcanic island in Greece. Vryokastro and the Maroulas mesolithic site come first, Katafyki Cave and Fykiada beach after; four hours takes them all in, and any month from May to September suits.

gem:karpas-peninsula.text: Karpas Peninsula is a remote coastal area in Cyprus with wide open beaches. Agia Trias Basilica and Panagia Kanakaria lead the sights, and Golden Beach rounds out a four-hour stop; May or June is the best window.

gem:halki.text: Halki is a quiet island in Greece, small enough to see on foot. Agios Theodoros comes first, the islet of Alimia second, with Atavyros visible across the water; four hours covers the island, best June through September.

gem:ikaria.text: Ikaria is a quiet island in Greece, known for its slow pace of life and small population. Kastro Koskina and Oenoe lead the list, and the peak of Kerkis rises nearby; four hours is enough, June through September the calmest stretch.

gem:tremiti-islands.text: Tremiti Islands is a remote island group in Italy, popular with divers. San Domino Island and the Santuario di Santa Maria a Mare come first, Torre Mileto for the beach after; four hours covers the group, best from May to July.

gem:le-castella.text: Le Castella is a small coastal area in Italy, built around a castle on the water. Capo Colonna and the Marine Protected Area Capo Rizzuto lead the sights, with Crotone close enough for a side trip; four hours is enough, best in May.

gem:runde.text: Runde is a quiet island in Norway, ringed by smaller islands and open coast. Heroy Church and Gurskoya come first, with Slogen rising above Nerlandsoya; five hours takes in the island, June to August the easiest season.

gem:lyngen-alps.text: Lyngen Alps is a wilderness area in Norway, built for skiing and hiking among steep peaks. Store Lenangstind and Tromsdalstinden dominate the skyline, Lyngen Church and Karlsoy Church quieter stops; four hours covers them, best in May, July or August.

gem:fredrikstad.text: Fredrikstad is a historic fortress city in Norway. Fredrikstad domkirke and Fredrikstad Bridge anchor the visit, with Onsoy Church and Glemmen gamle kirke rounding out nine hours; June, July and August work best.

gem:kristiansand.text: Kristiansand is a coastal city in Norway, popular with families for its beaches. Kristiansand Cannon Museum and Bystranda come first, Hamresanden beach and Flekkeroy Church after, across a full ten hours; summer months of June, July and August suit it best.

gem:sandhamn.text: Sandhamn is a romantic island in the Stockholm archipelago in Sweden. Gronskar lighthouse leads the way, with Ingaro and Grinda reachable by boat; five hours is enough, July or August the best time to go.

gem:molle-kullaberg.text: Molle is a small hiking village in Sweden, set against the Kullaberg headland. Kullen Lighthouse and Krapperup Castle add to the walk, with Brunnby kyrka nearby; three hours covers the village, June through August the mildest weather.

gem:vadstena.text: Vadstena is a small lakeside village in Sweden, built around its castle and abbey. Vadstena Castle and Vadstena Abbey take up most of a four-hour visit, with the lake of Vattern stretching alongside; June to August suits it best.

gem:swinoujscie.text: Swinoujscie is a seaside spa town in Poland. Swinoujscie Lighthouse and Stawa Mlyny come first, Karsibor and Miedzyzdroje beach after; six hours covers the town, best from June to August.

gem:lancut.text: Lancut is a baroque town in Poland, anchored by its castle and synagogue. Lancut Synagogue and the Saint Stanislaus church come first, with the Church of St Dorota in nearby Markowa; five hours covers the sights, May through September the easiest window.

gem:aukstaitija.text: Aukstaitija National Park is a lake-filled park in Lithuania. The Museum of Ancient Beekeeping and Lake Alksnaitis lead the way, with Tauragnas and Kretuonas among the lakes nearby; five hours is enough, June through August the easiest season.

gem:zemaitija.text: Zemaitija National Park is a lake district in Lithuania, home to the Plokstine missile base and the lake at Plateliai. Telsiai Cathedral and the Church of St Peter and St Paul add another five hours, best June through August.

gem:cape-kolka.text: Cape Kolka is a remote coastal area in Latvia. Slitere National Park and the Kolka lighthouse come first, with the Gipka Lighthouse further along the coast; four hours is enough, July or August the calmest weather.

gem:hiiumaa.text: Hiiumaa is a quiet island in Estonia, thick with nature reserves. Kopu Lighthouse comes first, Tihu Nature Reserve and the beach at Saaretirp after; four hours takes them in, July or August the best time to come.

gem:kihnu.text: Kihnu is a small, remote island in Estonia, quiet even in summer. Kihnu lighthouse and Kihnu Parish lead the way, with Sorgu and the beach at Kabli close by; four hours covers it, July or August the calmest crossing.

gem:castelo-rodrigo.text: Castelo Rodrigo is a remote medieval village in Portugal, ringed by hilltop castles. The Castle of Castelo Rodrigo and Castle of Marialva lead the sights, with the Coa Valley rock art nearby; five hours is enough, May, June or September the mildest months.

gem:miranda-do-douro.text: Miranda do Douro is a historic town in Portugal, perched above the Douro river. The Cathedral of Miranda do Douro and its castle take up most of a three-hour visit, with the Miranda Reservoir nearby; May, June and September bring milder weather.

gem:setubal.text: Setubal is a coastal city in Portugal on the Sado Estuary. Quinta da Bacalhoa and the Castelo de Sao Filipe come first, Figueirinha Beach and Albarquel Beach for the coast after, across nine hours; April, May and June suit it best.

gem:albufeira.text: Albufeira is a beach town in Portugal, popular with families. Praia da Marinha and Falesia Beach lead the sights, with Paderne Castle and Vilamoura nearby; six hours covers the town, May through September the long season.

gem:estremoz.text: Estremoz is a medieval town in Portugal, known for its wine and castle. The Castle of Estremoz and Igreja de Sao Francisco come first, with the Ducal Palace of Vila Vicosa nearby; five hours is enough, May or June the best time to go.

gem:almeida.text: Almeida is a quiet fortress village in Portugal. The Castle Fortress of Almeida and Royal Fortress of the Concepcion lead the sights, with Siega Verde and the Castle of Castelo Mendo nearby; three hours covers them, May, June or September the calmest months.

gem:rimetea.text: Rimetea is a small mountain village in Romania. Cheile Turzii and Trascau Fortress lead the way, with Cheile Valisoarei and Cheile Silosului for more hiking nearby; two hours is enough, May through September the easiest stretch.

gem:wonderful-bridges.text: Wonderful Bridges is a remote hiking area in the Rhodope Mountains of Bulgaria. The Marvelous Bridges and Golyam Perelik peak lead the way; four hours covers the walk, June through August the driest season.

gem:lukov.text: Lukov is a tiny village in Czechia, gathered beneath a ruined hilltop castle. Lukov Castle leads the sights, with Zlin-Lesna Zoo and the Vizovice Highlands rounding out a four hour visit best from May to September. Public transport is poor.

gem:paralimni.text: Paralimni is a coastal town in Cyprus known for long sandy beaches. Nissi beach and Othello Castle lead the sights, with the Lala Mustafa Pasha Mosque and Ganchvor monastery filling out four hours. April, May and October beat the summer heat.

gem:riihimaki.text: Riihimaki is a railway town in Finland built around its old train yards. The Finnish Railway Museum and Riihimaki railway station anchor a five hour visit, best from June to August. Loppijarvi lake sits close by, and public transport is good.

gem:johvi.text: Johvi is a historic town in Estonia perched above the Baltic Klint. Valaste Waterfall is the highlight, with Kukruse manor and its cemetery filling out five hours in July or August. It sits on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List.

gem:loenen.text: Loenen is a quiet village in the Netherlands on the edge of the Veluwe woodlands. Hoge Veluwe National Park and the Kroller-Muller Museum lead the list, about four hours of stops, best May through August. Public transport is poor.

gem:pathmos.text: Pathmos is a modest village in the Netherlands, close to Enschede and Hengelo. The Rijksmuseum Twenthe and the Basilica of St Plechelm are the draws, about four hours in total, best May through September. Public transport is poor.

gem:usti-nad-labem.text: Usti nad Labem is a city in Czechia guarded by the ruins of Strekov Castle. The castle and the hills of Ceske Stredohori give ten hours of sightseeing, best from May to September. Milesovka rises nearby for hikers.

gem:rb-k.text: Orbaek is a tiny village in Denmark on the island of Funen. Egeskov Castle and Nyborg Castle lead the sights, with the Great Belt Fixed Link close by, about three hours total. Public transport is poor, so June through August with a car works best.

gem:hudiksvall.text: Hudiksvall is a coastal town in Sweden with a cluster of historic parishes just inland. Halsingtuna kyrka leads the sights, with Idenors socken and Rogsta socken filling five hours, best in July or August. Transport stays limited.

gem:glinado.text: Glinado is a small village in Greece on Naxos Island. The Portara and the Archaeological Museum of Naxos are the draws, roughly three hours in total, best May through September. Mikri Vigla and Grotta beach cover the coast.

gem:tatabanya.text: Tatabanya is a city in Hungary built around Lake Oreg. Tata Castle and the Turul Monument at Banhida top the list, with Szelim-lyuk adding to nine hours of sightseeing. May, June and September are the months to visit.

gem:drammen.text: Drammen is a city in Norway centered on Bragernes kirke and the Drammen Bridge. Drammens museum and Ypsilon are worth the ten hours a full visit takes, best June through August. Bragernes strand covers the beach.

gem:revfulop.text: Revfulop is a small village in Hungary on the shore of Lake Balaton. Two hours covers the village, though Csobanc and Szent Gyorgy-hill draw visitors inland. Badacsony rises across the water, best May, June or September.

gem:bauska.text: Bauska is a historic town in Latvia, home to Bauska Castle and within reach of Rundale Palace. Bornsminde Manor rounds out a four hour visit, best from May to August. Public transport is good, so seeing both is easy.

gem:kandava.text: Kandava is a small village in Latvia gathered around its ruined castle. Kandava Castle and the hillfort at Kandavas pilskalns lead the sights, about three hours total, best June to August. Public transport is poor.

gem:elafonisos.text: Elafonisos is a small village in Greece close to Pavlopetri. The Church of Agia Sofia and Kastania Cave fill out a two hour visit, best from May to June or in September. Sarakiniko Beach is the spot to relax.

gem:posada.text: Posada is a village in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Nuraghe San Pietro and the Torre di San Giovanni lead a three hour visit, best from May to August. Spiaggia di Su Tiriarzu covers the coast.

gem:garbagna.text: Garbagna is a tiny village in Italy, one of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Castello di Borgo Adorno and Castello di Sorli are worth two hours, with Monte Gavasa rising just behind. Best seen May, June or September.

gem:compiano.text: Compiano is a small village in Italy, part of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Castello di Compiano and Palazzo Tardiani anchor three hours in the center, best June to August. Monte Pelpi suits a longer stop.

gem:frisanco.text: Frisanco is a small village in Italy, named among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. San Remigio and Castello Di Maniago lead three hours of sightseeing, best between May and September. Barcis lake makes an easy add.

gem:mazamet.text: Mazamet is a historic town in France, listed among Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. Chateau d'Hautpoul and the Terrasses d'Hautpoul lead four hours of sightseeing, best May, June or September. Pic de Nore rises nearby.

gem:caccuri.text: Caccuri is a small village in Italy, part of I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. Castello di Caccuri and Abbazia Florense are the highlights, about two hours total, best in May or June. Lago Ampollino is close for a lake stop.

gem:guerlesquin.text: Guerlesquin is a village in France, recognized as one of the Petites Cites de Caractere. The Chateau et manoir de Keroue and the Colombier de Lesmoal lead three hours of sightseeing, best June through September.

gem:wokingham.text: Wokingham is a market town in the United Kingdom, centered on St Michael and St Mary Magdalene church. Swallowfield Park and Deanery Garden are worth six hours, best June to September. Caversham Lock sits nearby.

gem:pontrieux.text: Pontrieux is a village in France, one of the Petites Cites de Caractere. La Roche-Jagu and the Temple de Lanleff are the highlights, filling three hours, best June through September. The old Gare de Brelidy - Plouec station adds a stop.

gem:guemene-sur-scorff.text: Guemene-sur-Scorff is a village in France, part of the Petites Cites de Caractere. The Calvaire de Locmeltro and Bornes milliaires de Locmeltro anchor three hours of sightseeing, best June through September. Lake Guerledan lies within reach.

gem:chatelaudren.text: Chatelaudren is a village in France, one of the Petites Cites de Caractere. The Eglise Notre-Dame du Tertre and the Menhir du Pre de Camet make an unusual pairing, filling three hours, best June through September.

gem:pleaux.text: Pleaux is a village in France, part of the Petites Cites de Caractere. Chateau de Branzac and the Eglise Saint-Sauveur de Pleaux fill two hours easily, best June to September. The saint Ferreol Church near Ally in Cantal is a further stop.

gem:marcoles.text: Marcoles is a village in France, one of the Petites Cites de Caractere. The Fortifications de Marcoles and the Eglise Saint-Martin de Marcoles anchor two hours, best June to September. Lac de Saint-Etienne-Cantales lies close by.

gem:apremont.text: Apremont is a quiet village in the Petites Cites de Caractere network of France. Chateau d'Apremont and Chateau de Commequiers are the sights that matter, with the Dolmen des Pierres-Folles adding prehistory to two hours, best June through September.

gem:aubigne-sur-layon.text: Aubigne-sur-Layon is a modest village on the Petites Cites de Caractere list of France. The Chateau du Grand-Riou and the Eglise Saint Denis anchor three hours of sightseeing, best May through September. The Menhir de la Grouas sits close by.

gem:verteuil-sur-charente.text: Verteuil-sur-Charente, in France, is part of the Petites Cites de Caractere villages. Chateau de Verteuil leads three hours of sightseeing, with Chateau de Bayers and Chateau de Chenon further along, best May through September.

gem:raulhac.text: Raulhac is a sleepy village among the Petites Cites de Caractere villages of France. Chateau de Cropieres and Chateau de Vixouze lead three hours of sightseeing, best June through September. Plomb du Cantal rises nearby.

gem:tusson.text: Tusson is a compact village in the Petites Cites de Caractere group of villages across France. Dolmens scattered around it, from the Pierre Blanche to Magnez and the Perottes, fill most of a three hour visit, best June to September.

gem:nanteuil-en-vallee.text: Nanteuil-en-Vallee, in France, is one of the Petites Cites de Caractere villages. The Abbaye Notre-Dame de Nanteuil is the centerpiece, with the Manoir d'Aizecq nearby, about three hours total, best June to September.

gem:saint-denis-d-anjou.text: Saint-Denis-d'Anjou is a calm village carrying Petites Cites de Caractere status in France. Its own Eglise Saint-Denis anchors the center, with the Prieure du Gravier nearby, filling three hours, best May through September.

gem:charroux-fr.text: Charroux is a tranquil village holding a Petites Cites de Caractere designation in France. Charroux Abbey and the Halles de Charroux lead two hours of sightseeing, with the porte de l'Aumonerie a quiet corner, best June through September.

gem:saulges.text: Saulges is an unassuming village named to the Petites Cites de Caractere list in France. The Grotte Mayenne-Sciences and Moulin de Thevalles are an unusual pairing, filling three hours, best June to September.

gem:brulon.text: Brulon is a modest village recognized under the Petites Cites de Caractere program in France. Chateau de Verdelles is the standout, with the Eglise Notre-Dame de Cheville close by, filling three hours, best June through September.

gem:foussais-payre.text: Foussais-Payre is an understated village counted among the Petites Cites de Caractere of France. Coulonges-sur-l'Autize nearby holds both a church and a chateau, filling much of a three hour stop, best May through September.

gem:oiron.text: Oiron is a village in France with Petites Cites de Caractere status. The Chateau d'Oiron and Abbatiale Saint-Jouin de Marnes lead the sights, worth about three hours, best May through September, with good transport for under a thousand residents.

gem:bourmont.text: Bourmont is a Petites Cites de Caractere village in France, built around the Eglise Notre-Dame de Bourmont. Two hours cover its churches, best June through September in a place of just six hundred people with good transport.

gem:le-thoureil.text: Le Thoureil is a village in France where the Dolmen de la Foret and Chateau de Montsabert anchor about four hours of exploring. The village also carries Petites Cites de Caractere status, best visited May through September.

gem:penistone.text: Penistone is a market town in the United Kingdom, with Cannon Hall and Wortley Hall the top draws across some five hours. Ladybower Reservoir sits nearby, and June to August brings good transport for its ten thousand residents.

gem:atherstone.text: Atherstone is a market town in the United Kingdom where Astley Castle and Merevale Hall lead a six-hour round of sights. Polesworth adds an easy stop, best June through August with good transport for a town of eleven thousand.

gem:forges-les-eaux.text: Forges-les-Eaux is a village in France listed among Les Plus Beaux Detours de France. The Abbaye Saint-Martin et Saint-Vulgain and Chateau de Gaillefontaine fill about two hours, best June through September.

gem:llanfyllin.text: Llanfyllin is a market town in the United Kingdom built around the Parish Church Of St Tysilio And St Mary. St Garmon's and Mathrafal round out three hours, best June to August with good transport.

gem:poffabro.text: Poffabro is a village in Italy named among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia. San Remigio and Santa Maria delle Grazie sit near the Castello Di Maniago, about three hours, best May through September. Barcis lake is close, though transport is poor.

gem:fosdinovo.text: Fosdinovo is a small town in Italy built around the Castello Malaspina and Fortezza Firmafede. Fortezza Castracani rounds out a good four hours worth exploring, best June through August, with good transport for just over four hundred people.

PNA.text: Pamplona is a historic city in Spain with Conjunto historico status. The Cathedral of Pamplona and Navarre Museum headline ten hours worth exploring, and the Ciudadela de Pamplona rounds it out. June through September works well, with excellent transport.

LMP.text: Lampedusa is an island in Italy, part of the Pelagian Islands group. Isola dei Conigli and the Door of Europe take about four hours to see, with Rabbit beach close by. Transport is limited, so plan for May through August.

NCL.text: Newcastle is a coastal city in the United Kingdom known for nightlife. The Tyne Bridge and Angel of the North anchor seventeen hours of sightseeing, with Sage Gateshead nearby. The best months are June through August, when transport turns excellent.

GRQ.text: Groningen is a university city in the Netherlands with a strong nightlife scene. The Groninger Museum and Martinitoren headline about ten hours worth exploring. Hoornse Meer lies close by for a swim, best reached June through August on excellent transport.

TSR.text: Timisoara is a city in Romania recognized as a European Capital of Culture. The Timisoara Orthodox Cathedral and Banat Village Museum take about six hours to see, with the Iosefin Synagogue close behind. April, May, June or September works best.

OMR.text: Oradea is a historic city in Romania with an art and thermal character. Sirul Canonicilor and Palatul Stern fill a good nine hours. April, May, June and September are the months to go, and transport is excellent.

gem:zaanse-schans.text: Zaanse Schans is a windmill village in the Netherlands, its own sights filling about six hours. The Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum sit in nearby Amsterdam, worth a side trip. The best time to visit is June through August, with good transport.

gem:dinant.text: Dinant is a town in Belgium set along the River Meuse. Rocher Bayard and the Abbaye Notre-Dame de Leffe take up about six hours, with Castle of Veves further out among the hills. Transport is poor, so plan for May through September.

gem:monsaraz.text: Monsaraz is a medieval village in Portugal, quiet and remote above the Alqueva Reservoir. The Castelo de Monsaraz alone is worth five hours. Transport is poor, so April and May, the two best months, are worth planning around.

gem:porvoo.text: Porvoo is a quiet coastal town in Finland built around Porvoo Cathedral. Porvoo Museum and the Old Town Hall stretch a visit to eight hours. June through August is best, though transport is limited for its fifty-two thousand residents.

gem:tartu.text: Tartu is a university city in Estonia named a European Capital of Culture. Tartu Cathedral and Tartu Town Hall take up about ten hours, with the Estonian National Museum close by. Toomemae park sits under a kilometer from the center.

gem:bansko.text: Bansko is a mountain town in Bulgaria beneath the slopes of Pirin. The Church of the Holy Trinity in Bansko is worth a stop, with Vihren and Todorka close by for hikers across some five hours. June through September is best despite poor local transport.

gem:melnik.text: Melnik is the smallest town in Bulgaria, a wine village on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List. Rozhen Monastery alone fills three hours. May, June, September or October suits a visit, though transport is poor.

gem:nerja.text: Nerja is a beach town in Spain built around the Cueva de Nerja. The Sierra de Tejeda rises behind it, while Torre de Maro rounds out a five-hour visit. May through August is the season, though transport is limited.

gem:besalu.text: Besalu is a medieval village in Spain centered on the Sinagoga de Besalu. The Lake of Banyoles and Santa Margarida Volcano round out about four hours. April, May, June and September work best, though transport is poor.

gem:valkenburg.text: Valkenburg is a castle village in the Netherlands, a family base for the countryside around it. Aachen Cathedral and Fort Eben-Emael make worthwhile day trips over the border. The village itself takes about four hours, best May to September.

gem:ystad.text: Ystad is a medieval coastal town in Sweden anchored by Greyfriars Abbey and Ystads Konstmuseum. Ale's Stones sits a short trip out. Six hours covers the sights, best June through August though transport is limited.

gem:krusevo.text: Krusevo is a mountain town in North Macedonia, its history led by Makedonium and the Battle of Meckin Kamen. Holy Trinity church rounds out roughly three hours. June through August makes the best season, and prices here stay affordable despite poor transport.

gem:titisee.text: Titisee is a lakeside spa village in Germany at the foot of Feldberg. The Hochfirstturm tower and nearby Schluchsee lake take about three hours, with Neustadt a short trip further. June through August is best.

gem:tisvildeleje.text: Tisvildeleje is a quiet beach village in Denmark near Frederiksborg Palace. Tibirke Kirke and Ramlose Molle sit close by, with Lake Esrum offering water views. Its sights take about three hours, best kept to July and August.

gem:thorn-nl.text: Thorn is a quiet historic village in the Netherlands, once tied to the Roman Catholic Diocese of Roermond. Stevensweert and the Kraekermolen make for about four hours. May through September is best, though transport is poor.

gem:deventer.text: Deventer is a medieval city in the Netherlands centered on Rijsterborgherpark and the Lebuinuskerk. Museum MORE stretches a visit to about ten hours. Bussloo offers a lake nearby, and June through August brings good transport.

gem:stavelot.text: Stavelot is a quiet village in Belgium, once the seat of the Principality of Stavelot-Malmedy. The Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps draws visitors nearby, and Signal de Botrange rises through the High Fens. The best season runs June through August.

gem:clervaux.text: Clervaux is a castle village in Luxembourg set in the Oesling hills. Clervaux Castle and Clervaux Abbey take up about four hours, with the Our river valley close by. June through August is best, with good transport.

gem:bourscheid.text: Bourscheid is a medieval area in Luxembourg centered on Bourscheid Castle and Brandenbourg Castle. Ettelbruck and Diekirch stretch a visit to about seven hours. June through September suits a visit, with good transport.

gem:externsteine.text: Externsteine is a hiking destination in Germany within the Teutoburg Forest. The Hermannsdenkmal and Grotenburg take about four hours, with Detmold close by. June through August is best, though transport is poor.

gem:weissensee-carinthia.text: Weissensee is a lake area in Austria within the Naturpark Weissensee. Millstatter See and Teurnia take up about six hours, with Latschur rising above the water. June through August suits a visit, though transport is poor.

gem:andros.text: Andros is a hiking island among the Aegean Islands and Greek Islands of Greece. The Tourlitis Lighthouse and Archaeological Museum of Andros make for about four hours. Ochi mountain rises over Tis Grias to Pidima beach, best May through September.

gem:sulmona.text: Sulmona is a mountain town in Italy known for its food and the Cattedrale di San Panfilo. Maiella National Park and Monte Amaro rise close by. May and June are the months to visit, though transport is poor.

gem:saltstraumen.text: Saltstraumen is a coastal village in Norway centered on Saltstraumen Bridge and Saltstraumen kirke. Bodo Cathedral sits a short trip away. Two hours covers the sights, best kept to July and August.

gem:hoddevik.text: Hoddevik is a remote surf beach in Norway near Maloy bridge. Silda and Selja sit offshore, with Hendanes Lighthouse rounding out about four hours. The best waves come June through August, though transport stays poor.

gem:smogen.text: Smogen is a small fishing village on the west coast of Sweden, known for granite skerries and seafood. Nordens Ark and the islands of Vajern, Malmon and Gaso top the list, roughly three hours best done in June or July.
