gem:voskopoja.text: Voskopoja is a mountain village in Albania built around two historic churches. St Mary's Church and St Michael's Church lead the sights, with the Fir of Drenove National Park nearby for time outdoors; five hours suits the whole visit, June through August.

gem:manasija.text: Manasija Monastery is a medieval fortress in Serbia, listed on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List. Ravanica and the Resava cave pair well with it, and four hours covers the core sights, best in May, June or September.

gem:lepenski-vir.text: Lepenski Vir is a remote archaeological site in Serbia, set inside the Iron Gates Natural Park. Tabula Traiana and Rudna Glava make good stops nearby, and four hours covers the core area; visit April through June or in September.

gem:primosten.text: Primosten is a small coastal town in Croatia, popular for its beaches. Sibenik Cathedral is a short trip away, and the islands of Prvic and Zlarin make easy boat stops; two hours covers the town itself, May through August.

gem:kratovo.text: Kratovo sits in North Macedonia, a quiet historic town set among nature. The Kratovo Clock Tower and the Stone town of Kuklica are the top sights, with Lesnovo Monastery a bit further out; five hours suits a full visit, May, June, July or September.

gem:berovo.text: Berovo is a quiet lake town in North Macedonia, set among countryside and forest. Berovo Lake is the main draw, and the Maleshevo Monastery and the Church of the Ascension of Christ round out a five-hour visit; come in May, June or September.

gem:brampton.text: Brampton is a small market town in the United Kingdom surrounded by castles. Carlisle Castle and Naworth Castle lead the list nearby, with Askerton Castle and Scaleby Castle further out; three hours covers Brampton itself, June through August.

gem:pilsrundale.text: Pilsrundale is a small village in Latvia built around a single grand palace. Rundale Palace is the reason to come, with Bauska Castle and Bornsminde Manor as easy add-ons; two hours is enough, best from May to August.

gem:saffron-walden.text: Saffron Walden is a historic market town in the United Kingdom, known for its gardens and museums. Audley End House and Gardens leads the sights, with Bridge End Gardens and the Fry Art Gallery rounding out six hours; come June through September.

gem:hereford.text: Hereford is a cathedral city in the United Kingdom with a strong run of historic sights. Hereford Cathedral comes first, and Belmont Abbey and the Hereford Museum are worth the extra time; plan for about nine hours, June through September.

gem:clitheroe.text: Clitheroe is a historic market town in the United Kingdom. Pendle Hill and Blackburn Cathedral are the main sights within reach, and Stonyhurst College is worth the detour; six hours covers it well, June through August.

gem:macerata.text: Macerata is a historic town in Italy built around its churches. The Sferisterio di Macerata leads the sights, with San Giuliano Church close behind; five hours suits a full visit, June through August.

gem:linkoping.text: Linkoping is a cathedral city in Sweden with enough sights to fill a full day. Linkoping Cathedral comes first, followed by the Swedish Air Force Museum and Vreta Abbey a little further out; plan around ten hours, June through August.

gem:lisburn.text: Lisburn is a cathedral city in the United Kingdom with a good spread of museums and gardens. St Peter's Cathedral and the Ulster Museum lead the sights, with Hillsborough Castle close by; seven hours covers the main list, June through August.

gem:saltash.text: Saltash sits on the River Tamar in the United Kingdom, a historic riverside town. The Royal Albert Bridge is the standout sight, with Plymouth Cathedral and Trematon Castle within easy reach; six hours covers it well, June through September.

gem:battle.text: Battle is a small market town in the United Kingdom named for its abbey grounds. Battle Abbey leads the sights, with Bodiam Castle and Pevensey Castle a short trip away; four hours suits the town itself, June through August.

gem:campobasso.text: Campobasso is a historic town in Italy built around its castle. Castello Monforte and Campobasso Cathedral are the leading sights, with Saepinum a bit further out; five hours suits a visit, best in May or June.

gem:freiberg.text: Freiberg is a town in Germany built around its churches, historic through and through. Freiberg Cathedral leads the list, and Jakobikirche and Schloss Freudenstein are close enough to add in the same day; six hours covers it, June through August.

gem:marienheide.text: Marienheide is a small historic town in Germany with several manor houses and churches to see. Schloss Gimborn leads the sights, with the Oberbergischer Dom and Gut Listringhausen filling out the day; six hours covers it, June through August.

gem:baden.text: Baden is a historic town in Switzerland, well kept and easy to see on foot. Habsburg Castle and Vindonissa lead the sights, with Lenzburg Castle a bit further afield to fill out the day; six hours suits a full visit, best from June to September.

gem:sitten.text: Sitten, also called Sion, is a town in Switzerland known for its churches and castles. Sion Cathedral, Tourbillon Castle and Valere Castle lead the sights, with Diablerets and Wildhorn nearby; six hours suits a full visit, June through August.

gem:jonkoping.text: Jonkoping is a cathedral city in Sweden with an unusual number of churches for its size. Sofiakyrkan and Osterangen Church lead the sights, with Vatterstranden beach nearby for a break; plan around ten hours, June through August.

gem:slagelse.text: Slagelse, in Denmark, has a strong cluster of historic monastery sights nearby. Soro Abbey and Soro Klosterkirke lead the list, with Antvorskov Kloster and Trelleborg close behind; six hours covers the main sights, June through August.

gem:terespol.text: Terespol is a small historic village in Poland, right by Brest. The Brest Fortress and Berestye Archeological Museum are the main draws nearby, with the Simeon Stylites church rounding out the visit; four hours covers it, May through September.

gem:potenza.text: Potenza is a historic city in Italy built around a run of old churches. The Cattedrale di San Gerardo leads the sights, with Chiesa di San Michele Arcangelo filling out the day; nine hours covers the main list, best in May or June.

gem:citta-di-castello.text: Citta di Castello is a historic town in Italy with its own cathedral, San Florido e Amanzio. The Communal Art Gallery adds an afternoon of art, while Sansepolcro Cathedral is an easy trip nearby; five hours suits the town itself, May or June.

gem:taramundi.text: Taramundi is a small historic village in Spain, listed as a historic grouping. The Cave of King Cintolo is the sight in the village itself, with the Catedral de Mondonedo a trip away; two hours covers Taramundi, June through September.

gem:jelgava.text: Jelgava is a historic cathedral city in Latvia. St Simeon and St Anne's Cathedral leads the sights, and the Railway History Museum branch adds variety; plan for about seven hours, May through August.

gem:aarau.text: Aarau is a town in Switzerland built around cathedral history and art. Habsburg Castle and Wasserflue top the list of sights, with Lake Hallwil close by for a swim. Six hours between June and September covers the best of it.

gem:diepenheim.text: Diepenheim is a village in the Netherlands set among castle grounds and quiet lanes. Sallandse Heuvelrug National Park and Kasteel Huize Ruurlo lead the sights, best seen between May and September. Transport is poor, so plan on a car for the four hour visit.

gem:altotting.text: Altotting is a town in Germany built around pilgrimage churches and history. Our Lady of Altotting and Burghausen Castle draw most visitors, with Raitenhaslach Cistercian Abbey close behind. Six hours between May and September covers the sights well.

gem:guilherand-granges.text: Guilherand-Granges is a small town in France, home to Valence Cathedral and Chateau de Crussol nearby. The castel of Tournon and Parc Jouvet round out the sights, best seen in May, June or September. Six hours covers the visit, and public transport is good.

gem:sainte-mere-eglise.text: Utah Beach anchors Sainte-Mere-Eglise, a small village in France close to the wartime landing sites. Chateau de Saint-Sauveur-le-Vicomte and Crisbecq Battery fill out about three hours, with July and August drawing the most visitors.

gem:calarasi.text: Calarasi is a village in Romania built around Island Vetren and the county library. Two hours covers the sights, best planned for May or September. Public transport here is poor, so many visitors come by car.

gem:osuna.text: Osuna is a town in Spain shaped by the Collegiate Church of Osuna and the Monastery of the Incarnation. Iglesia de San Carlos el Real rounds out a four hour visit, best timed for April or May.

gem:kraslava.text: Kraslava is a village in Latvia set beside Lake Dridzis, with Snudy and Sivers close by for a quiet two hours. June through August are the best months, though public transport is scarce.

gem:kungsbacka.text: Kungsbacka is a town on the coast of Sweden, shaped by the parishes of Fjaras, Tolo and Vallda around Lygnern. Six hours in June through August covers the area well, aided by good public transport.

gem:nachod.text: Nachod is a town in Czechia set below Jirova hora, with the Stolowe Mountains and Szczeliniec Wielki rising nearby. Six hours between June and September takes in these along with Rozkos Lake. Public transport here is good.

gem:velhartice.text: Velhartice is a small village in Czechia surrounded by the lakes Cerne jezero and Laka. Osser and Grosser Falkenstein rise nearby among the peaks, with Zwercheck filling out a four hour walk. June through August are best.

gem:liptovsky-mikulas.text: Liptovsky Mikulas is a town in Slovakia set below Chopok and the Low Tatras. Liptovska Mara and Tatralandia lead the sights, with Demanovska Ice Cave close by. The visit takes about five hours, best planned for June through August.

gem:desinic.text: Desinic is a village in Croatia on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List, anchored by Veliki Tabor. Olimje Castle and Podcetrtek Castle lie nearby, both worth folding into a two hour visit. May through August are the best months.

gem:baja.text: Baja is a small town in Hungary beside the Sugovica, known for Gemenc and its lesser mole rats. The Istvan Turr Bridge and Endre Ady Library fill about four hours of sightseeing, best from April to June or in September.

gem:kongsvinger.text: Kongsvinger is a town in Norway straddling the Glomma river, anchored by its fortress. Kongsvinger Fortress and Vinger Church lead a four hour visit, with the Women's Museum Norway close by. June and July are the best months to come.

gem:ornskoldsvik.text: Ornskoldsvik is a town in Sweden built around Paradiskullen hill and Hagglunds Arena. Genesmon and Sjalevads parish add to a five hour visit, best planned for June or July. Sjalevadsfjarden lake lies close by, and transport is good.

gem:liptovsky-hradok.text: Liptovsky Hradok is a small village in Slovakia at the edge of Tatra National Park and the Low Tatras. Chopok and the Western Tatras rise above town, with Liptovska Mara close by. The village takes about three hours, best from June to August.

gem:sligo.text: Sligo is a small town in Ireland known for the Carrowmore Megalithic Cemetery and the hill of Knocknarea. Parke's Castle and the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception fill about five hours, best from June to September near Lough Gill.

gem:huttenberg.text: Huttenberg is a tiny village in Austria below Zirbitzkogel and Ameringkogel, with Hochosterwitz Castle nearby. Gurk Cathedral and Schloss Strassburg fill an easy three hours, best kept for June through August, near Langsee.

gem:hukvaldy.text: Hukvaldy is a village in Czechia below Lysa hora, with its castle overlooking Stramberk and the Moravian-Silesian Beskids. Sipka adds to about four hours here, best from May through September, aided by nearby Olesna Reservoir.

gem:alteveer.text: Alteveer is a tiny village in the Netherlands beside Dwingelderveld National Park, home to Museum de 5000 Morgen. Huis te Echten and De Vlijt make up an easy three hours, ideally June through August near De Huttenheugte.

gem:teigebyen.text: Teigebyen is an area in Norway around Hurdalssjoen and Bjornsjoen, with Kjerkeberget and Mistberget rising above the water. Eidsvoll Church adds a historic stop to a five hour visit, best timed for June or July.

gem:aluksne.text: Aluksne is a small village in Latvia set among the lakes Aluksne, Hino and Murati. Aluksne Castle and the ruins of Marienburgas pils fill three quiet hours, with June through August the best stretch.

gem:sonderborg.text: Sonderborg is a small town in Denmark on the island of Als, anchored by Sonderborg Castle. Broager Church and Nydam Mose fill a six hour visit, at its best June through August, with Grasten Slotsso close by.

gem:tulcea.text: Tulcea is a city in Romania at the gateway to the Danube Delta, home to the Art Museum and Geamie Azizyie. Cetatea Aegyssus and Teatrul Jean Bart fill about five hours here, best from May, June or September.

gem:manger.text: Manger is a village in Norway near Herdla and Misje, with Vardetangen and the Nordhordland Bridge close by. Toska rounds out a two hour visit, with June through August the best window, in the shadow of Floyen.

gem:brienzwiler.text: Brienzwiler is a tiny village in Switzerland beneath the Eiger and Monch, close to the Reichenbach Falls. Wengen and Kleine Scheidegg add an easy three hours, at its best June through September, with Lake Brienz spread below.

gem:sappada.text: Sappada is a small village in Italy, one of the country's most beautiful, ringed by Monte Peralba and Monte Chiadenis. Monte Siera and the Chiesa di Santa Margherita fill about three hours, with June through August the best time, near the Wolayersee.

gem:frosolone.text: Frosolone is a village in Italy also on that list of the country's most beautiful villages, known for its Civic museum of cutting tools. San Giovanni church and Santa Maria del Carmine sit just over in Spinete, worth a two hour side trip best made in June.

gem:rocca-imperiale.text: Rocca Imperiale is a small village in Italy on the same beautiful-villages list, dominated by the Castello Svevo. The church of Santa Maria in Cielo Assunta and the Terme romane fill about two hours, with May through July the best time.

gem:monteverde.text: Monteverde is another of the honored villages in Italy, built around the Castello di Monteverde and a small ethnographic museum. Riserva naturale Grotticelle and the Parco Naturale Regionale del Vulture round out two hours, best in May or June.

gem:plombieres-les-bains-fr.text: Plombieres-les-Bains is a village in France built around thermal baths, including Bain Stanislas and the Bain National. Thermes Napoleon and the Cascade de Faymont round out about three hours, best from June through September.

gem:newmarket.text: Newmarket is a market town in the United Kingdom, anchored by Burwell Castle and Kirtling Tower. Dalham Hall and the Lower Mill add to about five hours, best from June through September.

gem:launceston.text: Launceston is a market town in the United Kingdom near Polyphant, with Kelly House and Crossgate Farmhouse among its old buildings. Treguddick and High Willhays rise nearby, filling about five hours, best from June through September.

gem:tiverton.text: Tiverton is a market town in the United Kingdom built around Tiverton Castle and Knightshayes Court. Bickleigh Castle and Cranmore Castle add two more stops to about five hours, best from June through August.

gem:alcester.text: Alcester is a small village in the United Kingdom, historically a market town, set near Ragley Hall and Coughton Court. Mary Arden's House and the Edstone Aqueduct fill about three hours, ideally June through September.

gem:petersfield.text: Petersfield is a market town in the United Kingdom on the edge of the South Downs National Park. The Vandalian Tower and Chalton Windmill lead a six hour visit, best from June through September, with Emsworth Millpond close by.

gem:liskeard.text: Liskeard is a market town in the United Kingdom near the Hurlers stone circle and Trethevy Quoit. St Cuby's Well and the Duloe stone circle round out a six hour visit, best from June through September.

gem:framlingham.text: Framlingham is a quiet village in the United Kingdom, once a market town, anchored by Framlingham Castle. Glemham Hall and Sir Robert Hitcham's Almshouses fill about three hours, best kept for June through September.

gem:sleaford.text: Sleaford is a market town in the United Kingdom near the Royal Air Force College Cranwell and Sleaford Castle. Heckington Windmill and Culverthorpe Hall round out a six hour visit, best from June through September.

gem:dereham.text: In the United Kingdom, Dereham is a small market town, its skyline marked by East Dereham Windmill. Bylaugh Hall and Letton Hall round out five hours of sightseeing, best planned for June through September.

gem:spalding.text: In the United Kingdom, Spalding is a market town known for Moulton Windmill and the Ayscoughfee Hall Museum. Its gardens and the war memorial fill out five hours of walking, best from June to September.

gem:chard.text: Chard is a historic market town, home to Forde Abbey and Whitestaunton Manor nearby. Six hours covers the abbey grounds, Chard School and Chard Museum, best between June and August.

gem:haverhill.text: Haverhill, a market town, is known for Bartlow Hills and Moyns Park just outside it. Bragg's Mill and Collis Mill round out about five hours here, best in June through September.

gem:bourne.text: Grimsthorpe Castle stands just outside Bourne, a market town built around its own Bourne Castle and Bourne Abbey. Little Bytham lies nearby too, with five hours enough for June through September visits.

gem:highworth.text: In the United Kingdom, Highworth is a village, close to Kelmscott Manor and Buscot Park. Hannington Hall and the Great Coxwell Barn take three hours to see properly, best kept to June through September.

gem:olney.text: Olney is a village, its Tickford Bridge overlooking the river walk each morning. Chicheley Hall and Castle Ashby House sit nearby, three hours enough between June and September.

gem:hailsham.text: Hailsham is a market town, best known for the Long Man of Wilmington carved into Wilmington Downs. Polegate Windmill and Wilmington Priory fill the rest of six hours, June through September the easiest months.

gem:ormskirk.text: Ormskirk is a market town, with Ormskirk Parish Church at its centre and Burscough Priory close by. Formby Beach is a short trip away, and five hours covers the sights between June and August.

gem:stowmarket.text: Stowmarket, a market town, neighbors Needham Market and the grounds of Haughley Castle and Haughley Park. Comb's Wood adds a quiet stop, with the Ipswich Wet Dock a further trip, five hours in total from June through September.

gem:southam.text: Southam is a village, home to Chesterton Windmill and the Ufton Fields Nature Reserve. Shuckburgh Hall and Offchurch Bury lie within easy reach, three hours enough June through September.

gem:market-harborough.text: Market Harborough is a market town, built around Foxton Locks and the old Foxton Inclined Plane. Kelmarsh Hall and The Tower House take up the rest of six hours, best from June to September.

gem:new-romney.text: New Romney is a market town, close to Dungeness Lighthouse and the wide flats of Romney Marsh. Camber Sands is nearby too, and five hours covers the Church of All Saints and the rest, best in June through August.

gem:ilminster.text: Ilminster is a small village, gathered around Barrington Court and Dillington House. Hinton House adds another stop, with Chard Museum and Chard School a short trip further, four hours enough June through September.

gem:pershore.text: Pershore is a quiet village, centred on Pershore Abbey and the church of St John the Baptist. Croome Court and Croome Park lie close by, three hours enough between June and September.

gem:queenborough.text: Queenborough is a village, its waterfront guarded by Queenborough Castle and Garrison Point Fort. Grain Tower and HMS London round out three hours, June through September the calmest months.

gem:beccles.text: Beccles is a market town, its own bell tower rising beside the church of All Saints. Bungay Castle and Mettingham Castle sit nearby, with six hours enough from July through September.

gem:mildenhall.text: Mildenhall is a market town, with Foxhole Heath and the ancient Black Ditches close by. Isleham Priory and Saint Mary's fill out five hours, June through September the best stretch.

gem:cranbrook.text: Cranbrook is a village, within reach of Scotney Castle and Sissinghurst Castle and Garden. Rolvenden Windmill and Pattyndenne Manor round out three hours, best kept to June through August.

gem:coleshill.text: Coleshill is an old village, ringed by Maxstoke Castle, Packington Hall and Packington Old Hall. Castle Bromwich Hall adds a fourth stop, four hours suiting June through August.

gem:newent.text: Newent is a village, edged by Collinpark Wood and Dymock Woods. Foscombe and Ariconium lie further out, with the Kempley Daffodil Meadow rounding out three hours, June through September.

gem:raunds.text: In the United Kingdom, Raunds is an old market town, gathered around Saint Peter's Church and Saint Laurence. Yielden Castle and Drayton House lie further afield, with Finedon Hall rounding out six hours, June through September the calmest stretch.

gem:horncastle.text: Horncastle is a village, near the site of the Battle of Winceby and the hamlet of Minting. Somersby Grange and St Benedict's Church round out three hours, best June through August.

gem:market-deeping.text: Market Deeping is a small market town, with Woodcroft Castle and Northborough Manor House close together. John Clare Cottage and Southorpe Meadow add variety, five hours enough between June and September.

gem:garstang.text: In the United Kingdom, Garstang is a quiet market town, set beside Wyresdale Park and the Inglewhite Congregational Church. St Mary & St Michael and All Saints' Church make up the rest of six hours, June through August the better months.

gem:leyburn.text: In the United Kingdom, Leyburn is a small village, flanked by Middleham Castle and Bolton Castle. Jervaulx Abbey and Semerwater both reward a detour, three hours covering the rest between June and August.

gem:wigton.text: Wigton is a village, with Holmcultram Abbey its main landmark and Skiddaw rising in view. Two hours takes in Cardew Lodge, Cardew House and Boltongate Church, June through August the clearest months.

gem:stanhope.text: In the United Kingdom, Stanhope is a small village, set in the North Pennines beside Stanhope Castle. Greenfoot Quarry and the West Rigg Open Cutting add an industrial edge, three hours enough June through August.

gem:bromyard.text: Bromyard is a quiet village, centred on Old St Bartholomew's Church and the Brockhampton Estate. Whitbourne Hall and Moreton Jeffries Church lie further out, three hours suiting June through September.

gem:kirkbymoorside.text: Kirkbymoorside is a village, close to Helmsley Castle and The Star Inn on the market square. Nunnington Hall and Saint Gregory's Minster round out three hours, best kept to July and August.

gem:whittlesey.text: In the United Kingdom, Whittlesey is a modest market town, within sight of Peterborough Cathedral and the wetlands of Nene Washes. Peterscourt and the Old Guild Hall fill out six hours, June through September the easiest months.

gem:allendale-town.text: Allendale Town is a tiny village, edged by Langley Castle and the wide Allendale Moors. Throssel Hole Buddhist Abbey and Briarwood Banks add a quieter stop, three hours enough June through August.

gem:locri.text: Locri is a town in Italy, built on the ruins of ancient Epizephyrian Locri and Locri Epizephiri. The Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Locri Epizefiri and Locri Cathedral fill about four hours, best in May or June.

gem:beligneux.text: Beligneux is a small village in France, near the Eglise Saint-Maurice de Saint-Maurice-de-Gourdans and the Moulin Girard. The Reservoir du Grand-Large and Lac des Eaux Bleues sit close by, four hours enough from May through September.

gem:winslow.text: Winslow is a village, gathered around Winslow Hall and St Michael and All Angels' Church. Claydon House and Horwood House lie a short trip out, three hours enough between June and September.

PVK.text: Preveza is a coastal town in Greece, shaped by the Battle of Actium and the ruins of Nicopolis. Castle of Bouka and the old battle sites fill about four hours, best in May or June, with Monolithi beach close by.

STR.text: Stuttgart is a city in Germany, home to the Porsche Museum and the Mercedes-Benz Museum. The Fernsehturm Stuttgart and Weissenhof Estate round out seventeen hours of sights, best May through September.

BTS.text: Bratislava is a city in Slovakia, built around Bratislava Castle and Grassalkovich Palace. The Slovak National Museum rounds out seventeen hours of sights, best April, May, June, August or September, with Devinska Kobyla and Zaruby rising nearby.

OTP.text: Bucharest is a city in Romania, dominated by the Palace of the Parliament. Curtea Veche and Cotroceni Palace add historic layers, with Morii Lake and Lake Snagov nearby, seventeen hours of sights best kept to April, May or September.

BEG.text: Belgrade is a city in Serbia, anchored by the National Museum of Serbia and Bajrakli Mosque. The Nikola Tesla Museum and National Theatre in Belgrade round out seventeen hours of sights, best April, May, June or September, with the Danube close by.

gem:doolin.text: Doolin sits on the coast of western Ireland, a village known for music and cliffs. The Cliffs of Moher lead, with The Burren and Doolin Cave nearby, in about two hours. Inis Oirr is an easy ferry ride away June through August, when pub sessions run late.

gem:aveiro.text: Aveiro is a canal city on the Atlantic coast of Portugal, built around a tidal lagoon. The Cathedral of Aveiro and the Ria de Aveiro lead the sights, nine hours total. June through August suits beach days at Costa Nova do Prado or Praia da Barra.

gem:stratford.text: Stratford-upon-Avon sits on the River Avon in Warwickshire, birthplace of William Shakespeare. Shakespeare's Birthplace and the Royal Shakespeare Theatre lead, six hours in all. June through September is best, when the Royal Shakespeare Company performs.

gem:ribe.text: Ribe occupies western South Jutland, Denmark, a medieval town full of old listed houses. Ribe Cathedral and Riberhus Slotsbanke stand out, with Mando and Ribe Vikingecenter close by, six hours. June through August is calmest for the marshes nearby.

gem:matka.text: Matka Canyon is a river gorge area in North Macedonia, good for hiking and Kozjak Lake. Vodno and Skopje Fortress rise nearby, the Millennium Cross above the canyon, in about seven hours. May, June or September suit it best.

gem:aland.text: Aland is a cluster of islands in Finland, given to sailing and quiet coastal villages. The Aland Museum and Aland Maritime Museum anchor a visit, with Pommern and Saint George Church, in four hours. July or August is best, when the islands are liveliest.

gem:bouillon.text: Bouillon rests in Wallonia, Belgium, built around a castle above the Semois river. Bouillon Castle is the main event, in about two hours, with Chateau de Sedan a trip into France. June through September suits it best, when trails are clear.

gem:balchik.text: Balchik is a small Black Sea town in Bulgaria, built into pale cliffs above the shore. Balchik Palace and its botanical garden lead, with Turgut Reis Mosque and Dionysopolis close by, four hours. May, June or September bring mild weather and fewer crowds.

gem:mogeltonder.text: Mogeltonder lies in Denmark, its main street lined with old houses leading to Schackenborg Slot. Hojer Molle and Tonder Kristkirke round out five hours of sights. June through August suits it best, when the streets are quietest.

gem:samso.text: Samso lies in central Denmark, an island between Zealand and Jutland, given to farms and quiet beaches. Kolby and Kanhavekanalen anchor the sights, with Endelave and Tuno close by, six hours in all. June through August is best for calm beaches.

gem:villany.text: Villany is a small wine village in Hungary, its cellars drawing more visitors than any single sight. Siklos Castle and Szarsomlyo hill rise nearby, though two hours covers the village itself. April, May, June or September is best, when the cellars are open.

gem:sarospatak.text: Sarospatak is a historic town in northeastern Hungary, in the Bodrog river valley and known locally as Patak. Lonyay Mansion and the Bridge of National Unity lead, four hours in total. April through September all work well for a visit.

gem:eszterhaza.text: Fertod lies in Hungary, known for baroque style and countryside near Ferto. Neusiedler See-Seewinkel National Park and Fertorakos mithraeum are nearby, two hours for the village. April, May, June or September suits it best.

gem:schiltach.text: Schiltach sits in the Black Forest, Germany, where the Schiltach stream meets the Kinzig river. Alpirsbach Abbey and the Triberg Waterfalls make easy day trips, four hours all told. June through September is greenest for the wooded hills.

gem:syvota-epirus.text: Sivota is a small coastal village in Greece, its bays and beaches drawing families over sightseers. Parga Castle and the ruins at Toryne make good day trips, two hours for the village itself. May or June is best, before the summer crowds arrive.

gem:asbyrgi.text: Asbyrgi is a canyon area in Iceland, part of Jokulsargljufur National Park. Dettifoss and Selfoss lead the waterfalls, with Hafragilsfoss close and Krafla rising beyond, in four hours. June through August is best, when trails are clear of snow.

gem:tarnow.text: Tarnow is a historic city in southern Poland, about eighty kilometers east of Krakow. The Cathedral Basilica and Sanguszko Palace lead, with Saint Martin's Peak nearby, ten hours needed. May through September is liveliest for the historic center.

gem:elblag-canal.text: Elblag Canal lies in Poland, named for the canal that links the surrounding lakes. Druzno and its nature reserve lead the sights, with an old water tower nearby, about five hours. May through August is best, when lake shallows draw birds.

gem:chaves.text: Chaves is a historic town in northern Portugal, near the Spanish border, built on Roman thermal springs. The Castle of Chaves and the Roman Bridge of Chaves lead, with Aquae Flaviae nearby, five hours. May or June brings the mild spa town atmosphere.

gem:densus-church.text: Densus Church stands in Romania, named for its stone church, on the UNESCO tentative list. Corvin Castle and Sarmizegetusa Ulpia Traiana make good day trips, two hours for the village. May through September is easiest for hilltop views nearby.

gem:pobiti-kamani.text: Pobiti Kamani lies in Bulgaria, on the UNESCO tentative list for its natural area. Varna nearby holds the Varna Necropolis and its cathedral, two hours for the village. May, June or September works best, with beaches near Varna easy to add on.

gem:tiraspol.text: Tiraspol is a city in Moldova, known for its statue of Alexander Suvorov and a remote feel. The Church of the Nativity and the Old Believers Pokrovskaya Church lead, eight hours for the center. May or September works best, before or after the summer heat.

gem:soroca.text: Soroca is a town in northeastern Moldova, home to the Soroca Fort and the Thanksgiving Candle monument. The fort and Cetatea Veche lead the sights, with the Cosauti reserve nearby, four hours in all. May, June or September is quietest for a visit.

gem:saharna.text: Saharna Monastery rests in Moldova, its cliffs and caves built around an old monastery. Tipova Monastery and the Cave Chapel lead within the Saharna reserve, in about two hours. May, June or September is driest for the reserve trails.

gem:pitlochry.text: Pitlochry occupies Perth and Kinross, its streets following the River Tummel. Loch Tummel and Ben Vrackie lead the sights, with Killiecrankie close by, about three hours. Ben Vrackie draws hikers June through August, when the glens are greenest.

gem:devils-bridge-wales.text: Devil's Bridge is a small area in Ceredigion, West Wales, centered on a gorge in the Coed Rheidol reserve. The Cambrian Mountains and Pumlumon Fawr rise nearby, seven hours for a full day out. June through August is driest for the reserve trails.

gem:hook-head.text: Hook Head rests on the coast of Ireland, marked by its lighthouse at the point. Slade Castle and Tintern Abbey lead the sights, about two hours, with Waterford a short trip further. June through September makes tides easiest to read.

gem:southwold.text: Southwold is a small seaside town in Suffolk, known for its lighthouse and quiet beaches. The Southwold Lighthouse and Hen Reedbeds lead, with Reydon Wood close by, three hours in all. July, August or September is liveliest for birds in the marshes.

gem:adare.text: Adare sits in County Limerick, Ireland, built at a ford on the River Maigue. Bunratty Castle and King John's Castle lead the sights, with St John's Cathedral close by, in about two hours. Adare is greenest and easiest on foot June through August.

gem:kopacki-rit.text: Kopacki Rit is a small town in Croatia, gateway to a wetland nature park on the Danube. Kopacki Rit Nature Park and the Upper Danube Valley reserve lead, about three hours. April, May, June or September brings migratory birds to the marshes.

gem:dugi-otok.text: Dugi Otok is an island off the coast of Croatia, ringed by nature reserves and quiet beaches. Park prirode Telascica anchors the reserve, with Ugljan, Pasman and Iz visible offshore, four hours in all. May through August keeps Kraljicina plaza calm.

gem:alfriston.text: Alfriston lies in the United Kingdom, an old market town of narrow lanes. The Long Man of Wilmington hill figure and Pevensey Castle sit close by, about four hours. June through September suits walking the countryside best.

gem:kiel.text: Kiel is a maritime city in Schleswig-Holstein, Germany, at the head of the Kieler Forde. The Kunsthalle and Schifffahrtsmuseum lead, with Warleberger Hof close by, ten hours. Falckensteiner Strand fills up June through August, when the harbor is liveliest.

gem:langport.text: Langport rests in Somerset, England, on the edge of the Somerset Levels wetlands. Glastonbury Tor and Glastonbury Abbey rise a short way off, about four hours. June through September is driest for the marshes nearby.

gem:neath.text: Neath rests in Glamorgan, South Wales, built around its own castle and close to Swansea. Neath Castle leads the sights, with Kenfig Castle further out, six hours for both towns. Day trips reach the Swansea and Neath Valleys easiest June through August.

gem:pickering.text: Pickering is a small market town in the United Kingdom, home to its own castle and parish church. Pickering Castle and the church of St Peter and Paul lead, with Beck Isle Museum close by, three hours. Castle Howard adds on nearby, best July or August.

gem:rottweil.text: Rottweil is a historic town in Germany, set between the Black Forest and the Swabian Jura. The elevator test tower dominates the skyline, with Lemberg and Dreifaltigkeitsberg nearby, six hours total. June through September clears the trails around Schonbuch.

gem:bialystok.text: Bialystok is the largest city in northeastern Poland, gateway to the Green Lungs of Poland forests. Bialystok Cathedral and Branicki Palace lead the sights, ten hours in all. May through August makes Biebrza National Park an easy add-on.

gem:piacenza.text: Piacenza is a historic city in Emilia-Romagna, Italy, built around Palazzo Farnese. Piacenza Cathedral and the Palazzo del Comune round out the sights, nine hours for the old center. April, May, June or September is quiet and easy to explore on foot.

gem:holstebro.text: Holstebro is a small town in Denmark, known for its art and history museums. Holstebro Museum and the Holstebro Kunstmuseum lead the sights, with Tvis Abbey and Tvis Molle close by, five hours total. June through August suits a relaxed pace best.

gem:sumeg.text: Sumeg is a village in Hungary, gathered below Sumeg Castle on its hill. Saint Anne Round Church in Kallosd and the Somlo and Csobanc hills round out about two hours, though buses are scarce. May through September is the season to come.

gem:opole.text: Opole is a city in Poland built around the Roman Catholic Diocese of Opole, with roughly ten hours to see it all. Czarnowasy and Turawskie Lake make easy half-day trips, and trains and buses run well. May through September is the easiest stretch.

gem:venlo.text: Venlo sits on the German border in the Netherlands, anchored by Offenbeek and Romerhuis and worth about ten hours. Sint-Martinusbasiliek and the Stadhuis fill an old town walk, with connections that run well. May through September works well.

gem:laval.text: Laval is a cathedral city in France, built around Laval Cathedral and the Chateau de Laval. Port-du-Salut Abbey rewards a short drive, and about ten hours covers the sights. May through September works well, with good transport.

gem:skara.text: Skara is a cathedral town in Sweden, anchored by Skara Cathedral and the Skara Sommarland park. Lake Hornborga and Varnhem Abbey are easy add-ons, and six hours takes in the center. June through August is prime time, with reliable transport.

gem:calatafimi.text: Calatafimi lies in Italy, a village near Segesta and Calatubo Castle, with Monte Polizzo and Mount Bonifato also close by. Two hours covers the main sights, though a car helps since buses are scarce. May or June is the time to come.

gem:wolfertschwenden.text: Wolfertschwenden lies in Germany, a village near Ottobeuren Abbey and St Lorenz Basilica, with Kempten Abbey also within reach and about four hours for the loop. Public transport is poor. June through August suits it best.

gem:balatonlelle.text: Balatonlelle is a village in Hungary on Lake Balaton, with Tihany Abbey and the Csobanc hill within reach across the water. Two hours covers the village itself, though a car or boat helps since transport is thin. May, June or September is the time to visit.

gem:bad-salzuflen.text: Bad Salzuflen is a city in Germany with close to ten hours of sightseeing on offer, though highlights like Bahnhof Herford and Herforder Munster actually sit in neighboring Herford. May through September is the easiest stretch.

gem:oosterend.text: Oosterend sits in the Netherlands, a village near Wieringen and the Dunes of Texel National Park. Noorderhaaks and the Eierland Lighthouse round out about three hours, and buses run rarely here. June through August is the season to come.

gem:belfort.text: Belfort is a city in France built around Belfort Cathedral and the Citadelle de Belfort, worth close to ten hours. Fort de Roppe adds a history detour, and Ballon d'Alsace rises nearby. June through September suits a visit best, with good transport.

gem:covilha.text: Covilha is a town in Portugal at the foot of Torre, the high point of the Serra da Estrela. The Serra da Estrela Natural Park and the old Muralhas da Cidade da Covilha fill about four hours. May, June or September is the time to go.

gem:strumica.text: Strumica is a town in North Macedonia known for Kolesino Falls and the Cathedral of Assumption of Blessed Virgin Mary. Veljusa adds half a day more, with six hours a fair estimate and transport that runs well. April, May, September and October suit it best.

gem:larisa.text: Larisa is a city in Greece where Yeni Mosque and the First Archaeological Theatre of Larisa anchor about seven hours. Mount Ossa is within reach for a longer day, and connections are reliable. April or May is the pick of the year.

gem:malmkoping.text: Malmkoping lies in Sweden, a village by the Baven lake, with Altaren, Naten and Traskaten nearby for a slow three hours. Dunkers socken rounds out the area, though a car helps since buses are scarce. June through August works best.

gem:grolloo.text: Grolloo lies in the Netherlands, a village near the Drents Museum and the Hondsrug ridge. Molen van Rolde and Hunebed D16 Balloo fill out about four hours, and 't Gasselterveld lake is close for a break. June through August is the time to come.

gem:ljungby.text: Ljungby is a town in Sweden where Ljungby Kyrka and the Smaland Runic Inscription 35 lead about five hours within Sunnerbo. Kanna socken and Tutaryds socken lie within the parish, and transport links are solid. June through August is prime time.

gem:male-brezno.text: Male Brezno lies in Czechia, a village near the Ceske Stredohori hills and Bukova hora TV Tower. PR Vrabinec rounds out about four hours, and Milesovka mountain rises close by, though transport is thin. May through September is the season to pick.

gem:alatskivi.text: Alatskivi sits in Estonia, a village on Lake Peipus, home to Alatskivi loss and the smaller Alatskivi kirik church. Two hours covers the castle grounds, and a car is worth arranging since buses are scarce. June through August is when to come.

gem:carlow.text: Carlow is a town in Ireland with Carlow Castle at its center and Ballyloughan and Ballymoon castles a short drive out. Kilkea Castle rounds out about four hours, and transport runs well. June through August is when to visit.

gem:mirandela.text: Mirandela is a town in Portugal built around the Castle of Mirandela and the old Ponte Velha sobre o rio Tua bridge. Paco dos Tavoras adds to about four hours, with transport that runs well. May is the one month singled out.

gem:pegeia.text: Pegeia is a village in Cyprus near Paphos Castle and the Tombs of the Kings. Paphos Archaeological Park and Saranta Kolones fill about two hours, and Coral bay and Lighthouse Beach suit an afternoon after. April or May is the time to visit.

gem:mesolongi.text: Mesolongi is a town in Greece by the Messolongi Lagoon, with Calydon and Pleuron among about four hours of nearby ruins. Varasova and Aracynthus round out the list, and transport is good. April or May is the pick of the year.

gem:targoviste.text: Targoviste is a city in Romania where the Chindia Tower and Dealu Monastery anchor about eight hours. Casa-Atelier Gheorghe Petrascu rounds things out, with transport that runs well. May, June or September suits it best.

gem:dobrna.text: Dobrna is a village in Slovenia near Vojnik and the Rogla hills, with Vitanje and Nova Cerkev filling out about three hours. Lake Smartno and Lake Velenje lie within reach for a swim, though buses are scarce here. May through August suits it best.

gem:dobra.text: Dobra is a village in Poland where the Zalew Mrozyczka lake is the local draw, though landmarks like the Archcathedral Basilica of St Stanislaus Kostka belong to nearby Lodz. Dobra itself takes about three hours. May through September is the season to come.

gem:sainte-menehould.text: Sainte-Menehould lies in France, a Petites Cites de Caractere village built around the Eglise Notre-Dame-du-Chateau de Sainte-Menehould. The Chateau de Braux-Sainte-Cohiere rounds out about two hours. June through September suits it best.

gem:campodimele.text: Campodimele is a Bandiera Arancione village in Italy ringed by Monte Appiolo, Monte Crispi and Monte Faggeto. The Santuario Madonna della Civita anchors about two hours, and Lago di Fondi lies within reach. May or June is the time to go.

gem:oriolo.text: Oriolo is a village in Italy, named among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, with Monte Soprano rising above it. The pinete di Montegiordano pine woods lie nearby for a short walk, two hours in all, though buses run rarely. May, June or September suits it best.

gem:brugnato-it.text: Brugnato is a village in Italy centered on the Concattedrale dei Santi Pietro, Lorenzo e Colombano. San Francesco adds to about three hours, and Guvano beach lies within reach, with transport that runs well. May through August is the time to come.

gem:travesio.text: Travesio is a village in Italy, listed among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, built around the Castello di Pinzano. San Remigio rounds out about three hours, and Lago di Cornino sits nearby. May through July suits it best.

gem:guardia-perticara.text: Guardia Perticara lies in Italy, a village named among I Borghi piu belli d'Italia, its Centro storico and Le Serre covered in about two hours. Lago di Pietra del Pertusillo lies within reach. May, June or September is the time to visit.

gem:grantham.text: Grantham is a market town in the United Kingdom, gathered around Belton House and Stoke Rochford Hall. Grantham House rounds out about five hours, with transport that runs well. June through September makes for an easy visit.

gem:sudbury.text: Long Melford and Gainsborough's House sit at the edge of Sudbury, a market town in the United Kingdom good for about six hours. Holy Trinity and Melford Hall fill out the rest, and connections are reliable. June through September is the season to come.

gem:wadebridge.text: Wadebridge is a market town in the United Kingdom, its railway station and Three Holes Cross the start of roughly three hours. Daymer Bay is close enough for an afternoon on sand, and transport runs well. June through September works best.

gem:coggeshall.text: Coggeshall Abbey and the Coggeshall Grange Barn anchor Coggeshall, a market town in the United Kingdom good for about three hours. Faulkbourne Hall lies a short way out, with transport that runs well. June through September works well.

gem:ashburton.text: Buckfast Abbey and the Haytor Granite Tramway put Ashburton, a market town in the United Kingdom, within reach of about four hours. Meadfoot Beach is close for a swim, and connections are reliable. June through August is the season to pick.

gem:north-walsham.text: North Walsham is a market town in the United Kingdom where Gunton Hall and Paston Great Barn lead roughly five hours. Bromholm Priory and Honing Hall complete the list, with good transport. July and August is the season to pick.

gem:sandy.text: Sandy, a market town in the United Kingdom, is built around Wardon Abbey and Eastcotts Castle, good for about six hours. Sandy Warren rounds out the day, and transport runs well. June through September works best.

gem:haslemere.text: Haslemere is a market town in the United Kingdom near Headley Grange and Undershaw, two of about five hours worth of sights. Shulbrede Priory completes the list, with reliable transport. June through September suits it best.

gem:callington.text: Callington is a market town in the United Kingdom, anchored by Cotehele and Cadsonbury. Sylvia's Meadow and Dupath Well round out the sights, which take about three hours and reward a visit between June and September.

gem:buckfastleigh.text: Buckfast Abbey is the reason most people stop in Buckfastleigh, a historic market town in the United Kingdom. Totnes Castle and Dartington Hall are close enough to add to the day, four hours in all, best planned for June, July or August.

gem:bungay.text: Bungay Castle gives this United Kingdom market town its name, backed up by Mettingham Castle and Ditchingham Hall close by. The sights take about three hours, best done June through September.

gem:pocklington.text: Pocklington is a market town in the United Kingdom where All Saints Church anchors the old center. Allerthorpe Common and the walk out to Everingham fill a full five hours, best saved for July or August.

gem:knighton.text: Knighton pairs two castles, Brampton Bryan and Clun, with the parkland of Stanage Park and Bedstone Court. It sits on the River Lugg, and the three-hour circuit suits June through August.

gem:malton.text: Castle Howard is the big name near Malton, a United Kingdom market town, with Kirkham Priory and Birdsall House adding to the grounds. The visit runs about three hours, best in July or August.

gem:swaffham.text: Swaffham sits close to Castle Acre, where the castle and priory draw most visitors, with West Acre Priory and Bailey Gate nearby. The visit runs about three hours, any time from June to September works well.

gem:louth.text: Louth sits on the edge of the Lincolnshire Wolds, a United Kingdom market town built around Louth Abbey and St James's Church. Louth railway station and the Wolds walks take about five hours, best kept to July or August.

gem:needham-market.text: Needham Market is a small United Kingdom market town near Stowmarket, with Shrubland Hall and Great Bricett Hall the grander stops. Comb's Wood adds a quieter hour, three in total, and June through September fits best.

gem:aylsham.text: Aylsham is ringed by grand halls: Blickling, Wolterton, Gunton and Bolwick all sit close by, with Salle Park rounding things out. The halls take about three hours to see properly, ideally in July or August.

gem:shefford.text: Wrest Park is the centerpiece outside Shefford, backed by Cainhoe Castle and Wardon Abbey. St Mary's Church at Lower Gravenhurst is worth the detour too, and four hours from June to September covers all of it.

gem:halesworth.text: Halesworth leans toward nature more than most United Kingdom market towns, with Reydon Wood and Hen Reedbeds close by. Sibton Abbey, Heveningham Hall and Holton Windmill fill the rest of a three-hour visit, best June to September.

gem:steyning.text: Steyning is a United Kingdom market town under Cissbury Ring and Edburton Castle Ring, with Bramber Castle just down the road. Jarvis Hall and Brighton City Airport are within reach too, six hours in all, best from June to September.

gem:great-torrington.text: Great Torrington centers on Rosemoor Garden, with Bideford Long Bridge and the hamlet of Frithelstock close by. Orleigh Court and Potheridge round things out, with three hours covering the whole visit between June and September.

gem:holt.text: Holt has two castles to its name, Baconsthorpe and Gresham, plus Blakeney Chapel further out. Kelling Heath and Kelling Hall add an easy extra hour, four in total, best in July or August.

gem:attleborough.text: Attleborough sits between two windmills, at Great Ellingham and Old Buckenham, with Wymondham Abbey the grander stop nearby. Buckenham Castle and Tacolneston Hall stretch the day to five hours, best from June to September.

gem:holsworthy.text: Holsworthy keeps its United Kingdom market town character around the Market Cross and St Petrock's Church. Grimscott lies just outside, and two hours anytime from June to September takes in the lot.

gem:spilsby.text: Spilsby is best known for Bolingbroke Castle at Old Bolingbroke, just outside town. Gunby Hall, Hanby Hall and the chapel at Raithby Hall fill out three hours, best tried June through August.

gem:rothwell.text: The Triangular Lodge is the odd landmark that puts Rothwell on the map, with Boughton House and Kelmarsh Hall the bigger estates nearby. Birch Spinney and Mawsley Marsh suit a slower morning, three hours altogether, best June to September.

gem:brigg.text: Brigg has two parish churches worth the stop, St Mary's and St Andrew's, plus Elsham Hall and the Wrawby Post Windmill nearby. Hibaldstow Bridge and the stops at Barnetby and Redbourne round out three hours, best June to September.

gem:struer.text: Struer is a market town in Denmark, built around Struer Kirke and the old mill at Aa Molle. Gimsing Kirke and Humlum Kirke sit close by, with the museum rounding out five hours, best between June and August.

gem:wiveliscombe.text: Wiveliscombe is surrounded by manor houses, Cothay Manor and Nynehead Court chief among them, with Fitzhead Court and Sandhill Park close by. Dunkery Hill rises nearby too, and four hours across June to August covers the estates.

gem:reepham.text: Reepham centers on three old churches, Saint Mary the Virgin, Saint Michael and All Angels, and Saint Faith's. Salle Park and Bylaugh Hall sit a short trip further out, three hours in all, best July or August.

gem:robertsbridge.text: Bodiam Castle is the biggest draw near Robertsbridge, with Battle Abbey and Senlac Hill close behind it. Bateman's rounds out three hours of sightseeing, best done June through August.

gem:storrington.text: Storrington sits below Cissbury Ring and Chanctonbury Ring, with Amberley Castle, Parham House and Castle Goring the grander stops. Six hours between June and September covers the ground, with Climping Beach and Littlehampton East Beach close by after.

gem:llanfairpwllgwyngyll.text: Llanfairpwllgwyngyll centers on St Gredifael's Church and St Mary's Church, with Gaerwen and Holland Arms stations nearby. Snowdon and Carnedd Llewelyn rise close by, and four hours from June to August covers the marsh at Malltraeth.

gem:brixen.text: Brixen centers on its Duomo, with the fortress at Fortezza and the abbey at Novacella just outside town. Sassolungo and the Kronplatz rise nearby, and six hours between June and September covers the town and the peaks.

gem:quartu-sant-elena.text: Quartu Sant'Elena sits beside Cagliari, with the Torre dell'Elefante and Teatro Lirico as the draw. The Orto Botanico and the Museo Archeologico Nazionale round out about ten hours, best from May to August, with Poetto beach nearby.

gem:loreto.text: Loreto is built around the Apostolic Palace, with the Museo Civico Villa Colloredo Mels and Chiesa San Vito close by. The Museo della Fisarmonica rounds out three hours, best from May to August, with Spiaggia Urbani nearby.

gem:albenga.text: Albenga centers on the Museo navale romano and the amphitheater grounds at Albingaunum. Torre Oddo and the former church of San Domenico add to a six-hour visit, best in May, June, July or September, with Laigueglia and Andora beaches close by.

gem:frontignan.text: Frontignan has more chapels than most towns its size, led by the Abbaye Saint-Felix-de-Montceau and Saint Paul's church. The chapels at Vic-la-Gardiole and Balaruc-les-Bains stretch the visit to five hours, best kept to May or June.

gem:nettuno.text: Nettuno sits next to Anzio, with Forte Sangallo and the Sicily-Rome American Cemetery marking the Battle of Anzio history. The Santuario di Santa Maria Goretti rounds out five hours, best from May to August, with Fanciulla d'Anzio beach close by.

gem:avigliana.text: Avigliana has two lakes of its own, Lago Grande and Lago Piccolo, right beside Monte Musine. Saint Michael's Abbey and the Castello di Rivoli make for a fuller six-hour day, best in May, June or September.

gem:kuhmo.text: Kuhmo carries a UNESCO Creative Cities Network label, built on the Kuhmo Arts Centre and the wartime history at the Kuhmo Winter War museum. Tuupala Museum and Tuupalan kartano round out two hours, best kept to June or July.

REU.text: Reus pairs Ferrari Land with a cluster of grand houses, Casa Navas, Casa Pinyol and Casa Rull among them. Excellent public transport makes the ten-hour spread easy, best from May to August, with Platja Altafulla within reach.

CUF.text: Cuneo centers on the Cattedrale di Santa Maria del Bosco and the Sinagoga di Cuneo. Cime du Gelas and Punta Marguareis rise within reach too, and eight hours between May, June and September covers the town and the nearest peaks.

CWL.text: Cardiff Castle and the Millennium Stadium anchor this United Kingdom city, with Llandaff Cathedral and Castell Coch adding to a seventeen-hour spread, best spread over several days from June to September. Pen y Fan is within reach for a mountain day.

VAR.text: Varna layers the Varna Archaeological Museum and Varna Necropolis over a coastal city built around Lake Varna. The aquarium and the Euxinograd grounds add to a seventeen-hour spread, best anywhere from May to September.

LCA.text: Larnaca pairs the Hala Sultan Tekke with the ruins of Ancient Kition and the Church of Saint Lazarus in the old town. Larnaca Castle and the Kamares Aqueduct round out eight hours, best kept to April or May, with the Larnaca Salt Lake close by.

TMP.text: Tampere sits between two lakes, Nasijarvi and Pyhajarvi, with the Moomin Museum and Sarkanniemi as the family draws. Tampere Orthodox Church and Tampere Theatre round out about ten hours, best from June to August, helped by excellent transport.

gem:eger.text: The Castle of Eger crowns this wine town in Hungary, above the Basilica in Eger and cellars cut into the hillside below. Eszterhazy Karoly University and the vineyards on Nagy-Eged hegy add to a visit of about nine hours, best made April through September.

gem:masuria.text: The Masurian Lakes spread across Poland, centered on Sniardwy and Lake Ros for sailing. Mazurski Park Krajobrazowy and Jezioro Nidzkie bring nature and quiet, with five hours enough between May and August.

gem:savonlinna.text: Olavinlinna castle rises from the water at Savonlinna, a lake town in eastern Finland known for music and quiet. Savonlinna Cathedral and Rauhalinna make for four unhurried hours, best planned for June through August.

gem:cachtice.text: Cachtice Castle stands above a small village in Slovakia, within reach of the White Carpathians and Beckov Castle. The three hours needed for the ruins and nearby Povazsky Inovec suit good transport links, best from May to September.

gem:skyros.text: Skyros is a quiet island in Greece with villages and beaches near Erinia and Platy Skyrou. The Monastery of Saint George and Kalamitsa round out a short visit of about four hours, best made June through August.

gem:kea.text: Kea is a hiking and diving island in Greece, with the ruins of Karthaia and the old town of Iulis holding most interest. Fykiada beach and the mesolithic site at Maroulas add five more hours, best from June through September, though transport stays limited.

gem:risor.text: Risor is a coastal village in Norway, near Lyngor Lighthouse and Sandoya. Two hours suit Risor Church and Sondeled Church nearby, best kept to June or July since transport stays limited.

gem:crooked-forest.text: The Crooked Forest is a stand of bent pine trees in Poland, prized for its quiet countryside setting. The parish churches of nearby Gryfino stretch a visit to about five hours, best planned May through September, with lake Steklno close by.

gem:pavilosta.text: Pavilosta is a small surf town on the coast of Latvia, its beaches watched over by Akmenrags lighthouse. Grinu Nature Reserve and the old stones at Dzenu upurakmens take up four hours, best kept to June through August.

gem:rummu-quarry.text: Rummu Quarry is a flooded quarry in Estonia, popular for diving and lake adventure. Padise klooster and Keila Waterfall lie nearby, with Toompea hill farther off, and five hours covers a summer visit from June to August.

gem:zalipie.text: Zalipie is a quiet countryside village in Poland known for local art traditions. The parish churches of nearby villages and Rezerwat Gory Wschodnie fill three hours, best visited between May and September.

gem:daugavpils.text: Daugavpils Fortress anchors this historic city in Latvia, alongside Martin Luther Cathedral and the Daugavpils Theatre. The lake beach at Stropu ezers adds an afternoon to nine hours of sightseeing, best planned for June through August.

gem:alcoutim.text: Castelo de Alcoutim overlooks the Guadiana International Bridge in this remote village in Portugal. The Castle of Mertola stands nearby, and five quiet hours cover the ruins best between April and May.

gem:belmonte.text: Castle of Belmonte watches over this quiet town in Portugal, at the foot of the Serra da Estrela mountains. The Cathedral of Guarda lies nearby, and five hours suit a visit timed for May or June, with good transport links throughout.

gem:berca-mud-volcanoes.text: The Berca Mud Volcanoes bubble up in a remote corner of Romania, centered on the Paclele Mici Mud volcanoes. Ratesti Monastery and the village of Scortoasa round out four hours, best saved for May, June or September.

gem:tyulenovo.text: Tyulenovo is a quiet diving village on the coast of Bulgaria, close to Shabla Lighthouse and Kaliakra. Durankulak lake and its archaeological complex add depth to a short two-hour stop, best made June through August.

gem:st-abbs.text: St Abbs is a small diving village on the coast of the United Kingdom, next to St Abb's Head National Nature Reserve. Coldingham Priory and Berwick Castle round out three hours nearby, best fit into June through September.

gem:waterford.text: Reginald's Tower stands on the waterfront at Waterford, a historic city in Ireland, near the Cathedral of the Most Holy Trinity. Portal tombs at Knockeen and Gaulstown lie within reach, and eight hours suit a summer visit from June through August.

gem:mirusha.text: Mirusha Waterfalls tumble through a family-friendly hiking area in Kosovo, near Radoniq Lake. Budisavci Monastery adds a quiet stop to three hours of walking, best planned for May, June or September.

gem:mamaia-sat.text: Mamaia-Sat is a small beach village on the coast of Romania, next to Lake Siutghiol. The Carol I Mosque and the old quarter of Tomis lie nearby, filling out two easy hours between May and September.

gem:ingolstadt.text: Ingolstadt centers on the Liebfrauenmunster and the old Kreuztor gate, a city in Germany with history at every turn. The museum mobile and the Oppidum of Manching add a full day of about ten hours, best timed for May through September.

gem:coningsby.text: Tattershall Castle and Bolingbroke Castle sit within reach of Coningsby, a village in the United Kingdom. Kirkstead Abbey and the Dogdyke Engine round out three hours nearby, best kept to June through September.

gem:ootmarsum.text: Ootmarsum centers its old streets on the Basilica of St Plechelm, a village in the Netherlands. Huis Singraven and its watermill fill four hours nearby, with Het Hulsbeek lake close by, best from May through August.
