gem:metsovo.text: Metsovo is a mountain village in Greece known for its wine and food, close to Pindus National Park. The Averoff Gallery and the slopes of Lakmos fill about two hours. Transport is poor, so June is best tackled with a rental car.

gem:shiroka-laka.text: Shiroka Laka is a quiet mountain village in Bulgaria, set among the Rhodope Mountains near Golyam Perelik. Two hours takes in the Uhlovitsa Cave and nearby Chepelare. Transport is poor, so driving in June through September works better.

gem:krushuna-falls.text: Krushuna Falls is a small village in Bulgaria built around its waterfalls, led by the Devetashka cave and Krushunksi waterfall. The cascades at Urushka maara add about two hours. Public transport is thin, so April, May, June, or September call for a car.

gem:lough-hyne.text: Lough Hyne is a quiet coastal village in Ireland, near Dunasead Castle and the ancient Drombeg stone circle. Two hours covers the main sights, with Sherkin Island and Mount Gabriel further out. Transport is poor, so June to August is easiest by car.

gem:gavle.text: Gavle, a historic city in Sweden, is centered on Gavle Castle and its old town. The Swedish Railway Museum and the Joe Hill museum nearby fill out about ten hours. The lake of Storsjon and good transport make June through August the easiest season.

gem:gie-en.text: Giessen is a historic city in Germany, home to the well-known Mathematikum and the ruins of Burg Gleiberg. Ten hours covers Vetzberg and a stop at Theater Giessen. Good transport and the lake at Hattsteinweiher make May through September comfortable.

gem:huelva.text: Huelva, a historic city in Spain, centers on the Catedral de la Merced and the Barrio Obrero. The Museo Provincial de Huelva and the Monasterio de Santa Maria de la Rabida fill out about ten hours. Playa La Antilla is nearby, April and May are best.

gem:serres.text: Serres is a historic city in Greece, its skyline marked by the Mehmet Bey Mosque and the Zincirli Mosque. The sights take about nine hours, including the Tower of Prodromos monastery. Transport is good, April, May, or October suit a visit best.

gem:gniezno.text: Gniezno is a historic city in Poland, led by the Primatial Basilica Metropolitan Cathedral of Gniezno. The Saint John the Baptist church in Gniezno rounds out about nine hours. Transport is good, and Jezioro Powidzkie suits a stay from May to September.

gem:skien.text: Skien is a historic city in Norway with several notable churches, led by Skien kirke and Gjerpen kirke. Borgestad kirke and Frogner Hovedgard round out about nine hours. The lakes of Norsjo and Farris make June through August the best season.

gem:rijssen.text: Rijssen is a small town in the Netherlands, close to the Sallandse Heuvelrug National Park and Holten. Six hours covers the Schildkerk and Pelmolen Ter Horst nearby. Transport is good, June through August is the easiest season to explore.

RNS.text: Rennes anchors the Brittany region of France, its center built around Rennes Cathedral and the Parlement de Bretagne. The Museum of Fine Arts of Rennes and Parc du Thabor round out about ten hours. Transport runs smoothly, May through September is best.

IAS.text: Iasi is a historic metro area in Romania, led by the Palace of Culture and the Trei Ierarhi Monastery. The full list, including the Frumoasa Monastery, takes about seventeen hours. Transport is excellent, best used May, June, or September.

ACI.text: Alderney is a quiet, remote island in the United Kingdom, ringed by the rocky outcrops of Ortac and Burhou, with about five hours covering Fort Tourgis and a ride on the Alderney Railway. Transport runs a limited schedule, so June through August works best.

gem:bitola.text: Bitola is an old Ottoman and Roman city in North Macedonia, with the ruins of Heraclea Lyncestis just outside town. Ten hours covers the Clock Tower of Bitola and Co-Cathedral of the Sacred Heart. Lake Strezevo is nearby, May, June, or September are best.

gem:ventspils.text: Ventspils is a coastal family town in Latvia, built around Ventspils Castle, with about four hours for the Church of Saint Nicholas in Ventspils and Ventspils Olimpiskais Stadions. Transport is limited, so June through August is easier by car.

gem:vestmanna.text: Vestmanna is a small coastal village in the Faroe Islands, a gateway to Streymoy. The sights take about three hours, with Vagar and Eysturoy visible across the water. Transport is poor, so June through August calls for a car or a tour.

gem:inishbofin.text: Inishbofin is a quiet, remote island off Ireland, within sight of Clare Island and Inishturk, with about four hours covering the sights and the beaches of Old Head Beach and Cross Strand. Transport is limited, June through August is the easiest season.

gem:hum-istria.text: Hum is a tiny medieval village in Croatia, with Holy Trinity Church at its center and under three hundred people. Two hours covers nearby Pazin Castle and the peak of Vojak on Ucka. Transport is poor, so June through August is simplest with a car.

gem:munster.text: Munster is a historic metro area in Germany, home to the Westphalian State Museum of Art and Cultural History. Burg Hulshoff and Schloss Munster round out about seventeen hours. Good transport and Halterner Talsperre make May through September easiest.

gem:ostrava.text: Ostrava is a historic city in Czechia. Top billing goes to Silesian Ostrava Castle and the Cathedral of the Divine Saviour, and Olesna Reservoir and the Lysa hora hills suit a side trip. Ten hours between May and September cover it well.

gem:gyula.text: Gyula is a small town in Hungary. Gyula Castle anchors the center, and the Jokai Theatre and the Church of the Assumption of Mary round out about three hours. April, May, June and September are best.

gem:almelo.text: Almelo is a city in Overijssel in the Netherlands. Bellinckhof and Hondeborg draw the most visitors, and Het Hulsbeek lake sits nearby. Ten hours cover the city, best between May and August.

BZR.text: Beziers is a wine city on the coast of southern France. The Pont Vieux and the Tunnel de Malpas are the standout stops, worth about ten hours. Plage Serignan naturiste lies close by, best from May to September.

LBA.text: Leeds Bradford is the gateway to Leeds, a major financial centre in Britain outside London. Headingley and the Leeds Corn Exchange come first, with Temple Newsam House filling seventeen hours. June through August suit the visit best.

LNZ.text: Linz sits on the Danube in Austria as capital of Upper Austria. The Ars Electronica Center and the New Cathedral come first, and the Old Cathedral and Brucknerhaus wait close behind. May through September, over about ten hours, covers it well.

gem:plzen.text: Pilsen gave the world the pilsner style of beer and holds the European Capital of Culture title. Techmania and the Great Synagogue top the list, with the Siege of Pilsen history nearby. Ten hours from May through September fit it all in.

gem:rumsiskes.text: Rumsiskes is a countryside area in Lithuania, best reached on a day trip from Kaunas. Kaunas Castle and the Kaunas Cathedral Basilica sit nearby, with the Ninth Fort further out. May through August bring the best weather, with about six hours needed.

gem:enniskillen.text: Enniskillen is the county town of Fermanagh in Northern Ireland, on the River Erne. Enniskillen Castle and Devenish Island top the visit, with Monea Castle worth the detour. Lough Erne suits a stay of about four hours between June and August.

FMM.text: Memmingen is a town in Bavaria, Germany. Ottobeuren Abbey and Kloster Buxheim come first, and the MEWO Kunsthalle plus Schloss Eisenburg follow. June through September work well for the six hours it takes, close to the Allgau.

AAL.text: Aalborg anchors North Jutland in Denmark. Lindholm Hoje and Kunsten stand out first, and Aalborg Zoo suits families with more time. Ten hours cover the city, best between June and August.

MMX.text: Malmo faces Copenhagen across the strait as capital of Scania in Sweden. The Turning Torso towers over the skyline, and Malmo Castle and Malmo Opera fill out seventeen hours. Ribersborg Beach suits a swim between June and August.

gem:szeged.text: Szeged sits in Csongrad-Csanad County in Hungary. The Votive Church and Szeged Synagogue come first, ahead of Domotor Tower. April, June or September fit a nine-hour visit best, ending with a bowl of fish soup.

gem:parnu.text: Parnu is a seaside spa town on the coast of Estonia. Tallinn Gate and Ammende Villa anchor the old quarter, with Punane torn and Endla Teater nearby. Parnu Beach draws crowds from June to August, in about six hours.

gem:liepaja.text: Liepaja stretches along the Baltic coast of Latvia. The Holy Trinity Cathedral and Liepaja Theatre draw the most attention, with Karosta and Liepaja Lake close by. June and August suit an eight-hour visit best.

gem:cricova.text: Cricova is a quiet wine village in Moldova, close to Chisinau. The National Library of Moldova and Nativity of Christ Cathedral sit nearby in Chisinau, with the Triumphal Arch too. May, June and September work best for the two hours it takes.

gem:bielefeld.text: Bielefeld anchors North Rhine-Westphalia in Germany. Rathaus and Stadttheater sit by the Sparrenburg fortress, with Neustadter Marienkirche nearby. June through September suit a full seventeen-hour visit.

gem:minden.text: Minden is a cathedral city in Germany, built around the Mindener Dom. The Minden Aqueduct and Bahnhof Minden round out about ten hours. Evangelische Kirche Hausberge is a short trip away, best between May and September.

gem:hassleholm.text: Hassleholm is a small town in Sweden, built around Finjasjon lake. Hovdala slott leads the sights, with Ignaberga nya kyrka and Finja kyrka nearby. June and August suit a five-hour visit best.

EGC.text: Bergerac sits in the Dordogne in France, a town built on wine. Chateau de Monbazillac and Chateau de Tiregand anchor the estates, with Chateau de Bridoire nearby. May to September suit a five-hour visit among the vines.

LIG.text: Limoges anchors the Limousin region of France as a UNESCO Creative Cities Network member. The Gare de Limoges-Benedictins and the Limoges Cathedral come first. June through September, across about ten hours, takes in the city.

PLQ.text: Palanga is a beach resort town on the Baltic coast of Lithuania. Palangos tiltas and the Palanga Amber Museum draw visitors first, with the Sventoji lighthouse close by. June, July and August are busiest, with about four hours needed.

OSI.text: Osijek leads the Slavonia region of eastern Croatia. The Museum of Slavonia and the Croatian National Theatre anchor a visit, with the Osijek Zoo and Aquarium nearby. April, May, June or September suit an eight-hour visit best.

gem:haapsalu.text: Haapsalu is a quiet spa town along the western coast of Estonia. Haapsalu Episcopal Castle anchors the old quarter, with the Silma Nature Reserve nearby. July and August suit a five-hour visit best, though buses run thin.

BDS.text: Brindisi sits on the Adriatic coast of Apulia in southern Italy. Castello Alfonsino and the Brindisi cathedral front the waterfront, with San Pietro degli Schiavoni nearby. May or June suit a nine-hour visit best.

RDZ.text: Rodez is a town in the Aveyron department of France. The Rodez Cathedral towers over the old streets, with Musee Denys-Puech and the musee Soulages nearby. June through September, across about six hours, covers the circuit.

KTW.text: Katowice anchors the Silesian Voivodeship in Poland and belongs to the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. Nikiszowiec and Giszowiec come first, with the Silesian Museum a short stop after. May through September fits the ten hours needed.

OUL.text: Oulu is the largest city in Northern Finland and holds the European Capital of Culture title. Oulun tuomiokirkko and Oulu Castle come first, with Hupisaaret park close by. Ten hours is plenty, best in July.

gem:boras.text: Boras sits in Vastergotland in Sweden, a city built on its textile trade. The Textile Museum of Boras and Boras museum tell the story, with Boras Arena nearby. June and August suit a nine-hour visit best.

gem:haskovo.text: Haskovo sits on the Upper Thracian Plain in Bulgaria. The Monument of the Holy Mother of God and the Church of the Assumption come first, with Charshiyska Mosque close by. Six hours cover the center, best in April, May, September or October.

gem:benalmadena.text: Benalmadena is a coastal town in Spain, dotted with old watchtowers. Torre Bermeja and Torre Quebrada draw the eye first, with Torre Molinos a short stop away. May and August suit a nine-hour visit best.

gem:magomadas.text: Magomadas is a small village in Italy near Bosa, home to about 450 people. The Castello di Serravalle and Saint Peter church sit nearby in Bosa. Bosa train station serves the area, best in April, June or September.

gem:suni.text: Suni counts just over eleven hundred residents near Bosa in Italy. The Chiesa di Nostra Signora de Sos Regnos Altos and the Castello di Serravalle sit nearby in Bosa. May, June and September make for the calmest visits.

gem:flussio.text: Flussio counts fewer than five hundred residents, tucked into Italy near Bosa. The Castello di Serravalle and the Concattedrale dell'Immacolata Concezione sit nearby in Bosa. April, May, June and September suit the trip best.

gem:montresta.text: Montresta has just over five hundred residents near Bosa in Italy. The Chiesa di Nostra Signora de Sos Regnos Altos and Saint Peter church sit nearby in Bosa. May, June and September suit the trip best.

REG.text: Reggio Calabria sits on the coast of Italy across from Sicily. Arena dello Stretto and Villa Genoese Zerbi front the waterfront, with Teatro Francesco Cilea nearby. May or June, in about ten hours, covers the waterfront.

AOI.text: Ancona serves as capital of the Marches, on the Adriatic coast of Italy. The Duomo di San Ciriaco and Mole Vanvitelliana anchor the old port, with the Museo archeologico nazionale delle Marche nearby. Ten hours from May through August covers the highlights.

PSR.text: Pescara is the largest city in Abruzzo, a seaside resort on the coast of Italy. Nave di Cascella and the Cattedrale di San Cetteo come first, with the Basilica della Madonna dei sette dolori close by. May through August, in about ten hours, suits it well.

LDE.text: Lourdes draws pilgrims to the Hautes-Pyrenees region of France for the Grotte de Massabielle. The Rosary Basilica and Chateau fort de Lourdes sit close together, with Pic du Jer nearby. May through September, in about six hours, takes in the highlights.

BHX.text: Birmingham anchors the West Midlands as Britain's second-largest city. Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery plus Aston Hall come first, with Birmingham Town Hall close by. June and August suit a full seventeen-hour visit.

EIN.text: Eindhoven is an industrial city in the Netherlands, built around Philips rather than a historic core. The Evoluon and van Abbe Museum lead, with Muziekgebouw Frits Philips Eindhoven for an evening; plan on ten hours, best from May to September.

BOJ.text: Burgas is a Black Sea city in Bulgaria known for beaches and nightlife alongside its salt lakes. Lake Atanasovsko and Lake Pomorie draw birdwatchers, and Poda Protected Area rounds it out; seven hours suffices, ideally in May, June or September.

gem:botosani.text: Botosani is a city in Romania built around textiles rather than tourism. Popauti Monastery and the Nicolae Iorga Memorial House are worth the detour, with Agafton Monastery further out; eight hours covers it well between May and September.

gem:jagodina.text: Jagodina is a small town in Serbia with a cluster of historic sites rather than crowds. Crni Vrh and Stara Crkva anchor a visit, and Jagodina Zoo suits families; three hours is plenty, best April through June or in September.

gem:portsmouth.text: Portsmouth is a coastal city in the United Kingdom, home to the Mary Rose and Portchester Castle. Southsea Castle and Spitbank Fort fill a full day, and Calshot Beach sits nearby for downtime; ten hours works well from June through September.

gem:formia.text: Formia is a small town in Italy on the coast, with the Cisternone Romano among its ancient remains. The Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Formia adds context; six hours suits it, best in April or May.

gem:sagama.text: Sagama is a tiny village in Italy, home to just over two hundred people. The Castello di Serravalle and Saint Peter church are the reasons to stop, with Spiaggia di Bosa Marina below; three hours suits it well, best in May, June or September.

gem:tinnura.text: Tinnura is a small village in Italy, under three hundred people. The Castello di Serravalle and Chiesa di Nostra Signora de Sos Regnos Altos are the sights, and Spiaggia di Bosa Marina lies below; three hours does the job, best May, June or September.

gem:tresnuraghes.text: Tresnuraghes is a village in Italy, home to just over a thousand people. The Castello di Serravalle and Concattedrale dell'Immacolata Concezione are worth the stop; allow three hours, best April through June or in September.

gem:roseto-degli-abruzzi.text: Roseto degli Abruzzi is a small seaside town in Italy, home to about sixteen thousand people. Santa Maria a Mare and the pinacoteca civica V. Bindi lead the stops; four hours is enough, best April through June or September.

FKB.text: Karlsruhe-Baden is the small gateway airport for Baden-Baden in Germany, a spa town rather than a destination itself. Schloss Rastatt and Hohenbaden Castle are worth the trip; three hours suffices, best May through September.

LCJ.text: Lodz is a major art city in Poland, part of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. The Izrael Poznanski Palace and White Factory lead the sights; seventeen hours would cover them all, best May through September.

BLL.text: Billund is a village in Denmark built almost entirely around one attraction. Legoland Billund and LEGO House anchor the visit, and Jelling Church makes a quieter stop nearby; three hours covers the main sights, best June through August.

TGM.text: Targu Mures is a historic city in Romania, its Teleki Library among the oldest sights in Transylvania. The Saint John the Baptist Church and Ascension of the Lord Cathedral anchor the center; ten hours covers it, best May, June, August or September.

INI.text: Nis is a historic city in Serbia built on Roman foundations, once known as Naissus. Skull Tower and Mediana are the top stops, with the Crveni Krst concentration camp for something heavier; eight hours is enough, best in May, June or September.

SKP.text: Skopje is a historic city in North Macedonia, its Skopje Fortress and Stone Bridge anchoring the old center. Vodno rises just outside for a hike; seventeen hours of sights are on offer, best April through June or in September.

gem:wilhelmshaven.text: Wilhelmshaven is a port city in Germany built around its naval history. The Marinemuseum and Kustenmuseum Wilhelmshaven cover that story, while Theater am Meer and the Botanischer Garten round out a visit; ten hours works well, best June through August.

gem:valjevo.text: Valjevo is a city in Serbia set among churches and monasteries rather than a single big draw. Celije Monastery and Crkva Uspenja Bogorodice lead the list; seven hours covers it, best April through June or September.

gem:lozenets.text: Lozenets is a small coastal village in Bulgaria, home to under seven hundred people. South beach and North beach are the main draw, with Arkutino and the Silkosiya Reserve nearby; two hours is plenty, best May, June or September.

gem:dunkirk.text: Dunkirk is a port city in France known first for its beaches rather than its old town. The Phare de Dunkerque anchors a walk through the center, with Plage de Zuydcoote further along the coast; count on ten hours, best June through August.

BZG.text: Bydgoszcz is a city in Poland along the Brda river, with well preserved architecture. Opera Nova and the Botanic Garden of Casimir the Great University lead the sights; seventeen hours of sights await, best May through September.

BJZ.text: Badajoz is a border city in Spain, its old center anchored by a Moorish citadel. The Alcazaba de Badajoz and Badajoz Cathedral lead the sights, with the Museo de Bellas Artes de Badajoz for an afternoon; nine hours is enough, best in April or May.

EMA.text: East Midlands covers the area around Derby in the United Kingdom, better known for museums than for crowds. The Derby Museum and Art Gallery and Pickford's House lead a day out; four hours is enough, best June through September.

gem:kecskemet.text: Kecskemet is a city in Hungary built around its churches and theatres rather than one big sight. The Reformed church and Lutheran Church anchor the center; give it eight hours, best April through June or September.

gem:garmen.text: Garmen is a small village in Bulgaria near ancient Nikopolis ad Nestum. The Karaca Pasa Mosque is the other reason to detour here, with Saint George Church nearby; three hours will do, best May, June or September.

gem:vranje.text: Vranje is a historic city in Serbia and part of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network. Vranjska Banja and the White Bridge lead a visit, with Pljackovica for a walk outside town; six hours covers it, best May, June or September.

gem:manfredonia.text: Manfredonia is a coastal city in Italy, with Monte Sant'Angelo rising just above it. San Michele arcangelo and Pulsano Abbey are the main stops, and the Museo Nazionale Archeologico rounds things out; plan on eight hours, best in April or May.

gem:san-benedetto-del-tronto.text: San Benedetto del Tronto is a seaside town in Italy, its Basilica Cattedrale di Santa Maria della Marina facing the water. The Faro and Torre dei Gualtieri are worth a look; five hours is enough, best May, June or September.

BES.text: Brest is a coastal city in Brittany, France, with the Chateau de Brest anchoring the old port. Pont de l'Iroise makes for a scenic walk, and plage du Moulin-Blanc is close by; ten hours covers it, best June through September.

RZE.text: Rzeszow is a city in Poland built up around Rzeszow Castle rather than one headline sight. The Muzeum Historii Miasta Rzeszowa adds context, and Rezerwat Lisia Gora sits just outside for greenery; ten hours covers it well, best from May through September.

DEB.text: Debrecen has long been tied to Protestant history in Hungary. The Protestant Great Church and Debrecen Reformed College anchor the center; eight hours is enough, best April through June or September.

CND.text: Constanta is a coastal city in Romania on the Black Sea, as much about nightlife and beaches as about old streets. The Carol I Mosque is the standout sight; eight hours in town is plenty, best May through September.

gem:hill-of-crosses.text: Hill of Crosses sits near Siauliai in Lithuania, a place for pilgrimage rather than a typical sightseeing stop. Siauliai Cathedral and Naisiai Manor combine well with a visit; six hours covers it, best June through August.

gem:druskininkai.text: Druskininkai is a spa town in Lithuania and a quiet base for families. Grutas Park and Snow Arena are the big draws, with the Joy of all who Sorrow Church for something calmer; four hours covers the highlights, best May through August.

gem:foggia.text: Foggia sits in Apulia, Italy, with Arpi marking its ancient roots. The Cattedrale and Teatro Umberto Giordano anchor the center, with Chiesa delle Croci for a quieter stop; eight hours is enough, best in April or May.

gem:asenovgrad.text: Asenovgrad is a city in Bulgaria at the foot of the Rhodope range, with Bachkovo Monastery just outside town. Asen's Fortress and the Church of St John the Baptist lead the sights; eight hours covers it, best April, May, September or October.

gem:chiclana-de-la-frontera.text: Chiclana de la Frontera is a city in Spain known for its beaches near Cadiz. Playa de Camposoto and Playa de Santa Catalina are the main draws; nine hours covers a full day, best May through July or in September.

CRV.text: Crotone is a coastal city in Calabria, Italy, with roots back to ancient Magna Graecia. The Area archeologica di Capo Colonna and Palazzo Barracco are the top stops, with Pitagora recalling its ancient legacy; eight hours fills a day, best in May.

BVE.text: Brive is a city in France in the Limousin region, its full name Brive-la-Gaillarde. Collegiale Saint-Martin and the Musee Labenche lead the sights, with Lac du Causse nearby for a break; nine hours covers it, best from May through September.

SZZ.text: Szczecin is a port city in Poland, with the Old City Town Hall anchoring its center. The Szczecin Philharmonic and Dabie Lake round out a visit; seventeen hours of sights await, best May through September.

TGD.text: Podgorica sits in Montenegro as a city built around Doclea and the Millennium Bridge, and the Cathedral of the Resurrection of Christ. The center takes about seven hours, best visited in May or June, with Lake Skadar and Lovcen nearby.

gem:eraclea.text: Eraclea is a village in Italy, with Torre Caligo and the Antiche Mura among its older sights. Two hours covers the center, best in May or June, and Spiaggia di Eraclea Mare or Laguna del Mort round out an afternoon nearby.

PRN.text: Pristina is a city of Kosovo, anchored by the National Library of Kosovo and the Cathedral of Saint Mother Teresa. The center rewards about fifteen hours, best in May, June, July or September, with Gracanica monastery and Batllava Lake nearby.

KIV.text: Chisinau is a city of Moldova, known for wine as well as the Cathedral of Divine Providence and the Rose Valley. The full circuit takes about seventeen hours, best in May, June or September, with Orheiul Vechi a fine day trip beyond Ghidighici Reservoir.

gem:fondi.text: Fondi is a town in Italy, where the Castello Baronale di Fondi and Abbazia di San Magno anchor a walkable old center. The sights take about five hours, best from April through June, with Lago di Fondi close enough for a swim afterward.

gem:seirijai.text: Seirijai is a small village in Lithuania, once a market town, with the Church of Our Lady of the Scapular as its main sight. Two hours covers the village, best between May and August, with lakes Dusia and Ancia within walking distance.

KOW.text: Knock is a small village in Ireland, known for religion, with County Mayo and nearby Kilkelly, Charlestown, Kilmovee and Carracastle all close at hand. Two hours suits a short stop, best in June, July or August, with Lough Talt a scenic detour nearby.

gem:tergu.text: Tergu is a small village in Italy, where the Castello dei Doria and Elephant Rock stand near Punta Tramontana beach. The highlights take about four hours, best from June through August, with Monte Elias offering a short hike beyond the village.

SNN.text: Shannon is a town in Ireland, in County Clare near Limerick, with Bunratty Castle and Thomond Park nearby. The town itself takes about three hours, best in June, July or August, and King John's Castle and St Mary's Cathedral are in Limerick too.

CRA.text: Craiova stands in Romania as a city anchored by Parcul Nicolae Romanescu and the Museum of Oltenia. Six hours suits it well, best in April, May, June or September, with Carol I National College and the Cathedral of Saint Demetrius nearby.

CRL.text: Charleroi is a city of Belgium, where BPS22 and Trazegnies Castle sit alongside reminders of the Battle of Charleroi. Ten hours suits a full day, best from May through September, with the Eau d'Heure lakes and Rochers de Freyr within easy reach.

BNX.text: Banja Luka is a city of Bosnia and Herzegovina, with the Ferhat Pasha Mosque and Kastel Fortress marking its old core. The center takes about five hours, best in May, June or September, with Banski Dvor and Mariastern Abbey for a longer stay.

gem:hengelo.text: Hengelo is a city of the Netherlands, with Station Hengelo as its own anchor and Rijksmuseum Twenthe a short trip away in Enschede. Ten hours suits both together, best from May through August, with Twickel and Delden as an easy add-on nearby.

gem:herning.text: Herning lies in Denmark as a city where HEART and the Carl-Henning Pedersen og Else Alfelts Museum lead its art scene. Herning Kirke and Baunekirken round out about eight hours, best in June, July or August, with Bolling lake and Fuglsang Lake close by.

LMZ.text: Lamezia Terme is a coastal city in Italy, with Bastione di Malta and Terina among its main sights. The sights fill about seven hours, best in May or June, and Monte Reventino near Botte Donato adds a mountain detour.

gem:dzhebel.text: Dzhebel is a small historic village in Bulgaria, with Dyavolski most and the Chamlaka Reserve as its main draws. Two hours covers the highlights, best in May, June or September, and public transport in the area is limited.

BCM.text: Bacau stands in Romania as a city anchored by Petricica and the George Bacovia Memorial House. Six hours covers the center, best in May, June or September, with the Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary nearby in the old quarter.

TZL.text: Tuzla stands in Bosnia and Herzegovina as a city where Bijela dzamija and Sarena dzamija give the old town its color. The mosques and Behram-Begova Medresa Tuzla take about seven hours, best in May, June or September, with Modrac Lake nearby.

gem:stykkisholmur.text: Stykkisholmur is a small village in Iceland, ringed by Helgafell and the peaks of Ljosufjoll and Drapuhlidarfjall. Two hours suits a quick stop, best in June or July, and public transport in the area is poor.

HHN.text: Frankfurt-Hahn is a small village in Germany, close to the Hunsruck hills. Burg Dill and the Evangelische Kirche Kappel round out about three hours, best from June through September, with the Lott-Festival and Grube Adolph-Helene nearby.
